Cook penne pasta according to package directions until al dente. Drain, reserving 100 ml pasta water.
Dice onion. Mince garlic. Add remaining 15 ml olive oil to the same skillet. Sauté diced onion 3-4 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic and smoked paprika. Sauté 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in crushed tomatoes and chicken broth. Bring to a simmer. Cook 5 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Reduce heat to low. Stir in heavy cream and American cheese slices until cheese is fully melted and sauce is smooth.
Add cooked pasta to the sauce. Toss to coat evenly. If sauce is too thick, add reserved pasta water gradually until desired consistency is reached.
Slice rested chicken breasts into thick medallions or substantial chunks.
Serve pasta onto plates. Arrange chicken medallions on top of the pasta. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken Thighs with Cheesy Scalloped Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of pan-seared chicken thigh, cheesy scalloped potatoes, and roasted broccoli is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The chicken thigh is golden brown with visibly crispy skin, placed as a whole piece, not sliced. Beside it, a neatly defined portion of creamy scalloped potatoes, showcasing the layers of thinly sliced potatoes and melted Gruyere cheese, with a golden-brown, bubbly top. Vibrant green, tender-crisp broccoli florets are arranged naturally next to the potatoes. The plate has moderate negative space, allowing each component to stand out. A small sprig of fresh thyme garnishes the chicken. The setting is a modern bistro, with a simple light wooden table surface and a white cotton napkin folded beside the plate. Natural, even lighting highlights the textures and colors of the food. The entire plate is visible, with a soft, out-of-focus background creating a casual yet refined restaurant atmosphere.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C. Grease a 20x20 cm baking dish or four individual ramekins.
Peel and thinly slice potatoes into 2-3 mm rounds. Set aside.
Melt butter in a saucepan over medium heat. Add flour and whisk for 1 minute to create a roux.
Gradually whisk in heavy cream and milk until smooth. Bring to a simmer, stirring constantly.
Add minced garlic, 1 sprig of thyme, salt, and pepper. Simmer for 2 minutes, then remove thyme sprig.
Stir in 100g of grated Gruyere cheese until melted and smooth. Remove from heat.
Arrange a layer of potato slices in the prepared dish. Pour a thin layer of cheese sauce over potatoes. Repeat layering, ending with sauce.
Bake scalloped potatoes for 40-50 minutes, or until potatoes are tender and top is golden brown and bubbly.
Toss broccoli florets with olive oil, salt, and pepper on a baking sheet. Roast in the oven with potatoes for the last 15-20 minutes, until tender-crisp.
Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Add chicken thighs, skin-side down.
Sear chicken for 8-10 minutes until skin is deeply golden and crispy. Do not move chicken during this time.
Flip chicken thighs. Transfer skillet to the preheated oven. Bake for 10-15 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F).
Remove chicken from oven. Let rest for 5 minutes before serving.
Portion scalloped potatoes and roasted broccoli onto plates. Place one pan-seared chicken thigh beside them. Garnish with fresh thyme sprigs.

recipes.recipe_name: Panang Chicken Gnocchi
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of vibrant Panang Chicken Gnocchi is presented in a clean, white porcelain bowl, set on a simple wooden table. The dish features tender, 2 cm cubed chicken pieces and pillowy, irregularly shaped gnocchi, all coated in a rich, creamy, reddish-orange Panang curry sauce. The sauce's surface shimmers with natural oils, indicating its depth. Scattered across the top are fresh, bright green Thai basil leaves, adding a pop of color and aromatic contrast. A few thin, bright red chili slices are artfully placed as a garnish. The overall composition is balanced, with moderate negative space around the edges of the bowl. Beside the bowl, a neatly folded cotton napkin and a traditional Thai-style serving spoon rest on the wooden surface, hinting at an authentic yet modern bistro setting. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and inviting colors.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately as a main course.
Offer steamed jasmine rice on the side for those who prefer extra sauce absorption.
Provide small bowls of extra fish sauce, lime wedges, and sliced bird's eye chilies for individual seasoning.
instructions: Prepare Gnocchi Dough: In a large bowl, combine flour and salt. Create a well in the center. Crack eggs into the well.
Mix Dough: Gradually mix flour into eggs using a fork, then hands, until a shaggy dough forms.
Knead Dough: Turn dough onto a lightly floured surface. Knead for 5-7 minutes until smooth and elastic. Cover with a damp cloth. Let rest 20 minutes.
Shape Gnocchi: Divide dough into 4 equal portions. Roll each portion into a long rope, about 1.5 cm thick. Cut ropes into 2 cm pieces. Lightly dust with flour to prevent sticking.
Cook Gnocchi: Bring a large pot of salted water to a rolling boil. Add gnocchi in batches. Cook until they float to the surface, plus 1 minute. Remove with a slotted spoon. Drain well. Set aside.
Start Curry: Heat vegetable oil in a large wok or deep skillet over medium heat. Add minced garlic and sliced shallots. Sauté until fragrant, about 1 minute.
Bloom Curry Paste: Add Panang curry paste. Stir-fry for 2-3 minutes until aromatic and oil separates.
Add Chicken: Add chicken cubes. Sauté until lightly browned on all sides.

Simmer Curry: Pour in coconut milk and water. Add fish sauce, palm sugar, and torn kaffir lime leaves. Bring to a gentle simmer. Cook for 10-12 minutes, or until chicken reaches 75°C (167°F) internal temperature. Stir occasionally.
Finish Sauce: Stir in coconut vinegar. Taste and adjust seasoning as needed.
Combine: Add cooked gnocchi to the curry sauce. Gently toss to coat. Simmer for 1-2 minutes to allow gnocchi to absorb flavors.
Serve: Ladle Panang Chicken Gnocchi onto individual plates. Garnish generously with fresh Thai basil leaves and optional red chili slices.
traditional_techniques: Balancing the four main Thai flavors: spicy, sour, salty, sweet

recipes.recipe_name: Garlic Chicken and Brown Rice Orzo Pilaf
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of Garlic Chicken and Brown Rice Orzo Pilaf is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. At the center, a fluffy, golden-brown mound of pilaf features distinct grains of brown rice and small orzo pasta, interspersed with finely diced caramelized onion and flecks of vibrant green fresh parsley. Nestled within and around the pilaf are several substantial, golden-brown seared chicken chunks, exhibiting a slightly crispy exterior and tender interior. The dish is garnished with a scattering of fresh chopped parsley and a bright yellow lemon wedge positioned artfully on the side of the pilaf. The overall composition is balanced and inviting, with moderate negative space. The plate rests on a simple light wooden table surface. A neatly folded white cotton napkin is placed beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its warm colors and inviting textures. The background is minimal and slightly blurred, suggesting a casual bistro atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with fresh lemon wedges for a bright finish
Pair with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and vinegar
instructions: Cut chicken thighs into 3 cm chunks. Season chicken with salt, pepper, and paprika.
Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add chicken chunks. Sear until golden brown on all sides. Remove chicken from pot. Set aside.
Dice the onion. Mince the garlic. Add onion to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and dried oregano. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add brown rice and orzo pasta to the pot. Stir to coat with pan drippings. Toast for 2 minutes.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a simmer. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom.
Return seared chicken to the pot. Stir gently.
Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until liquid is absorbed and rice and orzo are tender. Do not stir excessively.
Remove from heat. Let stand, covered, for 5 minutes.
Chop fresh parsley. Fluff pilaf with a fork. Stir in most of the parsley.
Serve immediately. Garnish with remaining fresh parsley and lemon wedges.

recipes.recipe_name: Compressed Fruit Composition, Blueberry Gel, and Banana Crisp
recipes.visual_description: An ultra-sophisticated, minimalist dessert is presented on a pristine round bone china plate with a subtle, elegant pattern. The composition features a vibrant, smooth smear of blueberry fluid gel as its base, creating an organic, flowing shape. Precisely cut 1.5 cm cubes of glistening compressed apple and pear are artfully arranged atop the gel, showcasing their translucent, firm texture and natural light colors. Beside them, a single, delicate, golden-brown banana crisp stands upright, providing a contrasting, crisp texture. A small pool of clear, pale lime-vanilla consommé gently surrounds the base of the fruit, adding a subtle sheen. The plate features abundant negative space, highlighting the architectural precision and simplicity of the elements. A few vibrant green micro basil leaves are strategically placed as the sole, precise garnish. The scene is lit with dramatic professional lighting, casting soft shadows, set on a premium white Carrara marble surface with a precisely folded white linen napkin in the background.
instructions: Prepare Compressed Fruit:
Peel, core, and cut apples and pears into precise 1.5 cm cubes.
In a small saucepan, combine 50 ml water, 20 g sugar, and a pinch of lime zest. Heat until sugar dissolves. Let cool.
Place fruit cubes and cooled syrup into a vacuum seal bag. Vacuum seal to compress. Refrigerate for at least 2 hours.
Prepare Blueberry Fluid Gel:
Combine blueberries with 50 ml water and 30 g sugar in a saucepan. Simmer until berries soften. Blend until smooth.
Strain the blueberry mixture through a fine-mesh sieve to remove solids. Discard solids.
Return strained puree to saucepan. Whisk in agar-agar powder. Bring to a boil, whisking constantly for 1 minute. Pour into a shallow dish. Refrigerate until firm.
Once firm, cut gel into cubes. Blend in a high-speed blender until completely smooth and fluid. Transfer to a squeeze bottle or piping bag. Keep chilled.
Prepare Banana Crisp:
Preheat oven to 100°C (212°F). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Slice bananas very thinly, about 1 mm, using a mandoline. Arrange slices in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet.
Bake for 45-60 minutes, or until golden brown and crisp. Check frequently to prevent burning. Let cool completely on a wire rack.
Prepare Lime-Vanilla Consommé:
In a saucepan, combine 150 ml water, 100 g sugar, lime zest, and vanilla bean (split and scraped).
Bring to a gentle simmer over medium heat, stirring until sugar dissolves. Simmer for 5 minutes.
Remove from heat. Let cool completely. Strain through a fine-mesh sieve. Discard zest and vanilla bean. Stir in lime juice to taste. Refrigerate until well chilled.
Assemble the Dish:
On each chilled plate, create an organic smear of blueberry fluid gel.
Artfully arrange 5-7 compressed apple and pear cubes on top of or beside the gel.
Carefully place one or two banana crisps next to the fruit.
Gently pour a small amount of the chilled lime-vanilla consommé around the base of the fruit components.
Garnish with a few delicate micro basil or mint leaves.

recipes.recipe_name: Chilled Fruit Composition with Lemon Evaporated Milk Foam
recipes.visual_description: A pristine white bone china plate holds an individual portion of a Chilled Fruit Composition. Precision-cut 1 cm cubes of vibrant red plum, pale yellow peach, crisp white apple, and translucent pear are artfully arranged in a flowing, organic cluster on one side of the plate. Each fruit cube is distinct, showcasing its natural color and texture. A delicate, airy cloud of lemon evaporated milk foam rests beside the fruit, its pristine white contrasting with the fruit's colors. The composition is minimalist with abundant negative space. A single, small, vibrant green mint leaf or micro-basil is placed precisely on the foam for a refined garnish. The plate rests on a premium grey veined marble surface. A pristine white linen napkin, folded into a precise triangle, and a delicate silver dessert spoon are placed beside the plate. Dramatic professional lighting creates soft shadows, highlighting textures. The background is ultra-minimalist and uncluttered.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve as a refreshing palate cleanser between courses.
Present as a light, elegant dessert after a multi-course meal.
instructions: Prepare simple syrup: Combine 30g sugar and 100ml water in a small saucepan. Heat until sugar dissolves. Cool completely.
Prepare fruits: Peel and core apple and pear. Peel peach and plum.
Cut fruits: Dice apple, pear, peach, and plum into precise 1 cm cubes. Ensure uniform size and clean edges.
Chill fruits: Gently toss diced fruits with 30 ml of cooled simple syrup. Chill in refrigerator for at least 30 minutes.

Prepare lemon evaporated milk foam: In a chilled bowl, combine evaporated milk, juice from half a lemon, and zest from the whole lemon. Whisk vigorously until light and frothy, resembling a delicate foam. Do not over-whisk.

Assemble dish: Arrange chilled fruit cubes artfully on individual plates, creating a natural, organic composition with ample negative space. Spoon a generous cloud of lemon evaporated milk foam alongside the fruit.
Serve immediately.
notes: Use only premium, perfectly ripe seasonal fruits for optimal flavor and texture.
Ensure all fruits are chilled thoroughly before plating for a refreshing experience.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Fermented Cabbage and Root Vegetables
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of pan-seared chicken breast is presented on a handcrafted, natural cream-colored ceramic plate. The chicken is a golden-brown whole piece or cut into thick medallions, resting beside a mound of vibrant, naturally colored roasted root vegetables – earthy orange carrots, pale yellow parsnips, and golden-brown potatoes, all cut into rustic 2 cm chunks. A small pile of glossy, pale green fermented cabbage provides a textural and color contrast. A rich, dark amber chicken bone broth reduction is artfully drizzled over the chicken and vegetables. The composition is minimalistic, with ample negative space. The plate sits on a light, textured reclaimed wood surface. A simple, undyed linen napkin in natural beige is casually folded beside the plate. Soft, natural light illuminates the scene from the side, highlighting the food's natural textures. The background is clean and slightly blurred, with a hint of natural plant life. The overall aesthetic is organic, clean, and highlights the inherent beauty of sustainable ingredients.
instructions: Prepare Chicken Bone Broth: Place chicken bones in a large pot. Add 1 peeled and quartered onion, 2 crushed garlic cloves, 1 sprig thyme, and 1 sprig rosemary. Cover with 2 litres cold water. Bring to a simmer. Skim any foam. Reduce heat to low. Simmer for 2-4 hours. Strain broth. Discard solids. Reduce broth in a saucepan over medium heat until thickened to a sauce consistency, about 200ml. Season with salt and pepper.

Prepare Root Vegetables: Preheat oven to 200°C. Peel carrots and parsnips. Cut carrots, parsnips, and potatoes into 2 cm chunks. Toss with 30ml olive oil, 2 crushed garlic cloves, 2 sprigs thyme, 1 sprig rosemary, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking tray. Roast for 30-40 minutes, or until tender and lightly browned.

Cook Chicken: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season with salt and pepper. Heat 30ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken breasts for 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown. Transfer skillet to preheated oven. Cook for 10-15 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove from oven. Rest chicken for 5 minutes.

Plate Dish: Place roasted root vegetables on a plate. Spoon fermented cabbage next to vegetables. Slice rested chicken breast into thick medallions or serve whole. Arrange chicken on plate. Drizzle chicken bone broth reduction over chicken and vegetables.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Beef Shepherd's Pie with Cauliflower-Potato Mash
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of hearty beef shepherd's pie is presented on a simple, round ceramic plate, set on a well-used wooden dining table. The golden-brown cauliflower-potato mash topping forms a rustic, slightly uneven crust, with visible fork tines creating textural ridges. Some of the rich, savory beef and vegetable filling, with its diced carrots, crumbled beef, and sliced mushrooms, peeks through at the edges. The natural colors of the ingredients are evident: the warm browns of the beef and mushrooms, the orange of the carrots, and the light green of the peas, contrasting with the creamy, off-white mash. A single, simple metal fork rests beside the plate. The lighting is warm and inviting, typical of a cozy family kitchen, with a casual, lived-in atmosphere in the background. The entire plate is visible, with modest, home-style portions that feel comforting and approachable.
instructions: Peel potatoes and cut into 2 cm chunks. Cut cauliflower into florets. Place potatoes and cauliflower in a large pot. Cover with cold water. Add a pinch of salt. Bring to a boil. Cook until very tender, about 15-20 minutes.
Drain potatoes and cauliflower well. Return to the pot. Add butter, milk or cream, and a pinch of salt and pepper. Mash until smooth and creamy. Set aside.
Preheat oven to 190°C (375°F).
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add ground beef. Cook, breaking it up with a spoon, until browned. Drain excess fat.
Add diced onion and diced carrots to the skillet. Cook for 5-7 minutes until softened. Add sliced mushrooms. Cook until mushrooms release their liquid and brown, about 5 minutes.
Stir in minced garlic and tomato paste. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in beef broth and Worcestershire sauce. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 5 minutes, allowing sauce to thicken slightly. Stir in fresh thyme. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Stir in frozen peas. Remove from heat.

Spoon the beef mixture evenly into an oven-safe baking dish or leave in the skillet. Spread the cauliflower-potato mash over the beef mixture. Use a fork to create peaks and ridges on the mash surface.
Bake for 25-30 minutes, or until the topping is golden brown and the filling is bubbling. Let stand for 5 minutes before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Beef and Mushroom Shepherd's Pie
recipes.visual_description: A deeply comforting, golden-brown Hearty Beef and Mushroom Shepherd's Pie, presented in a rustic, well-used ceramic baking dish. The surface of the potato-cauliflower mash topping is a rich golden hue with darker, crispy peaks and soft, creamy valleys, showing distinct fork marks. Below, the savory beef and mushroom filling, visible where the mash is slightly uneven, is a dark, rich brown, bubbling invitingly at the edges of the dish. The beef mince is browned and the mushrooms are tender. The dish sits on a sturdy, well-worn wooden dining table, suggesting a family meal. Everyday ceramic plates, possibly with a subtle earthy tone, are casually stacked nearby. A simple cloth napkin is loosely folded beside the dish. The lighting is warm and natural, casting soft shadows that emphasize the pie's texture. A single, generous portion is scooped onto a plain ceramic plate, showing the distinct layers of creamy mash and hearty beef filling. A sprinkle of fresh, vibrant green chopped parsley adds a touch of freshness. The overall scene evokes a cozy, lived-in kitchen atmosphere, focusing on wholesome, expertly prepared comfort food.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve directly from the baking dish, with a side of simple green salad if desired.
instructions: Peel and chop potatoes into large, even chunks. Cut cauliflower into florets. Dice the onion. Slice the mushrooms.
Place potatoes and cauliflower in a large pot. Cover with cold salted water. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer until very tender, about 15-20 minutes.
While vegetables cook, heat vegetable oil in a large oven-safe pan or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add beef mince and cook, breaking it up with a spoon, until browned all over. Drain excess fat.
Add diced onion to the pan with the beef. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes. Add sliced mushrooms and cook until softened and any liquid has evaporated.

Stir in plain flour and cook for 1 minute. Add tomato paste and cook for another minute. Gradually pour in beef stock and Worcestershire sauce, stirring constantly to prevent lumps. Bring to a simmer and cook until the sauce thickens, about 5-7 minutes. Season with salt and pepper.
Drain the cooked potatoes and cauliflower thoroughly. Return to the pot. Add milk and butter. Mash until smooth and creamy. Stir in grated cheddar cheese if using. Season with salt and pepper.

Pour the beef mixture into a suitable oven-safe baking dish (if not already in one). Spread evenly. Carefully spoon the potato-cauliflower mash over the beef mixture, spreading it to the edges. Create ridges with a fork for texture.
Place the baking dish on a baking tray. Bake in a preheated oven at 190°C (375°F) for 25-30 minutes, or until the topping is golden brown and the filling is bubbling.
Let the pie rest for a few minutes before serving. Garnish with chopped fresh parsley.
notes: For an extra rich flavour, a splash of red wine can be added with the beef stock.
Ensure the mash is not too wet, or it will sink into the filling.
The pie can be prepared ahead of time and refrigerated. Bake longer if baking from cold.
traditional_techniques: Browning meat for depth of flavor
Making a roux-like base for sauce thickening
Mashing root vegetables for a comforting topping

recipes.recipe_name: Homestyle Beef and Mushroom Shepherd's Pie with Cauliflower Mash
recipes.visual_description: A hearty, golden-brown Homestyle Beef and Mushroom Shepherd's Pie is presented in a rustic, oval ceramic baking dish, set on a well-worn wooden kitchen table. The mashed potato and cauliflower topping, casually spooned, forms a thick, slightly browned crust with inviting peaks. Beneath, the rich, savory beef mince, diced onion, and sliced mushrooms are visible where the topping is generously piled. The beef is finely crumbled, mixed with softened, translucent diced onion and earthy brown mushroom slices in a deep, glossy brown gravy. The overall palette is warm, with golden-browns, creamy whites, and deep umber tones. A simple white ceramic plate with a modest individual portion is placed beside the dish, showcasing a generous scoop of the pie, its layers clearly defined. A metal fork rests casually on the table next to the plate. The scene is lit by warm, inviting kitchen light, suggesting a comforting family meal.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe pan or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Add beef mince. Brown thoroughly, breaking it up. Drain excess fat.
Add diced onion and sliced mushrooms to the pan. Cook until softened, 5-7 minutes.
Stir in minced garlic and tomato paste. Cook for 1 minute.
Sprinkle flour over beef and vegetables. Stir for 1 minute.
Gradually pour in beef broth and Worcestershire sauce. Bring to a simmer. Cook until sauce thickens, about 5 minutes. Season with salt and pepper.
While beef simmers, boil chopped potatoes and cauliflower florets in salted water until very tender, 15-20 minutes.
Drain potatoes and cauliflower well. Return to the pot.
Add milk and butter. Mash until smooth. Season with salt and pepper.
Pour beef mixture into an oven-safe dish (if not using an oven-safe pan).
Spoon mashed potato and cauliflower topping over beef mixture. Spread evenly.
Bake for 25-30 minutes, or until topping is golden brown and filling bubbles.
Rest for 5 minutes before serving. Garnish with fresh parsley.
notes: This dish is excellent for making ahead and reheating.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Chicken & Tomato Pasta Soup
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of hearty Chicken & Tomato Pasta Soup is presented in a deep, rustic ceramic bowl on a well-used wooden dining table. The rich, reddish-orange broth is filled with generous chunks of seared chicken, small pasta shapes, and tender diced tomatoes. Flecks of green oregano are visible throughout. A casual sprinkle of vibrant green chopped fresh basil rests on top, alongside a small mound of finely grated Parmesan cheese, slightly melting into the hot soup. The components naturally overlap, creating a comforting and inviting appearance. The bowl sits on a simple, slightly imperfect everyday ceramic plate. A casually folded cloth napkin and a standard metal spoon are beside the bowl. Warm, cozy lighting from overhead kitchen fixtures illuminates the scene, enhancing the homely, lived-in atmosphere of a family kitchen.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm, crusty bread for dipping.
Offer extra grated Parmesan cheese at the table.
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add diced chicken. Cook until browned on all sides, about 5-7 minutes. Remove chicken and set aside.
Add diced onion to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and dried oregano. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in canned diced tomatoes and chicken broth. Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to medium-low. Add cooked chicken back to the pot. Simmer for 15 minutes.
Add pasta to the soup. Cook according to package directions until al dente, usually 8-10 minutes. Ensure chicken reaches 75°C (167°F).
Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Ladle hot soup into bowls. Garnish each serving with fresh chopped basil and grated Parmesan cheese.
notes: For added depth, use homemade chicken broth.
Leftover soup thickens. Add a splash of broth or water when reheating if desired.

recipes.recipe_name: Homestyle Beef and Mushroom Cottage Pie
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of Homestyle Beef and Mushroom Cottage Pie is presented in a sturdy, everyday ceramic bowl with natural imperfections. The topping is a thick, rustic layer of golden-brown mashed potato and cauliflower, showing textured peaks and valleys from fork marks. The rich, dark beef mince and sliced mushroom filling is visible around the edges where the mash slightly pulls away. The surface of the mash has a comforting, slightly crispy baked finish. The bowl rests on a well-worn, warm-toned wooden kitchen table. A simple, off-white linen napkin is casually folded beside the bowl. A standard metal fork lies next to the dish. The scene is illuminated by warm, soft ambient light, creating gentle shadows that highlight the textures of the pie, evoking a relaxed, lived-in family kitchen atmosphere. The entire dish and immediate surroundings are visible, with a modest portion size.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve hot with a side of steamed green peas or green beans.
Offer crusty bread for dipping into the rich sauce.
Enjoy as a comforting family meal.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.
Heat olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat.
Add beef mince. Cook until browned. Break up any clumps. Drain excess fat.
Finely dice the onion. Slice the mushrooms.
Add diced onion and sliced mushrooms to the pan with the beef. Cook until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Stir in tomato paste and Worcestershire sauce. Cook for 1 minute.
Pour in beef broth. Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low. Cook for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until sauce thickens slightly.
Season beef mixture with salt and pepper. Set aside.
Peel and cut potatoes into large chunks. Cut cauliflower into florets.
Place potatoes and cauliflower in a large pot. Cover with cold salted water. Bring to a boil. Cook until very tender, about 15-20 minutes.
Drain potatoes and cauliflower well. Return to the hot pot.
Add butter and milk. Mash until smooth and creamy. Season with salt and pepper.
Spoon the beef mixture into an ovenproof dish. Spread evenly.
Top the beef with the mashed potato and cauliflower mixture. Use a fork to create peaks and ridges on the surface.
Bake for 25-30 minutes, or until the topping is golden brown and the filling is bubbling.
Allow to rest for 5 minutes before serving.
notes: Ensure the beef mince is well-browned for maximum flavor.
Do not over-mash the potato and cauliflower; some small lumps add to the rustic charm.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Beef & Mushroom Cottage Pie with Cauliflower Mash Topping
recipes.visual_description: A single, modest portion of Hearty Beef & Mushroom Cottage Pie is presented in a rustic, deep ceramic bowl on a well-used wooden dining table. The mashed potato and cauliflower topping is golden-brown with visible fork-made ridges and peaks, indicating a comforting, homemade texture. The rich, dark brown beef mince filling with diced onion and sliced mushrooms is bubbling gently around the edges, peeking through the mash. A sprinkle of fresh, vibrant green chopped parsley sits on top, adding a touch of color. The dish is casually placed alongside a simple, everyday ceramic plate and standard metal cutlery. A casually folded cloth napkin rests beside the bowl. The scene is lit with warm, cozy kitchen lighting, emphasizing the comforting nature of the meal. The focus is entirely on the food, showcasing its natural textures and colors as prepared in a home kitchen.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve hot as a complete meal.
Can be accompanied by a simple side of steamed green vegetables like peas or green beans.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C (375°F).
Peel and dice the onion. Mince garlic cloves. Slice mushrooms thickly.
Heat vegetable oil in a large oven-safe pan or casserole dish over medium-high heat.
Add beef mince. Cook until browned, breaking it up with a spoon. Drain excess fat.
Add diced onion, minced garlic, and sliced mushrooms to the pan. Cook until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Stir in tomato paste and Worcestershire sauce. Cook for 1 minute.
Pour in beef stock. Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low. Cook for 10-15 minutes until sauce slightly thickens.
Meanwhile, peel and chop potatoes into 2 cm chunks. Cut cauliflower into florets.
Place potatoes and cauliflower in a large pot. Cover with salted water. Bring to a boil.
Cook for 15-20 minutes until very tender. Drain thoroughly.
Return potatoes and cauliflower to the pot. Add butter and milk. Mash until smooth. Season with salt and pepper.
Spoon the beef mixture into a 2-liter oven-safe baking dish if not using an oven-safe pan.
Top evenly with the mashed potato and cauliflower mixture. Use a fork to create peaks and ridges on the surface.
Bake for 25-30 minutes, or until the topping is golden brown and the filling is bubbling.
Remove from oven. Let rest for 5 minutes.
Garnish with chopped fresh parsley before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Slow-Braised Beef with Fermented Onion, Cauliflower-Potato Purée, and Crispy Mushrooms
recipes.visual_description: A single individual portion is presented on a handcrafted ceramic plate in a natural cream or beige tone, highlighting the dish with ample negative space. A smooth, off-white cauliflower-potato purée is mounded gently off-center. A substantial, dark brown chunk of slow-braised beef, with its natural irregular shape, rests deliberately beside the purée. Scattered sparingly over and around the beef are a few translucent, pale purple petals of pickled red onion, adding a subtle color contrast. Several thin, golden-brown crispy mushroom slices are arranged casually, leaning against the beef or purée, providing textural interest. A tiny sprig of fresh thyme or a single edible flower petal (from a sustainable source) provides a minimal, organic garnish. The overall composition is clean, unforced, and celebrates the natural beauty and textures of each ingredient. The plate is set on a light, natural bamboo or reclaimed wood table surface, emphasizing eco-conscious materials. An undyed linen napkin in a natural beige is folded simply beside the plate. The background is clean and minimalist, with a soft-focused hint of a green plant or natural element, maintaining an organic feel. Soft, diffused natural light illuminates the scene, enhancing the food's natural colors and textures.
instructions: Prepare pickled onions: Thinly slice one onion into rings. In a small saucepan, combine apple cider vinegar, water, sugar, and a pinch of salt. Bring to a simmer until sugar dissolves. Pour hot liquid over onion slices in a heatproof jar. Let cool to room temperature, then refrigerate for at least 1 hour.

Prepare beef for braising: Cut beef into 4 equal thick chunks. Season beef generously with salt and pepper. Heat olive oil in a heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear beef chunks on all sides until deeply browned. Remove beef from pot and set aside.

Build braising base: Dice the remaining onion, carrot, and celery. Add to the same pot. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened. Mince garlic and add to the pot, cooking for 1 minute until fragrant. Add mushroom stems (if using for zero-waste) to the pot.

Deglaze and simmer: Pour red wine into the pot, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom. Simmer for 2 minutes until slightly reduced. Pour in beef broth and add thyme sprigs. Return seared beef chunks to the pot. Liquid should almost cover the beef. Bring to a gentle simmer.

Braise beef: Cover the pot. Transfer to a preheated oven at 150°C (300°F) or maintain a very low simmer on the stovetop. Cook for 2.5-3 hours, or until beef is fork-tender. Remove beef from liquid and keep warm. Strain braising liquid through a fine-mesh sieve, discarding solids. Reduce liquid over medium-high heat until slightly thickened to a sauce consistency.

Prepare cauliflower-potato purée: Peel and dice potatoes and the remaining cauliflower florets (or use core/stem pieces for zero-waste). Place in a pot of salted cold water. Bring to a boil and cook until very tender, about 15-20 minutes. Drain well. Mash or blend the cooked potatoes and cauliflower with a splash of the reduced braising liquid, a knob of butter (optional), salt, and pepper until smooth and creamy.

Prepare crispy mushrooms: Thinly slice mushroom caps. Heat a dry pan over medium-high heat. Add mushroom slices in a single layer. Cook without stirring until moisture releases and mushrooms start to brown and crisp, about 5-7 minutes. Flip and cook other side. Season with salt and pepper. Alternatively, toss with a little olive oil and roast in a 200°C (400°F) oven until crispy.

Assemble the dish: Spoon a generous dollop of cauliflower-potato purée slightly off-center on each handcrafted ceramic plate. Place one braised beef chunk next to the purée. Arrange a few pickled onion petals artfully over and around the beef. Scatter crispy mushroom slices for texture. Drizzle a small amount of the reduced braising sauce over the beef and purée. Garnish with a tiny sprig of fresh thyme.

recipes.recipe_name: Hungarian Beef Goulash Soup
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Hungarian Beef Goulash Soup is presented in a clean white porcelain bowl, centered on a simple wooden table surface. The soup features a rich, reddish-brown broth, showcasing generous 3 cm cubes of braised beef, along with vibrant 1.5 cm diced carrots and creamy 1.5 cm diced potatoes. A dollop of bright white sour cream sits atop the soup, elegantly garnished with a sprinkle of fresh, bright green flat-leaf parsley. The composition is natural and hearty, balancing the deep, savory colors of the soup with the fresh accents. A folded cotton napkin is placed beside the bowl. Lighting is natural and even, highlighting the dish as the main subject in a modern bistro setting.
instructions: Cut beef chuck into 3 cm cubes. Season with salt and pepper.
Dice onions, mince garlic. Dice carrots and potatoes into 1.5 cm cubes.
Heat vegetable oil in a large pot over medium-high heat. Sear beef cubes until browned on all sides. Remove beef from pot.
Add diced onions to the pot. Cook until soft and deeply golden, about 8-10 minutes. Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Remove pot from heat. Stir in sweet paprika, caraway seeds, and marjoram. Mix well to coat onions.
Return pot to heat. Add crushed tomatoes and stir for 2 minutes.
Return seared beef to the pot. Pour in beef broth. Bring to a simmer.
Reduce heat to low. Cover pot and simmer for 1.5 hours, or until beef is nearly tender.
Add diced carrots and potatoes to the soup. Continue to simmer, uncovered, for another 20-30 minutes, or until vegetables are tender and soup has thickened slightly.
Adjust seasoning with salt and pepper as needed.
Ladle hot soup into individual bowls. Garnish each serving with a dollop of sour cream and fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Arroz con Pollo con Manzana y Tomate
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented in a wide, shallow white ceramic bowl, showcasing a generous individual portion. Golden-yellow rice, infused with saffron, forms the base. Two succulent, bone-in chicken thighs, their skin caramelized to a rich reddish-brown, are nestled within the rice. The rice is studded with soft, small diced red bell pepper, finely minced onion, and tender pieces of diced tomato and apple, contributing varied textures and subtle color. A vibrant sprinkle of fresh, finely chopped parsley garnishes the top, adding a pop of green. The composition is balanced and inviting, with moderate negative space. The setting is a modern bistro: a simple light wooden table, with the bowl centered on a clean white porcelain underplate. A neatly folded charcoal-grey cotton napkin and traditional Spanish-style flatware are placed beside the dish. A small rustic bread basket with two thick slices of crusty baguette rests nearby. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's warmth and authentic appeal.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with slices of crusty bread for dipping into the flavorful rice and sauce.
instructions: Season chicken thighs generously with salt and black pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large, wide pan or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs, skin-side down, for 5-7 minutes until golden brown and crispy. Flip and sear other side for 2-3 minutes. Remove chicken from pan and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add minced onion, small diced red bell pepper, and minced garlic to the pan. Sauté for 8-10 minutes until softened and translucent, creating a sofrito base.
Stir in smoked paprika and saffron threads. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add diced tomatoes and diced apple to the pan. Cook for 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until tomatoes break down slightly.
Add rice to the pan. Stir well to coat rice grains with the sofrito mixture. Cook for 2 minutes, toasting the rice slightly.
Pour in white wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan. Cook until wine is almost fully evaporated.
Return seared chicken thighs to the pan, nestling them into the rice mixture. Pour in hot chicken broth.
Bring liquid to a simmer. Reduce heat to low, cover the pan, and cook for 20-25 minutes. Do not stir frequently.
Check chicken internal temperature. It must reach 75°C (167°F). Continue cooking if needed.
Remove from heat. Let the Arroz con Pollo rest, covered, for 5 minutes.
Garnish generously with fresh chopped parsley before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Coq au Vin Blanc
recipes.visual_description: The dish features two whole, bone-in chicken thighs with crisp, golden-brown skin. They sit in a shallow, wide white porcelain bowl filled with a glossy, ivory-colored cream sauce. Thick-cut bacon lardons and browned, halved button mushrooms are distributed naturally around the chicken. Whole, softened shallots are visible in the sauce. Finely chopped flat-leaf parsley is sprinkled over the top for color. The plating is clean with moderate negative space. The setting includes a rustic wooden table, a linen napkin, and a side of crusty baguette slices. Lighting is natural and bright, emphasizing the textures of the seared skin and the velvety sauce consistency. The entire plate is visible.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a fresh, crusty baguette to soak up the sauce
Accompany with buttery mashed potatoes or buttered egg noodles
Pair with a chilled glass of the same dry white wine used in cooking
instructions: Season chicken thighs with salt and pepper.
Heat oil in a heavy pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken skin-side down until deep golden brown.
Flip chicken and sear for 2 minutes.
Remove chicken from the pan and set aside.
Add bacon lardons to the same pan. Fry until crisp.
Add halved mushrooms. Sauté until browned.
Stir in shallots and garlic. Cook for 2 minutes.
Pour in white wine. Scrape the pan bottom to release browned bits.
Add chicken stock and thyme sprigs.
Place chicken back into the pan.
Simmer on low heat for 20 minutes.
Confirm chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Transfer chicken to a warm plate.
Whisk heavy cream and butter into the pan juices.
Simmer until the sauce thickens slightly.
Return chicken to the sauce. Garnish with parsley.
notes: Use a high-quality dry white wine for the best sauce flavor
Do not boil the sauce vigorously after adding cream to avoid curdling
Keep the skin above the liquid level during braising to maintain crispness

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Cacciatore
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of rustic chicken cacciatore served in a shallow, cream-colored ceramic bowl with minor surface imperfections. Two whole, bone-in chicken thighs are the centerpiece, their skin appearing dark golden and tender from braising. The chicken is partially submerged in a thick, chunky tomato sauce featuring visible pieces of softened translucent onions and whole black olives. A single fresh rosemary sprig is placed casually on top. The bowl sits on a weathered dark wood kitchen table. Beside the bowl is a thick piece of torn crusty bread. The scene is illuminated by warm, soft overhead kitchen lighting, creating a cozy, authentic Italian home-dining atmosphere. A simple linen napkin and a stainless steel fork are placed to the left of the bowl.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty sourdough bread to soak up the tomato sauce
Pair with a side of simple polenta or rustic mashed potatoes
Traditional family-style dining involves placing the skillet in the center of the table
instructions: Season chicken thighs with salt and pepper on all sides.
Heat olive oil in a large deep skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken skin-side down for 6 minutes until golden brown.
Flip chicken and sear for 4 minutes. Remove chicken from skillet.
Add diced onion to the skillet. Sauté for 5 minutes until soft.
Stir in minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add crushed tomatoes, oregano, and the rosemary sprig.
Place chicken back into the skillet, nestled into the sauce.
Simmer on low heat for 30 minutes until chicken reaches 75°C internally.
Stir in the olives 5 minutes before serving.
notes: Use bone-in thighs for maximum flavor and protein content
Ensure the sauce reduces until thick to concentrate the savory tomato profile
Always check the thickest part of the chicken for a safe internal temperature of 75°C

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Cherry Tomato Confit and Tagliatelle
recipes.visual_description: A single portion is centered on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. A nest of golden tagliatelle forms the base, coated in a vibrant, glossy sauce of slow-roasted cherry tomatoes. The tomatoes are soft, some slightly burst, retaining their rich red color with hints of green from fresh basil. A golden-brown pan-seared chicken breast, sliced into thick medallions, is positioned artfully on top of the pasta. The chicken has a crisp, caramelized exterior and tender, juicy interior. A light drizzle of the tomato confit oil adds a sheen. Fresh, vibrant green basil leaves are scattered over the dish, with a dusting of finely grated Pecorino Romano cheese. The plate rests on a simple, light-colored wooden table surface. A neatly folded white cotton napkin is placed to the left. Natural, even lighting highlights textures and colors. The background is softly blurred, hinting at a casual bistro atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty ciabatta bread for dipping in the sauce.
Offer a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and red wine vinegar.
Pair with a light-bodied Italian red wine or a crisp white like Pinot Grigio.
Always offer extra grated cheese at the table.

ingredients.name: Pecorino Romano or Parmesan cheese, grated

instructions: Preheat oven to 150°C. In a small baking dish, combine halved cherry tomatoes, sliced garlic, a few sprigs of fresh basil, red pepper flakes (if using), and 150ml olive oil. Season with salt and pepper. Bake for 45-60 minutes, until tomatoes are soft and slightly wrinkled.

Season chicken breasts generously with salt and pepper. Heat 30ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken breasts for 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown. Transfer skillet to preheated oven and bake for 10-15 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Let rest 5 minutes.

While chicken rests, add diced shallot to the skillet with any remaining chicken drippings. Sauté 2 minutes until softened. Deglaze with white wine, scraping up any browned bits. Add chicken broth. Bring to a simmer. Stir in baked tomato confit and its oil. Add butter. Simmer gently for 5 minutes.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a rolling boil. Add fresh tagliatelle. Cook according to package instructions, usually 2-4 minutes, until al dente. Reserve 120ml pasta water.

Drain pasta. Add pasta to the skillet with the tomato sauce. Toss to coat, adding reserved pasta water as needed to create a glossy sauce. Slice rested chicken breasts into thick medallions. Plate pasta, top with chicken. Garnish with fresh basil leaves and grated Pecorino Romano.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Chicken and Mushroom Pasta
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of creamy chicken and mushroom pasta rests in a round, off-white ceramic bowl on a well-used wooden dining table. The golden-brown, 2 cm seared chicken cubes are nestled amongst the al dente pasta strands, which are thoroughly coated in a rich, pale cream sauce. Sliced, earthy brown mushrooms are interspersed throughout, adding depth. A scattering of fresh, vibrant green chopped parsley provides a pop of color on top. The dish is presented casually, as if just served from the stove, with the pasta naturally piled. The lighting is warm and natural, suggesting a cozy family kitchen setting. A simple fork rests beside the bowl on a plain cloth napkin, emphasizing the homely, unpretentious comfort of the meal.
instructions: Boil a large pot of salted water. Add pasta. Cook according to package directions until al dente. Drain pasta. Reserve 120ml pasta water.
Pat chicken breast cut into 2 cm cubes dry. Season with salt and pepper.

Heat olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Add chicken cubes. Sear until golden brown and cooked through, about 5-7 minutes. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken from pan. Set aside.

Reduce heat to medium. Add butter to the same pan. Add diced onion. Sauté until softened, about 3-4 minutes. Add sliced mushrooms. Cook until mushrooms are browned and tender, about 5-7 minutes. Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a simmer. Stir in heavy cream and grated Parmesan cheese. Cook, stirring constantly, until sauce thickens slightly, about 3-5 minutes.
Add cooked chicken back to the pan with the sauce. Add drained pasta. Toss to coat everything evenly. If sauce is too thick, add reserved pasta water, a little at a time, until desired consistency.
Taste and adjust seasoning. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley and extra grated Parmesan.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Lemon Herb Chicken with Roasted Root Vegetables
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of pan-seared lemon herb chicken breast, golden-brown with a seared crust, is plated on a simple, round, cream-colored ceramic plate. It rests beside a generous, naturally piled serving of roasted root vegetables. The vegetables include 2cm cubed potatoes, 1.5cm round carrots, and large onion wedges, all tender and lightly caramelized from roasting, showing their natural earthy colors. A light pan sauce, infused with lemon and herbs, is spooned over the chicken and vegetables. Fresh chopped parsley is scattered sparingly over the dish. The plate sits on a well-used wooden dining table, with a casually placed cloth napkin and simple flatware, bathed in warm, cozy kitchen lighting, creating a comforting, inviting home meal scene.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Wash and peel potatoes and carrots. Cut potatoes into 2cm cubes. Cut carrots into 1.5cm thick rounds. Cut onion into large wedges.
In a large bowl, combine potatoes, carrots, and onion. Add 30ml olive oil, leaves from 1 rosemary sprig, leaves from 1 thyme sprig, salt, and pepper. Toss to coat.
Spread vegetables in a single layer on a baking tray. Roast for 30-35 minutes, or until tender and lightly browned, turning halfway.
While vegetables roast, pat chicken breasts dry with paper towels. Season both sides with salt and pepper.
Heat remaining 15ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat.
Add chicken breasts to the hot skillet. Sear for 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown.
Mince garlic. Slice half of the lemon into thin rounds. Juice the other half.
Reduce heat to medium. Add minced garlic, lemon slices, remaining rosemary sprig, remaining thyme sprig, and chicken broth to the skillet with the chicken. Bring to a simmer.
Cover skillet and cook for 10-12 minutes, or until chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F).
Remove chicken from skillet and let rest on a cutting board for 5 minutes. Remove herb sprigs and lemon slices from pan sauce. Stir in lemon juice.
Chop fresh parsley.
Plate individual chicken breasts with a generous portion of roasted vegetables. Spoon pan sauce over the chicken and vegetables. Garnish with chopped parsley. Serve immediately.
notes: This recipe focuses on ingredients and cooking methods that are naturally low in cholesterol, utilizing lean skinless chicken breast and olive oil.
Ensure chicken is cooked to an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Loaded Pork & Bacon Garlic Bread
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a simple, slightly worn ceramic plate, sitting on a well-used wooden dining table. Natural, warm kitchen light illuminates the scene. A rustic, halved baguette forms the base, its cut surface golden brown and glistening with melted garlic butter. Hearty, irregular chunks of seared pork tenderloin are piled generously over the bread, displaying a golden-brown crust and tender interior. Scattered over the pork are golden, crisp pieces of crumbled bacon, adding texture and rich color. Bright green slices of pickled jalapeño are casually arranged among the pork and bacon, providing a vibrant contrast. A sprinkle of fresh, chopped parsley adds a final touch of color. The overall presentation is inviting, comforting, and unpretentious, reflecting a homemade meal.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C.
Prepare garlic butter: Mash garlic cloves into a paste. Mix with softened butter.
Slice baguette lengthwise. Spread garlic butter generously on both halves.
Bake garlic bread for 8-10 minutes, until golden and fragrant. Remove and set aside.
Cook bacon: Dice bacon into small pieces. Cook in a pan over medium heat until crispy. Remove bacon with a slotted spoon. Reserve rendered fat.
Cook pork: Cut pork tenderloin into 2 cm chunks. Season with salt and pepper.
Add olive oil and a small amount of reserved bacon fat to the pan. Increase heat to medium-high.
Sear pork chunks for 3-4 minutes per side until browned and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C).
Assemble: Place garlic bread halves on a serving plate. Top evenly with seared pork chunks.
Scatter crispy bacon pieces over the pork.
Arrange pickled jalapeño slices on top.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley. Serve immediately.
notes: This starter is designed to be substantial and satisfying, perfect for a casual meal.

recipes.recipe_name: Seared Pork Belly Salad with Crispy Bacon and Jalapeño Brioche Croutons
recipes.visual_description: The dish presents as a vibrant, composed salad, showcasing seared pork belly chunks as the centerpiece. Four substantial, golden-brown pork belly pieces, each with a visibly crispy skin and tender interior, are arranged artfully on a bed of fresh, mixed green lettuce (butter, arugula, frisée). Bright red cherry tomato halves and thin slices of red onion are interspersed throughout the greens, adding color and texture. Scattered generously over the salad are golden, toasted brioche croutons, cut into irregular 2 cm cubes, and crumbled pieces of crisp, dark brown bacon. The entire composition is lightly dressed with a glossy, pale green vinaigrette, hinting at the jalapeño. A few whole, bright green pickled jalapeño slices are placed thoughtfully, along with a sprinkle of vibrant green chopped fresh parsley. The presentation is clean and inviting, with moderate negative space on a white porcelain dinner plate, set on a simple wooden surface. A cotton napkin and standard flatware complete the modern bistro setting under natural, even lighting.
instructions: Score pork belly skin in a crosshatch pattern. Rub generously with salt and pepper.
Place pork belly skin-side up in a cold pan. Render fat over medium-low heat for 30 minutes until skin crisps.
Flip pork belly. Sear all sides for 10 minutes.
Transfer pork belly to a baking dish. Add 100ml water to the dish. Cover tightly with foil.
Bake at 160°C for 2 hours until tender.
Remove foil. Increase oven temperature to 200°C. Bake for 20-30 minutes until skin is very crispy.
Remove pork belly from oven. Rest 10 minutes. Cut into 2-3 cm thick chunks.
Cook bacon in a separate pan over medium heat until crispy. Drain on paper towels. Crumble when cool.
Cut brioche slices into 2 cm cubes. Toss with 15ml olive oil. Toast in a pan or oven until golden brown and crispy.

In a small bowl, whisk remaining 45ml olive oil, apple cider vinegar, Dijon mustard, honey, 30ml pickled jalapeño brine, and half of the sliced pickled jalapeños (finely chopped). Season with salt and pepper.
In a large bowl, combine mixed greens, cherry tomatoes, and red onion. Drizzle with vinaigrette. Toss gently to coat.
Divide salad among 4 plates. Arrange seared pork belly chunks on top.
Sprinkle with crispy bacon and brioche croutons. Garnish with remaining whole pickled jalapeño slices and fresh chopped parsley.
notes: For extra flavor, reserve some rendered pork belly fat to toss with the brioche croutons instead of olive oil.
The pork belly can be cooked ahead of time and reheated gently for serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Baked Chicken and Potato with Mozzarella
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Baked Chicken and Potato with Mozzarella is presented on a simple ceramic plate, on a well-used wooden dining table. The golden-brown chicken thigh is topped with melted, bubbly mozzarella. Thick-cut roasted potato wedges, roughly chopped caramelized onions, and tender roasted tomato pieces are arranged naturally alongside. Natural colors of golden chicken, creamy mozzarella, and varied browns/reds from the vegetables dominate. A light sprinkle of fresh green parsley adds freshness. The plating is natural, components touching, reflecting a comforting, home-style meal. Warm kitchen lighting illuminates the scene, creating a relaxed family dining atmosphere. A casually placed cloth napkin and standard flatware complete the homely setting.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (400°F).
In a large baking dish, combine potato wedges, chopped onion, chopped tomatoes, and minced garlic.
Drizzle with olive oil. Season generously with salt and black pepper. Toss to coat all vegetables.
Arrange chicken thighs among the vegetables in the baking dish.
Spread mayonnaise evenly over each chicken thigh.
Bake for 30 minutes.
Remove dish from oven. Sprinkle shredded mozzarella over the chicken and vegetables.
Return to oven. Bake for another 15-20 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) and cheese is melted and bubbly.
Remove from oven. Let rest for 5 minutes.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Savory Bread & Oat Bake
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous square portion of the savory bread and oat bake is centered on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. The top crust is golden-brown and slightly crisp, showcasing baked cheese and toasted bread edges. The interior, visible where the portion is cut, reveals a moist, custardy texture with distinct 2.5 cm bread cubes, soft oats, and pockets of melted Gruyere cheese. Flecks of vibrant green chopped thyme and rosemary are visible throughout. The overall color palette is warm golden-browns and creamy off-whites, with hints of green. A small, fresh sprig of thyme is placed delicately on the top crust as a garnish. The plate rests on a simple wooden table surface. A neatly folded cotton napkin is placed beside the plate. Lighting is natural and even, casting soft shadows. The background is minimally blurred, suggesting a casual bistro setting without distracting from the dish.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C (350°F). Grease a 20x30 cm baking dish with butter.
Heat olive oil in a large pan over medium heat. Add diced onion. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
In a large bowl, whisk eggs, milk, salt, and black pepper until well combined.
Add bread cubes, rolled oats, grated Gruyere, chopped thyme, and chopped rosemary to the egg mixture. Add sautéed onion and garlic. Stir gently to combine.
Pour the mixture into the prepared baking dish. Press down lightly to ensure bread is submerged.
Let the mixture sit for 15-20 minutes to allow the bread to soak up the liquid.
Bake for 40-50 minutes, or until the top is golden brown and the center is set. A knife inserted into the center should come out clean.
Remove from oven. Let it rest for 10 minutes before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Crispy Herb-Crusted Chicken with Roasted Garlic Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single, refined portion of Crispy Herb-Crusted Chicken is centrally placed on a clean, white porcelain dinner plate. The chicken breast, a whole piece, is pan-fried to a deep golden-brown, showcasing a crunchy, textured herb crust. Beside it, a neat pile of roasted Yukon Gold potato wedges, cut into thick chunks, displays a golden-brown exterior. A glistening, pale yellow lemon butter sauce is drizzled over the chicken and potatoes. Fresh, vibrant green parsley is subtly sprinkled, with a small sprig and a bright yellow lemon wedge positioned beside the chicken. The presentation is clean, professional, with moderate negative space. The plate rests on a simple, light-colored wooden table with a folded cotton napkin to the left. Soft, natural, even lighting illuminates the scene, suggesting a casual bistro setting.

ingredients.name: Fresh thyme, leaves picked and chopped

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Wash and cut potatoes into 2.5 cm wedges. In a large bowl, toss potatoes with 30ml olive oil, 4 minced garlic cloves, salt, and pepper. Spread in a single layer on a baking sheet. Roast for 30-35 minutes, or until tender and golden brown, flipping halfway.
While potatoes roast, prepare chicken. Place each chicken breast between two sheets of plastic wrap. Pound to an even 1.5 cm thickness using a meat mallet or rolling pin.
Prepare breading station. In one shallow dish, place flour. In a second dish, whisk eggs. In a third dish, combine rustic breadcrumbs, chopped parsley, chopped thyme, salt, and pepper.
Dredge each chicken breast in flour, shaking off excess. Dip into whisked egg, allowing excess to drip off. Press firmly into breadcrumb mixture, ensuring chicken is fully coated on both sides.

Heat remaining 30ml olive oil and 20g butter in a large non-stick skillet over medium-high heat. Once butter is melted and foaming, add chicken breasts. Do not overcrowd the pan; cook in batches if necessary.
Pan-fry chicken for 4-5 minutes per side, until golden brown and internal temperature reaches 75°C. Transfer cooked chicken to a wire rack set over a baking sheet to rest. Keep warm.

To make lemon butter sauce, reduce heat to medium-low. Add remaining 40g butter and 2 minced garlic cloves to the same skillet. Sauté garlic for 30 seconds until fragrant. Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a simmer, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan.
Squeeze juice from half of the lemon into the sauce. Simmer for 2-3 minutes until slightly reduced. Season with salt and pepper to taste.

To serve, place one crispy chicken breast on each plate. Arrange a generous portion of roasted garlic potatoes beside the chicken. Drizzle lemon butter sauce over the chicken and potatoes. Garnish with a fresh parsley sprig and a lemon wedge.

recipes.recipe_name: Tuscan Roast Chicken with Rosemary Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: Roasted chicken leg quarters, golden-brown and glistening, are arranged naturally on a clean white porcelain plate. Alongside, rustic wedges of rosemary-roasted potatoes, their edges slightly crisped and interiors tender. A scattering of fresh rosemary sprigs and bright lemon wedges provides vibrant green and yellow accents. The chicken skin exhibits a rich, savory crust, contrasting with the tender, juicy meat. Potatoes are cut into irregular, substantial wedges, showcasing their soft, starchy texture. A thick slice of airy focaccia bread, lightly toasted with olive oil and a sprinkle of sea salt, rests beside the main components. The overall presentation is inviting, natural, and abundant, set on a simple wooden surface with soft, even lighting, creating a warm, authentic Italian meal tableau.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and red wine vinegar.
Offer a glass of robust red wine, suchs as Chianti or Sangiovese.
Serve family-style on a large platter for a communal dining experience, then portion onto individual plates.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (392°F).
Pat chicken leg quarters dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Cut potatoes into substantial wedges. Place in a large bowl.
Add 3 sprigs of rosemary, smashed garlic cloves, 40 ml olive oil, 5 g salt, and 2 g pepper to potatoes. Toss to coat.
Arrange chicken and potatoes in a large roasting pan. Ensure chicken skin faces up.
Place lemon slices around chicken and potatoes.
Pour chicken broth into the bottom of the roasting pan.

Roast for 30 minutes. Flip potatoes. Continue roasting for another 25-35 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) and skin is golden and crispy. Potatoes should be tender.
Remove from oven. Let chicken rest in the pan for 5 minutes.
Toast focaccia slices lightly, if desired.
Serve chicken and potatoes on individual plates. Garnish with fresh rosemary sprigs and lemon wedges. Serve with toasted focaccia.
notes: Ensure chicken is fully dry before seasoning for crispy skin.
Adjust roasting time based on chicken size and oven calibration.

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Pork Belly Bites with Rosemary Glaze
recipes.visual_description: Golden-brown, tender braised pork belly cubes are casually arranged on a rustic, natural wooden board. Each 2-3 cm pork cube glistens with a rich, dark amber rosemary-infused glaze. The edges of the pork show a subtle crispness from the initial sear, contrasting with the tender interior. A few small, vibrant green sprigs of fresh rosemary are scattered amongst the bites, providing a simple, functional garnish. The plating is natural and unforced, with pieces touching and overlapping slightly, filling the board adequately without overcrowding. The scene is set on a well-used wooden kitchen table, bathed in warm, soft lighting, evoking a homely, comforting atmosphere. A casually placed simple cloth napkin is visible in the background.
instructions: Preheat oven to 160°C.
Score the skin of the pork belly in a crosshatch pattern.
Season pork belly generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a heavy, oven-safe pot over medium-high heat.
Sear pork belly skin-side down until golden brown and crispy, about 8-10 minutes. Flip and sear other sides briefly.
Remove pork belly from pot. Drain excess fat, leaving about 15 ml.
Add chopped onion and crushed garlic to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Return pork belly to the pot, skin-side up.
Pour in pork stock. Add thyme, rosemary, and bay leaves.
Bring liquid to a gentle simmer. Cover the pot tightly.
Transfer pot to the preheated oven. Braise for 2.5 to 3 hours, or until pork belly is fork-tender.
Carefully remove pork belly from the pot. Place on a cutting board. Let rest for 15 minutes.
Strain braising liquid into a saucepan. Discard solids and herbs.
Bring liquid to a boil over medium-high heat. Reduce to a thick, glossy glaze, about 10-15 minutes.
While glaze reduces, cut pork belly into 2-3 cm cubes.
Toss pork belly cubes gently with a few spoonfuls of the reduced glaze.
Arrange pork belly bites on a serving platter. Drizzle with remaining glaze. Garnish with small fresh thyme or rosemary sprigs.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Ricotta Mousse with Lingonberry Compote
recipes.visual_description: A minimalist presentation showcases natural textures and colors. A single portion of light, creamy off-white fermented ricotta mousse is served in a handcrafted, unglazed ceramic bowl with a wide, shallow base and natural, earthy tones. The mousse forms a soft, organic mound at the center. A vibrant pool of deep ruby-red lingonberry compote is spooned artistically alongside the mousse, creating a striking color contrast without fully covering the mousse. Scattered around the compote and on a small section of the mousse are clusters of golden-brown treacle-macadamia crumble, offering a rustic, textured element. The crumble pieces are irregular, showcasing the chopped macadamia nuts. The overall composition emphasizes negative space. The bowl sits on a light, textured bamboo or reclaimed wood surface. A natural, undyed linen napkin in beige is folded simply beside the bowl. Soft, diffused natural light illuminates the dish from the side, enhancing its organic beauty. The background is clean and uncluttered, with a hint of natural greenery out of focus, reinforcing the eco-conscious theme.
instructions: Place ricotta in a clean bowl. Cover loosely with a cloth. Let sit at room temperature for 4-8 hours until a mild tang develops. Refrigerate immediately after desired tang.

Combine lingonberries, 30g natural sweetener, and water in a small saucepan. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 5-7 minutes, stirring, until berries burst and sauce thickens slightly. Remove from heat. Stir in lemon zest. Cool completely.
Preheat oven to 160°C. In a bowl, combine chopped macadamia nuts, oat flour, black treacle, and a pinch of salt. Mix until crumbly.
Spread mixture on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper. Bake for 10-12 minutes, or until golden brown and fragrant. Let cool completely. Break into small clusters.
In a heatproof bowl set over a saucepan of simmering water, whisk egg yolks and 50g natural sweetener until pale, thick, and doubled in volume. Remove from heat.
Gently fold the fermented ricotta into the sabayon until just combined. Do not overmix. The mixture should be light and airy.
Divide mousse into 4 individual serving bowls or glasses. Chill for at least 2 hours to set.
Spoon cooled lingonberry compote over each mousse. Sprinkle with treacle-macadamia crumble. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Tinga de Pollo con Frijoles Charros
recipes.visual_description: The dish presents a rustic yet refined Mexican main course. Shredded, saucy Tinga de Pollo, rich reddish-brown from chipotles, is piled neatly in a deep white ceramic bowl, garnished with a generous sprinkle of crumbled white queso fresco and a few fresh cilantro sprigs. Beside it, in a slightly wider, shallow bowl, are the Frijoles Charros: creamy pinto beans studded with diced bacon, chorizo, and jalapeño, topped with finely chopped fresh cilantro. The colors are earthy and vibrant – deep red-browns, rich browns, and bright green. Textures include the tender shredded chicken, the soft, flavorful beans, and the fresh, crisp herbs and cheese. The scene is set on a simple wooden table, with warm corn tortillas stacked in a traditional woven tortilla warmer and a small bowl of lime wedges on the side, under natural, even lighting. A single portion is presented, showcasing the dish's hearty, authentic appeal.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas for scooping
Offer lime wedges for acidity
Serve with sliced radishes as a refreshing counterpoint
Accompany with Mexican crema or sour cream
instructions: Rinse pinto beans. Soak beans in water overnight. Drain. Alternatively, quick soak beans.

Place soaked beans in a large pot. Cover with 1.5 liters water. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat. Simmer until tender, about 1.5-2 hours. Season with salt halfway through cooking. Drain beans, reserve some liquid.

Place chicken thighs in a pot. Cover with 500 ml chicken broth. Bring to a simmer. Cook chicken until tender and internal temperature reaches 75°C, about 20-25 minutes. Remove chicken, shred using two forks. Reserve broth.
For Tinga: Slice half of the white onion into thin strips. Heat 15 ml oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add sliced onion. Sauté until softened and translucent, about 8 minutes.
Add shredded chicken to the skillet with onions. Stir to combine.

Blend tomatoes, 2 garlic cloves, chipotle peppers, and 125 ml reserved chicken broth until smooth. Pour sauce over chicken and onion in the skillet. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 15-20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until sauce thickens. Season with salt and pepper. Keep warm.
For Frijoles Charros: Dice bacon into small pieces. Dice Mexican chorizo. Dice remaining half of the white onion. Mince remaining 2 garlic cloves. Finely dice jalapeño.
In a separate pot or deep skillet, cook diced bacon over medium heat until crisp. Remove bacon with a slotted spoon; set aside. Leave rendered fat in the pot.
Add diced chorizo to the pot. Cook until browned and cooked through. Remove chorizo; set aside. Leave rendered fat.
Add diced onion and minced garlic to the pot with rendered fat. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes. Add diced jalapeño. Sauté for 2 minutes.

Add cooked pinto beans to the pot. Add 250 ml chicken broth (or reserved bean liquid), ground cumin, and dried oregano. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 15-20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until flavors meld and sauce slightly thickens.
Stir in cooked bacon and chorizo into the Frijoles Charros. Season with salt and pepper to taste. Keep warm.

Warm corn tortillas. Serve Tinga de Pollo and Frijoles Charros side-by-side. Garnish Tinga with crumbled queso fresco and fresh cilantro sprigs. Garnish Frijoles Charros with chopped fresh cilantro, sliced radishes, and lime wedges. Serve with warm tortillas and optional Mexican crema.
notes: For authentic flavor, use dried pinto beans and cook them from scratch. Canned beans can be used for convenience.
Adjust the amount of chipotle peppers to your preferred spice level.
The quality of chorizo significantly impacts the flavor of the Frijoles Charros.
traditional_techniques: Slow simmering (for beans and tinga sauce)

recipes.recipe_name: Sheet Pan Roasted Salmon and Root Vegetables
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Sheet Pan Roasted Salmon and Root Vegetables is presented on an everyday, natural ceramic plate. A golden-brown roasted salmon fillet rests centrally. Alongside it, a natural mound of roasted vegetables: tender 2cm diced potatoes with browned edges, vibrant 1cm sliced carrots, caramelized quartered red onions, and burst halved cherry tomatoes. The components are casually arranged, touching and overlapping, reflecting a homely, unpretentious style. A sprinkle of fresh chopped parsley adds a vibrant green contrast. The plate sits on a well-used wooden dining table with everyday stainless steel flatware. Warm, inviting kitchen lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its natural colors and comforting textures. The background is minimally blurred, suggesting a cozy, lived-in family kitchen with a simple cloth napkin, reinforcing the relaxed, home-cooked atmosphere. No elements are fanned; all pieces are presented naturally.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Wash and peel potatoes and carrots. Cut potatoes into 2cm cubes. Slice carrots into 1cm thick rounds. Quarter the red onion.
Halve the cherry tomatoes.
On a large sheet pan, combine cubed potatoes, sliced carrots, and quartered onion. Drizzle with 45ml olive oil, season with salt and pepper. Toss to coat evenly.
Spread vegetables in a single layer on the sheet pan. Roast for 20 minutes.
Remove sheet pan from oven. Push vegetables to one side. Place salmon fillets on the empty side of the pan. Drizzle salmon with remaining 15ml olive oil. Season salmon with salt and pepper.
Add halved cherry tomatoes to the pan with the other vegetables.
Return pan to oven. Roast for another 12-15 minutes, or until salmon reaches an internal temperature of 63°C and flakes easily, and vegetables are tender and lightly caramelized.
Chop fresh parsley.
Serve salmon and roasted vegetables immediately. Garnish with fresh parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Chicken Macaroni Bake
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Creamy Chicken Macaroni Bake is presented in a shallow, round white porcelain bowl. The dish features a golden-brown, bubbly cheese crust on top, indicating a perfectly baked finish. Below the crust, creamy, tender elbow macaroni is visible, intertwined with generous, rustic chunks of cooked chicken. Small, soft cubes of vibrant orange carrot and translucent diced onion are integrated throughout the rich, pale yellow sauce. A sprinkle of fresh, bright green chopped parsley garnishes the top, adding a pop of color and freshness. The overall presentation is comforting and hearty. The bowl rests on a simple light wooden table surface. A neatly folded white cotton napkin is placed to the side. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and inviting warmth. The background is softly blurred, maintaining focus on the food in a modern bistro setting.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C (375°F).
Cook macaroni according to package directions. Drain well. Set aside.
Dice chicken breast into 2-3 cm cubes. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat butter in a large oven-safe skillet or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Add chicken cubes. Cook until browned on all sides and cooked through. Internal temperature must reach 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken. Set aside.
Dice onion and carrot into small cubes. Mince garlic.
Add onion and carrot to the same skillet. Sauté 5-7 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute more.
Whisk mayonnaise, milk, and chicken broth in a bowl.
Stir half of the shredded cheddar cheese into the liquid mixture.
Return cooked chicken to the skillet with vegetables. Add cooked macaroni. Pour in the mayonnaise mixture. Stir well to combine.
Transfer mixture to a 20x30 cm baking dish if not using an oven-safe skillet.
Sprinkle remaining shredded cheddar cheese evenly over the top.
Bake 20-25 minutes, or until bubbly and cheese is golden brown.
Remove from oven. Let stand 5 minutes. Chop fresh parsley.
Garnish with chopped parsley before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Hungarian Paprika Chicken with Bell Peppers
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean, white porcelain dinner plate, showcasing a refined yet approachable restaurant style. Two thick, golden-brown seared chicken breast chunks are prominently placed towards the center. Surrounding the chicken is a rich, glossy, reddish-brown paprika sauce, studded with tender, vibrant red and green bell pepper strips and translucent, soft onion slices. The sauce has a moderate viscosity, clinging well to the chicken and vegetables. A small dollop of bright white sour cream is artfully placed on one chicken chunk, and a sprinkle of fresh, finely chopped green parsley adds a pop of color and freshness. The elements are well-proportioned with moderate negative space, avoiding overcrowding. The chicken chunks are whole, not sliced. The scene features a simple wooden table surface, a neatly folded white cotton napkin beside the plate, and standard flatware. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's inviting colors and textures.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with Nokedli (Hungarian dumplings).
Serve with egg noodles or boiled potatoes.
Offer a side of pickled cucumbers or cabbage.
instructions: Pat chicken chunks dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat vegetable oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken chunks until golden brown on all sides. Do not cook through. Remove chicken from pot.
Add sliced onions to the pot. Sauté until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes.
Stir in sweet Hungarian paprika. Cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly. Do not burn paprika.
Pour in chicken broth. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Bring to a simmer.
Return seared chicken chunks to the pot. Add bell pepper strips.
Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 25-30 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C and is tender.
In a small bowl, whisk together sour cream and flour until smooth.
Remove chicken from pot. Whisk sour cream mixture into the simmering sauce. Stir until sauce thickens slightly.
Return chicken to the pot. Simmer for 2-3 minutes more to heat chicken through.
Adjust seasoning with salt and pepper as needed.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley before serving.
notes: Ensure paprika does not burn when added to the hot oil, as it can turn bitter. Cook it briefly.
Adjust the thickness of the sauce by adding more flour slurry for a thicker sauce or a splash of broth for a thinner consistency.

recipes.recipe_name: Poulet aux Oignons Caramelisés
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Poulet aux Oignons Caramelisés is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. A golden-brown, seared bone-in chicken thigh is positioned slightly off-center. Abundant, glossy, deeply amber-brown caramelized onions are artfully arranged around the chicken, forming a savory bed. A rich, dark brown, slightly viscous sauce pools subtly around the base. A vibrant green fresh thyme sprig garnishes the chicken.
