Drizzle with a little extra virgin olive oil. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley or basil.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Mushroom Velouté
recipes.visual_description: A golden-brown pan-seared chicken breast, cooked whole, rests centrally on a round white porcelain plate. The skin is crisp and perfectly rendered. A rich, velvety mushroom cream sauce, studded with thinly sliced cremini mushrooms and vibrant green flecks of fresh thyme, is elegantly spooned over and around the chicken. Adjacent to the chicken, a neat cluster of roasted small potato wedges, their skins slightly crisped and interiors tender, are arranged alongside vibrant blanched haricots verts. The dish presents a harmonious balance of golden-brown, earthy mushroom tones, creamy white, and bright green hues. Moderate negative space surrounds the components. The plate rests on a simple light wooden table, accompanied by a neatly folded white cotton napkin and classic silver flatware. Natural, even lighting illuminates the textures and colors.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a crusty baguette for dipping into the rich sauce
Pair with a dry white wine, such as a Sancerre or Chardonnay

ingredients.name: Small potatoes (e.g., new potatoes, fingerlings), halved or quartered

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Toss potato wedges with a drizzle of olive oil, salt, and pepper. Roast for 25-30 minutes until tender and golden. Set aside.
Blanch haricots verts in boiling salted water for 2-3 minutes. Drain and immediately plunge into ice water to stop cooking. Drain well. Set aside.
Pat chicken breasts dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat 15ml olive oil and 10g butter in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat.

Sear chicken breasts skin-side down for 6-8 minutes until golden and crisp. Flip and sear for another 2-3 minutes. Transfer skillet to preheated oven. Bake for 10-15 minutes until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken from skillet. Rest on a cutting board, tented with foil.
Return skillet to medium heat. Add remaining 20g butter. Add sliced mushrooms and diced shallots. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened and browned.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Deglaze skillet with white wine. Scrape up any browned bits. Reduce wine by half.
Pour in chicken stock. Bring to a simmer. Reduce by half.
Stir in heavy cream and chopped fresh thyme. Simmer gently for 3-5 minutes until sauce slightly thickens. Season sauce with salt and pepper to taste.
Arrange roasted potatoes and blanched haricots verts on individual plates.
Place a whole pan-seared chicken breast beside the vegetables.
Spoon the mushroom cream sauce generously over and around the chicken. Garnish with fresh thyme sprigs.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
Resting the chicken after cooking is crucial for juicy results.

recipes.recipe_name: Belgian Beef Carbonnade
recipes.visual_description: The Belgian Beef Carbonnade is presented in a deep, pristine white porcelain bowl, showcasing a generous single portion. Large, tender chunks of braised beef, approximately 4-5 cm, are nestled amongst soft, caramelized onion slices, all coated in a glossy, dark brown, rich beer-based sauce. The sauce is thick and unctuous, clinging beautifully to the ingredients. A scattering of vibrant fresh chopped parsley adds a contrasting pop of green. The beef exhibits a fall-apart texture. The dish is placed on a simple wooden table. Alongside, a small white ramekin holds traditional cornichons and another a dollop of extra Dijon mustard. Natural, even lighting highlights the stew's deep, inviting colors and textures. A folded cotton napkin sits nearby, completing the casual bistro setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Traditionally served with crispy Belgian frites (fries)
Accompanied by a side of cornichons (small pickled gherkins)
Often served with a dollop of strong Dijon mustard
instructions: Preheat oven to 160°C.
Heat vegetable oil and butter in a large oven-safe pot over medium-high heat.
Add bacon lardons. Cook until crispy. Remove bacon with a slotted spoon. Set aside.
Season beef chunks generously with salt and pepper. Dredge beef lightly in flour.
Sear beef in batches until browned on all sides. Do not overcrowd the pot. Remove seared beef. Set aside.
Add sliced onions to the pot. Sauté until softened and translucent, about 8-10 minutes.
Deglaze the pot with dark beer, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom.
Return seared beef and cooked bacon to the pot.
Stir in beef stock, Dijon mustard, brown sugar, thyme sprigs, and bay leaves.
Bring the mixture to a simmer. Cover the pot tightly.
Transfer the pot to the preheated oven. Braise for 2.5 to 3 hours, or until beef is fork-tender.
Remove thyme sprigs and bay leaves before serving.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper as needed.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Brined Chicken with Roasted Root Vegetables
recipes.visual_description: A single roasted chicken leg quarter, its skin crisp and golden-brown, rests as the centerpiece on a handcrafted, cream-colored ceramic plate. Surrounding the chicken, in an organic, unforced arrangement, are roasted root vegetable chunks (2-3 cm), their natural colors of earthy orange, creamy white, and soft purple (if using heirloom varieties) visible, with slightly caramelized edges. A vibrant green herb oil is artfully drizzled over the chicken and vegetables, adding a fresh contrast. A subtle, glossy pan sauce pools around the elements, reflecting the soft, natural light. The plating emphasizes negative space, allowing each ingredient to stand out. The dish sits on a light, textured reclaimed wood surface. An undyed linen napkin in a natural beige tone and a minimalist background with subtle greenery complete the eco-conscious setting. The scene is clean, uncluttered, and highlights the pure beauty of the sustainable ingredients.

ingredients.name: Mixed root vegetables (carrots, parsnips, potatoes), scrubbed, skin on
Fresh parsley, leaves picked, stems reserved
Chicken stock (homemade from bones, if possible)

instructions: Place chicken leg quarters in a large bowl. Pour lacto-fermented vegetable brine over chicken. Ensure chicken is fully submerged. Cover and refrigerate for 12-24 hours.
Preheat oven to 200°C. Remove chicken from brine; pat very dry with paper towels. Discard brine.
Cut scrubbed root vegetables into 2-3 cm chunks. Toss vegetables with 30ml olive oil, rosemary, thyme, salt, and pepper.

Arrange chicken and vegetables in a single layer on a large roasting tray. Roast for 40-50 minutes, or until chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C and skin is golden and crisp. Vegetables should be tender.
While chicken roasts, combine parsley leaves and neutral oil in a small blender. Blend until smooth. Strain through a fine-mesh sieve, pressing solids to extract all oil. Reserve strained oil.

Remove chicken and vegetables from roasting tray. Place tray on stovetop over medium heat. Pour in chicken stock. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the tray. Simmer for 2-3 minutes, reducing slightly to create a light pan sauce.
Place one roasted chicken leg quarter on each plate. Arrange roasted root vegetables alongside. Drizzle with herb oil and pan sauce. Serve immediately.
notes: To make a simple lacto-fermented vegetable brine: Combine 1 liter filtered water, 1 tablespoon non-iodized salt, and 1 tablespoon sauerkraut juice or whey (as a starter) in a clean jar. Add clean vegetable scraps (e.g., carrot peels, onion ends, celery trimmings). Seal loosely and ferment at room temperature for 3-5 days, or until desired tanginess is achieved. Strain before use.
Maximize zero-waste: Use chicken bones for homemade stock. Reserve vegetable trimmings and herb stems for future broths or infusions.

recipes.recipe_name: Homestyle Mixed Fruit Salad
recipes.visual_description: A generous, vibrant Homestyle Mixed Fruit Salad fills a simple, deep white ceramic bowl on a well-used wooden kitchen table. Fruits are cut into natural, rustic shapes: plump strawberry halves, whole blueberries, halved green grapes, and casual cubes of cantaloupe and honeydew melon. Quartered kiwi rounds add bright green. The fruits are naturally piled, overlapping in an inviting, unpretentious mound, showcasing their fresh, bright colors of red, blue, green, and orange. A light sheen from the honey-lime dressing coats the fruit, highlighting textures. Roughly chopped fresh mint leaves are scattered on top. The bowl is slightly off-center. A crumpled white paper towel rests next to a simple metal spoon. Warm, soft light illuminates the cozy, lived-in scene, creating an impression of wholesome comfort food.
instructions: Wash all fruits thoroughly.
Hull strawberries. Cut into quarters or halves, depending on size.
Remove grapes from stems. Halve large grapes.
Cut cantaloupe and honeydew melons in half. Scoop out seeds. Remove rind. Cut melon flesh into 2 cm cubes.
Peel kiwi. Cut into 1 cm thick rounds, then quarter the rounds.
In a large mixing bowl, combine all prepared fruits.
Zest half the lime directly over the fruit. Squeeze juice from the entire lime into the bowl.
Add honey to the fruit.
Gently toss all ingredients until evenly coated.
Chill for at least 30 minutes before serving.
Roughly chop fresh mint leaves. Sprinkle over salad just before serving.
notes: The primary ingredient "black bean" specified in the prompt could not be incorporated into a sweet fruit salad while maintaining the "comfort food" and "homely" characteristics. This recipe focuses on delivering a classic, comforting fruit salad as per the "dish type" and "flavor profile" requirements.
For best flavor, use ripe, seasonal fruits.
Adjust honey amount to desired sweetness.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Chicken with Fermented Carrot & Garlic Noodles
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of roasted chicken with vegetables is presented on a handcrafted, matte cream ceramic plate. The plate's organic shape and natural texture evoke a sustainable aesthetic. A golden-brown, skin-on chicken thigh, cooked whole, is the focal point, positioned slightly off-center. Beside it, tender roasted potato wedges and thick-cut roasted carrot chunks display caramelized edges. Bright orange, lacto-fermented carrot batons are strategically placed, adding a pop of vibrant color and a contrasting texture. A bed of light, springy egg noodles, subtly coated with roasted garlic and olive oil, forms the base, peeking out from beneath the main components. Scattered unpeeled roasted garlic cloves add rustic charm. A delicate sprinkle of fresh green chives or parsley provides a final touch of natural freshness. The composition is clean, with ample negative space. The setting features a light, reclaimed wood surface, an undyed linen napkin in natural beige, and soft, diffused natural lighting from the side, creating a warm, inviting, and eco-conscious ambiance. No fanned meat slices. Portions are refined and restaurant-sized.
instructions: Prepare fermented carrots: Wash and peel 300g carrots. Cut into 5cm long batons. In a clean jar, dissolve 10g non-iodized salt in 500ml filtered water to make a brine. Pack carrot batons tightly into the jar. Pour brine over carrots, ensuring they are fully submerged. Use a fermentation weight or small clean bag filled with water to keep carrots submerged. Seal loosely. Ferment at room temperature for 3-5 days, or until desired tanginess is achieved. Burp daily. Store in refrigerator once fermented.
Preheat oven to 200°C. Line a baking tray with parchment paper.
Wash and quarter remaining 200g carrots and all potatoes. Toss with 15ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Arrange on one side of the baking tray.
Separate garlic head into individual cloves. Do not peel. Toss with 5ml olive oil. Add to the baking tray with vegetables.
Pat chicken thighs dry. Rub with 10ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Place skin-side up on the other side of the baking tray.

Roast for 25-30 minutes, or until chicken skin is golden and crispy, and internal temperature reaches 75°C. Vegetables should be tender and lightly browned. Remove from oven. Let chicken rest 5 minutes.
While chicken roasts, cook noodles according to package directions. Drain well.
In a large bowl, toss cooked noodles with roasted garlic cloves (squeezing garlic from skins) and a drizzle of olive oil. Season with salt and pepper.

Plate: Arrange a bed of garlic noodles on each plate. Top with roasted chicken thigh, roasted carrots, and roasted potatoes. Add a portion of fermented carrot batons. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley or chives.
Serve immediately.
notes: This recipe emphasizes zero-waste by utilizing chicken skin for crispiness and promoting fermentation for food preservation and enhanced flavor. Leaving potato and garlic skins on for roasting minimizes prep waste.

For the fermented carrots, ensure all equipment is sterilized to prevent unwanted mold. A true fermentation can take longer, but 3-5 days provides a good tangy start. The brine can be reused for a second batch of vegetables.
Chicken bones and vegetable scraps from prep can be used to make a flavorful stock for future use.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken Supreme with Potato Mille-Feuille and Glazed Carrot Baton
recipes.visual_description: A single, elegant pan-seared chicken supreme with its crispy, golden-brown skin, bone intact, is positioned thoughtfully on an expansive white bone china plate. Adjacent to it, a precisely cut, golden-edged potato mille-feuille reveals its delicate, stacked layers. Three to four vibrant orange glazed carrot batons are artfully arranged, adding a pop of color and architectural precision. A rich, glossy chicken jus is sparingly drizzled, creating a subtle pool or trail that connects the elements without overwhelming the ample negative space. A single, fresh sprig of micro arugula or chervil rests delicately on the chicken or near the potato, providing a final touch of verdant contrast. The presentation is ultra-minimalist, showcasing impeccable technique and premium ingredients. The plate sits on a polished dark wood table, illuminated by dramatic, focused lighting that creates soft shadows, emphasizing the dish's sculptural quality. A crisp, white linen napkin, folded into a precise triangle, completes the luxurious setting.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C. Peel potatoes. Slice very thinly, 1mm thick, using a mandoline. Layer potato slices tightly in a small, buttered baking dish (approx. 10x10 cm). Brush each layer with melted butter. Season with salt and pepper every few layers. Cover with parchment paper, then foil. Bake for 60 minutes, or until tender. Place a weighted object on top. Refrigerate overnight. Once chilled, cut into precise 4x4 cm squares.

Peel carrots. Cut into uniform 5 cm long batons, 1 cm thick. In a small saucepan, combine carrots, 50g butter, 100ml chicken stock, and a pinch of salt. Bring to a simmer. Cook, covered, until tender. Uncover. Increase heat. Reduce liquid until carrots are glazed and liquid evaporates.
In a small saucepan, reduce 300ml chicken stock over medium-high heat. Simmer until thickened to a light syrupy consistency. Keep warm.

Season chicken supreme all over with salt and pepper. Heat olive oil in an oven-safe pan over medium-high heat. Place chicken skin-side down. Sear for 8-10 minutes until skin is deep golden and crisp. Add 20g butter, 2 thyme sprigs, and 2 crushed garlic cloves to the pan. Flip chicken. Baste constantly with butter, thyme, and garlic for 2-3 minutes. Transfer pan to preheated 200°C oven. Roast for 10-12 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Rest chicken on a cutting board for 5 minutes before serving.
Gently warm potato mille-feuille squares in a non-stick pan or oven until heated through and edges are slightly crisp.

On each plate, place one warmed potato mille-feuille square slightly off-center. Place one rested chicken supreme next to it. Arrange 3-4 glazed carrot batons artfully. Drizzle a small amount of chicken jus around the components. Garnish with a few micro arugula leaves. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Lemon-Herb Yogurt Sauce and Savory Apple-Herb Pasta
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Pan-Seared Chicken with Lemon-Herb Yogurt Sauce and Savory Apple-Herb Pasta is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. A bed of al dente orecchiette pasta, tossed with small 1cm diced savory apple cubes and fresh green herbs, forms the base. A whole, golden-brown pan-seared chicken breast, cooked to perfection, rests slightly off-center atop the pasta. A creamy, pale white lemon-herb yogurt sauce is elegantly drizzled over the chicken and around the pasta, creating a visually appealing contrast. The dish is garnished with a sprig of vibrant fresh dill and a scattering of irregular, golden-brown toasted breadcrumbs, adding texture and color. A bright yellow lemon wedge is placed beside the chicken. The scene is set on a simple wooden table, with a crisp cotton napkin and standard flatware, under natural, even lighting in a modern bistro atmosphere. The background is softly blurred to keep the focus on the vibrant, well-composed dish.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a light green salad dressed with a vinaigrette.
instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat 1 tablespoon olive oil and 10g butter in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken breasts 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown. Internal temperature must reach 75°C.
Remove chicken from skillet. Rest on a cutting board, tented with foil.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Add pasta. Cook according to package directions until al dente.
While pasta cooks, tear bread into small irregular pieces. Heat 10g butter in a small skillet over medium heat.
Add torn bread to skillet. Toast until golden brown and crispy. Remove from skillet. Set aside.
Core and dice apple into small 1cm cubes. No need to peel. Heat remaining 10g butter in the same skillet used for bread over medium heat.
Add diced apple and minced garlic. Sauté 3-4 minutes until slightly softened. Season with a pinch of salt and pepper.
In a medium bowl, combine Greek yogurt, juice of half a lemon, 1 tablespoon chopped dill, and 1 tablespoon chopped parsley. Season with salt and pepper. Stir well.
Drain cooked pasta. Return to the large pot. Add sautéed apple, remaining 1 tablespoon chopped dill, and remaining 1 tablespoon chopped parsley. Add 1 tablespoon olive oil. Toss gently to combine.
Divide pasta among 4 plates. Place one whole pan-seared chicken breast on top of each pasta portion.
Drizzle lemon-herb yogurt sauce generously over chicken and pasta.
Garnish each plate with toasted breadcrumbs and a lemon wedge. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Consommé de Volaille Clarifié with Chicken Quenelles
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of crystal-clear, golden amber Consommé de Volaille is presented in a pristine white bone china consommé cup. Two to three perfectly oval, delicate white chicken quenelles rest gently at the bottom, visible through the transparent broth. A few precise droplets of vibrant green chervil oil are artfully swirled on the consommé's surface, creating subtle, organic patterns. A single, tiny sprig of micro chervil is meticulously placed on one quenelle, adding a delicate touch of green. The cup sits on a premium grey veined marble surface. The background is ultra-minimalist, emphasizing abundant negative space. A pristine white linen napkin, folded into a precise triangle, and an elegant demitasse spoon are positioned beside the cup. Dramatic professional lighting casts subtle shadows, highlighting the dish's sophisticated simplicity and refined execution.

ingredients.name: Micro chervil or micro dill (for garnish)

instructions: Prepare Chicken Stock: Combine chicken bones, charred onion, carrots, celery, leek, peppercorns, bay leaf, and thyme in a large pot. Add 3 litres cold water. Bring slowly to a simmer. Skim impurities. Simmer gently for 2-3 hours. Strain stock through a fine-mesh sieve. Chill completely.
Prepare Clarification Raft: Mince lean chicken meat very finely. Combine minced chicken, egg whites, and a pinch of salt in a bowl. Mix well.

Clarify Consommé: Add the cold clarification raft mixture to the cold chicken stock. Place pot over medium-low heat. Stir constantly until the raft begins to form and float. Stop stirring. Simmer gently for 30-45 minutes without disturbing, allowing the raft to clarify the liquid. Ensure the consommé does not boil vigorously.
Strain Consommé: Carefully ladle the crystal-clear consommé through a cheesecloth-lined sieve. Do not press the raft. Season consommé with salt to taste. Keep warm.

Prepare Chicken Quenelles: Dice cold chicken breast into small cubes. In a food processor, blend diced chicken with egg white until smooth. Gradually add very cold heavy cream while blending until a smooth, light mousse forms. Season with salt, white pepper, and nutmeg.

Poach Quenelles: Bring a pot of lightly salted water or chicken stock to a bare simmer. Using two spoons, shape small oval quenelles from the chicken mousse. Gently slide quenelles into the simmering liquid. Poach for 3-5 minutes, or until quenelles float and are cooked through. Internal temperature should reach 75°C (167°F). Remove with a slotted spoon. Drain well.

Prepare Chervil Oil: Blanch chervil briefly in boiling water. Immediately plunge into ice bath. Squeeze out excess water. Blend blanched chervil with grapeseed oil and a pinch of salt until smooth. Strain through a fine-mesh sieve or cheesecloth for a vibrant green oil.

Serve: Place 2-3 poached chicken quenelles in the bottom of each warm consommé cup. Carefully ladle the hot, crystal-clear consommé over the quenelles. Drizzle a few precise droplets of chervil oil onto the surface. Garnish with a single sprig of micro chervil or micro dill.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Chicken and Rice Skillet
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Spicy Chicken and Rice Skillet is presented in a shallow white porcelain bowl. Tender, golden-brown chicken chunks, about 3cm in size, are nestled atop a bed of fluffy, savory long-grain rice. The rice is infused with diced red bell peppers and onions, showcasing a warm, inviting color palette of whites, yellows, and soft reds. A generous layer of melted, bubbly cheddar cheese blankets the chicken and rice, creating a rich, glossy texture. A vibrant drizzle of red hot sauce zigzags across the cheese, adding a pop of color and a hint of spice. The dish is garnished with a sprinkle of freshly chopped green cilantro and a bright yellow lime wedge placed to the side. The bowl rests on a simple wooden table, accompanied by a silver fork and knife and a folded cotton napkin, all under natural, even lighting in a modern bistro setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas on the side.
Offer a bowl of salsa verde or pico de gallo as an accompaniment.
Pair with a fresh agua fresca.
instructions: Season chicken chunks with salt, pepper, cumin, chili powder, and smoked paprika.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add chicken chunks. Sear until golden brown on all sides and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C). Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside.
Add diced onion and bell pepper to the same skillet. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in rice. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring frequently, until lightly toasted.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a simmer.
Reduce heat to low. Cover skillet. Cook for 15-20 minutes, or until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed.
Return cooked chicken to the skillet. Gently fold into the rice.
Sprinkle shredded cheese evenly over the chicken and rice.
Cover skillet again. Cook for 3-5 minutes, or until cheese is melted and bubbly.
Remove from heat. Drizzle with hot sauce.
Garnish with fresh chopped cilantro and lime wedges. Serve hot.
notes: Adjust hot sauce to your preferred spice level.
For extra flavor, use a chipotle hot sauce.

recipes.recipe_name: Black Bean Mochi, Roasted Bell Pepper Glaze, Candied Eggplant Crisp
recipes.visual_description: Six to nine uniform miniature pieces are precisely arranged on a pristine white bone china platter. Each petit four is a spherical or cube-shaped black bean mochi, approximately 3cm in diameter, coated with a thin, glossy layer of vibrant ruby-red roasted bell pepper glaze. The glaze has a subtle translucency, allowing the dark mochi beneath to hint through. Adorning each mochi is a single, delicately curved, paper-thin candied eggplant crisp, golden-brown and translucent, providing an elegant architectural element and textural contrast. Abundant negative space surrounds the arrangement, emphasizing the purity of form and color. The platter rests on a polished white Carrara marble surface, illuminated by dramatic professional lighting that creates soft shadows, enhancing the minimalist elegance. A precisely folded pristine white linen napkin is placed to the side, completing the ultra-refined setting.

ingredients.name: Granulated sugar
ingredients.quantity: 80g (50g for bean paste, 30g for mochi dough)

instructions: Prepare black bean paste: If using dried beans, soak overnight. Cook beans until very tender. Drain. Blend cooked beans with 50g granulated sugar until smooth paste forms. Set aside.

Prepare mochi dough: In a bowl, combine glutinous rice flour, 30g granulated sugar, and 120ml water. Stir until smooth. Steam over high heat for 15 minutes, stirring every 5 minutes, until translucent and sticky. Let cool slightly.

Form mochi: Dust a clean surface with cornstarch. Knead the warm mochi dough briefly. Divide mochi dough into 6-9 equal portions. Flatten each portion. Place a small amount of black bean paste in the center. Carefully wrap the mochi dough around the paste to form a sphere or cube. Pinch seams closed. Roll gently to shape.
Prepare onion infusion: Combine 10g onion and 50ml water in a small saucepan. Simmer gently for 10 minutes. Strain, reserving the infused water. Discard onion.

Prepare red pepper glaze: Roast red bell peppers until skin is blistered and charred. Peel skin. Remove seeds. Blend roasted pepper flesh with the reserved onion-infused water until very smooth. Strain through a fine-mesh sieve to remove any solids. Return strained puree to saucepan. Add 40g granulated sugar and agar-agar powder. Bring to a simmer, stirring constantly for 2 minutes. Remove from heat. Stir in lemon juice. Cool slightly until it begins to thicken but is still pourable.

Prepare candied eggplant crisps: Wash eggplant. Slice eggplant paper-thin, ideally with a mandoline. Heat neutral oil to 160°C in a small saucepan. Fry eggplant slices in batches until golden brown and crispy. Transfer to a wire rack lined with paper towels to drain excess oil. Immediately sprinkle with a small amount of granulated sugar.

Assemble petit fours: Dip each mochi piece into the warm red pepper glaze, ensuring full coverage. Allow excess glaze to drip off. Place glazed mochi on a wire rack to set. Once glaze is set, carefully place one candied eggplant crisp on top of each mochi for garnish.

recipes.recipe_name: Crab and Pea Smash on Sourdough with Pickled Onion
recipes.visual_description: A thick slice of golden toasted sourdough bread serves as the base, positioned slightly off-center on a cream-toned, handcrafted ceramic plate. A generous, rustic layer of vibrant green pea smash, showing visible texture from the lightly crushed peas, is spread across the toast. Flaked, pristine white crab meat is piled naturally on top of the pea smash, maintaining its inherent form. Thinly sliced, translucent pink quick-pickled red onions are scattered artfully over the crab, providing a pop of color and acidity. A few small, fresh green mint leaves are placed sparingly as a natural garnish. The composition is clean and minimalist, allowing the natural colors and textures of the ingredients to shine. The entire plate is visible, with ample negative space. The setting features a light, textured wooden surface and soft, natural overhead light.
instructions: Thinly slice the red onion into rings. Place in a heatproof jar.
Combine apple cider vinegar, water, granulated sugar, and 5g sea salt in a small saucepan. Bring to a simmer, stirring until sugar and salt dissolve.
Pour the hot pickling liquid over the red onion rings. Let cool to room temperature, then refrigerate for at least 30 minutes.
Bring a pot of salted water to a boil. Add green peas and blanch for 2 minutes. Drain immediately and transfer to an ice bath to cool.
Drain peas thoroughly. Lightly smash peas with a fork in a bowl. Season with a pinch of salt, pepper, and a drizzle of olive oil. Do not over-mash.
Gently flake the fresh crab meat into a separate bowl. Drizzle with a little olive oil, season with salt and pepper. Toss gently.
Toast the sourdough bread slices until golden brown and crisp. This can be done in a toaster or pan.
To assemble, spread a generous layer of smashed green peas onto each toasted sourdough slice.
Top the pea smash with a natural mound of flaked crab meat.
Drain the pickled red onions. Scatter a few pickled onion rings over the crab and pea smash.
Garnish each toast with a few fresh mint leaves. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Portuguese Fish and Tomato Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Portuguese Fish and Tomato Rice is presented in a deep, rustic ceramic bowl. The dish is a comforting, wet rice stew, not dry. It showcases tender, flaky chunks of white fish (approximately 3-4 cm) interspersed throughout the moist, reddish-orange rice. The rice is infused with diced tomato and flecks of green parsley or cilantro. The natural colors of the ingredients are prominent. The plating is casual, with the components naturally overlapping, reflecting a homely preparation. A sprinkle of fresh green parsley or cilantro brightens the top. The bowl sits on a well-used wooden dining table. A simple, off-white cloth napkin is casually placed nearby. Warm, inviting lighting from a kitchen fixture illuminates the scene, enhancing the comfort food aesthetic.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread for dipping into the flavorful broth.
Accompany with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and vinegar.
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium heat. Add chopped onion. Cook until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Add minced garlic and bay leaf. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant. Do not brown garlic.
Stir in crushed tomatoes and paprika. Cook for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, allowing flavors to meld.
Add rice to the pot. Stir well to coat rice with the tomato mixture. Cook for 2 minutes.
Pour in fish or vegetable broth. Bring to a simmer. Season with salt and pepper.
Reduce heat to low. Cover the pot and cook for 10-12 minutes. Rice should be partially cooked.
Gently stir in fish chunks (3-4 cm) and half of the chopped parsley/cilantro. Ensure fish internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F).
Cover again and continue cooking for 5-8 minutes, or until fish is cooked through and flakes easily. Rice should be tender and the dish should be moist, like a thick stew.
Remove bay leaf. Taste and adjust seasoning if needed.
Serve immediately, garnished with remaining fresh parsley or cilantro.

recipes.recipe_name: Chocolate Puffed Rice Bites
recipes.visual_description: A close-up shot of six to nine uniform, glossy dark chocolate-coated puffed rice bites, arranged neatly on a rectangular white ceramic serving platter. Each bite is a compact square or rectangle, approximately 3x3 cm, showcasing the crisp texture of puffed rice bound by rich, dark chocolate. The surface of the chocolate is smooth with a slight sheen, some pieces revealing the embedded rice. The platter sits on a well-used wooden dining table, with a casually placed, slightly rumpled linen napkin in a neutral tone beside it. Warm, soft kitchen lighting illuminates the scene, creating gentle shadows and highlighting the bites' inviting texture. The background is minimally blurred, suggesting a cozy, lived-in family kitchen atmosphere with natural light.
instructions: Line a 20x20 cm baking tin with parchment paper. Ensure paper extends over edges for easy removal.
Combine dark chocolate, unsalted butter, and golden syrup in a heatproof bowl.
Place the bowl over a saucepan of simmering water (bain-marie). Do not let the bowl touch the water.
Melt ingredients slowly, stirring continuously until smooth and fully combined.
Remove the bowl from heat. Add puffed rice to the chocolate mixture.
Stir well until all puffed rice is evenly coated with the chocolate mixture.
Transfer the mixture into the prepared baking tin. Press down firmly and evenly using the back of a spoon or a spatula.
Refrigerate for at least 2 hours, or until the mixture is completely firm.
Once firm, lift the block from the tin using the parchment paper handles.
Place the block on a cutting board. Use a sharp knife to cut into 6-9 uniform small squares or rectangles.
Serve immediately. Store any leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator.

recipes.recipe_name: Bluefin Tuna Tartare Crisps with Confit Tomato
recipes.visual_description: Eight to twelve exquisite canapés are presented on a pristine white Carrara marble slab. Each features a precisely cut 2 cm square of golden, crispy fried sushi rice as its base. Perched atop is a small, perfectly mounded quenelle of vibrant, deep red Bluefin tuna tartare, showcasing meticulous dicing. Adjacent to the tuna, a single glossy, ruby-red confit cherry tomato half adds a pop of color and subtle sweetness. A few delicate, bright green micro shiso leaves are strategically placed. A tiny, glistening dollop of black caviar crowns each piece, adding a luxurious touch. The arrangement is minimalist and artful, with abundant negative space between each canapé, emphasizing precision and elegance. Soft, dramatic professional lighting casts subtle shadows, enhancing textures and highlighting sophisticated simplicity.
instructions: Prepare crispy rice: Cook sushi rice according to package directions. Spread cooked rice thinly on a baking sheet. Chill completely. Cut chilled rice into 2 cm x 2 cm squares. Deep-fry rice squares in neutral oil at 180°C until golden and crispy. Drain on paper towels. Season lightly with sea salt.

Make tomato confit: Preheat oven to 120°C. Halve cherry tomatoes. Place in a small oven-safe dish. Add 1 peeled garlic clove, 30 ml olive oil, a pinch of sea salt. Roast for 45 minutes until tender and slightly shriveled. Let cool. Remove garlic.
Prepare tuna tartare: Finely dice Bluefin tuna into 5 mm cubes. Mince shallot finely. Mince remaining garlic clove very finely or grate. Finely chop chives.
Combine tuna: In a bowl, gently mix diced tuna, minced shallot, minced garlic, chives, soy sauce, sesame oil, and lime juice. Season with sea salt and black pepper to taste. Mix just until combined.

Assemble canapés: Place crispy rice squares on a serving platter. Top each rice square with a small, precise mound of tuna tartare. Place one confit cherry tomato half next to or on top of the tartare.
Garnish: Finish each canapé with a few delicate micro shiso leaves and a small dollop of caviar. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Garlic Chicken Wings
recipes.visual_description: A generous pile of Spicy Garlic Chicken Wings is casually arranged on a large, rustic ceramic platter, showcasing their deep golden-brown, crispy skin generously coated in a glossy, vibrant red-orange hot sauce. Some wings are whole, others are drumettes and flats, piled naturally with some overlapping. Specks of minced garlic and a hint of red cayenne pepper are visible in the sauce. The plating is unpretentious, reflecting a homestyle comfort food. The platter sits on a well-used wooden dining table in a homely family kitchen setting. A casually placed, light-colored cloth napkin is nearby. The scene is bathed in warm, cozy kitchen lighting, emphasizing the inviting, lived-in atmosphere. The background is minimal, allowing the focus to remain on the hearty snack portion.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Pat chicken wings thoroughly dry with paper towels.
In a large bowl, toss wings with flour, salt, black pepper, and cayenne pepper until evenly coated.
Arrange coated wings in a single layer on a baking rack placed over a baking sheet.
Bake for 45-55 minutes, flipping halfway through, until wings are crispy and cooked through.
While wings bake, melt butter in a small saucepan over medium heat.
Add minced garlic to the melted butter. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in the hot sauce. Simmer for 2 minutes. Remove from heat.
Transfer cooked wings to a large clean bowl.
Pour the hot sauce mixture over the wings.
Toss until all wings are evenly coated. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Mediterranean Braised Chicken
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Mediterranean Braised Chicken is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. Two golden-brown, bone-in chicken thighs are nestled amidst a rustic stew of vibrant red and yellow bell pepper chunks, diced tomatoes, and translucent onion pieces. The seared chicken skin is crisp, contrasting with the tender meat. The sauce is thick and glossy, clinging to ingredients. Freshly chopped bright green parsley is sprinkled over the dish, adding a pop of color. The arrangement is organic, with moderate negative space. Chicken pieces are whole, not sliced. The plate rests on a light wooden table, accompanied by a white cotton napkin and silver flatware. A rustic ceramic bowl of crusty bread and a simple green salad are nearby, completing the casual bistro setting. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's rich colors and textures, with a softly blurred restaurant background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Crusty bread to soak up the sauce
Simple green salad

ingredients.name: Red bell pepper, cut into 2 cm chunks
Yellow bell pepper, cut into 2 cm chunks

instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs skin-side down for 5-7 minutes until golden brown and crispy. Flip and sear other side for 3-4 minutes. Remove chicken from pot.
Add diced onions to the pot. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened and translucent.
Add minced garlic and bell pepper chunks. Cook for 3-4 minutes until fragrant.
Pour in white wine, if using. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Cook for 2 minutes until liquid reduces slightly.
Stir in diced tomatoes, chicken stock, oregano, thyme, and bay leaf. Bring mixture to a simmer.
Return seared chicken thighs to the pot. Ensure chicken is mostly submerged in the sauce.
Reduce heat to low. Cover the pot and simmer for 30-40 minutes. Chicken should reach an internal temperature of 75°C.
Remove bay leaf. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley before serving.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken and Raisin Stew
recipes.visual_description: A single, homely portion of Chicken and Raisin Stew is presented in a deep, rustic ceramic bowl with natural imperfections. Large, tender chicken chunks are nestled among thinly sliced onions and plump, dark raisins. The stew features a rich, reddish-brown sauce from the tomatoes and spices, with visible specks of herbs. A scattering of fresh, roughly chopped green parsley provides a vibrant contrast. The bowl sits on a well-used wooden dining table, revealing its natural grain and a lived-in feel. A simple, basic spoon rests casually beside the bowl, and a torn piece of crusty Moroccan khobz (bread) is placed nearby, ready for dipping. The lighting is warm and inviting, typical of a cozy kitchen, emphasizing the comforting nature of the dish. The entire setup evokes a relaxed, family meal atmosphere, with minimal arrangement and focus on the hearty, comforting food.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with fluffy couscous or crusty bread like khobz to soak up the rich sauce.
Offer a side of refreshing mint tea to complete the meal.
instructions: Cut chicken thighs into large, rustic chunks. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear chicken chunks until lightly browned on all sides. Remove chicken from pot and set aside.
Thinly slice the onion. Add sliced onion to the pot. Cook until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Mince garlic. Grate fresh ginger. Add minced garlic and grated ginger to the pot. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add ground cumin, ground coriander, ground turmeric, sweet paprika, and ground cinnamon to the pot. Stir for 30 seconds until aromatic.
Return chicken chunks to the pot. Add canned diced tomatoes, chicken stock, and raisins. Stir to combine.
Bring the mixture to a simmer. Reduce heat to low, cover the pot, and cook for 30-40 minutes. Simmer until chicken is tender and cooked through.
Remove lid. Simmer for an additional 5-10 minutes to slightly thicken the sauce, if desired.
Chop fresh parsley. Stir half of the chopped parsley into the stew.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper as needed.
Serve hot, garnished with remaining fresh parsley.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Tomato & Pickled Onion Salad with Crispy Chicken and Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single starter portion is elegantly presented on a small, round, handcrafted ceramic plate in a natural cream or beige tone. The plate rests on a light bamboo or reclaimed wood table surface, emphasizing eco-conscious design. At the center of the plate, a vibrant, natural arrangement of ingredients forms a cohesive mound, leaving ample white space around the edges. Large wedges of light red, pre-fermented tomatoes, some with slightly softened edges, are interspersed with translucent, thinly sliced, quick-pickled red onion rings, showcasing their subtle pink hue. Small, irregularly shaped, golden-brown seared chicken chunks are nestled within the salad, providing a tender contrast. Shards of deeply golden, irregularly shaped crispy chicken skin are scattered on top, adding a rich, crackling texture. A few small, irregularly shaped crispy rice pieces, golden-brown and airy, are also lightly sprinkled over the ingredients. The dish is garnished with a single, small sprig of fresh green parsley or dill, adding a touch of natural color without being ornate. The overall composition is clean and minimalist, highlighting the pure beauty and natural textures of each ingredient. The lighting is soft and natural, casting gentle shadows that enhance the organic feel. An undyed linen napkin in a natural beige tone is subtly placed beside the plate. The background is clean and uncluttered, with a hint of natural elements like a leafy green plant visible in soft focus, maintaining the sustainable aesthetic. The entire plate is visible, showcasing a balanced and uncrowded presentation.

ingredients.name: Fresh dill or basil sprig (for fermentation)
Chicken breast or thigh, skin on
Fresh parsley or dill sprigs, for garnish

instructions: Prepare Fermented Tomatoes: In a clean jar, combine 500ml filtered water, 15g sea salt, 2 crushed garlic cloves, and 1 sprig fresh dill or basil. Stir to dissolve salt. Add halved or quartered tomatoes. Ensure tomatoes are fully submerged. Seal with an airlock lid or burp daily. Ferment at room temperature for 3-5 days, or until desired tanginess is achieved. Store in refrigerator.

Prepare Quick-Pickled Onions: In a small saucepan, combine 120ml white vinegar, 120ml water, 15g sugar, and 5g salt. Bring to a simmer, stirring until sugar and salt dissolve. Remove from heat. Place thinly sliced red onion rings in a heatproof jar. Pour hot pickling liquid over onions. Let cool to room temperature. Refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or until chilled.
Prepare Crispy Chicken & Rice: Separate chicken skin from breast/thigh. Cut chicken meat into small, bite-sized chunks (approx. 2cm). Season chicken chunks with a pinch of salt.
Heat a non-stick pan over medium heat. Add chicken skin, fat side down. Cook slowly until deeply golden and crisp. Remove skin, drain on paper towel. Chop crispy skin into small shards.

Increase heat to medium-high. Add chicken chunks to the same pan (add a tiny bit of olive oil if needed). Sear chicken chunks until golden brown on all sides and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C). Remove from pan.
Spread cooked rice thinly on a baking sheet or in a pan with a little olive oil. Bake at 180°C or pan-fry until crispy and golden. Break into small pieces.
Assemble Dish: Gently combine fermented tomato wedges, quick-pickled onion rings, seared chicken chunks, crispy chicken skin shards, and crispy rice pieces in a bowl. Do not overmix.
Divide the salad among four small, shallow white or cream-colored ceramic plates.
Garnish each portion with a small sprig of fresh parsley or dill. Finish with a sprinkle of flaky sea salt.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken and Millet Fritters with Caramelized Onion Dip
recipes.visual_description: A single starter portion of Chicken and Millet Fritters is casually arranged on a simple, round ceramic plate with natural imperfections. Three golden-brown, pan-fried fritters are gently stacked or overlapped, showcasing their crispy exterior and the flecks of millet and chicken within. Next to the fritters, a small, rustic ceramic bowl holds a generous dollop of creamy, light brown caramelized onion dip. A few fresh, finely chopped parsley leaves are sprinkled over the fritters for a touch of green. The entire plate sits on a well-used wooden dining table, suggesting a comfortable, lived-in family kitchen setting. Warm, natural lighting from kitchen fixtures illuminates the scene. A casually placed cloth napkin rests nearby. The background is minimal, focusing entirely on the homely, inviting presentation of the dish.
instructions: Place chicken breast in a pot. Cover with water. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat. Simmer 15 minutes, until cooked through. Internal temperature must reach 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken. Shred finely with two forks. Set aside.

Rinse millet thoroughly. Combine millet with 300 ml water in a saucepan. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low. Cover. Simmer 15 minutes, until water is absorbed. Remove from heat. Let stand covered 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork.
Peel one large yellow onion. Finely dice it. Set aside for fritters.

Peel the second large yellow onion. Thinly slice it. Heat 20 ml vegetable oil in a large pan over medium-low heat. Add thinly sliced onion. Cook slowly for 25-30 minutes, stirring occasionally, until deeply golden brown and caramelized. Season with a pinch of salt.
Blend caramelized onion with sour cream until smooth. Season dip with salt and pepper. Set aside.
In a large bowl, combine shredded chicken, cooked millet, finely diced raw onion, egg, flour, and finely chopped parsley. Season with salt and pepper. Mix well to combine.
Form mixture into 12 small, flat fritters, about 5 cm in diameter.
Heat remaining 30 ml vegetable oil in a large non-stick pan over medium heat. Fry fritters in batches for 3-4 minutes per side, until golden brown and cooked through. Drain on paper towels.
Serve fritters warm with the caramelized onion dip.
notes: Ensure chicken is fully cooked before shredding.
Adjust salt and pepper to taste in both fritters and dip.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Tomato & Chickpea Stew with Sourdough Croutons
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of hearty Fermented Tomato & Chickpea Stew is presented in a handcrafted, matte ceramic bowl with an earthy cream tone, allowing ample negative space around the dish. The stew is a rich, rustic red-orange hue from the fermented tomatoes, with visible whole chickpeas and tender, diced carrots, celery, and onions. Its texture is fluid and comforting, showcasing the natural variations of the ingredients. A scattering of golden-brown, irregularly shaped sourdough croutons rests on top, adding a crisp contrast, alongside a sprinkle of vibrant green, finely chopped fresh parsley. The bowl sits on a light, textured reclaimed wood surface. To the side, a simple, undyed linen napkin in natural beige is folded. Soft, diffused natural light illuminates the scene from the left, creating gentle shadows and highlighting the organic textures. A subtle, out-of-focus green plant element is visible in the minimalist background.
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add diced onion, carrot, and celery. Sauté until softened, about 8-10 minutes.
Add minced garlic, bay leaf, and oregano. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in diced fermented tomatoes and chickpeas.
Pour in vegetable broth. Bring mixture to a simmer.
Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer 20-25 minutes, allowing flavors to meld.
While stew simmers, prepare sourdough croutons: Cut stale sourdough into 2 cm cubes.
Toss bread cubes with a drizzle of olive oil, salt, and pepper.
Spread on a baking sheet. Bake at 180°C for 10-15 minutes, until golden and crisp.
Remove bay leaf from the stew.
Season stew with salt and pepper to taste.
Ladle stew into bowls. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley and sourdough croutons.
notes: To reduce waste, make your own vegetable broth from kitchen scraps (onion skins, carrot tops, celery ends).
Overripe tomatoes are excellent for fermentation; this recipe is perfect for using them up.
Adjust stew consistency by adding more broth or simmering longer.

recipes.recipe_name: Heirloom Tomato Composition
recipes.visual_description: A pristine, oversized white ceramic sharing platter serves as the canvas for this minimalist composition. Abundant negative space highlights the meticulously arranged elements. Clusters of vibrant confit cherry tomatoes, their skins gently wrinkled and glistening with oil, are placed organically. Beside them, precise 1cm translucent cubes of tomato consommé gelee shimmer, catching the light. A small, vibrant mound of finely diced heirloom tomato tartare, showcasing varied red hues and fresh chives, adds a textural contrast. A delicate drizzle of vivid green basil oil forms graceful, flowing lines around the components. Completing the ensemble, one or two irregularly shaped, golden-brown Parmesan tuiles stand upright, adding architectural height and a crisp texture. The dish is presented on a premium white Carrara marble surface, illuminated by dramatic professional lighting casting subtle, intentional shadows, with a pristine white linen napkin folded precisely nearby, emphasizing sophisticated simplicity.
instructions: Preheat oven to 120°C.
Place cherry tomatoes, olive oil, thyme, garlic, salt, pepper in a small ovenproof dish.
Roast for 45-60 minutes until very soft. Cool completely.
For Tomato Consommé: Blend chopped plum tomatoes, shallot, 5g basil.
Pass mixture through a fine-mesh sieve. Then pass through a coffee filter or cheesecloth overnight to yield clear consommé.
For Consommé Gelee: Measure 200ml clear tomato consommé.
Heat 50ml consommé with agar-agar in a small saucepan. Whisk constantly.
Bring to a simmer for 1 minute. Remove from heat. Add remaining consommé. Season with salt and sugar.
Pour into a shallow dish (approx. 1cm deep). Chill until set. Cut into 1cm cubes.
For Heirloom Tomato Tartare: Dice heirloom tomatoes into 5mm cubes.
Combine diced tomatoes with chives, extra virgin olive oil, salt, pepper. Mix gently.
For Basil Oil: Blanch 50g basil leaves for 10 seconds. Immediately transfer to an ice bath.
Squeeze basil dry. Blend basil with neutral oil and a pinch of salt until smooth.
Pass through a fine-mesh sieve or cheesecloth for clear oil.
For Parmesan Tuiles: Preheat oven to 180°C. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Arrange small mounds (approx. 5g each) of grated Parmesan. Leave space between mounds.
Bake for 5-7 minutes until golden and crisp. Cool on a wire rack.
Assembly: On a large, minimalist white serving platter, artfully arrange small clusters of confit cherry tomatoes, heirloom tomato tartare, and tomato consommé gelee cubes.
Drizzle basil oil sparingly around elements. Place 1-2 Parmesan tuiles elegantly alongside.
Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Southwestern Beef and Black Bean Stew with Corn Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Southwestern Beef and Black Bean Stew is presented in a deep, clean white porcelain bowl. Fluffy white rice forms a neat base, topped with a rich, thick stew. The stew features tender, braised beef chunks alongside dark black beans and vibrant yellow corn kernels. Hints of red from diced tomatoes and bell peppers are visible within the glossy, deep reddish-brown sauce. A generous dollop of white sour cream or crema sits on top, adorned with bright green chopped cilantro. A lime wedge rests beside the bowl. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a simple wooden table surface and a cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its comforting textures and colors. The entire plate is visible, with moderate negative space, creating a professional yet approachable presentation.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Warm corn tortillas
Tortilla chips
Lime wedges
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven or heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat. Season beef cubes with salt and pepper. Sear beef in batches until browned on all sides. Remove beef and set aside.
Add diced onion, bell pepper, and minced garlic to the pot. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened and fragrant.
Pour in beer, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Bring to a simmer.

Return beef to the pot. Add crushed tomatoes, beef broth, chili powder, cumin, smoked paprika, and oregano. Stir in hot sauce. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 1.5-2 hours, or until beef is very tender.
While stew simmers, cook rice according to package directions.
Stir rinsed black beans and frozen corn into the stew during the last 15 minutes of cooking. Continue to simmer, uncovered, allowing the stew to thicken slightly. Taste and adjust seasoning.

Serve the hot beef and black bean stew generously spooned over a bed of fluffy white rice. Garnish each portion with a dollop of sour cream or crema, a sprinkle of fresh chopped cilantro, and a lime wedge on the side.

recipes.recipe_name: Spanish Chicken and Chorizo Rice
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant Spanish Chicken and Chorizo Rice dish is centrally plated on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. The rice, cooked to a tender but not mushy consistency, forms a shallow, even layer, showcasing its rich golden-orange hue from saffron and paprika. Interspersed throughout are generous, irregular chunks of seared chicken, displaying a golden-brown crust, and thick, browned medallions of chorizo sausage, their edges slightly crisped. Bright red bell pepper cubes and golden corn kernels add bursts of color and texture, evenly distributed. A scattering of fresh, finely chopped green parsley provides a final vibrant contrast. The dish is presented with moderate negative space on the plate, allowing each element to be clearly seen without overcrowding. A crisp, simple side salad of mixed greens, lightly dressed, sits in a small, elegant white bowl beside the main plate. A quartered fresh lemon wedge is placed beside the rice for serving. The setting is a modern bistro, with a simple light wooden table surface. A grey linen napkin is folded neatly beside the plate. The scene is illuminated by natural, even lighting, creating subtle shadows and highlighting the dish's textures and colors. A rustic, dark-glazed ceramic serving bowl is visible in the soft-focus background, subtly hinting at a shared dining experience without distracting from the individual portion. Traditional flatware is placed beside the plate.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve directly from the skillet or paella pan for family-style dining.
Offer crusty bread for soaking up the flavorful juices.
Accompany with a dry white wine or sangria.
instructions: Prepare ingredients. Dice chicken thighs into 3 cm chunks. Slice chorizo into 1 cm thick rounds. Dice onion into small cubes. Dice red bell pepper into 1.5 cm cubes. Mince garlic.
Heat olive oil in a large, deep skillet or paella pan over medium-high heat. Add chicken chunks. Sear until golden brown on all sides. Remove chicken from pan. Set aside.
Add chorizo slices to the same pan. Cook until browned and crisp. Remove chorizo. Set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion and bell pepper to the pan. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic and smoked paprika. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in Arborio rice. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly, until rice grains are translucent at the edges.
Pour in canned diced tomatoes and chicken broth. Add saffron threads. Stir well. Bring to a simmer.
Return seared chicken to the pan. Reduce heat to low. Cover and cook for 15-18 minutes, or until rice is almost tender and liquid is mostly absorbed. Stir occasionally to prevent sticking.
Stir in frozen corn kernels and cooked chorizo. Cook uncovered for another 5 minutes, or until rice is fully cooked and liquid is absorbed. Ensure chicken reaches 75°C internal temperature.
Remove pan from heat. Let rest for 5 minutes.
Finely chop fresh parsley. Garnish the dish with chopped parsley. Serve with lemon wedges and a side of mixed salad greens.
notes: The chicken internal temperature must reach 75°C for safety.
Adjust liquid if rice seems too dry or wet during cooking.

recipes.recipe_name: Arroz con Pollo
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Arroz con Pollo presented on a clean white porcelain plate. Two whole, bone-in chicken thighs with deeply browned, crispy skin sit atop a bed of golden, saffron-stained rice. The rice grains are plump and distinct, interspersed with fine bits of softened onion and concentrated red tomato. The dish shows vibrant yellow and orange hues from the saffron and paprika. A generous sprinkle of bright green, finely chopped parsley is scattered over the top. A single lemon wedge is placed neatly on the side. The plate sits on a light oak wooden table with a folded white cotton napkin. Lighting is bright, natural, and even, highlighting the textures of the crispy skin and the moist rice grains.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of Alioli (garlic mayonnaise)
Accompany with crusty bread and a glass of chilled white wine
Present in a traditional terracotta cazuela for family-style dining
instructions: Season chicken thighs with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a wide shallow pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken skin-side down until golden and crispy.
Flip and brown the other side. Remove chicken from pan.
Add onion to the same pan. Sauté until translucent.
Stir in garlic and grated tomato. Cook until liquid evaporates and mixture darkens.
Add smoked paprika and rice. Stir to coat rice in oil for 2 minutes.
Pour in white wine. Deglaze the pan. Simmer until wine reduces by half.
Add hot stock and saffron. Stir once to distribute.
Place chicken thighs back into the pan on top of the rice.
Simmer undisturbed over medium-low heat for 18-20 minutes.
Ensure chicken reaches internal temperature of 75°C.
Remove from heat. Cover with a clean cloth. Rest for 5 minutes.
Garnish with fresh parsley before serving.
notes: Do not stir the rice once the stock is added to allow a crust to form on the bottom.
Use a wide pan to ensure even rice cooking.

recipes.recipe_name: Spiced Squash and Potato Tikki with Lemon-Chili Relish
recipes.visual_description: Eight to twelve golden-brown, crisp Spiced Squash and Potato Tikkis are arranged artfully on a dark slate board. Each tikki is perfectly round and flat, approximately 5 cm in diameter. A small, vibrant dollop of fresh lemon-chili relish sits on top of each tikki, showcasing finely diced red onion, bright green minced chili, and fresh coriander flecks. A few whole fresh coriander leaves are scattered sparingly on the board for added color. The tikkis have a crisp exterior and a soft interior, complemented by the fresh crunch of the relish. The dark slate board is placed on a simple wooden table. A clean white cotton napkin is folded neatly beside the platter. Natural, even lighting highlights the textures and colors. The background is minimal and slightly blurred, suggesting a casual bistro or restaurant ambiance.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with mint chutney or tamarind chutney on the side.
Can be served as part of a larger appetizer spread.
Often accompanied by hot chai.
instructions: Boil squash cubes until tender. Drain. Mash well.
Boil potato quarters until tender. Drain. Peel and mash.

In a bowl, combine mashed squash, mashed potato, half of the finely chopped onion, half of the minced green chilies, ginger-garlic paste, cumin powder, coriander powder, turmeric powder, garam masala, salt, and 1 tbsp chopped fresh coriander. Mix thoroughly.
Add breadcrumbs, 1 tablespoon at a time, until mixture is firm enough to shape.
Form 10-12 small, flat, round tikkis, about 5 cm diameter and 1.5 cm thick.
Heat 2-3 tablespoons oil in a large non-stick pan over medium heat.
Pan-fry tikkis in batches, 3-4 minutes per side, until golden brown and crisp. Add more oil as needed.
For the relish: In a small bowl, combine remaining finely chopped onion, remaining minced green chilies, juice of half lemon, a pinch of salt, and remaining chopped fresh coriander. Mix well.
Serve warm tikkis immediately. Top each with a small spoonful of lemon-chili relish.
notes: Adjust chili to desired spice level.
Ensure tikkis are firm enough to hold shape before frying.
Tikkis can be prepared ahead and reheated gently.

recipes.recipe_name: Hyderabadi Chicken Biryani
recipes.visual_description: The entire plate is captured in a professional shot. The dish is presented in a traditional wide-rimmed white porcelain bowl. Steamed long-grain Basmati rice displays a mix of snow-white and saffron-infused yellow grains. Large, moist chunks of marinated and steamed bone-in chicken thighs are buried partially in the rice, coated in a dark, aromatic masala. The top is scattered with crispy, deep-brown fried onions and vibrant green chopped mint and coriander. A small copper bowl of chilled cucumber raita sits to the left. The setting includes a dark wood surface, a silver spoon, and a crisp white cotton napkin. Natural light emphasizes the fluffy rice texture and the steam rising from the center. No meat is sliced.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Chilled cucumber and onion raita
Mirchi ka Salan
Fresh lime wedges and sliced red onions
instructions: Mix chicken chunks, yogurt, biryani masala, ginger-garlic paste, and 10g salt.
Marinate for 60 minutes.
Rinse rice until water runs clear.
Soak rice in water for 30 minutes.
Boil 2 liters water with cloves and cardamom.
Add rice and cook until 70% tender.
Drain rice immediately.
Place marinated chicken chunks in a heavy-bottomed pot.
Spread 50g fried onions, chopped mint, and coriander over chicken.
Layer rice over the herbs and onions.
Drizzle saffron-infused milk and ghee over rice.
Seal pot lid tightly with aluminum foil.
Cook on low heat for 30 minutes.
Verify chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Rest for 10 minutes before fluffing with a fork.
notes: Use high-quality aged Basmati rice for long, separate grains.
Do not stir the rice during the dum process to prevent breakage.

recipes.recipe_name: Plum and Oat Crumble Tartlets
recipes.visual_description: A single Plum and Oat Crumble Tartlet rests on a simple, round, off-white ceramic plate. The tartlet features a golden-brown, flaky shortcrust pastry shell with slightly crimped edges. Inside, a rich, deep purple plum filling, roughly chopped and slightly bubbling, peeks through a generous, golden-brown oat crumble topping. The crumble is irregularly textured, showcasing toasted oats and bits of baked flour. A dollop of softly whipped thickened cream sits beside the tartlet. The plate is on a well-used, light-colored wooden dining table, suggesting a comfortable Australian home kitchen. Warm, natural light illuminates the scene. A casually placed plain linen tea towel and a ceramic teacup are subtly visible in the background, reinforcing the homely, comforting aesthetic.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve warm with a cup of tea or coffee

ingredients.name: Fresh plums, pitted and roughly chopped

instructions: Prepare tartlet dough: Combine 150g flour and 75g cold butter. Rub butter into flour until crumbly. Add iced water gradually. Mix until dough forms. Form into a disc. Wrap and chill 30 minutes.
Prepare plum filling: Combine chopped plums, 50g caster sugar, 1 teaspoon cinnamon, and 10g butter in a saucepan. Cook over medium heat 5-7 minutes. Stir occasionally. Plums should soften slightly.
Prepare oat crumble: Combine rolled oats, 50g flour, brown sugar, 40g cold butter, and 0.5 teaspoon cinnamon. Rub butter into dry ingredients. Form coarse crumbs.
Preheat oven to 180°C (350°F).
Roll chilled dough on a lightly floured surface. Cut four circles to fit tartlet tins. Press dough into four 10cm tartlet tins.
Divide plum filling evenly into each pastry shell.
Top each tartlet generously with oat crumble.
Bake 25-30 minutes. Tartlets are done when crust is golden and filling is bubbling.
Let tartlets cool slightly in tins. Remove carefully.
Whip thickened cream until soft peaks form.
Serve warm tartlets with a dollop of whipped cream.
notes: Adjust sugar in plum filling based on plum sweetness.
Tartlets can be made ahead and reheated gently.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Chicken and Carrot Risotto
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of creamy Chicken and Carrot Risotto is presented in a wide, shallow white porcelain bowl. The risotto, with its characteristic fluid consistency, flows naturally within the bowl. Visible are tender, golden-brown diced chicken pieces, vibrant orange finely diced carrots, and hints of minced garlic. The dish boasts a warm, inviting off-white color from the Arborio rice and Parmesan, contrasted by the brighter hues of the vegetables and chicken. A generous sprinkle of fresh, bright green chopped parsley garnishes the top, adding a pop of color and freshness. The texture is rich and velvety. The bowl sits on a simple light wooden table surface, accompanied by standard silver flatware and a folded white cotton napkin, creating a clean, approachable bistro setting under even, natural lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately, as risotto loses its ideal consistency quickly.
Pair with a light green salad dressed with a simple vinaigrette.
Offer crusty Italian bread on the side for soaking up any remaining sauce.
instructions: Dice chicken thighs into 2cm cubes. Season chicken with salt and pepper. Finely dice the onion and carrots. Mince the garlic. Heat chicken stock in a separate saucepan; keep it hot.

Heat 1 tablespoon of olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add chicken cubes. Sear chicken for 4-5 minutes until golden brown and cooked through. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from the pot and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add remaining 1 tablespoon of olive oil to the pot. Add diced onion and carrots. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add Arborio rice to the pot. Stir constantly for 2 minutes to toast the rice kernels (tostatura).
Pour in the white wine. Stir until completely absorbed by the rice.
Begin adding the hot chicken stock, one ladleful at a time. Stir continuously. Wait until each ladleful is almost completely absorbed before adding the next. This process takes about 18-20 minutes.
When half the stock is added, return the cooked chicken to the pot. Continue adding stock and stirring.
The risotto is ready when the rice is al dente (firm to the bite but creamy). It should be fluid, not dry.
Remove the pot from heat. Stir in the butter and grated Parmesan cheese vigorously (mantecatura). This creates a creamy consistency. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Finely chop fresh parsley for garnish. Serve immediately in warm bowls. Garnish each serving with fresh parsley.
notes: The key to perfect risotto is constant stirring and gradual addition of hot stock. This releases starch from the rice, creating its signature creaminess.
Risotto should be creamy and fluid, not stiff or dry.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken Breast with Creamy Buckwheat Polenta and Sautéed Mushrooms
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean, white porcelain dinner plate, on a simple wooden table in a modern bistro setting. A single portion features a generous, free-form mound of creamy, light grey-brown buckwheat polenta. Two to three thick, golden-brown pan-seared chicken breast chunks rest atop the polenta; the chicken is presented in substantial pieces, never fanned. Sautéed mixed wild mushrooms, in varied brown tones with golden edges, are scattered around the polenta and chicken. Finely chopped fresh green parsley adds a vibrant color contrast. The overall color palette is warm and earthy, with varied textures. Moderate negative space creates a balanced, professional composition. A cotton napkin and traditional flatware are placed beside the plate. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's textures and colors.

ingredients.name: mixed wild mushrooms (e.g., cremini, shiitake, oyster), cleaned, sliced

instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season generously with salt and pepper. Heat 15 mL olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken breasts for 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown. Transfer skillet to a preheated oven at 180°C (350°F). Cook for 10-15 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Remove from oven. Let rest 5 minutes before serving.

In a large saucepan, combine chicken stock and milk. Bring to a gentle simmer over medium heat. Gradually whisk in buckwheat flour, stirring constantly to prevent lumps. Reduce heat to low. Cook, stirring frequently, for 15-20 minutes, until mixture thickens to a creamy polenta consistency. Stir in 30 g butter, Parmesan cheese, 3 g salt, and 1 g pepper until smooth. Keep warm.

While polenta cooks, heat 15 mL olive oil in a separate skillet over medium-high heat. Add mushrooms. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until browned and tender. Add minced shallot and garlic. Cook for 2 minutes until fragrant. If using, deglaze with white wine, scraping up any browned bits. Cook until wine evaporates. Stir in 15 g butter and fresh thyme. Season with 2 g salt and 1 g pepper.

Ladle a generous portion of creamy buckwheat polenta onto the center of each of 4 dinner plates. Slice each rested chicken breast into 2-3 thick chunks. Place chicken chunks atop the polenta. Spoon sautéed mushrooms around the chicken and polenta. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Chicken and Quinoa Bake
recipes.visual_description: A generous, comforting individual portion of Creamy Chicken and Quinoa Bake is centered on a round, simple cream-colored ceramic plate. The dish showcases large, tender chunks of chicken breast, nestled among fluffy quinoa grains. Bright green peas and soft orange carrot pieces are scattered throughout the creamy, rich sauce. The top features a golden-brown, bubbly crust of melted cheddar cheese. The casserole is naturally portioned, filling the plate. A light sprinkle of fresh, vibrant green chopped parsley provides a contrasting accent. The plate rests on a well-used, warm-toned wooden dining table. A casually placed, folded linen napkin and a simple metal fork are beside the plate. Warm, cozy kitchen lighting illuminates the scene, creating a relaxed, lived-in atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Often served with a simple green salad or crusty bread on the side.

ingredients.name: Boneless, skinless chicken breast or thigh

instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.
Melt butter in a large oven-safe pot or Dutch oven over medium heat.
Add diced onion. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Add chicken cubes. Cook for 5-7 minutes until lightly browned on all sides. The chicken will finish cooking in the oven.
Stir in quinoa, chicken broth, milk, and thyme. Bring to a simmer.
Reduce heat to low. Cover the pot. Cook for 15 minutes.
Stir in softened cream cheese until melted and smooth.
Stir in frozen peas and carrots.
Season with salt and pepper.
Sprinkle shredded cheddar cheese evenly over the top.
Bake uncovered for 20-25 minutes, or until cheese is bubbly and golden brown.
Remove from oven. Let stand 5 minutes before serving.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Chicken and Mushroom Risotto
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of creamy, free-flowing risotto is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The risotto is a warm, pale yellow hue, studded with tender, golden-brown seared chicken cubes (2cm) and sautéed earthy brown mushroom slices. Finely diced onion pieces are visible throughout the creamy rice. A vibrant sprinkle of fresh green chopped parsley garnishes the top, alongside delicate shavings of Parmesan cheese. The dish has a natural, organic arrangement, showcasing its rich texture. The plate is set on a simple wooden table, with classic silver Italian flatware (fork and spoon) placed beside it, and a folded cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish, with a softly blurred modern bistro background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread.
Pair with a light Italian white wine.
instructions: Dice chicken breast into 2cm cubes. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat 15ml olive oil in a large pot or deep pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken cubes until golden brown and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C). Remove chicken and set aside.
Add remaining 15ml olive oil and 15g butter to the same pot.
Sauté finely diced onion until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and sliced mushrooms. Cook until mushrooms are tender and browned, about 5-7 minutes.
Stir in Arborio rice. Toast rice for 2 minutes, ensuring all grains are coated.
Pour in white wine. Stir constantly until wine is fully absorbed.
Add one ladleful (about 250ml) of hot chicken broth. Stir continuously until liquid is absorbed.
Continue adding broth, one ladleful at a time. Stir constantly and wait for each addition to be absorbed before adding the next. This process takes about 20-25 minutes.
When rice is creamy and al dente, stir in cooked chicken.
Remove from heat. Stir in remaining 15g butter and grated Parmesan cheese.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve immediately. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley and extra shaved Parmesan.

recipes.recipe_name: Mexican Arroz con Pollo
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented in a shallow, matte-finished ceramic bowl on a dark wood table. The base is a vibrant, reddish-orange long-grain rice, cooked to a moist, free-flowing consistency. Two whole, golden-brown seared chicken thighs with crispy skin rest atop the rice. The chicken is not sliced. Accompanying the chicken are charred tomato wedges and small cubes of sautéed onion mixed within the grains. Garnishes include fresh, bright green cilantro leaves and thin wedges of lime placed on the side. The lighting is natural and even, highlighting the textural contrast between the crispy chicken skin and the soft rice. A linen napkin and a heavy silver fork sit beside the bowl.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas
Provide extra lime wedges for acidity
Accompany with pickled red onions
instructions: Remove stems and seeds from guajillo and arbol chilies.
Toast chilies in a dry skillet over medium heat for 2 minutes.
Soak toasted chilies in 200ml hot water for 10 minutes.
Blend soaked chilies, tomatoes, half the onion, and garlic until smooth.
Pat chicken dry and season with salt.
Heat oil in a heavy pot over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken skin-side down until golden and crispy.
Flip chicken and sear for 2 minutes then remove from pot.
Add rice and remaining onion to the pot.
Toast rice for 3 minutes until opaque and slightly golden.
Pour blended chili-tomato mixture into the rice.
Cook for 5 minutes while stirring until sauce thickens.
Add chicken stock and return chicken to the pot.
Reduce heat to low and cover with a tight lid.
Simmer for 20 minutes.
Verify chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove from heat and let rest covered for 5 minutes.
Fluff rice gently before serving.
notes: Use bone-in thighs to ensure the meat remains juicy during simmering
Do not over-toast the dried chilies as they can turn bitter
The rice should be moist and flavorful, absorbing all the chili-tomato broth

recipes.recipe_name: Spanish Braised Chicken with Saffron Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Spanish Braised Chicken is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, centrally placed on a simple wooden table. A golden-brown, seared bone-in chicken thigh rests atop tender, saffron-infused potato chunks and rustic braised tomato pieces. The potatoes display a vibrant golden hue; the tomatoes have softened into a savory, chunky sauce. Caramelized diced onions are integrated throughout. Fresh, vibrant green chopped parsley is sprinkled over the dish for contrast. The arrangement is organic and flowing. A cotton napkin, traditional fork, and knife are placed beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its warmth and inviting textures. The background shows a subtly blurred, casual restaurant setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread to soak up the sauce.
A simple green salad with a vinaigrette.
A glass of dry Spanish red wine.

ingredients.name: Potatoes (e.g., Yukon Gold or Desiree), medium
Saffron threads
ingredients.quantity: a generous pinch (approx 0.1g), steeped in 50ml hot water

instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs skin-side down until golden brown and crisp, about 6-8 minutes. Flip and sear other side for 3-4 minutes. Remove chicken.
Add diced onions to the pot. Sauté until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes.
Add minced garlic and smoked paprika. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in white wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Reduce by half, about 2-3 minutes.
Add chopped tomatoes, chicken broth, saffron with its steeping water, and potato chunks. Stir well.
Return chicken thighs to the pot, nestling them into the liquid. Bring to a simmer.
Reduce heat to low. Cover and braise for 30-40 minutes, or until chicken is cooked through (75 0C internal temperature) and potatoes are tender.
Uncover for the last 10 minutes if liquid is too thin. Adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley before serving.
