notes: Bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs yield the most flavor and stay moist.
Adjust the amount of smoked paprika to your preference for smokiness.

recipes.recipe_name: Sustainable Fish & Tomato Rice Broth
recipes.visual_description: A single individual portion of the savory broth is presented in a handcrafted ceramic bowl with a natural, unglazed finish in earth tones. The golden-hued, clear broth fills the bowl, allowing the tender, off-white short-grain rice grains to be visible at the bottom. Large, irregular chunks of flaked white fish are gently nestled within the broth. The dish is garnished minimally with small, torn pieces of creamy white fresh mozzarella, a vibrant green drizzle of basil oil, and a few fresh, deep green oregano leaves. The composition is clean and minimalistic, allowing ample negative space around the bowl. The setting features a light bamboo table surface, an undyed linen napkin in natural beige, and soft, natural lighting. The background is uncluttered, suggesting a sustainable, organic environment.

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.quantity: 2 litres for stock, plus for brine

instructions: Prepare Fermented Tomato (3-5 days in advance): Wash and dice tomatoes. Place in a clean 1-liter jar. Dissolve 15g salt in 750ml water to make a 2% brine. Pour brine over tomatoes, ensuring they are fully submerged. Loosely seal the jar. Ferment at room temperature for 3-5 days until slightly tangy and bubbly. Strain. Reserve the fermented tomato water. Roughly chop the fermented tomato solids (concassé).

Make Fish Stock: In a large pot, combine fish bones and trimmings, roughly chopped onion, celery, and crushed garlic cloves. Add 2 litres of cold water. Bring to a gentle simmer. Skim any foam. Simmer for 20-30 minutes. Strain the stock through a fine-mesh sieve. Discard solids.

Cook Rice: In a small saucepan, combine the short-grain rice with 300ml of the strained fish stock. Bring to a simmer. Cover and cook over low heat for 12-15 minutes, or until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed.

Poach Fish: Gently place fish fillets into the remaining hot fish stock. Poach for 5-8 minutes, or until fish is cooked through and flakes easily. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Carefully remove fish from stock. Flake into large, irregular chunks. Keep warm.

Prepare Basil Oil: Pick basil leaves from stems. Reserve stems. Blend basil leaves with olive oil until smooth. Strain through a fine sieve or cheesecloth to create a clear, vibrant green oil. Discard solids. (Use basil stems to infuse remaining stock if desired for extra flavor).

Assemble Soup: Combine the strained fish stock with the reserved fermented tomato water in a clean pot. Add the roughly chopped fermented tomato concassé. Bring to a gentle simmer. Season with salt and black pepper to taste. Do not boil.

Plate Dish: Ladle the hot broth into individual ceramic bowls. Add a portion of cooked rice to each bowl. Gently place the flaked fish chunks into the broth. Tear fresh mozzarella into small, irregular pieces and scatter over the soup. Garnish with a drizzle of basil oil and a few fresh oregano leaves. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Baked Cod with Mozzarella and Tomato Herb Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single modest portion of Baked Cod with Mozzarella and Tomato Herb Rice rests on an everyday, slightly off-white ceramic plate with a subtle rustic edge. A whole, moist baked cod fillet, topped with melted, slightly golden mozzarella, is placed on one side of the plate. Next to it, a generous, natural mound of vibrant red-orange tomato herb rice. The rice kernels are plump, coated in tomato, flecked with green herbs. Fresh basil leaves, torn simply, are scattered over both the fish and rice, adding fresh green contrast. The scene is set on a well-used, light-colored wooden kitchen table, showing natural grain. A simple fork and knife with classic European design are placed beside the plate. Warm, soft light from an overhead kitchen fixture illuminates the dish, creating a cozy, inviting atmosphere typical of a family meal.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and red wine vinegar.
Offer crusty artisan bread for dipping in any leftover tomato juices.
Serve alongside a glass of dry white wine or sparkling water.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Heat 1 tablespoon olive oil in a large saucepan over medium heat. Add diced onion. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and dried oregano. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in rice. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly, until lightly toasted.
Pour in diced tomatoes and 500ml vegetable broth. Bring to a simmer.
Reduce heat to low. Cover saucepan. Cook for 15-18 minutes, or until rice is tender and most liquid absorbed. Stir occasionally.
While rice cooks, pat cod fillets dry. Season both sides with salt and pepper.
Place cod fillets in a baking dish. Drizzle with remaining 1 tablespoon olive oil.
Bake cod for 12-15 minutes, or until cooked through and flakes easily. Cooking time depends on thickness.
During the last 3 minutes of baking, top each cod fillet with torn mozzarella. Return to oven until mozzarella is melted and bubbly.
Once rice is cooked, stir in dried basil and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper. Add more broth if rice is too dry.
Serve baked cod immediately with a generous portion of tomato herb rice. Garnish with fresh basil leaves.

recipes.recipe_name: Seared Turbot with Tomato Essence, Mozzarella Espuma, and Crispy Rice Wafer
recipes.visual_description: A single, refined portion of Seared Turbot with Tomato Essence, Mozzarella Espuma, and Crispy Rice Wafer is presented on a pure white, modern designer bone china plate, centered with abundant negative space. The perfectly seared turbot fillet, showcasing its moist, opaque white flesh and a delicate golden crust, is positioned slightly off-center. Adjacent to the turbot, a rich, glossy pool of deep ruby-red tomato essence creates a bold splash of color. Nestled nearby is a pristine white, ethereal cloud of buffalo mozzarella espuma, its airy texture contrasting with the solid elements. A single, irregularly shaped, golden-brown crispy risotto wafer stands upright, adding architectural height and delicate crunch. A few tiny, vibrant green micro basil leaves are precisely placed for a subtle pop of color. The composition is organic and flowing, avoiding rigid geometry. The plate rests on a luxurious white Carrara marble surface. A crisp white linen napkin, folded into a precise triangle, and elegant silver flatware are positioned to the side. Dramatic professional lighting casts soft, intentional shadows, highlighting the dish's textures. The background is ultra-minimalist, emphasizing the culinary masterpiece.
instructions: Prepare Tomato Essence: Halve San Marzano tomatoes. Toss with 1 sprig oregano and a drizzle of olive oil. Roast at 150°C for 45 minutes until softened. Blend roasted tomatoes. Pass mixture through a fine-mesh sieve or superbag. Reduce strained liquid over low heat until intensely flavored and slightly viscous. Season with salt. Whisk in a pinch of xanthan gum if desired for consistency. Keep warm.

Prepare Mozzarella Espuma: Gently warm 100 ml of vegetable stock. Add remaining fresh basil leaves. Steep for 15 minutes. Strain basil. Tear buffalo mozzarella into small pieces. Blend mozzarella with basil-infused stock and soy lecithin until very smooth. Season with salt. Pass mixture through a fine sieve into a 500 ml siphon. Charge with 2 N2O cartridges. Shake well. Keep warm in a bain-marie.

Prepare Crispy Risotto Wafers: Cook Arborio rice with remaining vegetable stock until very soft and sticky. Spread rice very thinly and evenly onto a silicone mat or parchment paper. Dehydrate in an oven at 80°C for 3-4 hours, or until completely dry and brittle. Heat neutral oil in a small pot to 180°C. Break dehydrated rice into irregular pieces. Fry pieces quickly, about 5-10 seconds, until puffed and golden. Drain on paper towels. Season lightly with salt.

Cook Turbot: Preheat oven to 180°C. Pat turbot fillets completely dry. Season generously with sea salt and white pepper. Heat 2 tablespoons of olive oil in an oven-safe, non-stick pan over medium-high heat until shimmering. Carefully place turbot fillets into the hot pan. Sear undisturbed for 3 minutes until a golden crust forms. Flip fillets. Transfer pan to the preheated oven. Cook for 5-7 minutes, or until turbot is cooked through and flakes easily. Internal temperature should reach 63°C.

Plate Dish: Warm four individual plates. Spoon a generous, artistic swipe or pool of the warm tomato essence onto each plate. Place one perfectly seared turbot fillet beside the essence. Dispense a delicate, airy cloud of mozzarella espuma next to the turbot. Gently place 1-2 crispy risotto wafers artfully on the plate for texture and height. Garnish with a few tiny micro basil leaves or a single oregano flower. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Chicken and Potato Gnocchi Stew
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of creamy chicken and potato gnocchi stew fills a deep, rustic ceramic bowl. Golden-brown seared chicken chunks are nestled among soft, pillowy gnocchi. Diced orange carrots, pale green celery, and translucent onion pieces are visible throughout the rich, light-beige sauce. The stew is topped with a sprinkle of bright green chopped fresh parsley. The bowl sits on a simple, well-worn wooden dining table. A plain, off-white ceramic plate is beneath the bowl. A metal fork and spoon rest casually beside it. A casually crumpled, light-colored cloth napkin completes the homely scene. Warm, inviting light illuminates the comforting dish.
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Add chicken cubes. Sear until golden brown on all sides. Remove chicken. Set aside.
Add diced carrots, celery, and onion to the pot. Sauté 5-7 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a simmer. Scrape up any browned bits.
Add gnocchi to the simmering broth. Cook 2-3 minutes, or until gnocchi float to the surface.
Return seared chicken to the pot. Stir in heavy cream.
Simmer 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until stew slightly thickens and chicken reaches 75°C internal temperature.
Season with salt and pepper. Adjust to taste.
Ladle stew into bowls. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Sourdough Chocolate Cake with Berry Compote
recipes.visual_description: A single elegant slice of rich, dark Sourdough Chocolate Cake rests on a matte, cream-colored ceramic plate. The cake's crumb is visibly moist and dense, with a deep, earthy brown hue. The slice is cleanly cut, revealing its uniform texture. Beside the slice, a vibrant ruby-red berry compote glistens, with some berries remaining whole or halved, showcasing their natural plumpness and varied textures. The plating is minimalistic, with ample negative space. The cake is not overly garnished, allowing its natural beauty to shine. The plate is set on a light, textured reclaimed wood surface. An undyed linen napkin in a natural beige is subtly placed nearby. Soft, diffused natural light illuminates the scene, highlighting the cake's textures and the compote's jewel-toned colors. The background is clean and uncluttered, with a hint of green from a distant plant, maintaining an eco-conscious aesthetic. The entire plate is visible, showcasing a single individual portion.

ingredients.name: Sourdough starter discard (fed, unfed, or active)

instructions: Preheat oven to 175°C. Grease and flour a 20 cm round cake pan.
Melt butter and chopped dark chocolate in a heatproof bowl set over a saucepan of simmering water. Stir until smooth. Remove from heat. Let cool slightly.
In a large bowl, whisk together granulated sugar and eggs until light and fluffy.
Stir in sourdough starter discard and milk into the egg mixture until combined.
In a separate bowl, whisk together flour, cocoa powder, baking soda, and salt.
Gradually add dry ingredients to the wet mixture, mixing until just combined. Do not overmix.
Fold in the cooled chocolate-butter mixture until no streaks remain.
Pour batter into prepared cake pan. Bake for 30-35 minutes, or until a wooden skewer inserted into the center comes out with moist crumbs.
Let cake cool in the pan for 10 minutes, then invert onto a wire rack to cool completely.
For the berry compote: Combine berries, sugar, and water in a small saucepan. Cook over medium heat, mashing berries slightly, until mixture thickens and berries break down, about 8-10 minutes.
Let compote cool. It will thicken further as it cools.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Cherry & Chocolate Tartlets
recipes.visual_description: A single round tartlet rests centered on a smooth, off-white handcrafted ceramic plate. The tartlet, approximately 10 cm in diameter, has a rustic, golden-brown sourdough discard crust with visible flakiness. Inside, a deep, glossy dark chocolate ganache fills the shell, its surface smooth and reflective. Beneath the ganache, hints of deep red, slightly translucent fermented cherry compote are visible at the edges, offering a textural contrast. The tartlet is presented with elegant simplicity, allowing its natural textures and rich colors to dominate. The plate sits on a light, reclaimed wood surface, subtly textured. Soft, diffused natural light illuminates the scene, creating gentle shadows. The background is clean and minimalist, with a hint of green from a blurred potted plant. No additional garnishes beyond the inherent beauty of the tartlet itself, emphasizing clean lines and natural elegance.
instructions: Prepare Fermented Cherry Compote: Wash and pit cherries. Combine cherries, sugar, lemon juice, and salt in a clean glass jar. Press down to release some liquid. Cover loosely with a lid or cloth. Let ferment at room temperature for 2-3 days, or until slightly bubbly and tangy. Stir daily. Refrigerate when desired tang is achieved.

Prepare Tart Shell Dough: Combine flour and salt in a bowl. Cut in cold butter until pea-sized crumbs form. Mix in sourdough discard and egg yolk. Add ice water, 5 ml at a time, until dough just comes together. Do not overmix. Form into a disc. Wrap in cling film. Chill for 30 minutes.

Bake Tart Shells: Preheat oven to 180°C. Roll dough thinly on a floured surface. Cut out four circles to fit 10 cm tartlet molds. Press dough into molds. Trim edges. Prick bottoms with a fork. Line with parchment paper and fill with baking weights. Bake for 15 minutes. Remove weights and parchment. Bake for 5-7 more minutes until golden. Cool completely on a wire rack.

Prepare Dark Chocolate Ganache: Place chopped chocolate in a heatproof bowl. Heat cream and butter in a small saucepan until simmering. Pour hot cream mixture over chocolate. Let stand for 1 minute. Stir gently from the center outwards until smooth and glossy.
Assemble Tartlets: Spoon a layer of fermented cherry compote into each cooled tart shell. Pour chocolate ganache over the compote, filling the tart shell. Gently tap to settle.
Chill and Serve: Refrigerate tartlets for at least 1 hour, or until ganache is set. Serve chilled.
notes: Sourdough discard adds a subtle tang and utilizes a common kitchen byproduct, promoting zero-waste.
Fermenting cherries enhances flavor complexity and acts as a natural preservation method, ideal for seasonal produce.
This recipe emphasizes minimal processing and natural ingredients for an eco-conscious dessert.

recipes.recipe_name: Beer-Braised Chicken with Mushrooms and Tomatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Beer-Braised Chicken with Mushrooms and Tomatoes is presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate. A generously sized, bone-in, skin-on chicken thigh, perfectly seared to a deep golden-brown, rests centrally. The chicken is surrounded by quartered cremini mushrooms, deeply caramelized, and vibrant whole green beans, cooked tender-crisp. Scattered among them are plump, burst cherry tomatoes, their red hues contrasting with the earthy tones. A rich, glossy, beer-infused sauce pools elegantly around the ingredients, clinging to the chicken and vegetables. The arrangement is natural and inviting, with moderate negative space. The dish sits on a simple light wooden table. A folded linen napkin and classic silver flatware are placed beside the plate. Natural, even lighting highlights the textures and colors, creating a professional yet approachable image.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with Spätzle or hearty mashed potatoes
Accompany with crusty rye bread to sop up the sauce
Pair with a glass of German lager or dark beer
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.

Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven or oven-safe pot over medium-high heat. Sear chicken thighs, skin-side down, until deeply golden brown and crisp, about 8-10 minutes. Flip and sear other side for 2-3 minutes. Remove chicken and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add butter to the pot. Add diced onion and cook until softened, about 5 minutes. Add quartered mushrooms and cook until browned, about 7-10 minutes.
Stir in minced garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant. Sprinkle flour over vegetables and stir for 1 minute to cook raw flour taste.
Pour in beer, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Bring to a simmer. Add chicken broth, thyme sprigs, and bay leaf. Season with salt and pepper.
Return chicken thighs to the pot, skin-side up. Ensure chicken is partially submerged in the liquid. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Cover the pot and transfer to a preheated oven at 180°C (350°F). Braise for 30 minutes.

Remove pot from oven. Stir in cherry tomatoes and green beans. Return to oven, uncovered, and braise for another 15-20 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) and vegetables are tender-crisp.
Remove thyme sprigs and bay leaf. Check seasoning and adjust if needed.
Serve hot, garnished with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Курица с томатным рисом и шафраном
recipes.visual_description: Блюдо подается на круглой белой фарфоровой тарелке, демонстрируя яркие цвета и текстуры. В центре тарелки находится небольшая порция насыщенного красно-оранжевого томатного риса, приготовленного до идеальной, слегка текучей консистенции. Поверх риса аккуратно выложены несколько золотисто-коричневых кусочков пассерованной курицы. Курица нарезана плотными, неправильными кусочками, демонстрируя сочную текстуру. Сверху блюдо украшено несколькими свежими, ярко-зелеными листьями базилика, добавляющими контраст и свежесть. Вокруг риса – чистое пространство тарелки. Стол – простой деревянный или ламинированный. Рядом с тарелкой – серебряные столовые приборы и сложенная хлопковая салфетка. Освещение естественное, равномерное, подчеркивающее свежесть ингредиентов.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Подавать немедленно
Сочетается со свежим хрустящим хлебом
instructions: Нарежьте лук мелким кубиком. Измельчите чеснок. Куриное филе нарежьте кусочками 2-3 см.
Разогрейте оливковое масло в большой сковороде на среднем огне. Добавьте кусочки курицы. Обжаривайте до золотисто-коричневой корочки со всех сторон. Выньте курицу. Отложите в сторону.
В ту же сковороду добавьте нарезанный лук. Пассеруйте 3-4 минуты до мягкости. Добавьте измельченный чеснок. Готовьте еще 1 минуту до появления аромата.
Добавьте рис в сковороду. Помешивайте 1 минуту, чтобы слегка обжарить.
Влейте измельченные томаты. Хорошо перемешайте.
Добавьте нити шафрана вместе с жидкостью, в которой они замачивались. Перемешайте.

Постепенно добавляйте теплый куриный бульон, по одному половнику за раз. Постоянно помешивайте. Дайте каждой порции впитаться, прежде чем добавлять следующую. Готовьте рис 15-18 минут до состояния аль денте.
Верните кусочки курицы в сковороду на последние 5 минут приготовления риса. Убедитесь, что внутренняя температура курицы достигла 75°C.
Снимите сковороду с огня. Вмешайте тертый Пармезан, если используете. Приправьте солью и перцем.
Дайте блюду постоять 2 минуты.
notes: Для лучшего вкуса используйте высококачественные консервированные томаты
Проверьте готовность курицы

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Potato & Onion Fritters with Savory Chili Jam
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of two perfectly golden-brown, rustic Fermented Potato & Onion Fritters rests on a handcrafted, matte cream ceramic plate. The fritters are irregularly shaped, showcasing the natural texture of the finely diced fermented potato and onion. Their surfaces are subtly crisp, a rich golden-brown from pan-frying. A generous, glossy dollop of deep red Savory Chili Jam sits beside the fritters, its smooth texture contrasting with the fritters' rougher exterior. The jam has a slight sheen, indicating its sweet and savory depth. Scattered around the plate, providing a touch of green, are a few small sprigs of fresh chives or flat-leaf parsley, and a few delicate, golden-brown crispy potato peels, adding a textural counterpoint and emphasizing the zero-waste ethos. The plating is minimalist and clean, allowing ample negative space on the plate. The entire dish is centered on a light, natural reclaimed wood table surface. Undyed linen napkins in a natural beige tone are subtly visible. Soft, diffused natural light illuminates the scene, enhancing the earthy color palette of the food and ceramics. The background is clean and uncluttered, with a hint of green from a distant plant, reinforcing the sustainable theme. The composition is unforced, highlighting the intrinsic beauty of the ingredients.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple side salad of seasonal greens.
Serve with a fermented vegetable slaw.
instructions: Prepare Fermented Potato & Onion:
Combine 500ml non-chlorinated water and 15g sea salt. Stir until salt dissolves. This is your brine.
Place 1 cm cubed potatoes, finely diced onions, 2 smashed garlic cloves, and 1 bay leaf (if using) in a clean glass jar.
Pour brine over vegetables. Ensure vegetables are fully submerged. Use a fermentation weight if needed.
Cover jar with an airlock lid or burp daily.
Ferment at room temperature (18-24°C) for 7-10 days. Taste for desired tanginess.
Store in refrigerator once fermented.
Prepare Savory Chili Jam:
Heat 5ml vegetable oil in a small saucepan over medium heat.
Add roughly chopped red chilies, roughly chopped red onion, 2 peeled garlic cloves, and grated ginger. Sauté 5 minutes until softened.
Add apple cider vinegar, maple syrup, soy sauce, 60ml water, and 2g salt.
Bring to a simmer. Cook 15-20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until mixture thickens.
Remove from heat. Blend with an immersion blender until smooth or chunky as desired.
Cool completely. Store in refrigerator.
Prepare Fritters:
Drain 600g fermented potato and onion mixture well. Pat dry with paper towels to remove excess moisture.
In a large bowl, combine drained fermented mixture, chickpea flour, nutritional yeast, finely chopped chives, and black pepper. Mix thoroughly until just combined. Do not overmix.
Form mixture into 8-10 small patties, about 1.5 cm thick.
Heat 60ml vegetable oil in a large non-stick pan over medium-high heat.
Carefully place fritters in hot oil. Do not overcrowd the pan.
Cook 4-5 minutes per side, until golden brown and crispy.
Transfer cooked fritters to a wire rack lined with paper towels to drain excess oil.
Prepare Potato Peel Crisps (Optional):
Preheat oven to 180°C (350°F).
Toss potato peels with 5ml olive oil and salt.
Spread in a single layer on a baking sheet.
Bake 15-20 minutes, or until crispy and golden. Watch carefully to prevent burning.
Serve:
Serve hot fritters with a generous dollop of savory chili jam. Garnish with potato peel crisps if desired.
notes: Ensure all equipment is clean and sanitized for fermentation.
Adjust chili jam spice level by varying chili type and quantity.
This recipe utilizes food scraps like potato peels and chili stems/seeds, contributing to a zero-waste kitchen.
The fermentation process adds complex flavor and aids digestion.

recipes.recipe_name: Arancini al Pollo e Pomodoro
recipes.visual_description: Four golden-brown arancini are elegantly arranged on a clean, round white porcelain plate, slightly off-center. Each arancino, about 6 cm in diameter, boasts a perfectly crispy, textured breadcrumb exterior. One is gently cut in half, revealing its creamy, saffron-hued Arborio rice interior, studded with melted white mozzarella and a rich, red chicken and tomato filling. The diced chicken pieces are visible within the vibrant tomato sauce. A small, artful swirl of bright red, smooth tomato passata is spooned beside the arancini. Fresh green basil leaves are scattered thoughtfully over the sauce and arancini for a pop of color. The plate rests on a simple light wooden table, accompanied by classic silver flatware and a folded white cotton napkin. Natural, soft lighting highlights the arancini's golden crispness, creating an inviting bistro atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve as an antipasto (starter) alongside other small bites.
Offer with a side of simple marinara or warmed tomato passata for dipping.
Traditionally served in Southern Italy, especially Sicily.

ingredients.name: Boneless, skinless chicken breast, diced into 1 cm cubes

instructions: Heat 15 ml olive oil in a small pan over medium heat. Add diced chicken. Cook until lightly browned, about 4-5 minutes. Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant. Pour in tomato passata. Season with salt and pepper. Simmer 10-12 minutes, or until chicken is cooked through (75°C internal temperature) and sauce thickens slightly. Stir in chopped basil. Set aside to cool.

Heat 30 ml olive oil in a medium saucepan over medium heat. Add diced onion. Cook until translucent, about 5 minutes. Add Arborio rice. Stir constantly for 2 minutes until rice grains are translucent at edges. Pour in white wine, if using. Stir until evaporated.

Add warmed chicken broth, one ladleful at a time, stirring continuously. Wait until liquid is almost absorbed before adding next ladle. Continue until rice is creamy and al dente, about 18-20 minutes.
Remove from heat. Stir in butter and Parmesan cheese. Season with salt. Spread risotto onto a baking sheet. Let it cool completely. This helps it firm up for forming.

Take a small amount of cooled risotto (about 60-70g). Flatten it in your palm. Place 1-2 cubes of mozzarella and a teaspoon of chicken-tomato filling in the center. Carefully mold the risotto around the filling to form a compact ball, about 5-6 cm in diameter. Ensure no filling is exposed. Repeat for all arancini.

Set up three shallow dishes: one with flour, one with beaten eggs, one with breadcrumbs. Roll each arancino first in flour, then dip in egg, then coat thoroughly in breadcrumbs. Press gently to ensure crumbs adhere.

Heat vegetable oil in a deep pot or Dutch oven to 175°C. Carefully lower 2-3 arancini into hot oil. Fry for 5-7 minutes, turning occasionally, until golden brown and crispy. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove arancini with a slotted spoon. Place on a wire rack lined with paper towels to drain excess oil.
Serve hot with a side of warmed tomato passata or marinara sauce for dipping. Garnish with fresh basil.
notes: Ensure risotto is completely cooled before forming balls; this prevents them from falling apart during frying.
Do not overcrowd the fryer to maintain oil temperature and ensure even cooking.

recipes.recipe_name: Arroz con Pollo
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Arroz con Pollo presented on a clean white porcelain plate. Two whole, bone-in chicken thighs with deeply browned, crispy skin sit atop a bed of golden, saffron-stained rice. The rice grains are plump and distinct, interspersed with fine bits of softened onion and concentrated red tomato. The dish shows vibrant yellow and orange hues from the saffron and paprika. A generous sprinkle of bright green, finely chopped parsley is scattered over the top. A single lemon wedge is placed neatly on the side. The plate sits on a light oak wooden table with a folded white cotton napkin. Lighting is bright, natural, and even, highlighting the textures of the crispy skin and the moist rice grains.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of Alioli (garlic mayonnaise)
Accompany with crusty bread and a glass of chilled white wine
Present in a traditional terracotta cazuela for family-style dining
instructions: Season chicken thighs with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a wide shallow pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken skin-side down until golden and crispy.
Flip and brown the other side. Remove chicken from pan.
Add onion to the same pan. Sauté until translucent.
Stir in garlic and grated tomato. Cook until liquid evaporates and mixture darkens.
Add smoked paprika and rice. Stir to coat rice in oil for 2 minutes.
Pour in white wine. Deglaze the pan. Simmer until wine reduces by half.
Add hot stock and saffron. Stir once to distribute.
Place chicken thighs back into the pan on top of the rice.
Simmer undisturbed over medium-low heat for 18-20 minutes.
Ensure chicken reaches internal temperature of 75°C.
Remove from heat. Cover with a clean cloth. Rest for 5 minutes.
Garnish with fresh parsley before serving.
notes: Do not stir the rice once the stock is added to allow a crust to form on the bottom.
Use a wide pan to ensure even rice cooking.

recipes.recipe_name: Mocha Fudge Brownies
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of two thick, dark chocolate brownie squares rests on an off-white, everyday ceramic plate. The brownies are rich, deep brown, with a slightly crinkled, shiny top crust that hints at a fudgy interior. A light dusting of powdered sugar subtly graces the top. The plate is casually placed on a well-worn, light wooden dining table. A simple, folded cloth napkin, perhaps in a muted check pattern, sits beside the plate. Warm, inviting light from a kitchen fixture illuminates the scene, creating a cozy, lived-in atmosphere. The background is minimal, showing just a hint of a comfortable family kitchen setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve warm with a scoop of vanilla ice cream.
Serve with a dollop of whipped cream.
Enjoy with a glass of cold milk or a cup of hot coffee.
instructions: Preheat oven to 175°C. Line a 20x20 cm square baking pan with parchment paper.
Melt chopped dark chocolate and butter in a heatproof bowl over a saucepan of simmering water or in a microwave. Stir until smooth. Remove from heat.
In a small bowl, dissolve instant coffee powder in 15ml hot water. Stir into the melted chocolate mixture.
In a separate large bowl, whisk eggs and granulated sugar until light and fluffy, about 2 minutes.
Pour the cooled chocolate mixture into the egg mixture. Add vanilla extract. Stir until just combined.
In a small bowl, whisk together all-purpose flour, unsweetened cocoa powder, and salt.
Add dry ingredients to the wet ingredients. Fold gently with a spatula until just combined. Do not overmix.
Pour batter into the prepared baking pan. Spread evenly.
Bake for 25-30 minutes, or until a toothpick inserted into the center comes out with moist crumbs, not wet batter.
Cool completely in the pan on a wire rack before cutting into thick squares.
notes: Do not overbake the brownies; they should be slightly undercooked in the center for a fudgy texture.
Ensure chocolate mixture is not too hot when adding to eggs to prevent scrambling.

recipes.recipe_name: Mediterranean Roasted Chicken with Fig-Tomato Salsa and Herb Orzo
recipes.visual_description: The dish features golden-brown roasted chicken thighs, cooked to perfection, showcasing crispy skin and tender meat. The chicken is positioned as a whole piece on a clean white porcelain plate. Alongside, a generous mound of light green herb orzo pasta, flecked with bright green chopped parsley and dill, appears moist and loosely arranged. Scattered around and on top of the chicken is a vibrant fig-tomato salsa, featuring small, irregular diced pieces of red tomato, purple-skinned figs, finely minced red onion, and crisp green cucumber, creating a fresh, colorful contrast. A light drizzle of olive oil glistens over the components. The overall composition is balanced with moderate negative space. The plate rests on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by a folded white cotton napkin and standard silver flatware. Natural, even lighting highlights the textures and colors of the ingredients, creating an inviting, casual dining atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with fresh crusty bread for dipping in pan juices or salsa.
A simple green salad with lemon-oregano dressing would also complement the meal.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt, black pepper, and dried oregano.
Preheat oven to 200°C. Place chicken on a baking tray. Roast for 30-40 minutes until internal temperature reaches 75°C and skin is golden and crisp.
While chicken roasts, cook orzo. Boil a pot of salted water. Add orzo and cook according to package directions until al dente. Drain well.
Prepare fig-tomato salsa. Dice cherry tomatoes, red onion, fresh figs, and cucumber into small, irregular pieces. Mince garlic.
In a bowl, combine diced tomatoes, red onion, figs, cucumber, and minced garlic. Drizzle with olive oil and red wine vinegar. Season with salt and black pepper. Stir gently to combine.
Prepare herb orzo. In a separate bowl, toss cooked orzo with finely chopped fresh parsley and dill. Drizzle with olive oil and a squeeze of fresh lemon juice. Season with salt and black pepper.
To plate, place a generous portion of herb orzo on each plate. Arrange a roasted chicken thigh beside the orzo. Spoon the fig-tomato salsa over the chicken or alongside.
Serve immediately with slices of crusty bread.

recipes.recipe_name: Lemon Herb Roasted Chicken with Crispy Potatoes and Feta
recipes.visual_description: A single golden-brown roasted chicken thigh, skin crispy and glistening, rests prominently on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. Beside it, a generous portion of roasted potato wedges, their skins golden and slightly charred, interiors fluffy. Bright white crumbled feta cheese is scattered over the chicken and potatoes, creating a striking contrast. Thin, vibrant green fresh parsley is sprinkled as a garnish. A few charred lemon wedges are placed near the chicken. The composition is organized yet organic, with ample negative space around the elements. The plate sits on a simple light wooden table. A folded cotton napkin and standard restaurant flatware are placed to the side. Natural, even light illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and rich colors. The background suggests a casual bistro atmosphere, maintaining focus on the food.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple horiatiki (Greek salad)
Offer with a side of tzatziki sauce
Accompany with crusty bread for dipping

ingredients.name: Potatoes (small, waxy like new potatoes or Yukon Gold)

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Pat chicken thighs dry with paper towels.
Cut potatoes into 3-4 cm wedges.
Mince garlic cloves.
In a large bowl, combine chicken thighs, potato wedges, 30ml olive oil, minced garlic, dried oregano, dried thyme, salt, pepper, and red pepper flakes (if using). Toss to coat all ingredients evenly.
Arrange chicken and potatoes in a single layer on a large baking sheet. Ensure chicken skin is facing up for crisping.
Roast for 30 minutes.
Remove baking sheet from oven. Squeeze juice from half of the lemon over chicken and potatoes. Add the remaining lemon half, cut into wedges, to the pan.
Return to oven. Roast for another 20-30 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C and potatoes are tender and crispy.
Remove from oven. Let the chicken and potatoes rest on the baking sheet for 5 minutes.
Serve immediately. Crumble feta cheese generously over each chicken thigh and potato portion. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches 75°C internal temperature for food safety.
For crispier potatoes, avoid overcrowding the baking sheet; use two sheets if necessary.

recipes.recipe_name: Veal Massaman Curry with Broccoli Rabe and Mushrooms
recipes.visual_description: A rich, aromatic Veal Massaman Curry, presented in a deep, rustic ceramic bowl. Tender 3-4 cm cubes of slow-simmered veal are nestled within the creamy, reddish-brown curry sauce. Vibrant 5 cm pieces of broccoli rabe and thick slices of earthy mushrooms are generously distributed throughout the dish, offering contrasting textures and colors. The curry's surface shimmers, indicating its luscious consistency. Beside the main bowl, a neatly mounded portion of fluffy white jasmine rice sits in a smaller, simple porcelain bowl. The dish is garnished with thinly sliced bright green spring onions and a fresh lemon wedge, providing a pop of color and freshness. The setting features a natural wooden table, with a traditional Thai-style soup spoon resting alongside the main bowl. Natural, warm lighting illuminates the scene, highlighting the dish's inviting appeal.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with steamed jasmine rice.
Offer a side of prik nam pla (fish sauce with chilies and lime) for those who prefer more spice.
Eaten with a spoon and fork, or primarily a spoon for the curry.
instructions: Cut veal into 3-4 cm cubes. Season with salt.
Wash broccoli rabe. Trim tough ends. Cut into 5 cm pieces.
Clean mushrooms. Slice thick.
Mince garlic. Thinly slice green onions. Cut lemon into wedges.
Cook jasmine rice according to package directions. Keep warm.
Heat vegetable oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear veal cubes in batches until browned on all sides. Remove veal from pot. Set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add minced garlic to the pot. Sauté 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add Massaman curry paste. Stir-fry paste 2 minutes until aromatic.
Pour in coconut milk. Stir to combine with paste. Bring to a simmer.
Add fish sauce and palm sugar. Stir until sugar dissolves.
Return seared veal to the pot. Bring to a gentle simmer. Cover and cook 60-75 minutes, or until veal is fork-tender. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F).
Add broccoli rabe and sliced mushrooms to the curry. Cook 5-7 minutes, until vegetables are tender-crisp.
Taste and adjust seasoning if needed. Add more fish sauce or palm sugar to balance flavor.
Ladle curry into serving bowls. Garnish with thinly sliced green onions and a lemon wedge. Serve immediately with jasmine rice.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Potato & Onion Fry
recipes.visual_description: A generous, rustic portion of "Spicy Potato & Onion Fry" is served on a round, earthy terracotta plate. The cubed potatoes, approximately 2 cm, are golden-brown with slightly crisped edges from frying, showcasing their tender interior. Interspersed among the potatoes are soft, caramelized slivers of onion and vibrant green chilies. The dish has a warm, inviting palette of yellows, oranges, and browns from the spices, with fresh green specks of chopped coriander scattered over. The texture is a mix of soft potato and onion with a slight outer crisp. The plate is placed on a well-used wooden dining table, with a simple ceramic bowl of plain yogurt and a stack of warm, round roti bread on the side. A cloth napkin is casually draped nearby. The scene is bathed in warm, natural kitchen light, evoking a comforting family meal.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm roti or plain basmati rice.
Accompany with a side of plain yogurt or a simple raita.
instructions: Wash and peel potatoes. Cut into 2 cm cubes.
Heat 3 tablespoons oil in a large heavy-bottomed pan or wok over medium heat.
Add 1 teaspoon cumin seeds. Let them splutter.
Add sliced onions. Sauté until light golden brown.
Add minced garlic, grated ginger, and slit green chilies. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add 0.5 teaspoon turmeric powder, 1 teaspoon coriander powder, and 0.5 teaspoon red chili powder. Stir well for 30 seconds.
Add potato cubes. Mix thoroughly to coat with spices.
Add salt to taste. Stir.
Cover the pan. Cook on low heat for 15-20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until potatoes are tender.
Remove lid. Increase heat to medium-high. Cook for another 5-7 minutes, stirring, until potatoes are lightly browned and crisp at edges.
Stir in 0.5 teaspoon amchur powder.
Garnish with fresh chopped coriander leaves. Serve hot.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Tomato and Cucumber Salad
recipes.visual_description: The salad is presented in a handcrafted, matte cream ceramic bowl, set against a light, reclaimed wood surface. Vibrant halved fermented cherry tomatoes, their skins slightly softened and deepened in color, are gently mixed with thinly sliced crisp cucumber and finely diced orange bell pepper. Scattered amongst these are plump, cooked chickpeas, providing a subtle contrast in texture and color. The components are lightly tossed with a clear, herb-flecked vinaigrette, ensuring each piece glistens. The dish rests on a bed of fresh, vibrant arugula. Garnish includes delicate fresh dill sprigs and a few finely julienned cucumber peels, adding a touch of natural green. The overall presentation is minimalistic and clean, highlighting the natural beauty and fresh colors of the ingredients, with ample negative space. A natural beige linen napkin and a simple, unadorned ceramic spoon complete the eco-conscious setting under soft, diffused natural light.

ingredients.name: Bell pepper trimmings (cores, seeds, inner white bits)

instructions: Prepare fermented tomatoes: Halve cherry tomatoes. Dissolve 10 g sea salt in 250 ml water to make a brine. Place halved tomatoes in a clean jar. Pour brine over tomatoes, ensuring they are fully submerged. Seal jar loosely. Ferment at room temperature for 2-3 days, or until slightly tangy and bubbly. Refrigerate once desired tang is reached.
Make bell pepper infused oil: Gently heat olive oil with bell pepper trimmings in a small saucepan over low heat for 10 minutes. Do not brown. Strain oil and discard trimmings. Let cool.
Prepare vegetables: Thinly slice or dice cucumber. Dice bell pepper into small cubes. Rinse and drain cooked chickpeas.

Prepare dressing: In a small bowl, whisk together infused olive oil, white wine vinegar, Dijon mustard, minced garlic, chopped fresh dill, and chopped fresh parsley. Season with salt and black pepper. Add 15-30 ml of the fermented tomato brine for extra flavor and probiotics.
Assemble salad: In a large bowl, gently combine the fermented tomatoes, sliced cucumber, diced bell pepper, and chickpeas. Pour dressing over ingredients and toss gently to coat.
Serve: Arrange fresh arugula or mixed greens on individual plates. Spoon the salad mixture over the greens. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Mughlai Chicken Korma with Potato and Dried Fruits
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant Mughlai Chicken Korma is presented in a shallow, matte white ceramic bowl. The rich, creamy golden-brown curry, studded with tender chunks of chicken, small diced potatoes, and bright green peas, glistens under natural light. A light sprinkle of fresh chopped parsley garnishes the top, adding a fresh contrast. Beside the bowl, on a simple wooden table, sits a small white ramekin of cool, white cucumber-dill raita, flecked with green. A piece of warm, slightly charred naan bread is folded neatly next to the bowl. A small, elegant glass bowl holds a few thin slices of fresh banana. The overall presentation is clean and inviting, with moderate negative space, highlighting the dish as the centerpiece. Ingredients are cooked until tender, maintaining their distinct colors and textures. The chicken pieces are whole, not fanned.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm naan bread or basmati rice.
Accompany with cucumber raita to balance the richness.
Offer fresh banana slices as a sweet palate cleanser.
instructions: Cut chicken thighs into 3cm chunks. Finely chop onions. Mince garlic. Grate ginger. Puree tomatoes. Peel and dice potatoes into 2cm cubes. Chop dried figs. Grind walnuts.
Heat 2 tablespoons vegetable oil and 20g butter in a large pot over medium heat. Add chopped onions. Sauté until golden brown, about 8-10 minutes.
Add minced garlic and grated ginger. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in turmeric powder, cumin powder, coriander powder, red chili powder (optional), and 1/2 teaspoon black pepper. Cook for 30 seconds, tempering spices.
Add pureed tomatoes and ketchup. Cook until the oil separates, about 5-7 minutes.
Add chicken chunks. Sear on all sides until lightly browned. Stir in salt to taste.
Whisk yogurt until smooth. Gradually add whisked yogurt to the pot, stirring constantly to prevent curdling. Bring to a gentle simmer.

Add diced potatoes, ground walnuts, chopped figs, and raisins. Stir in cocoa powder. Cover and simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until chicken is cooked through (internal temperature 75°C) and potatoes are tender. Stir occasionally.
Stir in green peas and remaining 30g butter. Cook for another 3-5 minutes until peas are tender. Stir in garam masala.
For Cucumber-Dill Raita: Grate cucumber. Chop fresh dill. Combine grated cucumber, chopped dill, 200g plain yogurt, a pinch of salt, and a pinch of black pepper in a small bowl. Mix well.
For Carrot-Cabbage Slaw: Shred carrot and green cabbage. Combine in a bowl. Season lightly with salt.
Hard-boil eggs. Peel and halve them.
Slice banana into thin rounds.
Serve hot korma garnished with fresh chopped parsley. Serve with raita, slaw, hard-boiled egg halves, sliced banana, and warm naan bread or rice.

recipes.recipe_name: Tuscan Herb Chicken and Potato Gratin
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Tuscan Herb Chicken and Potato Gratin is presented centrally on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. The gratin features a rich, golden-brown crust from the baked Parmesan and melted mozzarella, with visible creamy, tender potato slices peeking out from the sides. Seared chicken medallions, cut into thick chunks, are nestled within the layers, their slightly browned edges visible. Freshly torn vibrant green basil leaves are scattered generously over the top, providing a pop of color and freshness. The dish's textures range from the crispy top to the soft, creamy interior. The plate is placed on a simple wooden table surface, suggesting a modern bistro setting. A neatly folded white cotton napkin is positioned beside the plate. Standard European flatware is arranged to the side. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's warmth and inviting textures. The entire plate is visible, with moderate negative space around the gratin, ensuring a professional yet approachable presentation.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple green salad dressed with a light vinaigrette.
Accompany with crusty artisanal bread for dipping in the creamy sauce.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C. Lightly grease a 23x33 cm baking dish.
Slice potatoes thinly, about 3mm thick. Slice onion thinly. Mince garlic.
Cut each chicken breast into 2-3 thick medallions or chunks. Season chicken with salt and pepper.

Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken medallions for 2-3 minutes per side until golden brown. Do not cook through. Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add remaining 15 ml olive oil and butter to the skillet. Add sliced onions. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened and translucent.
Add minced garlic and dried oregano. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in chicken stock and heavy cream. Bring to a gentle simmer. Season with salt and pepper. Remove from heat.
Arrange a layer of sliced potatoes in the prepared baking dish. Top with half of the seared chicken medallions and half of the sliced onions.
Sprinkle with half of the shredded mozzarella. Pour half of the cream sauce over the layers.
Repeat the layers: remaining potatoes, remaining chicken, remaining onions, remaining mozzarella. Pour remaining cream sauce over the top.
Sprinkle grated Parmesan cheese over the entire gratin.
Cover baking dish with foil. Bake for 40 minutes.
Remove foil. Continue baking for 20-25 minutes, or until potatoes are tender and top is golden brown and bubbly. Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
Tear fresh basil leaves. Sprinkle generously over the hot gratin before serving. Let gratin rest for 10 minutes before serving.
notes: Slice potatoes uniformly thin for even cooking.
Do not overcrowd the baking dish to ensure proper bubbling and browning.

recipes.recipe_name: Spanish Garlic Chicken
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Spanish Garlic Chicken is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. Two golden-brown, pan-seared bone-in chicken thighs are arranged centrally, their skin crisp and glistening. A rich, glossy, light amber garlic sauce pools around the chicken, studded with tender, slightly translucent slices of garlic. Freshly chopped vibrant green parsley is generously scattered over the chicken and sauce, adding a burst of color. A bright yellow lemon wedge sits beside the chicken, ready to be squeezed. The overall presentation is clean and inviting, with moderate negative space. The dish is set on a simple light wooden table surface, accompanied by a folded white cotton napkin and a small side of crusty artisan bread for dipping. Lighting is natural and even, creating a warm, inviting casual bistro atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread to sop up the garlic sauce.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season chicken with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs skin-side down until golden and crisp, about 8-10 minutes.
Flip chicken. Cook for 5 minutes. Remove chicken from skillet.
Reduce heat to medium. Add sliced garlic to skillet. Sauté until fragrant, about 2 minutes. Do not brown.
Pour in white wine. Scrape up browned bits from bottom of skillet. Simmer for 2 minutes.
Add chicken stock, bay leaf, and red pepper flakes. Bring to a simmer.
Return chicken to skillet. Cover. Reduce heat to low. Simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until chicken reaches 75°C internal temperature.
Remove bay leaf. Stir in lemon juice and most of the fresh parsley.
Serve hot. Garnish with remaining fresh parsley and lemon wedges.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Tomato and Caramelized Onion Tagliatelle
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, centrally placed on a simple light wooden table surface. A single individual portion of al dente tagliatelle forms a neat nest, allowing the vibrant roasted cherry tomatoes, some beautifully burst, and deep amber caramelized onion strands to peek through. The pasta strands are coated in a light, glossy sauce, showcasing a natural color palette of reds, oranges, and golden browns. Coarse, golden-brown garlic breadcrumbs are sprinkled generously over the top, providing a textural contrast. Large, delicate shavings of pale yellow Parmigiano Reggiano are scattered artistically over the pasta, catching the light. Fresh, bright green basil leaves are scattered for a pop of color and freshness. The composition is balanced, with moderate negative space. A cotton napkin is folded neatly beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, emphasizing its rustic elegance. Traditional European flatware is placed alongside.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of crusty bread.
Pair with a light red wine or sparkling water.
Finish with a drizzle of high-quality extra virgin olive oil.
instructions: Slice red onions thinly. Heat 30ml olive oil in a large pan over medium-low heat. Add onions. Cook slowly for 25-30 minutes until deeply caramelized and tender. Stir occasionally. Add 15ml red wine vinegar during the last 5 minutes. Set aside.

Preheat oven to 200°C. Halve cherry tomatoes. Toss with 15ml olive oil, 2 minced garlic cloves, salt, pepper, and red pepper flakes. Spread on a baking sheet. Roast for 20-25 minutes until softened and slightly burst.

Pulse stale bread pieces in a food processor until coarse crumbs form. Heat 15ml olive oil in a small pan over medium heat. Add 2 minced garlic cloves. Cook for 30 seconds until fragrant. Add breadcrumbs. Toast, stirring frequently, for 5-7 minutes until golden and crispy. Season with a pinch of salt. Set aside.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a rolling boil. Add tagliatelle. Cook according to package directions until al dente. Reserve 250ml pasta cooking water before draining.
Add roasted tomatoes and caramelized onions to the large pan. Gently mash some tomatoes with the back of a spoon. Add 125ml reserved pasta water. Simmer gently for 2 minutes.

Add drained tagliatelle to the sauce pan. Add remaining 125ml pasta water, if needed, to achieve desired consistency. Toss well to coat. Add most of the grated Parmigiano Reggiano and roughly torn basil. Toss again.
Divide pasta among four warm plates. Garnish each serving generously with crispy garlic breadcrumbs and shaved Parmigiano Reggiano. Drizzle with extra virgin olive oil.

recipes.recipe_name: Octopus and Olive Ragout with Pappardelle and Creamy Polenta
recipes.visual_description: The dish is plated on an everyday, off-white ceramic plate, resting on a well-used wooden dining table. A generous portion of golden pappardelle pasta is gently tossed with a rich, rustic octopus and olive ragout. The ragout, a deep reddish-brown, features tender, 2-3 cm diced octopus chunks and halved dark Kalamata olives. The pasta is al dente, coated in the savory sauce. Beside the pasta, a modest scoop of creamy, pale yellow polenta showcases its smooth texture. The dish is casually garnished with fresh chopped vibrant green flat-leaf parsley and a light dusting of grated Parmesan cheese. The setting is a homely family kitchen, with warm, cozy lighting from overhead fixtures. A simple cloth napkin and standard flatware are casually placed. The background is minimal, hinting at a lived-in atmosphere, making the comforting food the focal point.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread for dipping.

ingredients.name: Parmesan cheese
ingredients.quantity: 50 g, grated, plus extra for serving

instructions: Prepare Octopus: Place octopus in a large pot. Cover with cold water. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat. Simmer for 45-60 minutes until very tender. Drain. Let cool slightly. Dice octopus into 2-3 cm chunks.
Start Ragout: Heat 2 tablespoons olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium heat. Add diced onion. Cook 5-7 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Build Flavor: Add diced octopus. Cook 2 minutes. Pour in red wine, if using. Simmer 3 minutes until reduced by half. Stir in crushed tomatoes, vegetable broth, halved olives, and dried lavender.
Simmer Ragout: Bring to a gentle simmer. Reduce heat to low. Cover. Cook 30-40 minutes, stirring occasionally, until flavors meld and sauce thickens slightly. Season with salt and black pepper.

Cook Polenta: Bring 750 ml water and 1/2 teaspoon salt to a boil in a medium saucepan. Slowly whisk in polenta. Reduce heat to low. Cook 5-7 minutes, stirring constantly, until thick and creamy. Stir in butter and grated Parmesan.
Cook Pasta: While ragout simmers, cook pappardelle according to package directions in salted boiling water until al dente. Drain, reserving 120 ml pasta water.
Combine Pasta and Ragout: Add drained pasta to the ragout. Add a splash of reserved pasta water if needed to loosen sauce. Toss gently to combine.
Serve: Divide pasta and ragout among four shallow bowls. Serve creamy polenta alongside or in separate small bowls. Garnish generously with fresh chopped parsley and extra grated Parmesan.
notes: Ensure octopus is cooked until very tender for the best texture.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Tuscan Chicken Pasta
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Creamy Tuscan Chicken Pasta is artfully plated on a round, clean white porcelain dinner plate. The creamy fettuccine, intertwined with golden-brown chicken chunks and vibrant green spinach, forms a neat mound in the center. Interspersed are deep red sun-dried tomato slices and earthy brown mushroom slices. The chicken chunks are irregularly shaped, about 2 cm, displaying a seared crust. A light drizzle of the creamy sauce coats the pasta, showing its rich texture. A sprinkle of freshly grated Parmesan cheese and finely chopped fresh basil leaves garnish the top, adding contrasting color and freshness. The arrangement is organic, allowing ingredients to show naturally. The plate is positioned on a simple light wooden table. A folded white cotton napkin and classic silver fork and spoon are placed beside the plate, with a small Italian-style bread roll. Natural, soft lighting highlights the textures and colors.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple green salad dressed with vinaigrette.
Offer crusty Italian bread for dipping in the sauce.
Pair with a glass of dry white wine, like a Chianti Classico.

ingredients.name: Sun-dried tomatoes, oil-packed, drained and sliced

instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season with salt and pepper.

Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken thighs 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C). Remove chicken. Let rest. Cut into 2 cm chunks.
Add diced onion to the skillet. Sauté 3 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic and sliced mushrooms. Sauté 5-7 minutes until mushrooms are tender and browned.
Stir in sun-dried tomatoes and red pepper flakes (if using). Cook 1 minute.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a simmer. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the skillet.
Add heavy cream and grated Parmesan cheese. Stir until cheese is melted and sauce slightly thickens.
While sauce simmers, cook fettuccine according to package directions in salted water until al dente. Drain, reserving 120 ml pasta water.
Add fresh spinach to the sauce. Cook until wilted, about 1-2 minutes.
Add cooked pasta and chicken chunks to the sauce. Toss to combine. If sauce is too thick, add reserved pasta water as needed.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
notes: For extra richness, add a knob of butter at the end.
Adjust red pepper flakes to desired spice level.

recipes.recipe_name: Red Wine and Orange Kanten with Almond Milk Jelly
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Red Wine and Orange Kanten with Almond Milk Jelly is presented in a modest, simple, round ceramic bowl, placed on a well-worn light wooden kitchen table. The kanten jellies are cut into rough 2cm cubes, displaying a mix of deep ruby red from the red wine and a creamy off-white from the almond milk. Small, bright orange zest specks are visible throughout the red kanten, adding visual interest. The cubes are casually spooned into the bowl, creating a natural, slightly overlapping arrangement that feels unpretentious and homemade. A simple, plain cloth napkin is casually placed beside the bowl. Natural light from a window softly illuminates the scene, casting gentle shadows and enhancing the homely atmosphere. The background is softly blurred, showing hints of a lived-in kitchen, perhaps a simple teacup or a small, potted plant. The focus remains entirely on the comforting dessert, inviting a relaxed, family-style enjoyment. A small, unadorned spoon rests beside the bowl, ready for consumption.
instructions: Prepare Red Wine Kanten: Combine red wine, 100ml water, 50g sugar, and 2g agar-agar powder in a small saucepan.
Bring mixture to a boil over medium heat. Stir constantly until agar-agar and sugar dissolve completely. Cook for 2-3 minutes.
Remove from heat. Stir in orange zest.
Pour red wine mixture into a shallow rectangular dish (approximately 15x10 cm). Let cool slightly, then refrigerate for at least 1 hour until firm.
Prepare Almond Milk Kanten: Combine almond milk, 30g sugar, and 2g agar-agar powder in a separate small saucepan.
Bring mixture to a boil over medium heat. Stir constantly until agar-agar and sugar dissolve completely. Cook for 2-3 minutes.
Remove from heat. Let cool slightly.
Pour almond milk mixture into a similar shallow rectangular dish. Refrigerate for at least 1 hour until firm.
Once firm, cut both kanten jellies into small, rough 2cm cubes.
Gently mix the red wine and almond milk kanten cubes in a serving bowl.
Serve chilled.

recipes.recipe_name: Slow-Cooked Lamb Shank with Pickled Root Vegetable Risotto
recipes.visual_description: A single slow-cooked lamb shank, deeply browned, rests centrally on a generous portion of creamy, flowing risotto. The risotto is off-white, speckled with vibrant orange diced carrots, pale yellow parsnip, and light green celeriac, all cut into small, irregular chunks. A few very thin, crispy baked root vegetable peels are delicately placed on the side of the plate. A fresh sprig of rosemary or thyme garnishes the lamb. The dish is presented on a handcrafted ceramic plate in an earthy cream tone, placed on a light reclaimed wood surface. An undyed linen napkin sits beside the plate. Soft, natural light illuminates the scene. The background is clean and minimalist, with a subtle hint of green from a blurred plant, emphasizing natural beauty and sustainability. The entire plate is visible, with ample negative space. The presentation is simple, unforced, and highlights the natural colors and textures of the ingredients.

ingredients.name: Carrots
ingredients.quantity: 2 medium (100g diced for braise/risotto, 50g for pickling)

ingredients.name: Parsnip
ingredients.quantity: 1 large (100g diced for braise/risotto, 50g for pickling)

ingredients.name: Celeriac
ingredients.quantity: 1/2 small (50g diced for braise/risotto, 50g for pickling)

instructions: Prepare pickled root vegetables. Combine white wine vinegar, water, sugar, 1 teaspoon salt, bay leaf, and black peppercorns in a saucepan. Bring to a boil. Remove from heat. Pour over 150g mixed root vegetables cut into small, irregular chunks. Let cool completely. Store in refrigerator.
Season lamb shanks with salt and pepper. Heat 30ml olive oil in a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear shanks until deeply browned on all sides. Remove shanks from pot.
Add remaining 30ml olive oil to the pot. Add diced onion, 100g diced carrots, and diced celery. Sauté until softened, about 8 minutes. Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute.
Optional: Pour in white wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Reduce liquid by half.
Return lamb shanks to the pot. Add rosemary and thyme sprigs. Pour in vegetable broth to cover shanks. Bring to a simmer. Cover the pot. Transfer to a preheated oven at 160°C.
Braise lamb for 2.5-3 hours, or until very tender and falling off the bone.
Carefully remove shanks from the pot. Strain the braising liquid into a separate bowl, discarding any solids. Skim excess fat from the liquid.
To make risotto: Heat a clean, separate large pot over medium heat. Add 50g diced celeriac and 50g diced parsnip. Sauté for 3 minutes. Add Arborio rice. Toast rice 1 minute, stirring constantly.

Add a ladle of warm braising liquid to the rice. Stir continuously until liquid is absorbed. Continue adding liquid, one ladle at a time, stirring until absorbed before adding more. This process takes about 20-25 minutes.

When rice is al dente and creamy, stir in the remaining 50g diced carrots, 50g diced celeriac, and 50g diced parsnip (from the braise/risotto portion). Gently fold in the pickled root vegetables and grated Parmesan cheese (if using).
Ladle risotto onto individual plates. Place one lamb shank on top of each risotto portion. Garnish with a fresh sprig of rosemary or thyme. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Potato Gratin, Glazed Carrots, and Dijon Cream Sauce
recipes.visual_description: A single, perfectly pan-seared chicken breast, golden-brown and glistening, rests prominently on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. Beside it, a neat, rectangular portion of potato gratin with a golden, bubbly, cheesy crust. Vibrant orange glazed carrot batons are artfully arranged nearby, showing a slight sheen. A creamy, pale yellow Dijon sauce is elegantly spooned beside the chicken, with a few drops accentuating its form. A few roasted cherry tomatoes, slightly burst and caramelized, add a touch of deep red, along with a fresh thyme sprig for a herbaceous green accent. The plate is positioned on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by a folded cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting highlights the textures and colors of the dish, set against a subtly blurred modern bistro background.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C.
Peel and thinly slice potatoes. Layer half in a 20x20cm baking dish. Season with salt, pepper, and half the grated cheese. Add remaining potatoes. Top with rest of cheese.
Pour 150ml cream over potatoes. Bake 45-50 minutes until tender and golden.
Peel carrots. Cut into 5cm batons.
In a pan, melt 15g butter. Add carrots and 50ml water. Season with salt. Cook over medium heat, covered, until tender-crisp. Uncover, cook until water evaporates and carrots are lightly glazed.
Season chicken breasts with salt and pepper.
Heat 15ml olive oil in a large oven-safe pan over medium-high heat. Sear chicken 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown.
Transfer pan with chicken to preheated oven. Cook 10-12 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove chicken from pan. Rest 5 minutes.
For sauce, add remaining 15ml olive oil and 15g butter to same pan. Sauté minced garlic and sliced onion until softened, about 3 minutes.
Deglaze with chicken stock, scraping up browned bits. Simmer 2 minutes.
Stir in remaining 50ml cream and Dijon mustard. Simmer until slightly thickened. Season with salt and pepper.
Roast cherry tomatoes on a small baking tray with a drizzle of olive oil and a thyme sprig for 10-15 minutes in the same oven as chicken/gratin until softened.

Plate one chicken breast. Place a portion of potato gratin next to it. Arrange glazed carrots. Spoon Dijon cream sauce over and around chicken. Garnish with roasted cherry tomatoes and fresh thyme sprigs.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Potato & Gruyère Croquettes and Thyme Jus
recipes.visual_description: A single pan-seared chicken breast, golden-brown and glistening, rests slightly off-center on a clean white porcelain plate. The chicken is presented as a whole piece, showcasing its perfectly seared crust. Adjacent to the chicken, two to three golden-fried potato and Gruyère croquettes are neatly arranged, their crispy, textured surfaces visible. A vibrant pile of glossy, orange glazed carrot batons adds a pop of color beside them. A rich, dark brown thyme jus is artfully drizzled around the plate, creating a professional, restrained pattern. A small, verdant sprig of fresh thyme garnishes the dish, providing a natural accent. The overall composition is balanced and inviting, with moderate negative space. The plate sits on a simple wooden table surface. A neatly folded white cotton napkin is placed beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the scene, highlighting the textures and colors of the food. The background is minimal, suggesting a modern bistro setting with a casual atmosphere. Standard, clean flatware is placed alongside the plate.
instructions: Prepare potatoes: Peel and cut potatoes into 2cm cubes. Place in a pot. Cover with cold salted water. Bring to a boil. Cook until fork-tender, about 15-20 minutes.
Drain potatoes. Return to the hot pot. Mash thoroughly until smooth. Stir in grated Gruyère cheese and 2 finely chopped thyme sprigs. Season with salt and pepper. Set aside to cool slightly.
Form croquettes: Once cool enough to handle, shape the potato mixture into 8-12 cylindrical croquettes, about 5cm long. Place on a tray.

Bread croquettes: Set up a breading station. Place flour in one shallow dish, beaten eggs in another, and panko breadcrumbs in a third. Dredge each croquette in flour, then egg, then breadcrumbs. Ensure full coating. Place back on tray. Chill for 30 minutes.

Prepare carrots: Peel carrots. Cut into 1cm thick batons, about 5cm long. Heat 20g butter in a pan over medium heat. Add carrots. Cook for 5-7 minutes until slightly tender-crisp. Add 50ml chicken stock and 1 tablespoon of butter. Cook until liquid reduces and carrots are glazed. Season with salt and pepper. Keep warm.

Cook chicken: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season generously with salt and pepper. Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Add chicken breasts. Sear for 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown. Internal temperature must reach 75°C (167°F). If breasts are thick, transfer skillet to a preheated oven at 180°C for 5-10 minutes to finish cooking. Remove chicken. Rest on a cutting board for 5 minutes.

Make thyme jus: Pour off excess fat from the chicken skillet, leaving 1 tablespoon. Add remaining 200ml chicken stock and 4 thyme sprigs to the hot pan. Bring to a simmer. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom. Reduce liquid by half, about 5-7 minutes. Strain the jus to remove thyme sprigs. Stir in remaining 10g butter. Season with salt and pepper.

Fry croquettes: Heat vegetable oil in a deep pot or Dutch oven to 175°C. Fry croquettes in batches for 3-4 minutes until golden brown and crispy. Use a slotted spoon to transfer to a paper towel-lined plate to drain excess oil. Season lightly with salt.

Plate the dish: Place one seared chicken breast (or half a breast if very large) on each plate. Arrange 2-3 potato croquettes beside the chicken. Add a neat pile of glazed carrot batons. Drizzle the thyme jus around the plate. Garnish with a small fresh thyme sprig.

recipes.recipe_name: Kimchi and Shrimp Jeon
recipes.visual_description: Golden-brown, irregular-shaped Kimchi and Shrimp Jeon are arranged casually on a simple, round, white ceramic plate. Some pancakes slightly overlap, showcasing their crispy edges. Visible textures of chopped red kimchi, pink shrimp pieces, and vibrant green onion bits peek through the golden-brown rice flour batter. A small, dark brown dipping sauce bowl, topped with white sesame seeds, sits beside the pancakes. The setting is a well-used light wooden dining table. A pair of sleek metal chopsticks rests on the table next to the plate. A small white rice bowl is placed nearby. Warm, inviting light filters in from a kitchen window, casting soft shadows. A casually folded beige cloth napkin completes the homely scene.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve hot with soy-vinegar dipping sauce.
Often enjoyed with other Korean side dishes (banchan) and a bowl of steamed rice.
instructions: Chop kimchi into small pieces. Chop shrimp into small pieces. Chop green onions. Thinly slice the half onion.
In a large bowl, whisk together rice flour, cold water, and egg until smooth.
Add chopped kimchi, chopped shrimp, chopped green onions, and sliced onion to the batter. Mix well to combine all ingredients.
Heat 2-3 tablespoons of vegetable oil in a large non-stick pan over medium-high heat.
Pour ladlefuls of the batter mixture into the hot pan. Spread slightly to form round pancakes, about 10-12 cm in diameter. Do not overcrowd the pan.
Cook each pancake for 3-4 minutes per side, until golden brown and crispy. Ensure shrimp is cooked through.
Transfer cooked pancakes to a wire rack to drain excess oil. Repeat with remaining batter.
For the dipping sauce, combine soy sauce, rice vinegar, sesame oil, and toasted sesame seeds in a small bowl. Stir well.
Serve the hot Kimchi and Shrimp Jeon immediately with the dipping sauce.
notes: For extra crispy pancakes, use less batter per pancake and cook slightly longer until very golden.
Adjust the amount of water in the batter for desired consistency; it should be thick enough to coat ingredients but still pourable.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Raspberry-Ginger Glaze
recipes.visual_description: A single pan-seared chicken breast, cooked whole, sits prominently on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The chicken is golden-brown from searing, topped with a generous layer of melted, bubbly fresh mozzarella that clings to its surface. A vibrant, glossy raspberry-ginger glaze pools around the base of the chicken, its rich red color contrasting with the chicken and cheese. The sauce has visible small pieces of broken-down raspberries and fine specks of ginger. Fresh green basil leaves are artfully scattered over the chicken and sauce, adding a pop of color and freshness. The plate is positioned on a simple light wooden table surface. A neatly folded cotton napkin and standard restaurant-style flatware are placed beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and colors against a soft, unobtrusive background, creating a professional yet inviting presentation.
instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken breasts for 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown.
Transfer skillet to a preheated oven at 190°C. Bake for 8-10 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken from skillet; set aside.
Return skillet to medium heat. Add minced garlic and grated ginger. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add raspberries, chicken broth, red wine vinegar, and honey to the skillet. Bring to a simmer.
Cook, stirring occasionally, for 5-7 minutes until sauce thickens slightly and raspberries break down. Mash any remaining large raspberry pieces.
Place chicken breasts back into the skillet with the sauce. Top each chicken breast with mozzarella slices.
Cover skillet loosely or return to oven for 2-3 minutes until mozzarella is melted and bubbly.
Serve chicken immediately, spooning extra glaze over each piece. Garnish with fresh basil.

recipes.recipe_name: Baked Beef and Mushroom Rigatoni
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Baked Beef and Mushroom Rigatoni is presented in a deep, white porcelain gratin dish, filling it generously. The top crust features a bubbly, golden-brown layer of melted mozzarella, offering glimpses of the rich, reddish-brown tomato sauce beneath. Tender, dark brown chunks of slow-cooked beef are interspersed throughout the sauce and rigatoni, alongside soft, sliced cremini mushrooms. The rigatoni tubes are perfectly al dente, thoroughly coated in the savory sauce. Fresh, vibrant green basil leaves are scattered artfully over the melted cheese, providing a pop of color and freshness. The dish sits on a simple wooden table, with a crisp white cotton napkin and traditional silver flatware to its side, under soft, natural lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of crusty ciabatta or rustic Italian bread for dipping into the sauce.
Offer extra grated Parmesan cheese at the table for individual preference.
instructions: Season beef chunks generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven or oven-safe pot over medium-high heat. Brown beef chunks on all sides until deep golden. Remove beef and set aside.
Add diced onion to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Add minced garlic and sliced mushrooms. Cook for 5 minutes until mushrooms soften and release moisture.
Pour in red wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Reduce by half.
Stir in crushed tomatoes, beef stock, and dried oregano. Bring to a simmer.
Return browned beef to the pot. Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 2-2.5 hours, or until beef is very tender. Stir occasionally.
While beef simmers, cook rigatoni according to package instructions until al dente. Drain well.
Preheat oven to 190°C.

Remove beef from sauce. Shred or break beef chunks into smaller, manageable pieces with a fork. Return beef to sauce. Stir in fresh basil leaves and half of the grated Parmesan cheese. Taste and adjust seasoning.
Add cooked rigatoni to the beef and mushroom sauce. Toss to coat evenly.
Transfer the pasta mixture to a large oven-safe baking dish. Distribute evenly.
Scatter torn mozzarella pieces over the top of the pasta.
Bake for 20-25 minutes, or until cheese is melted, bubbly, and lightly golden.
Let stand for a few minutes before serving. Garnish with remaining fresh basil and grated Parmesan.
notes: Ensure beef is cooked until fork-tender for best results.
Cook pasta al dente as it will continue to cook in the oven.

recipes.recipe_name: Mandarin Upside-Down Cake
recipes.visual_description: A generous, single slice of Mandarin Upside-Down Cake is centrally plated on a simple, round, white ceramic plate. The top of the cake, now facing upwards, reveals a beautiful mosaic of thinly sliced, caramelized mandarin rounds, their vibrant orange segments glistening against a rich, golden-brown caramel. The cake crumb beneath is a soft, pale yellow, indicating a moist, tender texture. The mandarin slices are naturally arranged, slightly overlapping. The plate rests on a warm, well-worn wooden kitchen table. A casually folded, light blue linen napkin is beside the plate. In the background, slightly out of focus, the remaining whole cake sits on a plain white cake stand. Soft, natural light from a nearby window illuminates the scene, creating a cozy, inviting atmosphere.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C. Grease and line an 18cm round cake pan with baking paper.
Melt 30g butter in a small saucepan over medium heat. Stir in 100g brown sugar until dissolved and smooth. Pour caramel into prepared cake pan.
Wash and thinly slice mandarin rounds (from 3-4 mandarins). Remove any seeds. Arrange mandarin slices over the caramel in the pan.
In a medium bowl, whisk together 150g all-purpose flour, 120g granulated sugar, 10g baking powder, and 2g salt.

In a separate large bowl, cream remaining 30g softened butter until light and fluffy. Beat in 2 large eggs, one at a time, until combined. Stir in 5ml vanilla extract, 5g mandarin zest, and 30ml mandarin juice.
Gradually add dry ingredients to wet ingredients, alternating with 80ml milk, beginning and ending with dry. Mix until just combined. Do not overmix.
Pour cake batter gently over mandarin slices in the pan. Spread evenly.
Bake for 30-35 minutes, or until a skewer inserted into the center comes out clean.
Cool cake in the pan for 10 minutes. Place a serving plate over the pan. Carefully invert cake onto the plate. Remove pan and baking paper.
Serve warm or at room temperature.

recipes.recipe_name: Coconut Lemon Bars
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of two Coconut Lemon Bars rests on a simple, slightly chipped white ceramic plate. The bars are cut into neat squares, approximately 5x5 cm. Each bar features a distinct golden-brown shortbread crust at the bottom, about 1 cm thick. Above the crust, the lemon filling is a vibrant, opaque yellow, approximately 2 cm thick, with visible strands of shredded white coconut embedded throughout. The top surface of the bars is lightly crinkled and generously dusted with a fine, even layer of white powdered sugar, creating a soft, snowy appearance. The bars are arranged casually on the plate, slightly overlapping. The plate sits on a well-used, light-colored wooden dining table, illuminated by warm, natural kitchen lighting. A simple cloth napkin, folded casually, is placed beside the plate. The background is softly blurred, showing hints of a home kitchen environment.
