The composition is clean and minimalist, with ample negative space. A few fresh dill sprigs are scattered for garnish. The overall palette is organic and fresh, emphasizing natural ingredient colors and textures. A natural beige linen napkin and simple, modern flatware complete the eco-conscious setting under soft, natural light.
instructions: Prepare fermented tomatoes: Halve cherry tomatoes. Dissolve 5g salt in 250ml water to create a brine. Place tomatoes in a clean jar. Pour brine over tomatoes. Seal jar. Let ferment at room temperature for 24-48 hours. Drain before use.
Cook potatoes: Wash potatoes. Dice into 2cm cubes. Boil potatoes in salted water until tender, about 10-15 minutes. Drain well. Let cool slightly.

Cook chicken: Dice chicken breast into 1.5cm cubes. Season with salt and pepper. Heat a pan over medium-high heat. Sear chicken cubes until golden brown and cooked through, about 5-7 minutes. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C. Set aside.
Prepare apple: Core and dice apple into 1.5cm cubes.

Make dressing: In a small bowl, whisk together Dijon mustard, apple cider vinegar, and a pinch of salt and pepper. Slowly whisk in olive oil until emulsified. Chop fresh dill finely. Stir dill into dressing.

Assemble salad: In a large bowl, combine cooled diced potatoes, diced apple, and drained fermented tomatoes. Add cooked chicken cubes. Pour dressing over ingredients. Toss gently to combine. Serve immediately.
notes: To reduce waste, save potato cooking water for vegetable broth. Apple cores can be used to make homemade apple cider vinegar.
Adjust fermentation time for tomatoes based on desired tanginess.

recipes.recipe_name: Tostadas de Papa y Champiñones con Salsa Roja
recipes.visual_description: A single, generously portioned Tostada de Papa y Champiñones rests on a rustic, slightly worn ceramic plate, showcasing homely Mexican comfort food. The golden-brown, crispy corn tostada forms the base, piled high with a savory, crumbled mixture of tender, light brown potatoes and earthy sautéed cremini mushrooms. A vibrant, deep red Salsa Roja is spooned generously over the filling, its fresh, slightly chunky texture visible. Crumbled white Cotija cheese is scattered over the salsa, adding a contrasting color and texture. A few fresh, bright green cilantro leaves are casually placed on top. The plate sits on a well-used wooden kitchen table, bathed in warm, inviting light. A simple cloth napkin and a lime wedge are nearby, completing the authentic, lived-in family kitchen scene. The entire plate is visible, with natural negative space around it.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately while tostadas are crispy.
Offer extra lime wedges for squeezing over the tostadas.
Provide a small bowl of additional Salsa Roja on the side for those who prefer more heat or moisture.
instructions: Prepare Salsa Roja: Roughly chop tomatoes, half onion, garlic, and chili. Place in a saucepan with 100 ml water. Simmer 10 minutes until softened. Blend until smooth. Season with salt. Set aside.
Prepare Potatoes: Peel and dice potatoes into 1 cm cubes. Boil until tender, about 10-12 minutes. Drain well. Lightly mash or crumble the potatoes; do not make them smooth.

Cook Mushroom Mixture: Slice mushrooms thinly. Dice remaining half onion finely. Mince garlic. Heat 15 ml oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add diced onion and cook until softened, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic and sliced mushrooms. Sauté until mushrooms are browned and tender, about 7-10 minutes.

Combine Filling: Add crumbled potatoes to the mushroom mixture. Crumble in dried Mexican oregano. Mix well. Season generously with salt and pepper. Cook for another 3-5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until flavors meld.

Prepare Tostadas: Heat 2 cm of vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Fry corn tortillas one at a time until golden and crispy, about 1-2 minutes per side. Drain on paper towels. Season lightly with salt.

Assemble Tostadas: Spread a generous portion of the potato and mushroom mixture onto each crispy tostada. Spoon a desired amount of Salsa Roja over the top. Crumble Cotija cheese over the salsa. Garnish with fresh cilantro leaves.
notes: For extra flavor, roast the tomatoes and chili for the salsa before blending.
Ensure potatoes are well-drained to prevent a watery filling.
Cotija cheese is a traditional Mexican cheese; queso fresco can be used as an alternative.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Corn and Pickled Onion Salad
recipes.visual_description: This vibrant Mexican salad is presented in a handcrafted, rustic ceramic bowl with earth-toned glazes. Shredded romaine lettuce forms the base, creating a fresh green foundation. Roasted corn kernels, with their golden-yellow hue and slight char, are scattered generously alongside deep black beans, creating a striking color contrast. Diced avocado pieces, creamy and light green, are interspersed throughout. Thinly sliced pickled red onions, a vibrant fuchsia, provide pops of color and a crisp texture. Fresh cilantro leaves are roughly chopped and sprinkled over the top, adding a bright green garnish. Irregularly torn sourdough croutons are artfully arranged on the surface, offering a golden, crunchy element. A rich, dark mole-inspired dressing is visibly drizzled over the ingredients, hinting at its complex flavor. The entire plate is visible, with ample negative space around the central dish, set on a light reclaimed wood table surface with an undyed linen napkin in natural beige. Soft, natural lighting highlights the ingredients' natural colors and textures.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas on the side for scooping.
Offer additional lime wedges for guests to squeeze over their salad.
Pair with a glass of agua fresca, such as horchata or jamaica.
instructions: Prepare pickled red onions: Thinly slice red onions. Combine apple cider vinegar, water, 1 teaspoon salt, and a pinch of sugar in a saucepan. Bring to a simmer. Pour over sliced onions in a heatproof jar. Let cool, then refrigerate for at least 4 hours, or overnight.

Make sourdough croutons: Preheat oven to 180°C. Tear sourdough bread into small, irregular pieces. Toss with 30 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking sheet. Bake for 10-15 minutes until golden and crisp. Cool completely.
Roast corn: Preheat oven to 200°C. Toss corn kernels with 15 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking sheet. Roast for 15-20 minutes, stirring once, until lightly charred. Let cool.
Prepare the dressing: In a small bowl, whisk together remaining olive oil, lime juice, unsweetened cocoa powder, chipotle hot sauce, and a pinch of salt and pepper until emulsified.
Assemble the salad: Wash and chop romaine lettuce into bite-sized pieces. Drain and rinse black beans. Dice avocados.
In a large serving bowl, combine romaine lettuce, roasted corn, black beans, diced avocado, and chopped cilantro. Add pickled red onions, drained.
Drizzle the dressing over the salad. Toss gently to combine all ingredients evenly.
Top with the sourdough croutons just before serving to maintain crispness.
notes: The pickled red onions can be made up to a week in advance and stored in the refrigerator.
For extra spice, add a pinch of chili powder to the roasted corn.
This recipe is designed to minimize waste; stale sourdough bread is repurposed into delicious croutons.

recipes.recipe_name: Filipino Beef Mechado with Annatto Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Filipino Beef Mechado is presented on a simple, round, off-white ceramic plate with natural imperfections, placed on a well-used wooden dining table. Thick, fork-tender beef chunks are nestled amidst a rich, reddish-brown tomato-based stew. The stew features vibrant green peas, golden corn kernels, and earthy quartered mushrooms, all coated in the savory sauce. The ingredients are arranged naturally, slightly overlapping. Adjacent to the stew is a generous scoop of bright orange-hued annatto rice. The scene is lit by warm, cozy kitchen lighting, creating a comforting, lived-in atmosphere. A basic stainless steel fork rests beside the plate. The overall presentation is homely and inviting, focusing on the hearty nature of the dish.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with extra plain rice or more annatto rice.
Offer fresh calamansi or lime wedges on the side for a tangy squeeze.
Traditionally served with a side of 'atchara' (pickled green papaya) to cut through the richness.
instructions: Cut beef chuck into 4 cm thick chunks. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Brown beef chunks on all sides. Remove beef and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add minced garlic and diced onion to the pot. Sauté until fragrant and softened, about 3-5 minutes. This is called 'gisa'.
Stir in tomato paste and diced tomatoes. Cook for 5 minutes until tomatoes soften.
Return beef to the pot. Pour in beer, water, soy sauce, and calamansi juice. Add bay leaves and black peppercorns.
Bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 2-2.5 hours, or until beef is very tender. Stir occasionally.
While beef simmers, prepare annatto water. Soak annatto seeds in hot water for 10 minutes. Press seeds to extract color. Strain and discard seeds.
Cook white rice according to package directions. Use the annatto water as part of the liquid for cooking the rice to give it a vibrant orange color.
After beef is tender, add quartered mushrooms, corn kernels, and green peas to the stew. Simmer for another 10-15 minutes, until vegetables are tender-crisp.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and sugar if needed. Ensure internal temperature of beef reaches 75°C (167°F).
Serve hot with annatto rice.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Katsu Donburi with Creamy Sauce
recipes.visual_description: A golden-brown chicken katsu, sliced into thick, substantial pieces, rests atop a generous bed of fluffy white Japanese short-grain rice in a wide, shallow white ceramic donburi bowl. The crispy katsu is generously drizzled with a rich, creamy, pale ivory sauce, which pools slightly on the rice. Bright green scallions, finely chopped, are scattered over the top, providing a fresh contrast. A few vibrant red flakes of shichimi togarashi add a subtle pop of color. The dish is presented on a simple light wooden table, with natural, even lighting casting soft shadows. A pair of elegant wooden chopsticks rests beside the bowl on a white linen napkin. The background is minimally blurred, hinting at a casual, modern bistro atmosphere, allowing the focus to remain squarely on the well-portioned, inviting dish.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a small bowl of miso soup.
Offer a side of pickled ginger (gari) for palate cleansing.
Serve with a simple side salad dressed with a light vinaigrette.
instructions: Rinse rice until water runs clear. Cook rice according to package directions. Keep warm.
Place chicken thighs between two sheets of cling film. Pound gently to an even 1.5 cm thickness. Season chicken with salt and pepper.

Set up a breading station: one shallow dish with flour, one with beaten egg, one with panko breadcrumbs. Dredge each chicken thigh in flour, shaking off excess. Dip in egg, then coat thoroughly with panko, pressing gently to adhere.

Heat vegetable oil in a deep pot or wok to 170°C. Carefully lower breaded chicken into hot oil. Fry for 5-7 minutes, turning once, until golden brown and cooked through. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C. Drain on a wire rack lined with paper towels.
While chicken fries, thinly slice the small onion. Chop scallions finely, separating white and green parts.
In a small saucepan, combine dashi stock, soy sauce, mirin, and brown sugar. Bring to a simmer. Add thinly sliced onion and cook until softened, about 3-5 minutes.
Remove saucepan from heat. Whisk in mayonnaise until smooth and creamy. Adjust sweetness or savory notes if needed.
Slice each cooked chicken katsu into thick, uniform pieces.
To serve, place a generous portion of cooked rice in a donburi bowl. Arrange sliced chicken katsu on top of the rice. Generously drizzle the creamy sauce over the katsu and rice.
Garnish with finely chopped green scallions. Optionally, sprinkle with shichimi togarashi for a touch of spice.

recipes.recipe_name: Baked Coconut Oatmeal Pudding
recipes.visual_description: A warm, golden-brown square of Baked Coconut Oatmeal Pudding sits on a simple, round ceramic plate with a slight rim. The pudding has a soft, slightly rustic texture on top, showing hints of the baked oats and a comforting, inviting appearance. Its edges are gently browned, contrasting with the creamy interior visible if a piece is slightly askew. The plate rests on a well-used wooden dining table, showing natural grain and minor imperfections, suggesting a lived-in family kitchen. A casual cloth napkin in a neutral tone is folded beside the plate. The scene is illuminated by warm, cozy light, casting soft shadows and highlighting the comforting nature of the dessert. A simple spoon is placed next to the pudding, ready for enjoyment.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C. Grease a 20x20 cm baking dish.
In a large bowl, combine rolled oats, whole wheat flour, sugar, baking powder, salt, and cinnamon. Whisk well.
In a separate bowl, whisk eggs, milk, melted coconut oil, and vanilla extract until blended.
Pour wet ingredients into dry ingredients. Stir until just combined. Do not overmix.
Pour mixture into the greased baking dish.
Bake for 30-35 minutes, or until the pudding is set and golden brown on top. A toothpick inserted into the center should come out clean.
Let cool slightly before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Arugula, Chicken, and Wild Rice Salad
recipes.visual_description: The Arugula, Chicken, and Wild Rice Salad is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, showcasing a vibrant mix of colors and textures. A bed of fresh, dark green arugula forms the base, topped with a generous, artful mound of mixed ingredients. Golden-brown, diced chicken cubes are interspersed among the ruby red halved cherry tomatoes, crisp 1 cm diced cucumber, and thinly sliced purple-red onion rings. Dark, earthy wild rice grains are visible throughout, adding textural contrast. Crumbled white feta cheese is scattered over the top, providing bright accents. A light, glistening lemon-herb vinaigrette coats all components, enhancing their natural sheen. The plate is moderately filled, allowing for ample negative space around the edges. A cotton napkin rests beside the plate on a simple wooden table, under natural, even lighting, creating a professional yet approachable bistro setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread for dipping in any residual dressing.
instructions: Rinse 150g wild rice. Combine with 750ml water and 1g salt in a saucepan. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 40-45 minutes until tender and water is absorbed. Fluff with a fork. Let cool.

Pat 400g chicken breasts dry. Season with 2g salt and 1g black pepper. Heat a grill pan or large skillet over medium-high heat. Cook chicken for 6-8 minutes per side, until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken. Rest for 5 minutes. Dice into 1.5 cm cubes.
Wash 150g arugula. Halve 200g cherry tomatoes. Dice 1 large cucumber into 1 cm cubes. Thinly slice 1 small red onion.
In a small bowl, whisk together 80ml olive oil, 40ml lemon juice, 15g chopped fresh dill, 15g chopped fresh parsley, 1 minced garlic clove, 2g salt, and 1g black pepper.

In a large mixing bowl, combine cooled wild rice, diced chicken, halved cherry tomatoes, diced cucumber, thinly sliced red onion, and 100g crumbled feta cheese. Add arugula. Pour dressing over salad. Toss gently to combine.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Chicken Thighs with Root Vegetables
recipes.visual_description: A single, roasted chicken thigh, skin-on and bone-in, rests centrally on a modest, round ceramic plate. The chicken skin is deeply golden and visibly crisp, showing slight char marks. Surrounding the chicken is an abundant, casual arrangement of roasted root vegetables: chunky, tender potatoes with slightly browned edges, vibrant orange carrot chunks, and soft, caramelized onion wedges. The vegetables are rustic-cut and naturally piled, displaying their varied textures and earthy tones. A scattering of fresh, chopped green parsley provides a functional, bright garnish over the dish. The plate is positioned on a warm, well-worn wooden dining table, with a simple, folded cloth napkin and standard flatware nearby. The scene is bathed in soft, inviting kitchen light, evoking a comforting, lived-in family atmosphere.

ingredients.name: Carrots
ingredients.quantity: 300g, peeled and cut into 2-3 cm chunks

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Pat chicken thighs dry with paper towels. Season generously with half of the salt and pepper.
In a large bowl, combine potato chunks, carrot chunks, and onion wedges.
Drizzle vegetables with olive oil. Add remaining salt, pepper, rosemary, thyme, and garlic powder. Toss to coat evenly.
Spread seasoned vegetables in a single layer on a large baking tray.
Place chicken thighs skin-side up on top of the vegetables on the same tray.
Roast for 35-45 minutes. Chicken skin should be crispy and golden. Vegetables should be tender and lightly caramelized.
Check internal temperature of chicken. It must reach 75°C.
Remove from oven. Let rest 5 minutes before serving.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Herb & Rice Fritters with Quick Pickled Onion & Poached Chicken
recipes.visual_description: A small starter portion of three golden-brown Herb & Rice Fritters arranged organically on a handcrafted, matte cream ceramic plate. Each fritter, approximately 5 cm in diameter, is crisp on the exterior, revealing a tender, herb-flecked rice and shredded chicken interior. A delicate mound of thinly sliced, vibrant pink quick pickled red onion tops each fritter, adding a contrasting pop of color and tangy texture. A few fresh, small thyme leaves are scattered artfully around the fritters as a natural garnish. The plate rests on a light, reclaimed wood surface, highlighting the dish with soft, natural lighting. The background is clean and minimalist, with subtle hints of natural elements like blurred green foliage, creating an eco-conscious and inviting scene.

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.quantity: 1 tsp (for pickling brine, plus more for seasoning)

instructions: Prepare Quick Pickled Red Onion: Thinly slice the red onion. In a small saucepan, combine 120ml white vinegar, 120ml water, 1 tbsp sugar, and 1 tsp salt. Bring to a simmer. Stir until sugar and salt dissolve. Pour hot brine over sliced onions in a heatproof jar. Let cool. Refrigerate for at least 30 minutes.

Cook Rice: Rinse rice under cold water until water runs clear. In a saucepan, combine rinsed rice with 500ml water or vegetable stock and a pinch of salt. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 15-20 minutes, until water is absorbed and rice is tender. Remove from heat. Let stand covered for 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork. Let cool completely.

Poach Chicken: Place chicken breasts in a saucepan. Cover with cold water or vegetable stock. Add a pinch of salt, 1 smashed garlic clove, and one thyme sprig. Bring to a gentle simmer over medium heat. Simmer for 15-20 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken from liquid. Let cool slightly. Shred chicken finely using two forks.

Prepare Fritter Mixture: Finely chop remaining garlic, thyme leaves, savory leaves, and rosemary leaves. In a large bowl, combine cooled cooked rice, shredded chicken, chopped herbs, and chopped garlic. Add 2 tbsp flour and 1 egg. Season with salt and pepper. Mix well until everything is combined and forms a cohesive mixture.

Form and Fry Fritters: Heat 2 tbsp olive oil in a large non-stick pan over medium heat. Form the rice mixture into small, flattened patties, approximately 4-5 cm in diameter. Cook fritters for 3-4 minutes per side, until golden brown and crisp. Cook in batches to avoid overcrowding the pan. Transfer cooked fritters to a plate lined with paper towel to drain excess oil.
Plate and Serve: Arrange 3-4 fritters elegantly on each plate. Top each fritter with a small mound of quick pickled red onion. Garnish with a few fresh herb leaves.

recipes.recipe_name: Ande Ki Sabzi (Egg Curry)
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant, rich Indian Egg Curry is presented in a deep, rustic ceramic serving bowl. The thick, reddish-brown tomato and onion gravy coats the whole, light golden-brown fried boiled eggs. Bright green peas are scattered throughout the sauce, adding pops of color and texture. A generous sprinkle of fresh, finely chopped coriander leaves garnishes the top, providing a fresh green contrast. The gravy has a glossy sheen, indicating a well-cooked, emulsified sauce. The eggs are whole, showcasing their integrity. The bowl is centered on a simple wooden table surface. Beside it, a clean white porcelain plate holds a single portion of fluffy basmati rice. A neatly folded cotton napkin is placed next to the plate. The scene is lit with natural, even lighting, creating a warm, inviting atmosphere. The background is minimally blurred, suggesting a casual restaurant setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Served hot with steamed Basmati rice, fresh Roti, or Naan bread.
A side of cooling cucumber raita or spicy pickle complements the dish.
instructions: Hard boil eggs. Cool, peel, and make small slits on each egg.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a pan. Lightly fry boiled eggs until golden. Set aside.
In the same pan, add remaining oil. Add cumin seeds. Let them splutter.
Add diced onions. Sauté until golden brown.
Add minced garlic and grated ginger. Sauté 1 minute until fragrant.
Add pureed tomatoes. Cook until oil separates, about 5-7 minutes.
Add coriander powder, turmeric powder, and red chili powder. Cook 2 minutes, stirring constantly. Add a splash of water if needed to prevent burning.
Add green peas and 250ml water. Bring to a simmer.
Add fried eggs to the gravy. Season with salt.
Cover and simmer 10 minutes, allowing flavors to meld.
Stir in garam masala. Cook 1 minute.
Garnish with fresh coriander leaves. Serve hot.
notes: The gravy consistency should be thick enough to coat the eggs but still flow.
Adjust chili powder for desired spice level.
traditional_techniques: Tempering spices (Tadka) at the beginning of cooking to infuse oil with flavor.
Slow simmering (Dum) to allow flavors to meld and deepen.

recipes.recipe_name: Savory Pork and Potato Croquettes
recipes.visual_description: Three golden-brown Savory Pork and Potato Croquettes are casually arranged on a cream-colored ceramic plate with a slightly uneven rim. Each croquette is roughly cylindrical, showcasing a crispy, textured breadcrumb coating. A few small, finely chopped green chives are scattered over the croquettes for a fresh color contrast. The plate rests on a well-worn, light wooden kitchen table, revealing natural grain and minor imperfections. A simple, folded blue and white checkered cloth napkin is placed beside the plate. The scene is lit with warm, soft light, typical of a cozy kitchen, creating inviting shadows. A plain silver fork and knife are positioned to the right of the plate. The overall presentation is unpretentious and homely, emphasizing comfort and approachability.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Served with a simple ketchup or a light sour cream dip on the side.
instructions: Boil peeled and quartered potatoes in salted water until tender. Drain well. Mash until smooth.
Heat olive oil in a large pan over medium heat. Add finely diced onion and finely diced carrot. Cook for 5-7 minutes until softened.
Add ground pork and minced garlic to the pan. Break up pork with a spoon. Cook until pork is browned and cooked through. Drain any excess fat.
Combine cooked pork mixture with mashed potatoes in a large bowl. Season with salt and pepper. Mix well.
Set up a dredging station: one shallow dish with flour, one with beaten eggs, and one with breadcrumbs.
Form the mixture into 12-16 cylindrical croquettes, about 5-6 cm long.
Roll each croquette first in flour, then in beaten egg, then coat thoroughly in breadcrumbs.
Heat vegetable oil in a deep pan or pot to 175°C. Fry croquettes in batches for 3-4 minutes, turning occasionally, until golden brown and crispy.
Remove croquettes with a slotted spoon. Place on a wire rack lined with paper towels to drain excess oil.
Serve hot, garnished with finely chopped fresh chives or parsley.
notes: For best results, chill the croquette mixture for 30 minutes before shaping to make them easier to handle.

recipes.recipe_name: Pork and Potato Croquettes with Carrot-Onion Puree
recipes.visual_description: A single starter portion of three golden-brown pork and potato croquettes rests on a clean white porcelain plate. The croquettes are cylindrical, approximately 6 cm long, with a visibly crispy, textured crust. A vibrant, smooth orange carrot-onion puree is artfully swirled beside the croquettes, creating a soft color contrast. Sprinkled over the croquettes and puree are a few small, deeply browned, crispy pork lardons, adding textural crunch. Fresh, finely chopped chives provide a bright green accent. The composition is balanced with moderate negative space, showcasing the dish elegantly. The setting features a simple light wooden table surface, a grey cotton napkin beside the plate, and standard silver flatware. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and colors against a subtle, blurred bistro background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve as an elegant starter course in a casual European dining setting.
instructions: Cut pork shoulder into 5 cm chunks. Braise pork in water or stock until very tender, approximately 2 hours. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C. Drain and shred pork. Reserve 50 g of shredded pork for crispy lardons.
Peel and cube potatoes. Boil potatoes in salted water until tender. Drain well. Mash potatoes until smooth.
Halve the onion. Finely dice one half of the onion. Sauté diced onion in a pan with a little oil until translucent. Add to mashed potatoes.
Combine shredded pork (except reserved 50 g) and mashed potatoes. Season with salt, pepper, and a pinch of nutmeg. Mix thoroughly.
Form the mixture into 12 cylindrical croquettes, each approximately 6 cm long.

Set up a dredging station: one plate with flour, one bowl with beaten eggs, one plate with panko breadcrumbs. Roll each croquette first in flour, then in egg, then coat thoroughly in panko breadcrumbs.
Heat vegetable oil in a deep pot or fryer to 170°C. Fry croquettes in batches for 3-4 minutes until golden brown and crispy. Drain on paper towels.

For the carrot-onion puree: Peel and roughly chop remaining half onion and carrots. Sauté in a saucepan with butter until softened, about 8 minutes. Add vegetable stock. Simmer until vegetables are very tender. Blend until completely smooth. Season with salt and pepper.
For crispy lardons: Heat a small pan. Add reserved shredded pork. Cook over medium-high heat until crispy and browned. Drain excess fat.

To plate: Spoon a swirl of carrot-onion puree onto each plate. Arrange three croquettes neatly beside the puree. Sprinkle crispy pork lardons over the croquettes and puree. Garnish with finely chopped fresh chives. Serve immediately.
notes: Croquettes can be prepared and breaded in advance, then refrigerated until ready to fry.

recipes.recipe_name: Cocoa Pappardelle with Braised Beef Short Ribs and Pistachio Gremolata
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate, showcasing a single, refined portion. Deep brown cocoa pappardelle is loosely coiled at the base. Generous, irregular chunks of dark, mahogany-colored braised beef short ribs are nestled atop the pasta. A glossy, dark brown, slightly viscous braising sauce cascades over the short ribs and pasta, creating a lustrous sheen. The dish is crowned with a vibrant sprinkle of pistachio gremolata – bright green chopped pistachios, fresh green finely chopped parsley, and bright orange zest. Rich colors of meat and pasta contrast with the fresh green and orange garnish. Plating is organized yet natural. The scene features a simple wooden table, a fork and knife, and a crisp white cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish, with a softly blurred, casual restaurant background.
instructions: Pat short ribs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven or heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat.
Sear short ribs on all sides until deeply browned. Work in batches if necessary. Remove ribs and set aside.
Add diced onion, carrots, and celery to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 8-10 minutes.
Add minced garlic and tomato paste. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Pour in red wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Reduce wine by half.
Return seared short ribs to the pot. Add beef broth, thyme sprigs, and bay leaf. Bring to a simmer.
Cover the pot tightly. Transfer to a preheated oven at 160°C (325°F). Braise for 2.5-3 hours, or until short ribs are very tender.
Remove short ribs from the pot. Skim excess fat from the braising liquid. Discard thyme and bay leaf.

Bring braising liquid to a simmer over medium heat on the stovetop. Reduce until slightly thickened. Stir in butter and dark chocolate until melted and smooth. Season sauce with salt and pepper to taste.
Shred the braised short ribs into large, rustic chunks using two forks.
For the gremolata: finely chop pistachios and parsley. Grate orange zest. Combine all ingredients in a small bowl.
Cook pappardelle according to package directions in salted boiling water until al dente.
Drain pasta. Toss lightly with a spoonful of the braising sauce.
Plate pasta first. Top with generous chunks of shredded short ribs. Spoon additional rich sauce over the meat and pasta.
Garnish generously with pistachio gremolata. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Crispy Honey-Soy Pork Bites
recipes.visual_description: A single starter portion of golden-brown, glistening crispy honey-soy pork bites is presented on a simple, round ceramic plate with a slightly rustic edge. The pork belly cubes, approximately 2.5 cm, are irregularly piled in the center, showcasing their caramelized, sticky glaze and deeply crisped skin. A few pieces are slightly overlapping, creating a natural, inviting arrangement. The dark, rich glaze pools slightly at the base of the pork pile. A light sprinkle of white toasted sesame seeds and vibrant green, thinly sliced spring onions are scattered over the top, adding a pop of color and fresh contrast. The plate rests on a well-worn, warm-toned wooden dining table, suggesting a cozy, lived-in family kitchen setting. A casually placed, light-colored cloth napkin is visible in the background, along with the soft, warm glow of kitchen lighting, creating an inviting and homely atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Served immediately as an appetizer.
Can be accompanied by a small bowl of steamed rice for a more substantial snack.
instructions: Place pork belly in a saucepan. Cover with 500 ml water. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat. Simmer 45 minutes until tender.
Remove pork belly from water. Let cool completely. Pat dry thoroughly.
Cut pork belly into 2.5 cm cubes.

Heat vegetable oil in a large non-stick pan over medium-high heat. Add pork cubes, skin-side down first. Cook 8-10 minutes, turning often, until all sides are golden brown and crispy. Remove from pan. Drain excess fat.

In a small saucepan, combine soy sauce, honey, grated ginger, minced garlic, rice vinegar, and sesame oil. Bring to a simmer over medium heat. Cook 3-4 minutes, stirring, until sauce thickens slightly and becomes sticky.
Add crispy pork cubes to the sauce. Toss gently to coat all pieces evenly.
Serve immediately. Garnish with toasted sesame seeds and sliced spring onions.

recipes.recipe_name: Coffee-Crusted Pork Loin with Vanilla Cream Sauce
recipes.visual_description: A seared and roasted pork loin, cut into thick, succulent medallions, is arranged neatly on a clean white porcelain plate. The pork displays a rich, dark brown crust from the coffee rub, with a tender, pale pink interior visible on the cut surfaces. A creamy, light beige vanilla-infused pan sauce is generously drizzled over the pork and pools elegantly around it. Alongside, vibrant roasted root vegetables – golden potato wedges, bright orange carrot chunks, and creamy white parsnip chunks – are artfully placed, showing their slightly caramelized edges and tender textures. A sprinkle of fresh green thyme leaves adds a final touch of color and freshness. The dish is presented on a simple wooden table with natural, soft lighting, highlighting the appetizing textures and warm colors.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Prepare vegetables. Peel carrots and parsnips, cut into thick chunks. Cut potatoes into wedges. Toss vegetables with 15ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking sheet.
Combine ground coffee, brown sugar, smoked paprika, garlic powder, 5g salt, and 2g black pepper in a small bowl. This is the coffee rub.
Pat pork loin dry. Rub generously with the coffee mixture, ensuring full coverage.
Heat 15ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Sear pork loin on all sides until deep golden brown, about 2-3 minutes per side.

Transfer skillet with pork to the preheated oven. Add the baking sheet of vegetables to the oven. Roast pork and vegetables for 20-25 minutes, or until pork reaches an internal temperature of 63°C. Vegetables should be tender and lightly caramelized.
Remove pork from oven. Transfer to a cutting board. Tent with foil. Let rest for 10 minutes. Pork temperature will rise to 68-70°C.
While pork rests, make the sauce. Return skillet to medium heat. Add 15g butter. Add diced shallot. Cook until softened, about 2 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant. Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a simmer. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan.
Reduce heat to low. Whisk in softened cream cheese until smooth. Stir in vanilla extract and half of the fresh thyme.
Add remaining 45g butter, one tablespoon at a time, whisking constantly until fully incorporated and sauce is glossy. Season sauce with salt and pepper to taste.
Slice rested pork loin into thick medallions. Do not fan out slices.
Plate sliced pork with roasted vegetables. Spoon generous amount of vanilla cream sauce over the pork. Garnish with remaining fresh thyme.

recipes.recipe_name: Rustic Pork Meatballs in Tomato Sauce
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous starter portion of rustic pork meatballs is presented in a deep, off-white ceramic bowl, brimming with a rich, simmering tomato sauce. The meatballs, roughly spherical and browned from searing, are nestled closely, showcasing their hearty texture. Specks of fresh, chopped green parsley are sprinkled over the vibrant red sauce, adding a pop of color. The sauce itself appears thick and slightly chunky, clinging to the meatballs. Alongside the bowl, a thick slice of crusty, golden-brown artisan bread, torn rather than neatly cut, rests on a simple wooden board, inviting the diner to dip. The scene is set on a well-used, light wooden dining table, with warm, soft kitchen lighting illuminating the dish. A casually folded beige linen napkin and a simple silver fork complete the homely, inviting atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread for dipping
Sprinkle with extra grated Parmesan cheese
instructions: Finely dice onion and garlic. Roughly chop parsley.
In a large bowl, combine ground pork, breadcrumbs, egg, Parmesan, half of the chopped parsley, salt, and pepper. Mix by hand until just combined. Do not overmix.
Roll mixture into golf-ball sized meatballs. Make about 16-20 meatballs.
Heat olive oil in a large deep pan or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear meatballs in batches until browned on all sides. Do not overcrowd the pan. Remove browned meatballs and set aside.
Add diced onion to the same pan. Sauté 3-4 minutes until softened. Add finely diced garlic and dried oregano. Sauté 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in crushed tomatoes. Bring to a simmer. Season with a pinch more salt and pepper if needed.
Return seared meatballs to the pan. Ensure meatballs are mostly submerged in sauce.
Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer 20-25 minutes, or until meatballs are cooked through.
Garnish with remaining fresh parsley. Serve hot.
notes: These meatballs are excellent served as a starter with crusty bread.

recipes.recipe_name: Homestyle Pork and Potato Fritters
recipes.visual_description: A small portion of golden-brown Homestyle Pork and Potato Fritters is casually arranged on a simple, round, off-white ceramic plate. Two or three fritters, each roughly 6 cm in diameter and 2 cm thick, are slightly overlapping, showcasing their crispy, pan-fried exterior. The fritters have visible flecks of finely diced onion and grated carrot within their soft, mashed potato and ground pork interior. The plate rests on a well-used wooden dining table, revealing its natural grain. A simple, silver fork is placed to the side. The scene is illuminated by warm, natural light, creating a cozy, lived-in atmosphere typical of a family kitchen. No elaborate garnishes are present, emphasizing the dish's comforting, unpretentious nature.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve hot, optionally with a side of sour cream or chives.
instructions: Peel potatoes. Cut into 2 cm chunks. Boil in salted water until tender, about 15 minutes. Drain well. Mash until smooth.
Finely dice onion. Grate carrot.

Heat 15 ml vegetable oil in a large pan over medium heat. Add ground pork. Cook, breaking up with a spoon, until browned and cooked through, about 8-10 minutes. Drain excess fat. Remove pork from pan.
Add another 15 ml vegetable oil to the same pan. Add diced onion and grated carrot. Sauté until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
In a large bowl, combine mashed potatoes, cooked pork, sautéed onion and carrot, egg, and flour. Season with salt and black pepper. Mix well.
Form the mixture into 12 fritters, each about 6 cm in diameter and 2 cm thick.
Heat remaining 100 ml vegetable oil in a large non-stick pan over medium-high heat.
Fry fritters in batches, about 3-4 minutes per side, until golden brown and cooked through. Ensure they are heated through.
Transfer fritters to a plate lined with paper towel to drain excess oil.
Serve hot.
notes: Ensure fritters are golden and crispy on the outside.

recipes.recipe_name: Poulet Rôti à la Moutarde et sa Sauce Profonde, Pommes de Terre au Cheddar
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a simple, rustic white ceramic plate, embodying homely French comfort. A golden-brown, roasted chicken thigh, cooked until the skin is crisp and the meat tender, sits centrally. Alongside, chunky roasted potato wedges, their skins slightly blistered, are casually arranged. Some potatoes are lightly coated with melted, bubbling cheddar cheese. A rich, deep brown pan sauce, glossy and thick, is generously spooned over the chicken and around the potatoes, creating small pools. The plate is garnished with a scattering of freshly chopped flat-leaf parsley, providing a vibrant green contrast. The setting is a well-worn wooden kitchen table, with natural light. A plain linen napkin and simple flatware are casually placed. The presentation is unpretentious, focusing on hearty comfort.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple green salad dressed with vinaigrette.
Crusty baguette for dipping in the sauce.
A glass of red wine, such as a Beaujolais or a simple Bordeaux.

ingredients.name: Potatoes (e.g., Yukon Gold or Russet), cut into thick wedges
Dry red wine (e.g., Merlot or Pinot Noir)

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Pat chicken thighs dry. Rub chicken with 15g Dijon mustard, 15ml olive oil, 2g salt, and 1g black pepper.
Toss potato wedges with remaining 15ml olive oil, 3g salt, and 1g black pepper.
Place chicken and potatoes on a large baking tray. Ensure chicken skin is facing up.
Roast for 35-45 minutes. Chicken internal temperature must reach 75°C. Potatoes should be tender and golden.
While chicken roasts, prepare sauce. Heat a small saucepan over medium heat. Add finely diced pineapple. Cook until lightly caramelized, about 5 minutes. Remove pineapple and set aside.
Add shallots to the same pan. Sauté until softened, about 3 minutes. Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Deglaze pan with red wine. Scrape up any browned bits. Simmer for 2 minutes until reduced by half.
Stir in chicken stock, strong coffee, remaining 15g Dijon mustard, and the caramelized pineapple. Bring to a simmer.
Reduce heat to low. Stir in chopped dark chocolate and peanut butter. Whisk until melted and sauce is smooth. Simmer for 5-7 minutes, until sauce slightly thickens. Taste and adjust seasoning.
Five minutes before chicken is done, remove potatoes from oven. Sprinkle grated cheddar over potatoes. Return to oven for 5 minutes, until cheese is melted and bubbly.
Remove chicken and potatoes from oven. Let chicken rest for 5 minutes.
Plate chicken and potatoes. Spoon generous amount of sauce over chicken and potatoes. Garnish with fresh parsley. Serve immediately.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches 75°C internal temperature for food safety.
The small amount of chocolate and peanut butter in the sauce adds depth and richness without overpowering the classic French flavors.
Caramelizing the pineapple first mellows its sweetness and integrates it better into the savory sauce.

recipes.recipe_name: Caramelized Onion, Bacon & Gruyere Tartlets
recipes.visual_description: Four individual Caramelized Onion, Bacon & Gruyere Tartlets are presented on a rustic wooden serving board. Each tartlet features a golden, flaky puff pastry base with a slightly raised, well-defined crust. The center of each tartlet holds a generous, deeply caramelized onion filling, showcasing rich brown tones. Interspersed within the soft onions are crisp, diced bacon pieces, adding texture and a contrasting reddish-brown hue. Melted, bubbly Gruyere cheese forms a creamy, golden-brown layer over the filling. A few vibrant green fresh thyme sprigs are artfully placed on top of each tartlet for garnish, providing a fresh color pop. The tartlets are arranged with moderate negative space on the board. The background is a simple wooden table, illuminated by natural, even lighting, suggesting a relaxed bistro setting. The entire plate is visible, highlighting the professional yet approachable presentation.
instructions: Thinly slice yellow onions. Dice bacon into 1 cm pieces. Shred Gruyere cheese.
Heat butter and olive oil in a large pan over medium-low heat. Add sliced onions.
Cook onions slowly for 30-40 minutes. Stir occasionally. Onions should be deeply golden brown and very soft. This is caramelized onion.
While onions cook, cook diced bacon in a separate pan over medium heat. Cook until crisp. Drain bacon on paper towels.
Preheat oven to 190°C (375°F).
Unroll puff pastry. Cut into 8 equal rectangles or circles. Place pastry pieces on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper.
Score a 1 cm border around the edge of each pastry piece. Do not cut through.
In a bowl, whisk eggs and heavy cream. Season with salt and pepper.
Spread caramelized onions evenly over the center of each pastry piece, inside the scored border.
Sprinkle cooked bacon bits and shredded Gruyere cheese over the onions.
Pour egg mixture carefully over the cheese and bacon. Distribute evenly among tartlets.
Bake for 20-25 minutes. Pastry should be puffed and golden. Filling should be set and lightly browned.
Remove from oven. Garnish with fresh thyme sprigs. Serve warm.

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Pork with Root Vegetables
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of hearty Braised Pork with Root Vegetables is presented in a deep, clean white porcelain bowl. Tender, rich brown chunks of braised pork are nestled among creamy white potato wedges and vibrant orange carrot rounds. Each ingredient retains its distinct shape. The dish is enveloped in a glossy, dark amber braising liquid that coats the pork and vegetables. The sauce is thick but still flows gently around the components. A sparse scattering of freshly chopped bright green parsley is sprinkled over the top, providing a pop of fresh color. The bowl sits on a simple light wooden table surface. A neatly folded cream-colored cotton napkin and traditional silver flatware are placed beside the bowl. The setting is clean and uncluttered, with natural, even lighting from above, creating subtle shadows that add depth to the rustic yet refined presentation.
instructions: Trim excess fat from pork shoulder. Cut pork into 4-5 cm chunks. Pat dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven or heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat. Sear pork chunks in batches until deeply browned on all sides. Do not overcrowd the pot. Remove pork and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add chopped onions to the pot. Sauté until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes. Add minced garlic and tomato paste. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Pour in red wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Bring to a simmer. Cook until wine is reduced by half.
Return pork to the pot. Add chicken stock, fresh thyme sprigs, and bay leaves. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 1.5 hours.
Peel potatoes and carrots. Cut potatoes into 3-4 cm wedges. Cut carrots into thick 2 cm rounds.
Add potatoes and carrots to the pot. Stir gently. Continue to simmer, covered, for another 45-60 minutes, or until pork and vegetables are fork-tender. Ensure pork reaches 75°C (167°F).
Remove thyme sprigs and bay leaves. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper as needed.
Let the stew rest for 10 minutes before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Poulet Rôti Saveurs Moutarde & Café avec Pommes de Terre au Fromage
recipes.visual_description: A single roasted chicken thigh, golden and crisp-skinned from roasting, rests prominently on a rustic ceramic plate. Beside it is a generous mound of golden-brown roasted potato chunks, some with melted cheddar cheese clinging to their surfaces. Lightly browned pineapple pieces are interspersed among the potatoes. Pan juices, subtly deepened by the melted dark chocolate, naturally pool around the base of the chicken. A few fresh thyme sprigs are casually placed on top. The plate sits on a well-worn wooden dining table. A simple white linen napkin is casually folded beside it, with a traditional French fork and knife. Warm, inviting light from a nearby window illuminates the scene, creating soft shadows, evoking a homely kitchen atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve directly from the roasting dish at the table for a shared, homely experience.
Offer crusty baguette slices to sop up the flavorful pan juices.
Accompany with a simple green salad dressed with vinaigrette.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Pat chicken pieces dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
In a bowl, whisk together Dijon mustard and brewed coffee.
Toss chicken in mustard-coffee mixture. Marinate 15 minutes.
Wash potatoes. Cut into 3cm chunks. Toss with olive oil, salt, pepper, and smashed garlic. Add thyme sprigs.
Arrange potatoes, garlic, and thyme in a large roasting dish.
Place chicken pieces skin-side up among potatoes.
Roast for 30 minutes.
Cut pineapple into 2cm chunks. Add to the roasting dish. Stir potatoes and pineapple.
Continue roasting for another 20-25 minutes, or until chicken reaches 75°C internal temperature and skin is golden and crisp.
Remove dish from oven. Sprinkle grated cheddar over potatoes and chicken.
Finely chop dark chocolate. Scatter over hot pan juices. Stir gently to combine into the pan sauce.
Rest chicken 5 minutes before serving.
notes: The small amount of dark chocolate adds depth and color to the pan sauce, not sweetness.
The pineapple offers a subtle sweet and acidic counterpoint to the savory chicken and potatoes.

recipes.recipe_name: Stuffed Chicken Breast with Beef and Cheddar
recipes.visual_description: A single, generously portioned stuffed chicken breast sits prominently on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The chicken, with its golden-brown, seared crust, is presented as a whole, plump piece, showcasing its inviting texture. Beside it, a vibrant, smooth orange quenelle of carrot and onion puree provides a striking color contrast. The puree's silky texture is evident, catching the light. A delicate sprig of fresh parsley garnishes the plate, adding a touch of green. The overall plating is professional, with moderate negative space, allowing each element to stand out. The scene is set on a simple wooden table, with natural, even lighting, creating a warm, inviting bistro atmosphere. A folded cotton napkin rests beside the plate, completing the refined yet approachable presentation.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a light side salad or steamed green beans.
Pair with a crisp white wine like Chardonnay or Sauvignon Blanc.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C (375°F).
Dice half of the onion finely. Mince garlic.
In a pan, heat 1 tablespoon olive oil. Sauté diced onion until softened, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic; cook 1 minute more.
Transfer sautéed onion and garlic to a bowl. Add ground beef, grated cheddar, parsley, breadcrumbs, egg, 1/2 teaspoon salt, and 1/4 teaspoon pepper. Mix thoroughly until combined.
Pat chicken breasts dry. Using a sharp knife, butterfly each chicken breast: make a horizontal cut almost all the way through, opening it like a book.
Season the inside and outside of each chicken breast with salt and pepper.

Divide the beef and cheese mixture into four equal portions. Place one portion onto one half of each butterflied chicken breast. Fold the other half over the filling. Secure with toothpicks if needed.
In an oven-safe skillet, heat 2 tablespoons olive oil over medium-high heat. Carefully place stuffed chicken breasts in the skillet. Sear for 3-4 minutes per side, until golden brown.
Transfer the skillet with chicken to the preheated oven. Roast for 15-20 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F) at the thickest part.
While chicken roasts, prepare carrot and onion puree. Peel and chop carrots into 1cm rounds. Chop remaining half onion into large chunks.
In a saucepan, melt 25g butter over medium heat. Add chopped carrots and onion. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until slightly softened.
Pour in chicken stock. Bring to a simmer. Cover and cook for 15-20 minutes, or until carrots are very tender.

Carefully transfer cooked carrots and onions with cooking liquid to a blender. Add remaining 25g butter and heavy cream. Blend until completely smooth and creamy. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Remove chicken from oven. Let rest 5 minutes before serving. Remove toothpicks.
Spoon a generous portion of carrot and onion puree onto each plate. Place one stuffed chicken breast beside the puree. Serve immediately.
notes: Ensure chicken is fully cooked to 75°C (167°F) internal temperature.
Do not overfill chicken breasts to prevent stuffing from escaping during cooking.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken and Cauliflower Bake with Crispy Bacon and Parmesan
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of the Chicken and Cauliflower Bake is presented in a rustic, deep ceramic bowl. The top crust is a rich, golden-brown from the baked parmesan, with visible crispy, dark brown crumbled bacon scattered across. Beneath the crust, creamy white sauce envelops tender, light-yellow cauliflower florets and irregular, rough chunks of cooked chicken. The textures are varied: crisp bacon, soft cauliflower, moist chicken, and a smooth, bubbly sauce. The bowl sits on a well-used, warm-toned wooden dining table. A simple metal fork rests beside the bowl on a casually folded beige linen napkin. Warm, inviting kitchen lighting illuminates the scene, creating a cozy, homely atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve hot from the oven.
Accompanied by crusty bread or a simple green salad.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.
Poach chicken breasts in simmering water for 15-20 minutes, until cooked through. Internal temperature must reach 75°C. Cool slightly. Shred chicken into rough chunks.
Cut cauliflower into medium florets. Steam or boil florets until tender-crisp, about 5-7 minutes. Drain well.
Cook bacon in a large pan over medium heat until crispy. Remove bacon, drain on paper towels. Crumble bacon. Reserve 2 tablespoons for topping.
Melt butter in a saucepan over medium heat. Stir in flour. Cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly, to form a roux.
Gradually whisk in milk until smooth. Continue whisking until sauce thickens, about 5-7 minutes.
Stir in 75 g of the grated parmesan, salt, pepper, and nutmeg.
Combine shredded chicken, cauliflower florets, and the cheese sauce in a large baking dish.
Sprinkle remaining 25 g parmesan and reserved crumbled bacon over the top.
Bake for 20-25 minutes, or until golden brown and bubbly.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Beef Medallions with Smoked Cheddar and Bacon Crumble
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate, set on a simple light wooden table surface in a modern bistro setting. A single thick-cut, pan-seared beef medallion, displaying a rich, deep brown crust from searing, rests slightly off-center. Its interior, if slightly visible, suggests a tender, juicy texture. A glossy, dark brown pan sauce is artfully spooned under and around the base of the beef, creating a subtle pool. Generously sprinkled over the top of the beef medallion and spilling slightly onto the sauce is a vibrant crumble of golden-crisp, finely diced bacon intermingled with melted, orange-yellow smoked cheddar cheese. The warmth of the cheese creates a soft, inviting texture against the crisp bacon. Freshly chopped bright green parsley is sprinkled over the crumble, providing a pop of color and freshness. The overall composition is professional yet approachable, with moderate negative space. Standard silver flatware (fork and knife) is neatly placed beside the plate, with a folded natural cotton napkin nearby. The scene is illuminated by natural, even lighting, highlighting the textures and colors of the food with minimal background distractions.
instructions: Dice bacon into small pieces. Cook in a dry pan over medium heat until crispy. Remove bacon with a slotted spoon. Drain excess fat, reserving 15ml.
Grate smoked cheddar cheese. Combine grated cheese with crispy bacon bits. Set aside.
Pat beef sirloin dry. Cut into 4 thick-cut medallions, about 150g each. Season generously with salt and black pepper.

Heat olive oil and reserved bacon fat in a large pan over medium-high heat. Sear beef medallions for 3-4 minutes per side for medium-rare, or until desired doneness is reached. Cook to internal temperature of 70°C (158°F) for medium-well, or 75°C (167°F) for well-done.
Remove beef from pan. Rest on a cutting board, tented with foil.
Add butter to the same pan. Sauté finely diced shallots until softened, about 2 minutes. Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in beef broth. Bring to a simmer, scraping up browned bits from the bottom of the pan. Reduce liquid by half, about 3-5 minutes, until slightly thickened.

To serve, place a beef medallion on each plate. Spoon a generous amount of pan sauce over and around the beef. Sprinkle the smoked cheddar and bacon crumble generously over each medallion. Garnish with chopped fresh parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Walnut & Tatsoi Broth with Kudzu Gel and Egg Cloud
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of clear, amber-hued broth is presented in a handcrafted, unglazed ceramic bowl in a soft cream color. The broth's surface holds a delicate, ethereal cloud of bright white egg white, light and airy. Submerged gently in the broth are a few translucent, shimmering 1 cm cubes of kudzu gel, catching the light. Vibrant dark green tatsoi leaves, freshly picked, float gracefully on the broth, providing a natural color contrast. A subtle shimmer of verjus is visible on the surface. The bowl is set on a light, textured reclaimed wood surface, accompanied by a natural beige undyed linen napkin. Soft, diffused natural light illuminates the dish, emphasizing its purity and simple elegance. The background is clean and minimalist, featuring subtle natural textures or a hint of green foliage.

ingredients.name: Vegetable scraps (onion skins, carrot peels, celery ends)
Fermented vegetable brine (e.g., from sauerkraut or pickles)

instructions: Separate tatsoi leaves from stems. Set leaves aside. Combine walnuts, tatsoi stems, vegetable scraps, water, and peppercorns in a large pot. Bring to a simmer. Cook gently for 45 minutes.
Strain broth through a fine-mesh sieve. Discard solids. Return strained broth to a clean pot. Stir in fermented vegetable brine. Keep warm; do not boil. Season with salt.

Whisk kudzu starch with 100 ml cold water until smooth. Pour into a small saucepan. Heat over medium-low, stirring constantly, until mixture thickens and becomes translucent. Spread kudzu mixture evenly on a small, lightly oiled plate. Chill until firm, about 30 minutes. Cut into 1 cm cubes.
Whisk egg whites vigorously in a clean bowl until soft peaks form.
Gently ladle hot broth into serving bowls. Carefully place a few kudzu gel cubes into each bowl. Spoon a delicate cloud of whisked egg white onto the surface of the broth.
Drizzle each serving with 5 ml verjus. Garnish with fresh tatsoi leaves. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Chicken and Butternut Squash
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of Roasted Chicken and Butternut Squash rests on a rustic, round ceramic plate with an earthy, muted tone. A golden-brown, crispy-skinned chicken thigh is the centerpiece, positioned naturally. Alongside it are irregularly shaped, tender 2-3 cm chunks of roasted butternut squash, exhibiting vibrant orange hues and slight caramelization. Thick, tender red onion wedges, softened and slightly charred at the edges, intersperse with the squash. A few whole, creamy roasted garlic cloves are nestled among the vegetables. Freshly chopped parsley is sprinkled over the dish, adding a pop of green. The arrangement is casual, with components touching and overlapping, reflecting a homely plating style. The plate sits on a well-used wooden dining table. A simple metal fork and knife are placed beside the plate. A casually folded linen napkin completes the inviting, lived-in scene under warm, cozy kitchen lighting. The entire plate is visible, with adequate negative space around the food.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Line a large baking tray with parchment paper.
Peel butternut squash. Cut squash into 2-3 cm chunks.
Peel red onion. Cut onion into thick wedges.
Do not peel garlic cloves.
In a large bowl, combine chicken thighs, squash chunks, onion wedges, and whole garlic cloves.
Drizzle with olive oil. Add dried rosemary, dried thyme, salt, and black pepper. Toss to coat all ingredients evenly.
Spread ingredients in a single layer on the prepared baking tray. Do not overcrowd the tray.
Roast for 30 minutes. Flip chicken and vegetables.
Continue roasting for another 20-30 minutes, or until chicken skin is golden and crispy, squash is tender, and chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove from oven. Let rest for 5 minutes.
Roughly chop fresh parsley. Sprinkle over the roasted chicken and vegetables before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Tomato Chicken Pasta
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Creamy Tomato Chicken Pasta is presented on a clean, white porcelain dinner plate, centrally placed on a simple wooden table. The penne pasta is coated in a luscious, creamy reddish-orange tomato sauce, forming a gently mounded pile. Nestled within and atop the pasta are several golden-brown, seared chicken medallions, cut into thick, substantial chunks, showcasing their tender interior. The dish is garnished with vibrant green chopped fresh parsley, providing a fresh contrast. The overall presentation is clean and professional, with moderate negative space around the food. A standard silver fork and knife rest beside the plate on a white cotton napkin. The scene is illuminated by natural, even lighting, creating a casual yet refined bistro atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with standard flatware.
instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season with salt and pepper.

Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken breasts 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked to an internal temperature of 75°C. Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside. Let rest 5 minutes.
Cook penne pasta according to package directions until al dente. Drain, reserving 100 ml pasta water.
Dice onion. Mince garlic. Add remaining 15 ml olive oil to the same skillet. Sauté diced onion 3-4 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic and smoked paprika. Sauté 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in crushed tomatoes and chicken broth. Bring to a simmer. Cook 5 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Reduce heat to low. Stir in heavy cream and American cheese slices until cheese is fully melted and sauce is smooth.
Add cooked pasta to the sauce. Toss to coat evenly. If sauce is too thick, add reserved pasta water gradually until desired consistency is reached.
Slice rested chicken breasts into thick medallions or substantial chunks.
Serve pasta onto plates. Arrange chicken medallions on top of the pasta. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Umami Harvest Plate
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a handcrafted, cream-toned ceramic plate with ample negative space. Two seared beef medallions, their surfaces caramelized with a rich miso glaze, anchor the center. Alongside, several golden-brown, pan-fried 2cm cubes of fermented tofu offer a contrasting texture. Dashi-braised seasonal vegetables are arranged naturally: vibrant green bok choy halves, tender 1cm thick diagonal carrot slices, and whole shiitake mushrooms, their earthy tones highlighted by the dashi's gentle sheen. A delicate scattering of thinly sliced fresh ginger and a sprinkle of toasted sesame seeds add subtle accents. The composition is organic and unforced, celebrating the natural beauty of each ingredient. The plate rests on a light reclaimed wood surface, accompanied by simple wooden chopsticks and a small, unglazed rice bowl. Soft, natural light illuminates the scene, enhancing the food's authentic colors.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of steamed brown rice.
Offer a small bowl of clear dashi broth as a light accompaniment.
instructions: Prepare dashi stock: Combine kombu and katsuobushi with water. Heat gently. Strain. Alternatively, prepare dashi from powder per package instructions.
Make miso glaze: Whisk together 40g miso paste, 30ml soy sauce, mirin, and sake (if using). Grate half of the fresh ginger into the glaze.
Marinate beef: Pat beef sirloin dry. Cut into thick medallions, approximately 2-3 cm thick. Coat beef medallions with half of the miso glaze. Marinate for 15 minutes.

Prepare dashi-braised vegetables: In a large pot, combine dashi stock, remaining 20g miso paste, and 30ml soy sauce. Bring to a simmer. Peel carrots and cut into 1cm thick diagonal slices. Remove stems from shiitake mushrooms. Add carrots and shiitake to the simmering dashi. Simmer for 5 minutes. Halve bok choy lengthwise. Add bok choy to the pot. Simmer until vegetables are crisp-tender. Remove vegetables, keep warm. Reserve dashi broth.
Cook tofu: Cut fermented tofu into 2cm cubes. Heat sesame oil in a pan over medium heat. Pan-fry tofu cubes until lightly golden on all sides. Set aside.
Sear beef: Heat vegetable oil in a skillet over medium-high heat. Sear marinated beef medallions for 3-4 minutes per side until well browned and internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Glaze beef: Add remaining miso glaze to the pan with the seared beef. Cook for 1-2 minutes, spooning glaze over beef, until slightly thickened.

Plate: Arrange seared beef medallions, pan-fried fermented tofu, and dashi-braised vegetables artfully on individual plates. Drizzle with some reserved dashi broth. Thinly slice the remaining fresh ginger for garnish. Garnish with thinly sliced fresh ginger and toasted sesame seeds. Serve immediately.
notes: Utilize vegetable trimmings when making dashi from scratch to minimize food waste.
Choose locally sourced, seasonal vegetables for optimal flavor and sustainability.

recipes.recipe_name: Bacon and Gruyère Stuffed Chicken Breast
recipes.visual_description: A single, elegantly plated Bacon and Gruyère Stuffed Chicken Breast rests on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The golden-brown seared chicken breast is presented whole, cut diagonally in half to reveal the rich, melted Gruyère cheese, crispy diced bacon, and tender caramelized onion filling. A small pool of glistening pan sauce lightly coats the plate beneath and around the chicken. Beside the chicken, a neat pile of roasted baby potatoes, quartered, displays a soft, golden exterior. The dish is garnished simply with a sprinkle of bright green chopped chives over the chicken. The composition is balanced, leaving moderate negative space on the plate. The setting features a simple wooden table surface, a grey cotton napkin folded beside the plate, and subtle, natural, even lighting that highlights the textures and colors of the dish. The background suggests a modern bistro, clean and unobtrusive.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C (375°F).
Dice bacon into small pieces. Cook bacon in a large oven-safe skillet over medium heat until crispy. Remove bacon with a slotted spoon. Reserve 15 ml bacon fat in the skillet. Drain excess fat.

Finely dice the yellow onion. Add onion to the skillet with reserved bacon fat. Cook over medium-low heat for 8-10 minutes until caramelized and soft. Stir in cooked bacon and fresh thyme. Remove from heat. Let cool slightly.
Stir shredded Gruyère cheese into the bacon and onion mixture. Set aside.
Place each chicken breast between two sheets of plastic wrap. Pound chicken to an even 1 cm thickness using a meat mallet or rolling pin.
Spoon a quarter of the bacon-cheese mixture onto one end of each pounded chicken breast. Roll chicken tightly to enclose the filling. Secure with toothpicks if needed.

Heat 15 ml olive oil in the same skillet over medium-high heat. Season chicken rolls with salt and pepper. Sear chicken for 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown. Do not overcrowd the skillet; sear in batches if necessary.
Transfer skillet to the preheated oven. Bake for 15-20 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Remove toothpicks.

While chicken bakes, prepare the pan sauce. Carefully drain any excess fat from the skillet. Deglaze the skillet with white wine, scraping up any browned bits. Reduce by half. Add chicken stock. Bring to a simmer and reduce by one-third. Stir in butter until melted. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve chicken immediately. Spoon pan sauce over each portion. Garnish with chopped fresh chives.

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Beef with Root Vegetables
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of hearty Braised Beef with Root Vegetables is presented in a deep, pristine white porcelain bowl, centered on a rustic wooden table. Large, fork-tender chunks of braised beef, boasting a rich, dark brown hue, are nestled amongst substantial pieces of roasted carrots and parsnips. The vegetables are cut into thick, irregular chunks, retaining their vibrant orange and creamy white colors. A generous pool of glossy, dark brown braising liquid, thickened to a luxurious consistency, envelops the ingredients. The dish is elegantly garnished with a light sprinkling of freshly chopped bright green flat-leaf parsley, adding a touch of freshness. The overall presentation is clean, professional, and inviting, with moderate negative space. Beside the bowl, a neatly folded white cotton napkin and classic silver flatware suggest a refined, casual dining experience.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread to soak up the rich sauce
Pair with mashed potatoes or creamy polenta
instructions: Preheat oven to 160°C.
Pat beef chunks dry. Season beef generously with salt and black pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear beef in batches until deeply browned on all sides. Do not overcrowd the pot. Remove seared beef from pot. Set aside.
Add chopped onion, carrots, and celery to the pot. Sauté 5-7 minutes until softened.
Add smashed garlic and tomato paste. Cook 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Stir in flour. Cook 1 minute, stirring.
Pour in red wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot with a wooden spoon. Bring to a simmer.
Add beef stock, thyme sprigs, and bay leaves. Return seared beef to the pot. Ensure beef is mostly submerged in liquid.
Bring the liquid to a gentle simmer. Cover pot tightly with a lid.
Transfer pot to preheated oven. Braise 2 hours.
If using, add parsnips (cut into thick chunks) to the pot. Stir gently.
Continue braising 1-1.5 hours, or until beef is fork-tender and vegetables are cooked through.
Remove thyme sprigs and bay leaves before serving.
Taste and adjust seasoning if needed.
notes: For best results, use a good quality dry red wine like Cabernet Sauvignon or Merlot. Avoid cooking wines.
Beef chuck, short ribs, or brisket are excellent cuts for braising due to their marbling and connective tissue that breaks down into tender, flavorful meat.

recipes.recipe_name: Mexican Beef & Ancho Chili Stew
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of Mexican Beef & Ancho Chili Stew is presented in a deep, rustic, matte-glazed ceramic bowl, showcasing its rich, inviting colors. The stew features tender, dark reddish-brown beef chunks, approximately 3-4 cm, nestled among vibrant orange diced carrots and soft, deep red tomato fragments. The thick, savory sauce, infused with rehydrated ancho chilies, coats the ingredients evenly, exhibiting a subtle sheen. A generous sprinkle of bright green, freshly chopped cilantro garnishes the top, adding a fresh contrast. The bowl sits on a simple, light-colored wooden table surface, accompanied by a clean white porcelain side plate holding a stack of warm, soft corn tortillas. A dark grey cotton napkin is folded neatly beside the bowl. The scene is illuminated by natural, even lighting from the side, creating soft shadows and highlighting the stew's hearty texture and rich color palette. The background is clean and slightly blurred, suggesting a casual bistro atmosphere, allowing the dish to remain the focal point. The presentation is organized but not overly arranged, emphasizing a professional yet approachable restaurant style.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Warm corn tortillas
A side of Mexican rice
A dollop of crema or sour cream
Pickled red onions
instructions: Rehydrate ancho chilies: Place dried ancho chilies in a bowl. Cover with hot water. Soak 20 minutes until soft. Drain. Remove stems and seeds.

Sear beef: Heat olive oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Season beef chunks with salt and pepper. Sear beef in batches until browned on all sides. Remove beef from pot. Set aside.
Sauté aromatics: Add diced onions to the pot. Cook 5-7 minutes until softened and translucent. Add minced garlic and diced carrots. Cook 3 minutes more.
Build flavor base: Add rehydrated ancho chilies, chopped tomatoes, minced jalapeño (if using), cumin powder, and dried oregano to the pot. Cook 5 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Simmer stew: Return seared beef to the pot. Pour in beef broth. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer 2.5-3 hours, or until beef is very tender. Stir occasionally.
Thicken (optional): If a thicker stew is desired, mix masa harina or cornstarch with 30 ml cold water to form a slurry. Stir into the simmering stew. Cook 5 minutes, stirring, until thickened.
Adjust seasoning: Taste the stew. Add more salt and pepper if needed.
Serve: Ladle hot stew into bowls. Garnish with fresh chopped cilantro.
notes: For deeper flavor, roast the fresh tomatoes and chilies before adding to the stew.
The stew improves in flavor the next day.

recipes.recipe_name: Pasta alla Norma
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of rigatoni pasta is presented in a wide, shallow white porcelain bowl. Each tube of pasta is evenly coated in a vibrant, glossy tomato sauce. Large 2cm cubes of eggplant, fried to a rich golden-brown with visible caramelized edges, are distributed throughout the dish. A central mound of snow-white Ricotta Salata is coarsely grated over the top, providing a sharp textural contrast. Three fresh, deep green basil leaves are placed intentionally off-center. The bowl sits on a dark walnut wood table under soft, natural side lighting. A neutral grey cotton napkin and a polished silver fork rest beside the bowl. The arrangement is clean, focusing on the vivid red, white, and green colors.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a glass of Nero d'Avola red wine
Present with extra Ricotta Salata on the side
Provide crusty bread to clean the sauce
instructions: Cut eggplant into 2cm cubes.
Sprinkle cubes with salt. Let sit for 30 minutes.
Rinse eggplant and pat dry with paper towels.
Heat 200ml olive oil in a pan. Fry eggplant cubes until golden brown.
Drain eggplant on paper towels. Set aside.
Mince garlic cloves.
Heat 15ml olive oil in a large skillet. Sauté garlic for 1 minute.
Add tomato passata. Simmer on low heat for 15 minutes.
Boil 4 liters of salted water. Cook rigatoni until al dente.
Drain pasta. Reserve 50ml pasta water.
Add pasta and half the eggplant to the sauce.
Toss over heat for 1 minute. Add pasta water if dry.
Plate pasta. Top with remaining eggplant.
Grate ricotta salata over the top. Garnish with basil.
notes: Ensure eggplant is dried thoroughly before frying to achieve a crisp texture.
Use aged Ricotta Salata, not fresh ricotta, for the authentic salty flavor profile.
Do not overcook the pasta; it must maintain a firm bite.

recipes.recipe_name: Caramelized Onion and Potato Financiers with Garlic-Honey Drizzle
recipes.visual_description: A single, golden-brown financier rests elegantly on a pristine white porcelain plate. The financier, slightly domed with a delicate crisp edge, reveals a tender, moist interior with subtle flecks of caramelized onion and grated potato. A glossy, amber roasted garlic and honey drizzle artfully pools beside it and lightly coats the top. A scattering of finely chopped, golden-brown crispy chicken skin crumble provides a contrasting texture and a unique savory-sweet note. The plate sits on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by a folded white cotton napkin and a polished silver fork. Natural, even lighting highlights the financier's inviting warmth and the delicate sheen of the glaze. The overall presentation is clean, minimalist, and inviting, showcasing the innovative dessert.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C. Grease and flour financier molds.
Thinly slice onions. Cook in a pan with a little butter over low heat for 45-60 minutes until deeply caramelized and sweet. Puree lightly if desired, set aside.
Render chicken skin in a dry pan over medium-low heat until very crispy and golden. Remove skin, drain fat. Chop crispy skin finely. Toss with a pinch of salt and sugar, set aside.
Roast whole garlic head at 180°C for 30-40 minutes until cloves are soft. Squeeze out cloves. Mash with honey and 15ml water to form a smooth drizzle.
Grate potatoes finely. Squeeze out excess moisture thoroughly using a clean cloth.
Brown the 150g unsalted butter in a saucepan until nutty and golden. Strain to remove solids, cool slightly.
In a bowl, whisk almond flour, all-purpose flour, and powdered sugar. Add egg whites and mix until combined. Fold in grated potato and pureed caramelized onion.
Gradually whisk in the cooled browned butter until the batter is smooth.
Pour batter into prepared financier molds, filling about two-thirds full. This recipe makes 8-10 financiers.
Bake for 15-20 minutes, or until golden brown and a skewer inserted comes out clean. Cool in molds for a few minutes, then transfer to a wire rack to cool completely.
To serve, place 2-3 financiers per plate. Drizzle generously with the garlic-honey mixture. Sprinkle with crispy chicken skin crumble.
notes: This dessert explores the boundaries of sweet and savory, utilizing traditionally savory ingredients in a refined, dessert-focused preparation.

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Chicken with Tomato, Olives, and Thyme
recipes.visual_description: A single golden-brown braised chicken thigh, skin-on, is centered on a round white porcelain dinner plate. It is generously spooned with a rustic, rich red tomato and Kalamata olive sauce. The sauce features whole, burst cherry tomatoes and plump, dark olives, with visible specks of fresh green thyme and red chili flakes. A fresh sprig of thyme rests atop the chicken. A light drizzle of vibrant green olive oil completes the dish. The plate is presented on a simple light wooden table. A crisp white cotton napkin is folded neatly beside the plate, and a small bowl of crusty, artisanal bread is placed nearby, inviting a traditional Mediterranean dining experience. Lighting is natural and even, highlighting the dish's warmth and texture.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread for dipping in the sauce.
Accompanied by a simple green salad.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat 15ml olive oil in a large, oven-safe pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs skin-side down for 6-8 minutes until golden and crispy. Flip and sear for 2 minutes. Remove chicken from pan. Reserve rendered fat.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion to pan. Sauté for 5 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic and sliced chili. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in white wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan. Simmer for 2 minutes until reduced by half.
Add cherry tomatoes, Kalamata olives, 4 thyme sprigs, and chicken broth to the pan. Bring to a simmer.
Return chicken thighs to the pan, skin-side up. Ensure chicken is partially submerged in the sauce.
Cover the pan. Transfer to a preheated oven at 180°C (350°F).
Braise for 25-30 minutes, or until internal temperature of chicken reaches 75°C (167°F).
Remove from oven. Discard thyme sprigs from sauce. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Serve immediately, garnished with fresh thyme.

recipes.recipe_name: Seared Beef Medallions with Roasted Cauliflower & Ginger-Scallion Dressing
recipes.visual_description: A single individual portion of a modern, low-calorie main course. The dish is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate, centered on a simple light wooden table surface. A thick, roasted cauliflower steak, with a tender interior and lightly caramelized, golden-brown edges, forms the base.
