recipes.recipe_name: Plant-Based Ragu with Creamy Polenta
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of plant-based ragu with creamy polenta is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. The creamy, golden-yellow polenta forms a smooth, fluid base, naturally spread across the plate. Generous spoonfuls of rich, deep red-brown plant-based ragu are heaped over the center of the polenta. The ragu features visible, textured chunks of browned plant-based mincemeat intertwined with finely diced, softened carrots, celery, and onions. A few vibrant green fresh basil leaves are scattered artfully over the ragu, providing a pop of color and freshness. The dish is presented on a simple wooden table surface, with natural, even lighting. Standard silver flatware is placed neatly beside the plate, and a white cotton napkin rests nearby. The background is minimally blurred, suggesting a casual bistro setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread for dipping.
instructions: Dice onion, carrot, celery. Mince garlic.
Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add diced onion, carrot, celery. Cook 8-10 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute.
Add plant-based mincemeat. Break it up. Cook 5-7 minutes until browned.
Add red wine or 100 ml vegetable broth. Scrape pot to deglaze. Simmer 3 minutes until reduced by half.
Stir in crushed tomatoes, remaining 200 ml vegetable broth, dried oregano. Season with salt, pepper.
Bring ragu to a gentle simmer. Reduce heat to low. Cover. Cook 30-60 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Prepare polenta. Bring 1 litre water or plant-based milk to boil in saucepan. Season with salt.
Whisk in polenta slowly. Reduce heat to low.
Cook polenta, stirring frequently, 15-20 minutes until creamy. Add hot water if too thick.
Stir plant-based butter and nutritional yeast into polenta. Adjust seasoning.
Spoon polenta onto plates. Top with ragu.
Garnish with fresh basil.

recipes.recipe_name: Pohana Piletina i Prženi Krumpir (Breaded Chicken and Fried Potatoes)
recipes.visual_description: A generous, rustic platter of golden-brown, crispy breaded chicken strips and perfectly fried potato wedges. The chicken pieces are irregularly shaped, showcasing their natural form, not fanned or neatly arranged. The potato wedges are golden with slightly blistered skins, scattered around the chicken. A light scattering of vibrant green, finely chopped fresh parsley provides a color contrast. The dish is presented on a simple, well-used wooden dining table. Everyday ceramic plates, possibly with minor imperfections, are stacked nearby. A casually placed, light-colored cloth napkin is draped to one side. The lighting is warm and inviting, typical of a cozy family kitchen, emphasizing the comforting, unpretentious nature of the snack. Portions are ample, inviting casual sharing.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and vinegar.
Offer a side of ajvar or mayonnaise for dipping.
Enjoy as a hearty snack or light meal with family and friends.
instructions: Cut chicken breast into 2 cm thick strips. Season chicken with salt, pepper, and paprika.
Prepare breading station: Place flour in one shallow dish, beaten eggs in a second, and breadcrumbs in a third.
Dredge each chicken strip in flour, shaking off excess. Dip in beaten egg, then coat thoroughly in breadcrumbs. Press breadcrumbs gently to adhere.
Wash and peel potatoes. Cut potatoes into 1.5 cm thick wedges.
Heat vegetable oil in a large deep pan or pot to 170°C. Do not overcrowd the pan.
Fry potato wedges in batches for 6-8 minutes. Fry until golden brown and tender inside. Drain on paper towels. Season with salt immediately.
Increase oil temperature to 175°C. Fry breaded chicken strips in batches for 4-6 minutes. Fry until golden brown and cooked through. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C. Drain on paper towels.
Chop fresh parsley finely.
Arrange fried chicken and potato wedges on a large serving platter. Sprinkle generously with fresh parsley. Serve hot with lemon wedges on the side.
notes: For extra crispness, use Panko breadcrumbs.
Do not overcrowd the frying pan; fry in batches to maintain oil temperature and ensure even cooking.
Adjust salt and pepper to your preference.

recipes.recipe_name: Greek Mincemeat Keftedes with Tomato Sauce and Orzo
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Greek Mincemeat Keftedes with Tomato Sauce and Orzo is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, centered on a simple wooden table surface. A neat mound of pale yellow orzo pasta forms the base. Several golden-brown, spherical keftedes (meatballs) are nestled atop the orzo, partially submerged in a rich, deep red tomato sauce that clings to the meatballs and pasta. The sauce is vibrant, with a slight sheen. The dish is garnished generously with vibrant green, finely chopped fresh parsley and a few small sprigs of fresh mint, adding a burst of color and freshness. A scattering of white, crumbly feta cheese provides textural contrast. The overall composition is balanced and appealing, with moderate negative space. Silver flatware is placed beside the plate. A folded white cotton napkin rests nearby. The scene is lit with natural, even light, creating a inviting, casual dining atmosphere. A small traditional Greek bowl containing extra crumbled feta and a sprig of mint sits subtly in the background, enhancing cultural authenticity without distracting from the main dish.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread (psomi) for dipping into the sauce.
Pair with a simple Greek salad (Horiatiki Salata) on the side.
Enjoy with a glass of dry white Greek wine or retsina.
instructions: Finely grate half the onion. Mince 2 cloves of garlic.

In a large bowl, combine beef mincemeat, lamb mincemeat, grated onion, minced garlic, breadcrumbs, egg, half the dried oregano, half the chopped fresh mint, half the chopped fresh parsley, 1 tsp salt, and 1/2 tsp black pepper. Mix until just combined. Do not overmix.
Form the mixture into 20-24 spherical meatballs (keftedes), about 4 cm in diameter.
Heat 2 tbsp olive oil in a large deep pan or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear the meatballs in batches until browned on all sides. Do not cook through. Remove meatballs and set aside.
Finely dice the remaining half onion. Mince the remaining 2 cloves of garlic.
Add the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil to the pan. Add diced onion and sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
If using, pour in red wine and scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan. Simmer until reduced by half.
Stir in crushed tomatoes, remaining dried oregano, remaining salt and pepper, and sugar. Bring to a simmer.

Carefully return the seared meatballs to the sauce. Ensure they are mostly submerged. Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 25-30 minutes, or until meatballs reach an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F). Stir occasionally.
While meatballs simmer, cook orzo pasta according to package directions in salted water until al dente. Drain well.
Serve the Greek mincemeat keftedes and tomato sauce over a bed of cooked orzo. Garnish with crumbled feta cheese, fresh chopped parsley, and fresh mint.
traditional_techniques: Simmering a rich tomato-based sauce (kokkinisto style)

recipes.recipe_name: Croatian Roasted Chicken and Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Croatian Roasted Chicken and Potatoes is presented on a simple, round ceramic plate with a natural, slightly imperfect finish. The plate sits on a well-used wooden dining table. A golden-brown, crispy-skinned roasted chicken thigh is the centerpiece, positioned naturally. Around it are large, irregular chunks of roasted potatoes, some with caramelized edges, along with soft, tender roasted onion quarters and whole roasted garlic cloves. The chicken skin is visibly crisp, showcasing its rich, deep brown color. The potatoes vary in color from golden to deeper brown. The dish appears hearty and comforting, with a few fresh parsley leaves roughly chopped and sprinkled over, adding a pop of green. A simple cloth napkin is casually placed beside the plate. The scene is lit by warm, natural kitchen lighting, creating a cozy family dining atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and vinegar.
Accompany with crusty bread for soaking up the pan juices.
Enjoy with a glass of local Croatian red wine.

ingredients.name: Chicken thighs with bone and skin

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Prepare a large roasting pan.
Pat chicken thighs dry. In a bowl, toss chicken with 30 ml olive oil, paprika, salt, and pepper. Rub well to coat.
Peel potatoes. Cut potatoes into thick 4 cm chunks. Peel and quarter the onion. Peel garlic cloves; leave whole.
Add potatoes, onion, and garlic to the roasting pan. Drizzle with remaining 30 ml olive oil, season with salt and pepper. Toss to coat.
Place seasoned chicken thighs on top of the vegetables in the roasting pan. Tuck bay leaves among the ingredients.
Pour chicken broth or water into the bottom of the pan.
Roast for 45 minutes. Turn chicken and potatoes. Continue roasting for 20-30 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C and potatoes are tender and golden-brown.
Rest chicken for 5 minutes before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Chiles Rellenos de Picadillo con Salsa Roja
recipes.visual_description: A single Chiles Rellenos de Picadillo rests on a clean white porcelain plate, centered on a vibrant, smooth pool of red-orange tomato-chipotle salsa. The poblano pepper is plump from its savory mincemeat filling, encased in a delicate, golden-fried egg batter (capeado) with a slightly irregular, puffed texture. Visible through the pepper’s slit are hints of the dark mincemeat, golden raisins, and pale almonds. A sprinkle of fresh green chopped cilantro garnishes the chile. The plate sits on a simple wooden table, accompanied by a neatly folded cotton napkin. The setting evokes a modern bistro with authentic Mexican touches, illuminated by natural, even lighting to highlight the dish's rich colors and textures. A small stack of warm corn tortillas may be subtly placed in the background.
instructions: Roast poblano peppers over open flame or under broiler until skin blisters and blackens. Place in a plastic bag for 10 minutes to steam. Peel, deseed, and make a slit down one side of each pepper. Set aside.
Heat olive oil in a pan over medium heat. Add diced onion and cook until softened, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add beef mincemeat to the pan. Cook, breaking it apart, until browned. Drain any excess fat.

Stir in diced tomatoes, par-boiled diced potato, raisins, chopped almonds, cinnamon, and cloves. Cook for 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until flavors meld and potato is tender. Season with salt and pepper. Set aside as the picadillo filling.

For the Salsa Roja: Combine roasted tomatoes, chipotle, roughly chopped onion, garlic, and chicken broth in a blender. Blend until smooth. Pour into a saucepan and simmer over medium-low heat for 10-15 minutes, allowing sauce to thicken slightly. Season with salt.
Stuff each roasted poblano pepper with the prepared picadillo filling. Gently close the slit.
For the egg batter (capeado): In a clean bowl, whisk egg white until stiff peaks form. Gently fold in the egg yolk. Carefully fold in the flour until just combined.
Heat vegetable oil in a deep skillet to 175°C (350°F). Dip each stuffed poblano pepper into the egg batter, ensuring it is fully coated. Carefully place into the hot oil.
Fry chiles for 2-3 minutes per side, turning gently, until golden brown and puffed. Remove and drain on paper towels.
To serve: Ladle a generous pool of Salsa Roja onto each plate. Carefully place one Chiles Rellenos on top of the sauce. Garnish with fresh chopped cilantro.

recipes.recipe_name: Slow-Cooked Pork and Mincemeat Ragu
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Slow-Cooked Pork and Mincemeat Ragu is presented on a round, clean white porcelain dinner plate. A generous mound of broad pappardelle pasta is coated in a rich, deeply colored reddish-brown ragu. Tender, shredded pork pieces and fine mincemeat are visibly integrated throughout the sauce. The ragu exhibits a glossy, unctuous texture. A light dusting of finely grated pale yellow Parmesan cheese rests atop the ragu. Fresh, vibrant green basil leaves are scattered over the dish as a final garnish, providing a pop of color. The plate sits on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by a folded cotton napkin and a traditional fork and spoon. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's warmth and texture. The entire plate is visible, with moderate negative space.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread to sop up the sauce.
Offer extra grated Parmesan cheese at the table.
Pair with a robust red wine.
instructions: Pat pork cubes dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear pork cubes in batches until browned on all sides. Remove pork from pot.
Add diced pancetta to the pot. Cook until crispy. Remove pancetta.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion, carrot, and celery to the pot. Cook until softened, about 8-10 minutes. This is the soffritto.
Add minced garlic and tomato paste. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Deglaze the pot with red wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom. Simmer until wine reduces by half.
Return seared pork to the pot. Add beef mincemeat, breaking it up with a spoon. Cook until browned.
Stir in crushed tomatoes, beef broth, bay leaves, rosemary, and thyme. Bring to a simmer.
Cover the pot. Reduce heat to low. Simmer for at least 2.5-3 hours, or until pork is very tender and easily shreds with a fork. Stir occasionally.
Remove bay leaves, rosemary, and thyme sprigs.
Shred pork chunks directly in the pot using two forks. Mix thoroughly with the sauce.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Cook pasta according to package directions until al dente. Drain pasta.
Toss cooked pasta with a generous amount of ragu. Serve immediately.
notes: For best flavor, prepare the ragu a day in advance. Flavors deepen overnight.
Ensure pork is shredded into small, manageable pieces for easy eating with pasta.

recipes.recipe_name: Herb Roasted Chicken Thighs with Root Vegetables
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of Herb Roasted Chicken Thighs with Root Vegetables is presented on a simple, round, off-white ceramic plate with a slightly rustic edge. Two golden-brown, crispy-skinned chicken thighs are positioned naturally, slightly overlapping, showcasing their whole form. Beside them, a generous mound of roasted root vegetables – chunky potato pieces with soft, slightly browned edges, bright orange carrot chunks, and tender, caramelized red onion wedges – are casually arranged. Several smashed garlic cloves, their skins slightly browned, are nestled among the vegetables. Sprigs of fresh rosemary and thyme are scattered loosely over the dish, adding small flecks of green and a fresh aroma. The chicken is cooked through, with visible tender meat where the skin might be slightly pulled. The overall presentation is warm and inviting, typical of a home-cooked meal. The plate sits on a well-used, light wooden dining table. A simple, folded light-colored cloth napkin and a standard fork and knife are placed casually beside the plate. Warm, natural light illuminates the scene, creating a cozy family kitchen atmosphere.

ingredients.name: Potatoes, e.g., Yukon Gold, cut into 3-4 cm chunks
Carrots, peeled and cut into 3-4 cm chunks
Garlic cloves, smashed with skin on
Fresh rosemary, leaves picked and chopped

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (390°F).
Pat chicken thighs dry with paper towel. This ensures crispy skin.
In a large bowl, combine chicken, potatoes, carrots, red onion, garlic, olive oil, rosemary, thyme, salt, and pepper. Toss ingredients until evenly coated.
Spread the mixture in a single layer on a large baking sheet. Do not overcrowd the pan; use a second sheet if necessary for even roasting.
Roast for 35-45 minutes. Flip chicken and vegetables halfway through cooking.

Continue roasting until chicken skin is golden brown and crispy. Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F). Insert a meat thermometer into the thickest part of a thigh, avoiding the bone.
Remove from oven. Let rest for 5 minutes before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Seared Pork Loin with Roasted Tomato and Garlic Sauce
recipes.visual_description: Seared pork loin medallions are artfully arranged on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, showcasing their golden-brown crust and juicy interior. The pork is sliced into thick 2-3 cm medallions. A rich, rustic roasted tomato and garlic sauce is generously spooned over and around the pork, its deep red color contrasting beautifully with the golden meat. Whole roasted cherry tomatoes and tender garlic cloves are visible within the sauce, adding texture and visual interest. Fresh bright green basil leaves are scattered as a vibrant garnish. The plate features appropriate negative space, ensuring a professional yet approachable presentation. The setting is a modern bistro, with the plate resting on a simple wooden table. A folded cotton napkin and a small, rustic ceramic bowl of Kalamata olives are subtly placed nearby. Natural, even lighting illuminates the scene, emphasizing the dish's fresh ingredients and inviting colors.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty artisan bread for dipping into the sauce.
Accompany with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and lemon.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Place cherry tomatoes, unpeeled garlic cloves, and red onion slices on a baking tray. Add 30 ml olive oil and thyme sprigs. Season with salt and pepper.
Roast for 25-30 minutes. Tomatoes should be soft and slightly caramelized. Garlic should be tender.
Remove garlic from skins. Discard thyme sprigs.
Transfer roasted tomatoes, garlic, and onion to a bowl. Mash gently with a fork to create a rustic sauce. Stir in red wine vinegar. Adjust seasoning.
Pat pork loin dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat remaining 30 ml olive oil in an oven-safe pan over medium-high heat.
Sear pork loin for 3-4 minutes per side until golden-brown all over.
Transfer pan to preheated oven. Roast for 10-15 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 63°C. Remove from oven.
Rest pork loin on a cutting board for 5-10 minutes. This allows juices to redistribute.
Slice pork loin into thick 2-3 cm medallions.
Spoon roasted tomato and garlic sauce onto plates. Arrange pork medallions over the sauce. Garnish with fresh basil leaves.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Tempeh & Melon Grain Bowl
recipes.visual_description: A single individual portion is presented in a handcrafted, unglazed ceramic bowl, natural off-white. The bowl sits slightly off-center on a light, reclaimed wood surface. Plating is minimalistic with ample white space. Dark brown rice forms a base. Adjacent, golden-brown, pan-seared tempeh cubes are arranged organically. Bright, translucent pickled honeydew melon cubes add a pale green pop. A rustic dollop of amber apricot chutney rests near the tempeh. Vibrant sautéed kale leaves provide contrast. The dish is garnished with toasted pumpkin seeds and fresh dill sprigs. An undyed linen napkin is casually folded beside the bowl. Soft, diffused natural light creates gentle shadows. The background is clean and minimalist, with a subtle green plant hint, reinforcing the eco-conscious theme.
instructions: Cut tempeh into 2cm cubes. Mix soy sauce, rice vinegar, ginger, garlic, and sesame oil. Marinate tempeh cubes for 30 minutes.

Rinse brown rice. Combine rice and vegetable broth in a pot. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 40-45 minutes until liquid is absorbed and rice is tender. Let stand 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork.

Peel melon, remove seeds, cut flesh into 1.5cm cubes. In a small saucepan, combine apple cider vinegar, water, sugar, salt, and peppercorns. Bring to a simmer, stirring until dissolved. Remove from heat. Place melon cubes in a heatproof jar. Pour hot pickling liquid over melon. Let cool. Refrigerate for 1 hour.

Finely dice dried apricots and shallot. Combine diced apricots, shallot, apple cider vinegar, water, and chili flakes (if using) in a small saucepan. Bring to a gentle simmer. Cook for 5-7 minutes, stirring, until apricots soften and liquid thickens. Season with salt.
Heat a non-stick pan over medium-high heat. Add marinated tempeh cubes. Cook, turning, for 8-10 minutes until golden brown and slightly crispy.
In the same pan, quickly sauté chopped kale or spinach for 2-3 minutes until wilted.
Divide cooked brown rice among four bowls. Arrange tempeh cubes, pickled melon, and sautéed greens next to the rice. Spoon apricot chutney over tempeh or on the side.
Sprinkle with toasted pumpkin seeds and fresh herb sprigs. Serve immediately.
notes: Vegetable broth can be made from kitchen scraps (carrot peels, onion skins, celery ends, mushroom stems) simmered in water for 30 minutes.
The pickled melon can be made ahead and stored in the refrigerator for up to a week.
Tempeh can be pan-fried or baked for a hands-off approach.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Tomato & Onion Pasta with Savory Pasta Crumble
recipes.visual_description: A single generous portion of rigatoni pasta sits centrally on a handcrafted ceramic plate in a warm, earthy beige. The pasta is coated in a rustic, subtly reddish-brown sauce, a blend of slow-cooked fresh and tangy fermented tomatoes and onions. Interspersed are soft, translucent pieces of caramelized fresh onion and tender, slightly darker fermented onion slivers. A sprinkle of bright green, torn fresh basil leaves adds a pop of color and freshness. The dish is crowned with a scattering of golden-brown, irregularly shaped crispy pasta crumble, providing textural contrast. The plate rests on a light, natural-textured reclaimed wood surface. A simple, undyed linen napkin in a natural beige is folded neatly to the side. Soft, natural light illuminates the scene from the left, casting gentle shadows. The background is clean and minimalist, with a hint of green from a blurred plant.

ingredients.name: Leftover dry pasta pieces or ends

instructions: Prepare fermented tomatoes: Quarter 600g tomatoes. Place in a clean jar. Dissolve 10g salt and 5g sugar in 500ml water to make a brine. Pour brine over tomatoes. Ensure tomatoes are fully submerged using a weight. Ferment at room temperature for 3-5 days until tangy. Refrigerate.
Prepare fermented onions: Thinly slice 1 medium onion. Place in a clean jar. Cover with the same 2% brine. Ferment for 3-5 days. Refrigerate.
Drain fermented tomatoes and onions. Roughly chop fermented tomatoes. Reserve some brine for later.
Make pasta crumble: Break leftover dry pasta into small, irregular pieces. Heat 20ml olive oil in a pan. Fry pasta pieces until golden and crispy. Drain on paper towel. Season with a pinch of salt.

Sauté aromatics: Dice 1 medium fresh onion. Mince garlic. Heat 40ml olive oil in a large pan. Add diced fresh onion. Sauté until translucent, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add tomatoes and fermented onions: Add roughly chopped fermented tomatoes to the pan. Cook for 5-7 minutes, breaking them down with a spoon. Add fermented onions. Stir well.
Cook pasta: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Add rigatoni. Cook according to package directions until al dente. Reserve 250ml pasta water before draining.

Combine and finish: Add drained pasta to the pan with the tomato-onion mixture. Add nutritional yeast. Add reserved pasta water gradually, stirring to create a sauce that coats the pasta. Add a splash of reserved fermentation brine for extra tang if desired.
Garnish: Tear fresh basil leaves.
Serve: Plate pasta. Top with savory pasta crumble and fresh basil.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Mushroom Pasta
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of penne pasta served in a shallow, off-white ceramic bowl with natural imperfections. The pasta tubes are thoroughly coated in a thick, velvety ivory sauce created from reduced mushroom stock and heavy cream. Small, translucent bits of finely diced onion are visible within the sauce. The arrangement is casual and asymmetrical, with the pasta mounded in the center of the bowl. Freshly cracked black pepper and finely chopped green parsley provide dark and vibrant accents against the pale cream sauce. A light dusting of finely grated Parmesan cheese covers the top. The bowl sits on a well-worn wooden table alongside a simple metal fork and a white cloth napkin under warm, domestic kitchen lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty ciabatta bread
Pair with a glass of light red wine
Present in the center of the table for family-style sharing
instructions: Boil 4 liters of salted water in a large pot.
Cook penne 2 minutes less than the package instructions.
Melt butter in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add diced onion and minced garlic to the skillet.
Sauté until onions are translucent and soft.
Pour in mushroom stock and bring to a simmer.
Reduce stock by half until flavor intensifies.
Stir in heavy cream and simmer for 3 minutes.
Drain pasta and add directly to the sauce.
Add Parmesan cheese to the skillet.
Toss pasta vigorously for 1 minute to emulsify the sauce.
Season with salt and plenty of black pepper.
Garnish with chopped parsley before serving.
notes: Use high-quality mushroom stock for a deep savory profile.
Ensure the pasta is al dente to maintain texture in the cream sauce.
Adjust stock reduction time to control sauce thickness.

recipes.recipe_name: Slow-Braised Pork Terrine with Pickled Green Tomatoes & Mustard Crumb
recipes.visual_description: A single slice of dense, slow-braised pork terrine forms the centerpiece, a rectangular block of earthy brown, showcasing the natural texture of shredded pork. It rests on a handcrafted cream ceramic plate, leaving generous white space. Beside the terrine, a small, vibrant pile of quick-pickled green tomato wedges gleams, their pale green skins contrasting with the pork. Scattered around are golden-brown, toasted mustard seed breadcrumbs, adding a rustic texture. A delicate drizzle of golden olive oil glistens on the terrine. The setting features a light, reclaimed wood table surface, an undyed natural linen napkin, and soft, diffused natural lighting. A minimalist background with subtle greenery completes the eco-conscious, ingredient-focused presentation.
instructions: Cut pork shoulder into 5cm chunks. Season with salt and pepper.

Heat 15ml olive oil in a heavy pot. Sear pork chunks until browned on all sides. Add chopped onion, minced garlic, and thyme sprigs. Cook 5 minutes. Add 100ml water. Cover pot. Braise over low heat for 2.5-3 hours, until pork is very tender.

Remove pork from pot. Shred pork with two forks. Discard thyme. Mix shredded pork with a few tablespoons of braising liquid. Press firmly into a small terrine mold or loaf pan lined with cling film. Chill for at least 4 hours, or overnight, until firm.

Slice green tomatoes into 5mm thick rounds, then halve them. In a small saucepan, combine white wine vinegar, sugar, 100ml water, 10g salt, and 5g peppercorns. Bring to a boil, stirring to dissolve sugar. Pour hot brine over tomato slices in a heatproof jar. Let cool. Refrigerate for at least 1 hour.

Tear stale bread into small pieces. Toast in a dry pan until golden. Let cool. Blend into coarse breadcrumbs. In a small pan, heat 15ml olive oil. Add mustard seeds. Cook until fragrant and popping. Add breadcrumbs. Toast until golden and crisp. Season with a pinch of salt.

Slice chilled pork terrine into 1.5cm thick portions. Place one slice on each plate. Drain pickled green tomatoes. Arrange a small pile of pickled tomatoes beside the terrine. Sprinkle toasted mustard crumb over and around the terrine and tomatoes. Drizzle with remaining olive oil. Garnish with a few fresh parsley leaves. Serve immediately.
notes: Utilize leftover braising liquid for future sauces or stocks.
Green tomatoes can be sourced locally and seasonally.
Stale bread is repurposed into a flavorful crumb, promoting zero-waste.

recipes.recipe_name: Arroz con Pollo
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Arroz con Pollo presented on a clean white porcelain plate. Two whole, bone-in chicken thighs with deeply browned, crispy skin sit atop a bed of golden, saffron-stained rice. The rice grains are plump and distinct, interspersed with fine bits of softened onion and concentrated red tomato. The dish shows vibrant yellow and orange hues from the saffron and paprika. A generous sprinkle of bright green, finely chopped parsley is scattered over the top. A single lemon wedge is placed neatly on the side. The plate sits on a light oak wooden table with a folded white cotton napkin. Lighting is bright, natural, and even, highlighting the textures of the crispy skin and the moist rice grains.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of Alioli (garlic mayonnaise)
Accompany with crusty bread and a glass of chilled white wine
Present in a traditional terracotta cazuela for family-style dining
instructions: Season chicken thighs with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a wide shallow pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken skin-side down until golden and crispy.
Flip and brown the other side. Remove chicken from pan.
Add onion to the same pan. Sauté until translucent.
Stir in garlic and grated tomato. Cook until liquid evaporates and mixture darkens.
Add smoked paprika and rice. Stir to coat rice in oil for 2 minutes.
Pour in white wine. Deglaze the pan. Simmer until wine reduces by half.
Add hot stock and saffron. Stir once to distribute.
Place chicken thighs back into the pan on top of the rice.
Simmer undisturbed over medium-low heat for 18-20 minutes.
Ensure chicken reaches internal temperature of 75°C.
Remove from heat. Cover with a clean cloth. Rest for 5 minutes.
Garnish with fresh parsley before serving.
notes: Do not stir the rice once the stock is added to allow a crust to form on the bottom.
Use a wide pan to ensure even rice cooking.

recipes.recipe_name: Classic Chicken and Potato Soup
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Classic Chicken and Potato Soup is presented in a clean, white porcelain bowl, resting on a simple wooden table surface. The soup features a clear, golden broth with evenly diced 2 cm chicken breast cubes and tender 2 cm potato cubes. Finely diced, translucent onions are subtly integrated into the broth. A scattering of bright green chopped fresh parsley provides a vibrant contrast and fresh aroma. The arrangement is professional yet approachable, with moderate negative space. A neatly folded cotton napkin is placed beside the bowl. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its comforting colors and textures within a casual bistro-style background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread for dipping.
instructions: Dice chicken breast into 2 cm cubes. Season with salt and pepper.
Peel and finely dice onions. Peel and mince garlic. Peel and dice potatoes into 2 cm cubes.
Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Add diced chicken to the pot. Sear chicken until lightly golden on all sides, about 4-5 minutes. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken from pot and set aside.
Add diced onions to the same pot. Sauté until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes. Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in chicken stock. Scrape bottom of pot to release any browned bits. Add thyme sprigs and diced potatoes.
Bring soup to a boil. Reduce heat to medium-low. Simmer for 15-20 minutes, or until potatoes are tender.
Return cooked chicken to the pot. Simmer for 2-3 minutes to heat chicken through.
Remove thyme sprigs. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Finely chop fresh parsley for garnish.
Ladle soup into bowls. Garnish each serving with chopped fresh parsley.
notes: Ensure chicken is cooked thoroughly to 75°C (167°F) internal temperature.
Dicing ingredients uniformly ensures even cooking and appealing presentation.

recipes.recipe_name: Cheesy Chicken and Rice Bake
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of Cheesy Chicken and Rice Bake is served in an everyday, slightly imperfect ceramic bowl. The dish presents a comforting mix of tender white rice, golden-brown chicken chunks, vibrant red diced tomatoes, and yellow corn kernels. Melted, gooey cheddar cheese forms a golden crust over the top, with some cheese visibly bubbling on the edges. Freshly chopped green basil leaves are scattered over the top, adding a pop of color and freshness. The chicken is cut into substantial cubes, and the vegetables are diced, showing clean knife work. The components are naturally layered, creating a hearty, wholesome appearance. The bowl sits on a well-used wooden dining table, with a simple metal fork resting casually beside it. Warm, soft lighting illuminates the scene, evoking a cozy, lived-in family kitchen atmosphere. The presentation is homely and inviting, focusing on the dish as a satisfying, approachable comfort meal.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve directly from the baking dish at the table for a family-style meal
Pair with a simple green salad
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.
Cut chicken breast into 2 cm cubes. Season with salt, pepper, and paprika.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken cubes for 3-4 minutes until browned. Do not cook through. Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside.
Dice onion and carrot. Mince garlic.
Add onion and carrot to the skillet. Sauté for 5 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in uncooked rice, diced tomatoes (undrained), corn (drained), and chicken broth. Bring mixture to a simmer.
Return seared chicken to the skillet. Stir to combine.
Sprinkle shredded cheese evenly over the top.
Bake for 20-25 minutes, or until rice is tender and chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C.
Remove from oven. Let stand 5 minutes.
Chop fresh basil. Sprinkle over the bake before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken and Potato Fritters
recipes.visual_description: Three golden-brown Chicken and Potato Fritters are stacked casually on a simple, round ceramic plate, showing their slightly irregular, homemade shapes. The fritters boast a visibly crispy, textured exterior, speckled with finely chopped green parsley and grated potato. A generous dollop of creamy white sour cream or Greek yogurt is placed naturally beside the fritters, gently garnished with a pinch of fresh chopped parsley. The entire plate rests on a well-used wooden dining table, exuding a homely, lived-in feel. A slightly crumpled, neutral-toned cloth napkin and a rustic fork are casually positioned nearby. Warm, soft kitchen lighting bathes the scene, highlighting the comforting appeal of the dish in a relaxed family dining setting. The background is softly blurred, hinting at a cozy kitchen environment.
instructions: Place chicken breasts in a pot. Cover with water. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat. Simmer until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F), about 15-20 minutes. Remove chicken. Let cool slightly. Shred chicken using two forks.
Peel potatoes. Grate them coarsely. Place grated potatoes in a clean kitchen towel. Squeeze out as much excess water as possible.
Finely dice the small onion. Mince garlic cloves. Chop fresh parsley.
In a large bowl, combine shredded chicken, squeezed grated potatoes, egg, plain flour, diced onion, minced garlic, and chopped parsley.
Season the mixture generously with salt and black pepper. Mix all ingredients thoroughly until well combined.
Heat a generous amount of vegetable oil in a large frying pan over medium heat.
Spoon about 50g of the mixture per fritter into the hot oil. Flatten slightly to form patties approximately 7-8 cm in diameter. Do not overcrowd the pan; cook in batches if necessary.
Fry each side for 3-4 minutes, or until the fritters are golden brown and cooked through. Ensure chicken and potato are fully cooked.
Remove fritters from the pan. Place them on a plate lined with paper towels to drain excess oil.
Serve warm, optionally with a dollop of sour cream or Greek yogurt on the side.
notes: Squeezing excess water from grated potatoes is crucial for crispy fritters. Do this thoroughly.

recipes.recipe_name: Tom Kha Gai (Thai Coconut Chicken Soup)
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of vibrant Tom Kha Gai is presented in a deep, glossy white ceramic bowl, resting on a simple light wooden table. The creamy, off-white coconut milk broth fills the bowl, with tender, irregularly cut 2cm chicken chunks and delicate, wavy oyster mushroom slices visible beneath the surface. Bright green chopped cilantro leaves are generously scattered over the top, providing a fresh contrast. A few thin, bright red slices of bird's eye chili are artfully placed among the cilantro, hinting at a subtle heat. The soup's surface has a subtle sheen from the coconut milk. A traditional ceramic Asian soup spoon rests inside the bowl, invitingly. Beside the bowl, a pair of dark wooden chopsticks lies neatly on a white cotton napkin. A small, matching white ceramic bowl filled with fluffy, white jasmine rice sits nearby, ready to accompany the soup. The overall presentation is clean, balanced, and inviting, with natural, even lighting casting soft shadows, highlighting the dish as the focal point. The background is a subtly blurred modern bistro setting, suggesting a relaxed dining atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve hot with a side of steamed jasmine rice.
Offer a small dish of fish sauce with sliced bird's eye chilies on the side for those who prefer more heat.
Enjoy with a traditional ceramic soup spoon and chopsticks.
instructions: Cut chicken breast into 2cm cubes.
Thinly slice galangal. Bruise lemongrass stalks and cut into 5cm pieces. Tear kaffir lime leaves.
Heat vegetable oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add sliced galangal, bruised lemongrass, and torn kaffir lime leaves. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in chicken stock and bring to a simmer.
Add chicken cubes. Cook for 5-7 minutes until chicken is cooked through (internal temperature 75°C).
Stir in coconut milk. Bring soup to a gentle simmer. Do not boil vigorously.
Add oyster mushrooms, torn or sliced. Cook for 2-3 minutes until mushrooms are tender.
Remove from heat. Stir in fish sauce and lime juice. Add palm sugar if desired, dissolving completely.
Taste and adjust seasoning with more fish sauce or lime juice if needed.
Ladle hot soup into individual serving bowls.
Garnish with fresh chopped cilantro and thin slices of red chilies.
notes: Ensure chicken is cooked to 75°C internal temperature for food safety.
Do not vigorously boil coconut milk after adding it, as it can cause it to separate. Maintain a gentle simmer.

recipes.recipe_name: Red Wine-Chestnut Fruit Salad
recipes.visual_description: The fruit salad is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dessert plate, forming a vibrant, mounded pile. It showcases deep purples from plum wedges and halved grapes, pale yellow from 2cm pear cubes, and rich brown from quartered figs. Caramelized chestnuts, whole or halved, are interspersed throughout, adding texture and color. A glistening red wine-verjus syrup coats the fruits, enhancing their natural sheen. The plating is clean and balanced, with moderate negative space. A small, fresh mint sprig provides a touch of green. The plate sits on a simple wooden table with a white cotton napkin and dessert fork. Natural, even lighting highlights the fresh ingredients. The background features a softly blurred modern bistro setting, keeping focus on the dish.
instructions: Prepare Chestnuts: Heat a small pan over medium heat. Add 50g sugar and 30ml water. Stir until sugar dissolves. Add cooked chestnuts. Cook, stirring occasionally, until water evaporates and sugar caramelizes around chestnuts. Remove from heat. Set aside to cool.

Prepare Red Wine-Verjus-Chili Syrup: In a small saucepan, combine red wine, verjus, 75g sugar, and halved Thai green chili. Bring to a simmer over medium heat. Reduce heat to low. Simmer gently for 15-20 minutes, or until syrup thickens slightly and coats the back of a spoon. Remove Thai green chili from syrup. Let syrup cool completely.
Prepare Fruits: Wash all fruits. Cut pears into 2cm cubes. Quarter figs. Halve red grapes. Cut plums into 2cm wedges. Remove pits.
Assemble Fruit Salad: In a large bowl, gently combine prepared fruits. Add caramelized chestnuts. Pour cooled red wine-verjus-chili syrup over fruits and chestnuts. Gently toss to coat.
Serve: Divide fruit salad among four individual serving bowls or plates. Garnish with a fresh mint sprig. Serve immediately.
notes: Adjust Thai green chili quantity to your preference for subtle heat.
Best served chilled.
Seasonal fruits can be substituted, ensuring a balance of textures and flavors.

recipes.recipe_name: Eggplant and Mushroom Chili-Sesame Salad
recipes.visual_description: The Eggplant and Mushroom Chili-Sesame Salad is presented in a deep, rustic ceramic bowl, showcasing a medley of earthy tones and vibrant accents. Roasted eggplant cubes, their deep purple skins slightly wrinkled and their flesh tender, are mixed with golden-brown sautéed mushroom slices. Halved black olives add a contrasting dark hue and briny texture. Thin slices of bright red chili are scattered throughout, providing pops of color and a hint of heat. The ingredients are loosely tossed, allowing some to overlap naturally. A light, glossy sheen from the chili-sesame dressing coats each piece, reflecting the warm, inviting light. The salad is generously garnished with vibrant green chopped green onions and a sprinkle of toasted sesame seeds. The bowl sits on a well-worn wooden kitchen table, accompanied by simple chopsticks, suggesting a casual, comforting home meal.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve alongside steamed jasmine rice.
instructions: Cut eggplant into 2 cm cubes. Season lightly with salt.
Heat 1 tablespoon olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Add eggplant cubes. Cook, stirring occasionally, until tender and lightly browned, about 8-10 minutes. Remove from pan.

Slice mushrooms. Add remaining 1 tablespoon olive oil to the same pan. Add sliced mushrooms. Sauté until golden brown and softened, about 5-7 minutes. Season with a pinch of salt and pepper. Remove from pan.
Halve black olives. Thinly slice red chili. Mince garlic. Grate ginger.
In a small bowl, whisk together soy sauce, rice vinegar, toasted sesame oil, minced garlic, grated ginger, and a pinch of sugar. Adjust chili to taste.
In a large serving bowl, combine cooked eggplant, sautéed mushrooms, halved olives, and sliced chili. Pour dressing over the salad. Toss gently to coat all ingredients.
Chop green onions. Garnish salad with chopped green onions and sesame seeds. Serve warm or at room temperature.
notes: This salad can be enjoyed warm or at room temperature.

recipes.recipe_name: Tomato and Brown Rice Salad
recipes.visual_description: The Tomato and Brown Rice Salad is presented in a deep, rustic ceramic bowl on a well-used wooden dining table. Fluffy cooked brown rice forms the base. Vibrant red, chopped ripe tomatoes are scattered generously, their juicy surfaces glistening. Earthy, pan-sautéed mushroom slices with golden-brown edges are interspersed throughout. Bright orange shredded carrots add color and crunch. Cubes of creamy white mozzarella are nestled among the vegetables. Fresh green basil leaves, roughly torn, are casually mixed in. The salad is lightly coated in a glistening balsamic vinaigrette. The presentation is casual and abundant. The bowl sits on a simple wooden table with a casually placed cloth napkin. Warm, inviting kitchen light creates a cozy family dining atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of crusty Italian bread.
Offer extra virgin olive oil for drizzling at the table.
instructions: Rinse brown rice. Combine rice and water in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 40-45 minutes, or until water is absorbed and rice is tender. Fluff with a fork. Let cool completely.
While rice cools, prepare vegetables. Chop tomatoes into bite-sized pieces. Slice mushrooms. Shred carrots.
Heat 15 ml of olive oil in a pan over medium heat. Add sliced mushrooms and sauté until softened and lightly browned, about 5-7 minutes. Season with a pinch of salt and pepper. Let cool.
In a small bowl, whisk together remaining 45 ml olive oil, balsamic vinegar, minced garlic, salt, and black pepper to make the dressing.
In a large mixing bowl, combine cooled brown rice, chopped tomatoes, sautéed mushrooms, shredded carrots, and cubed mozzarella.
Pour dressing over the salad ingredients. Gently toss to combine everything evenly.
Add fresh basil leaves, roughly torn, and gently toss again.
Serve immediately or chill for later.

recipes.recipe_name: Rustic Beef and Mushroom Ragù with Creamy Brown Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Rustic Beef and Mushroom Ragù with Creamy Brown Rice is centered on a clean, white porcelain dinner plate. A mounded portion of light brown, creamy rice forms the base. Over this, a rich, dark red-brown beef and mushroom ragù is generously ladled, showcasing tender, 2-3 cm diced beef chunks, soft sliced mushrooms, and small diced carrots in a thick, glossy tomato sauce. Torn pieces of fresh, milky white mozzarella are scattered over the hot ragù, visibly melting. Vibrant green, torn fresh basil leaves are placed on top for color contrast. The dish is naturally arranged with moderate negative space. The plate rests on a simple, light wooden table, illuminated by natural, even lighting. A folded white cotton napkin and standard silver flatware are neatly placed, emphasizing a casual bistro setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread to sop up the sauce.
Offer extra grated Parmesan cheese at the table.
instructions: Season beef chunks generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven or heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat. Sear beef in batches until browned on all sides. Remove beef and set aside.

Add diced onion and carrots to the pot. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic and sliced mushrooms. Cook for another 5 minutes until mushrooms release their liquid and begin to brown.
Deglaze the pot with red wine, scraping up any browned bits. Simmer until wine reduces by half.
Return seared beef to the pot. Stir in crushed tomatoes, beef broth, and bay leaf. Bring to a simmer.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 2-3 hours, or until beef is fork-tender. Stir occasionally.

While ragù simmers, cook brown rice. Rinse brown rice thoroughly. Combine brown rice with 750 ml water and a pinch of salt in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 40-45 minutes, or until water is absorbed and rice is tender.
Once rice is cooked, stir in butter and grated Parmesan cheese until creamy. Keep warm.
Remove bay leaf from ragù. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
To serve, spoon a generous portion of creamy brown rice onto each plate. Ladle a large serving of beef and mushroom ragù over the rice.
Scatter torn fresh mozzarella pieces over the hot ragù. Garnish with fresh basil leaves. Serve immediately.
notes: For best flavor, prepare the ragù a day in advance. Reheat gently before serving.
Ensure beef is fork-tender before serving. If not, continue simmering.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Chicken & Seasonal Rice Bowl
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of the Fermented Chicken & Seasonal Rice Bowl is presented on a handcrafted ceramic plate in an earthy cream tone, allowing ample white space. A mound of fluffy brown rice anchors the center. Beside it, golden-brown seared chicken chunks are arranged naturally. Vibrant green blanched broccoli florets and bright snap peas are placed alongside, their textures distinct. A vibrant pile of quick-fermented, thinly shredded cabbage, julienned carrots, and sliced radish adds a pop of color and tang. The arrangement is clean and unforced, highlighting each ingredient's natural beauty. A light drizzle of sesame oil glistens on the chicken. The setting features a reclaimed wood table surface, an undyed linen napkin, and soft natural lighting from the side, with a clean background subtly showing natural elements.

ingredients.name: Fresh spring onion greens, thinly sliced

instructions: Cut chicken thighs into 3-4 cm chunks. In a bowl, combine chicken with lacto-fermented vegetable brine, minced garlic, grated ginger, and soy sauce. Marinate for at least 30 minutes, or up to 4 hours in the refrigerator.

For quick-fermented vegetables: In a separate bowl, combine shredded cabbage, julienned carrots, thinly sliced radish, chopped dill or cilantro, sea salt, rice vinegar, and 15ml water. Massage ingredients together for 2-3 minutes until vegetables soften slightly. Set aside.

Rinse brown rice thoroughly. In a medium saucepan, combine rice with 500ml water or vegetable broth and a pinch of salt. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 40-45 minutes, or until water is absorbed and rice is tender. Let stand covered for 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork.

While rice cooks, prepare sautéed vegetables. Bring a pot of lightly salted water to a boil. Blanch broccoli florets for 2-3 minutes until tender-crisp. Add snap peas for the last minute. Drain immediately and refresh in cold water to stop cooking. Drain well.

Heat 15ml neutral oil in a large skillet or wok over medium-high heat. Add marinated chicken chunks in a single layer. Sear chicken for 4-5 minutes per side, turning occasionally, until golden brown and cooked through. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from skillet and set aside.
In the same skillet, add blanched broccoli and snap peas. Sauté for 2-3 minutes until slightly warmed and lightly charred. Season with salt and black pepper.

To assemble bowls: Divide cooked brown rice among four serving bowls. Arrange cooked chicken chunks alongside the rice. Add sautéed seasonal vegetables and a generous portion of the quick-fermented vegetables to each bowl. Drizzle with optional sesame oil. Garnish with thinly sliced spring onion greens. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Savory Beef and Cheddar Crostini
recipes.visual_description: The Savory Beef and Cheddar Crostini are presented on a simple, well-used wooden dining table, evoking a homely family kitchen. Thinly sliced baguette rounds are lightly toasted to a golden hue, forming the base. Each crostini is generously topped with richly browned, crumbled ground beef, seasoned and cooked until tender. Over the beef, a layer of melted, bubbling yellow-orange cheddar cheese cascades, showing a gooey, inviting texture. The arrangement is casual and natural, with 8-12 pieces loosely placed on a rustic ceramic platter or wooden board. A light sprinkle of vibrant green, finely chopped fresh parsley adds a touch of color. The beef is crumbled, onion finely diced, and garlic minced, ensuring a harmonious bite. Warm, cozy lighting from kitchen fixtures highlights the comforting textures and inviting colors. Portions are modest and approachable, ready for family enjoyment.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve warm as a casual appetizer
Offer with other comfort food snacks
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C. Slice baguette into 1 cm thick rounds. Arrange on a baking sheet. Lightly brush with olive oil.
Bake baguette slices for 8-10 minutes until golden and crisp. Set aside.
Heat remaining olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add finely diced onion. Cook 3-4 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Add ground beef to skillet. Break it apart with a spoon. Cook until browned and crumbled. Drain any excess fat.
Season beef with salt and black pepper to taste. Stir well.
Spoon beef mixture onto each toasted baguette slice. Top generously with shredded cheddar cheese.
Return crostini to baking sheet. Bake for 5-7 minutes, or until cheese is melted and bubbly.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley before serving.
notes: For best results, serve immediately while cheese is still warm and gooey.

recipes.recipe_name: Sweet Tomato Confit Tartlet with White Chocolate Crémeux
recipes.visual_description: Six to nine perfectly uniform miniature tartlets are arranged with architectural precision on an elegant, rectangular white porcelain serving platter. The platter rests on a pristine white Carrara marble surface. Each tartlet features a thin, pale golden almond sablé disc, precisely 4cm in diameter. A smooth, glossy dome of off-white white chocolate crémeux is piped onto each sablé. Centered atop the crémeux is a small, translucent dollop of rich, ruby-red sweet tomato confit. A single, vibrant green micro-basil leaf is meticulously placed on the tomato confit, providing a precise, contrasting garnish. Abundant negative space surrounds the tartlets, emphasizing their minimalist composition. The scene is bathed in dramatic professional lighting, casting subtle, elegant shadows that highlight the textures and forms. A pristine white linen napkin, folded into a sharp triangle, is positioned discreetly in the background, adding to the luxurious, uncluttered aesthetic. The entire composition embodies sophisticated simplicity and flawless execution, reflecting Swiss precision in culinary art.
instructions: Prepare the Almond Sablé: In a bowl, combine butter, icing sugar, all-purpose flour, almond flour, and salt. Rub with fingertips until crumbly. Form into a disc. Wrap and chill 30 minutes.
Preheat oven to 160°C.
Roll out sablé dough to 3mm thickness. Cut 6-9 uniform 4cm diameter rounds. Place on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper. Bake 12-15 minutes, until pale golden. Cool completely.

Prepare the Sweet Tomato Confit: Halve cherry tomatoes. Place in a small saucepan with granulated sugar, vanilla seeds, and lemon zest. Cook over very low heat for 30-40 minutes, stirring occasionally, until tomatoes are soft and liquid is syrupy. Mash gently with a fork. Cool completely.

Prepare the White Chocolate Crémeux: Chop white chocolate finely. Place in a heatproof bowl. In a small saucepan, gently heat cream until simmering. Whisk egg yolk in a separate bowl. Slowly pour hot cream over egg yolk, whisking constantly. Return mixture to saucepan. Cook over low heat, stirring constantly with a spatula, until thickened slightly and coats the back of a spoon (nappe consistency). Do not boil.
Pour hot cream mixture over chopped white chocolate. Let stand 1 minute. Whisk until smooth and glossy. Cover surface with plastic wrap. Chill at least 2 hours, until firm.

Assemble the Petit Fours: Transfer white chocolate crémeux to a piping bag with a plain round tip. Pipe a neat dome of crémeux onto each cooled almond sablé disc. Place a small, precise dollop of sweet tomato confit on top of the crémeux. Garnish each petit four with a single micro-basil leaf.
Serve immediately or keep chilled until serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Cacciatore
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of rustic chicken cacciatore served in a shallow, cream-colored ceramic bowl with minor surface imperfections. Two whole, bone-in chicken thighs are the centerpiece, their skin appearing dark golden and tender from braising. The chicken is partially submerged in a thick, chunky tomato sauce featuring visible pieces of softened translucent onions and whole black olives. A single fresh rosemary sprig is placed casually on top. The bowl sits on a weathered dark wood kitchen table. Beside the bowl is a thick piece of torn crusty bread. The scene is illuminated by warm, soft overhead kitchen lighting, creating a cozy, authentic Italian home-dining atmosphere. A simple linen napkin and a stainless steel fork are placed to the left of the bowl.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty sourdough bread to soak up the tomato sauce
Pair with a side of simple polenta or rustic mashed potatoes
Traditional family-style dining involves placing the skillet in the center of the table
instructions: Season chicken thighs with salt and pepper on all sides.
Heat olive oil in a large deep skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken skin-side down for 6 minutes until golden brown.
Flip chicken and sear for 4 minutes. Remove chicken from skillet.
Add diced onion to the skillet. Sauté for 5 minutes until soft.
Stir in minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add crushed tomatoes, oregano, and the rosemary sprig.
Place chicken back into the skillet, nestled into the sauce.
Simmer on low heat for 30 minutes until chicken reaches 75°C internally.
Stir in the olives 5 minutes before serving.
notes: Use bone-in thighs for maximum flavor and protein content
Ensure the sauce reduces until thick to concentrate the savory tomato profile
Always check the thickest part of the chicken for a safe internal temperature of 75°C

recipes.recipe_name: Slow-Roasted Heirloom Tomato, Basil Emulsion, Gruyère Tuile
recipes.visual_description: A single, elegant starter portion is presented on a pristine white bone china plate with a subtle, modern rim. The plate rests on a smooth, cool white Carrara marble surface. Dramatic, directional lighting casts soft shadows, enhancing the dish's architectural precision and the abundant negative space. The focal point is a small, artful cluster of slow-roasted heirloom tomato pieces, varying in natural shapes and vibrant hues of deep red, sunny yellow, and mottled orange. Their surfaces appear slightly shriveled and glossy from the olive oil, revealing their tender, concentrated texture. Adjacent to the tomatoes, a single, delicate Gruyère tuile stands upright, its translucent, golden-brown form showcasing fine, crisp texture. A precise, small drizzle or 2-3 tiny, perfectly formed dots of bright emerald-green basil emulsion are placed intentionally near the tomato cluster, adding a vibrant color contrast and a hint of freshness. A crisp, white linen napkin, folded into a precise triangle, is positioned to the side. The background is utterly minimalist, allowing the dish to command full attention, embodying sophisticated simplicity and masterful execution.
instructions: Preheat oven to 120°C. Halve or quarter heirloom tomatoes. Arrange cut-side up in an oven-safe dish.
Add olive oil, sliced garlic, and thyme sprigs. Season with salt and pepper. Roast for 1.5 to 2 hours until very tender but holding shape.
Remove from oven. Let cool slightly in the oil.
Bring a small pot of water to a boil. Prepare an ice bath. Blanch fresh basil leaves for 10 seconds. Immediately transfer to ice bath.
Drain basil well and pat dry. In a high-speed blender, combine blanched basil with 30 ml of the reserved olive oil from roasted tomatoes.
Blend until completely smooth and vibrant green. Pass emulsion through a fine-mesh sieve. Season with a tiny pinch of salt.
Preheat oven to 180°C. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper. Grate Gruyère cheese finely.
Sprinkle small, thin circles (approx. 4-5 cm diameter) of grated cheese onto parchment. Leave space between them.
Bake for 5-7 minutes until golden brown and crisp. Watch carefully. Immediately transfer tuiles to a wire rack to cool.
Select a wide, shallow plate. Arrange 3-5 small, irregular pieces of slow-roasted heirloom tomato artfully on one side. Leave abundant negative space.
Place a small, delicate Gruyère tuile upright next to the tomatoes. Drizzle 1-2 small, precise dots or a thin line of basil emulsion near the tomatoes. Serve immediately.
notes: The slow roasting process intensifies the tomato's sweetness and umami, creating a luxurious texture.
The Gruyère tuile provides a delicate, salty crunch that complements the soft tomatoes and fresh emulsion.
Ensure the basil emulsion is very smooth and vibrant green for optimal visual impact.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Consommé with Heirloom Tomato Essence
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of this elegant consommé is presented in a deep, pristine white bone china bowl. The liquid is a crystal-clear, luminous amber, filling the bottom of the bowl. Four perfectly cooked, tender chicken medallions, cut into clean 2.5cm cubes, are artfully arranged in the center, their pristine white flesh contrasting with the consommé. Scattered around the chicken are a few vibrant ruby-red heirloom tomato brunoise cubes, adding precise bursts of color. A delicate drizzle of concentrated tomato essence creates subtle swirls of deeper red on the surface. A single, verdant micro basil leaf or small, fresh basil leaf is meticulously placed as a final, fresh accent. The bowl rests on a premium white Carrara marble surface, beside a precisely folded white linen napkin. Dramatic, focused lighting casts soft shadows, highlighting the dish's refined simplicity against an ultra-minimalist background, emphasizing abundant negative space.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Roast chicken carcass or wings on a baking tray for 30 minutes until golden. Transfer roasted bones to a large pot.
Add 3 liters cold water, halved onion, carrot, celery, and garlic to the pot. Bring to a simmer over medium heat. Skim any impurities from the surface.
Reduce heat to low. Simmer gently for 4 hours. Strain stock through a fine-mesh sieve. Chill stock completely in an ice bath, then refrigerate until thoroughly cold. Skim all fat from the cold stock.

Finely mince 200g of raw chicken breast. In a clean large pot, combine the cold, defatted chicken stock with the minced chicken, 3 finely diced egg whites, and 50g finely diced heirloom tomato. Stir well to combine.
Place the pot over medium-low heat. Slowly bring the mixture to a bare simmer without stirring. A 'raft' of solids will form on top. Create a small hole in the raft to allow steam to escape.

Simmer very gently for 45 minutes, ensuring the liquid remains clear. Carefully ladle the clear consommé through the hole in the raft, passing it through a fine-mesh sieve lined with a damp cheesecloth. Do not press the raft. Keep consommé warm.

Blanch 500g heirloom tomatoes in boiling water for 30 seconds. Immediately transfer to an ice bath. Peel, deseed, and roughly chop the tomatoes. Blend chopped tomatoes briefly. Pass blended tomato through a fine-mesh sieve, pressing gently to extract a clear liquid essence. Season this essence with a pinch of salt.
Cut remaining 400g chicken breast into 16 uniform 2.5cm cubes or thick medallions. Season lightly with salt and white pepper.

Gently poach chicken pieces in simmering, lightly salted water or a small amount of the clarified consommé for 8-10 minutes, or until the internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken from liquid.
Finely dice the 50g heirloom tomato into a small brunoise.
To assemble each serving: Place 4 pieces of poached chicken in a warm, deep serving bowl. Add 1 tablespoon of heirloom tomato brunoise.
Carefully pour 150ml of warm clarified consommé around the chicken and tomato. Drizzle 1 teaspoon of the tomato essence over the consommé.
Garnish with 1-2 small fresh basil leaves. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Heirloom Tomato Velouté with Basil Espuma and Pumpernickel Croutons
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Heirloom Tomato Velouté is presented in a sophisticated, wide, shallow bone china bowl, showcasing abundant negative space. The velouté, a deep, rich red-orange hue, is perfectly smooth and velvety. Centrally positioned atop the soup is a delicate, airy cloud of bright green basil espuma. Around the espuma, a precise scattering of tiny, golden-brown pumpernickel croutons adds textural contrast. A few vibrant micro basil leaves are artfully placed for a final touch of color and freshness. The bowl rests on a premium grey-veined marble surface. A pristine white linen napkin, folded into a precise triangle, and elegant, brushed steel flatware complete the ultra-minimalist, high-end setting under dramatic professional lighting with purposeful shadows.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C (350°F).
Halve heirloom tomatoes. Toss with 5 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Roast 20-25 minutes until softened and slightly caramelized.
Finely dice shallot and garlic. Sauté in 5 ml olive oil in a saucepan over medium heat until translucent, about 3 minutes.
Add roasted tomatoes and vegetable stock to the saucepan. Bring to a simmer. Cook 10 minutes.
Carefully blend the soup until perfectly smooth using an immersion blender or high-speed blender. Pass through a fine-mesh sieve for a silky texture.
Return soup to clean saucepan. Stir in heavy cream. Season with salt and pepper. Keep warm.
For Pumpernickel Croutons: Dice pumpernickel bread into 5mm cubes. Toss with remaining 5 ml olive oil. Toast in a dry pan or oven until crisp and golden. Set aside.

For Basil Espuma: Blanch 20g fresh basil leaves in boiling water for 10 seconds. Immediately transfer to ice bath. Drain well. Blend blanched basil with 50ml hot water and lecithin powder until smooth. Strain through fine-mesh sieve. Transfer to a siphon bottle, charge with N2O cartridge. Shake well. If no siphon, whisk vigorously to create foam.

To serve: Pour hot tomato velouté into a warm, wide, shallow bowl. Dispense basil espuma centrally over the soup. Scatter pumpernickel croutons around the espuma. Garnish with micro basil or basil flowers. Serve immediately.
notes: Ensure the velouté is strained for the silkiest texture.
For a deeper tomato flavor, use a mix of ripe heirloom varieties.

recipes.recipe_name: Alpine Tomato Consommé with Basil Essence
recipes.visual_description: A clear, vibrant ruby-red consommé fills a handcrafted, cream-colored ceramic bowl. The liquid's surface is pristine, reflecting light, with a subtle sheen from the basil essence. A few small, perfectly formed fresh basil leaves float delicately on top, their deep green contrasting with the soup's red. The bowl sits on a light, naturally textured reclaimed wood table. Adjacent to the bowl, a small, undyed linen napkin in a natural beige tone is neatly folded. The background is clean and minimalist, with soft natural light illuminating the scene. A hint of green foliage from a potted plant is subtly visible in the background, adding to the eco-conscious feel. The presentation is simple, elegant, and highlights the pure essence of the tomato.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a slice of fresh, rustic whole grain bread.

ingredients.name: Vegetable scraps (onion ends, carrot peels, celery leaves/ends, mushroom stems)

instructions: Prepare vegetable broth: Combine tomato cores and skins, vegetable scraps, parsley stems, and garlic in a pot. Add water. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 30 minutes. Strain broth into a clean bowl. Discard all solids.
Prepare tomato base: Roughly chop ripe tomatoes. In a separate pot, heat 10 ml olive oil over medium heat. Add chopped tomatoes. Cook until softened, about 10 minutes.
Combine: Add the strained vegetable broth to the softened tomatoes. Simmer for 15 minutes.

Blend and strain: Carefully blend the soup until very smooth. Pass the blended soup through a fine-mesh sieve or cheesecloth into a clean pot for a clear consommé. Press solids firmly to extract all liquid. Discard remaining solids.
Season: Return the consommé to the clean pot. Gently heat. Season with salt and black pepper to taste.

Prepare basil essence: Finely chop basil stems. Place in a small heatproof bowl. Heat remaining 5 ml olive oil until warm. Pour over basil stems. Let steep for 10 minutes. Strain the oil, discarding the stems.
Serve: Ladle hot consommé into a bowl. Drizzle with the basil essence. Garnish with a few fresh basil leaves.
notes: For extra clarity, you may pass the consommé through a coffee filter or multiple layers of cheesecloth.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Tomato Consommé with Herb Oil
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of clear, amber-hued Fermented Tomato Consommé rests in a handcrafted, unglazed ceramic bowl of natural cream or beige tone. The consommé is perfectly transparent. A few drops of vibrant, emerald-green herb oil are artfully dotted on the surface, some forming small, delicate pools, others subtly marbling into the clear liquid. A whisper of finely grated, bright yellow preserved lemon zest is delicately sprinkled over one side of the bowl. The overall presentation is minimalistic and clean, with ample white space around the bowl on a light-colored, subtly textured stone or light wood surface. A simple, undyed linen napkin in a natural beige tone is folded neatly beside the bowl. Natural, soft light illuminates the scene, highlighting the liquid's clarity and the subtle sheen of the oil. The background is uncluttered, suggesting a natural, eco-conscious environment with perhaps a hint of green from a distant plant.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve as a delicate starter course.
Accompany with a small piece of crusty, artisanal sourdough bread.
instructions: Roughly chop tomatoes. Place in a clean jar with 5 g salt.
Cover jar loosely with a lid or cloth. Let ferment at room temperature (20-24°C) for 3-5 days. Burp daily. Liquid will form and bubble.
Strain fermented tomatoes through a fine-mesh sieve lined with cheesecloth. Collect clear liquid. Gently press solids to extract more liquid. Discard solids or reserve for another use.
Combine strained tomato liquid with 200 ml water.
Lightly whisk egg white. Add to tomato liquid. Bring mixture slowly to a simmer over medium heat, stirring gently until raft forms. Stop stirring.
Simmer gently for 15-20 minutes without disturbing the raft.
Carefully ladle clear consommé through a clean cheesecloth-lined sieve. Do not disturb the raft. Discard raft.
Combine parsley, chives, and olive oil in a blender. Blend until smooth and vibrant green. Strain through a fine-mesh sieve or coffee filter for a clear oil.
Finely grate a small amount of preserved lemon peel for zest.
Gently reheat consommé if needed. Pour into a handcrafted ceramic bowl. Drizzle with herb oil. Garnish with preserved lemon zest.
notes: The leftover fermented tomato pulp can be dehydrated and ground into a savory powder, or used as a base for a flavorful sauce, contributing to zero-waste.
Adjust fermentation time based on desired acidity and ambient temperature. Taste daily.

recipes.recipe_name: Herbed Roasted Chicken and Quinoa Medley
recipes.special_requests: No sour, gluten free, no potato, no tomatoes, no mint, diabetic like diet with lack of appetite
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean, simple white porcelain dinner plate, centered on a natural wooden table surface in a modern bistro setting. A single roasted boneless, skinless chicken thigh, golden-brown and tender, rests next to a generous, naturally mounded portion of fluffy quinoa. The quinoa is vibrantly interspersed with roasted vegetables: tender green zucchini half-moons, bright yellow and orange bell pepper chunks, and soft purple red onion wedges, all showing slight charring from roasting. A scattering of fresh, bright green chopped parsley garnishes the entire dish, providing a fresh contrast. The composition is balanced, with moderate negative space. Natural, even lighting illuminates the textures and colors of the ingredients. Simple, clean cutlery and a folded cotton napkin are placed beside the plate, completing a refined yet approachable presentation.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Rinse quinoa thoroughly under cold water. Combine quinoa and vegetable broth in a medium saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 15 minutes, or until liquid is absorbed and quinoa is fluffy. Let stand covered for 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork.

Cut zucchini into 2 cm thick half-moons. Cut bell peppers into 2 cm chunks. Cut red onion into 2 cm wedges. Place all cut vegetables on a large baking sheet. Drizzle with 30ml olive oil. Season with half of the salt, pepper, dried oregano, garlic powder, and smoked paprika. Toss to coat evenly.

Pat chicken thighs dry. Place on a separate baking sheet. Drizzle with remaining 30ml olive oil. Season with remaining salt, pepper, and fresh rosemary and thyme sprigs. Ensure chicken is seasoned well.

Roast vegetables for 20 minutes. Add chicken thighs to the oven with the vegetables. Continue roasting for another 20-25 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C and vegetables are tender-crisp. Remove rosemary and thyme sprigs from chicken before serving.
Combine roasted vegetables with the cooked quinoa in a large bowl. Toss gently to mix. Taste and adjust seasoning if needed.
Portion the quinoa and vegetable medley onto four plates. Place one roasted chicken thigh alongside each portion. Garnish generously with fresh chopped parsley. Serve immediately.
notes: This recipe is designed to be naturally gluten-free and suitable for a diabetic-like diet, focusing on lean protein, complex carbohydrates, and abundant non-starchy vegetables.
The flavors are savory and aromatic, appealing to a palate with lack of appetite without being heavy or overly rich.

recipes.recipe_name: Poached Fermented Apple & Pear with Dark Chocolate & Apple Skin Crisp
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of poached fruit is elegantly arranged on a handcrafted, unglazed ceramic plate in a natural cream tone. Three to four plump, pale golden-brown apple and pear wedges are artfully placed on one side, leaving ample negative space. The fruit retains its natural shape and skin texture, glistening with vanilla-infused liquid. Fine, irregular dark chocolate shavings are scattered sparingly over the fruit and plate. A single, brittle, curled shard of crispy apple skin stands upright beside the fruit, offering rustic texture. This clean, unforced composition highlights each component's natural beauty. The plate rests on a light, textured bamboo surface. An undyed linen napkin is folded simply beside it. Soft, natural light illuminates the scene, with a hint of blurred greenery in the minimal background, emphasizing nature and sustainability.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Served as a light, refreshing end to a meal, emphasizing natural flavors.
Can be accompanied by a small glass of mineral water.

ingredients.name: Natural sweetener (maple syrup or local honey)

instructions: Prepare Fermented Fruit: Wash apple and pear. Do not peel. Cut apple and pear into 2 cm thick wedges. Remove core. In a clean 500ml jar, combine 250ml filtered water and 5g sea salt. Stir to dissolve. Add fruit wedges to the jar. Ensure fruit is fully submerged. Cover loosely with a lid or airlock. Ferment at room temperature (18-22°C) for 3-5 days. Taste daily. Fermentation is complete when fruit is slightly tangy and retains some firmness.

Prepare Apple Skin Crisp: Carefully peel a small section of apple skin (approx. 5x5 cm) from the leftover apple. Lay skin flat on a baking tray lined with parchment paper. Bake at 100°C for 20-30 minutes until completely dry and crispy. Watch closely to prevent burning.

Prepare Poaching Liquid: Drain fermented fruit. Reserve brine for other uses. In a small saucepan, combine 100ml fresh water, scraped vanilla seeds, and vanilla pod. Add 5g natural sweetener if desired. Bring to a gentle simmer.

Poach Fruit: Add fermented apple and pear wedges to the simmering vanilla liquid. Poach gently for 5-7 minutes, until fruit is tender but still holds its shape. Remove fruit with a slotted spoon. Reduce poaching liquid slightly for a light syrup.
Prepare Dark Chocolate: Use a vegetable peeler or grater to create thin shavings from the dark chocolate.

Assemble: Arrange poached fruit wedges neatly on one side of a minimalistic white or cream plate. Drizzle a small amount of the vanilla poaching liquid over the fruit. Sprinkle dark chocolate shavings over and around the fruit. Place the crispy apple skin shard upright next to the fruit.
notes: The fermented fruit offers a unique tangy counterpoint to the sweetness.
Reserve fermentation brine for dressings or a refreshing drink.
Adjust sweetener in poaching liquid to personal preference and fruit ripeness.

recipes.recipe_name: Compressed Apple & Pear, Vanilla Crémeux, Dark Chocolate, Apple Fluid Gel
recipes.visual_description: A Michelin-starred dessert is presented on a pristine white bone china plate with generous negative space. A flowing, organic arrangement of precisely cut 1 cm compressed apple and pear cubes forms the base, showcasing their translucent, pale golden hue. Beside them, two distinct, impeccably smooth quenelles of creamy white vanilla bean crémeux sit opposite two glossy, dark brown quenelles of intense dark chocolate crémeux. A delicate, translucent pool or artful drizzle of vibrant apple-pear fluid gel gleams on the plate, adding a subtle touch of green-gold. The composition is clean, architectural, and minimalist, emphasizing the purity of each component. A single, tiny, vibrant green micro-basil leaf or edible flower is strategically placed as the sole garnish. The setting is a luxurious, polished light grey marble surface, with a crisp white linen napkin folded precisely. Dramatic, focused lighting casts soft shadows, highlighting the dessert's textures and forms against an ultra-minimalist background.
instructions: For Compressed Apple & Pear: Peel and core apple and pear. Cut into precise 1 cm cubes. Split 1/4 vanilla bean pod, scrape seeds. Combine vanilla seeds with 50 ml water and 10 g sugar to make a light syrup. Place fruit cubes and vanilla syrup in a vacuum-seal bag. Seal under full vacuum. Chill for 1 hour.

For Vanilla Bean Crémeux: Hydrate 1 g gelatin leaf in cold water. Split remaining 1/4 vanilla bean pod, scrape seeds. Heat 50 ml heavy cream and 50 ml whole milk with vanilla pod and seeds to a simmer. Remove vanilla pod. Whisk 2 egg yolks with 10 g sugar until pale. Slowly temper hot cream mixture into egg yolks. Return mixture to saucepan. Cook over medium-low heat, stirring constantly, until mixture thickens to coat the back of a spoon (nappe consistency). Remove from heat. Stir in hydrated gelatin until dissolved. Pass through a fine-mesh sieve. Pour into a shallow dish. Cover surface with plastic wrap. Chill completely for at least 3 hours, or until firm.

For Dark Chocolate Crémeux: Hydrate 1 g gelatin leaf in cold water. Finely chop dark chocolate. Heat 50 ml heavy cream to a simmer. Pour hot cream over chopped chocolate. Let sit for 1 minute. Stir gently from the center until smooth and emulsified. Stir in hydrated gelatin until dissolved. Pour into a small piping bag or shallow dish. Chill until firm enough to pipe or quenelle.

For Apple-Pear Fluid Gel: Juice remaining apple and pear scraps (or use fresh juice) to yield 50 ml. Strain juice through a fine-mesh sieve. In a small saucepan, combine 50 ml apple-pear juice, 10 ml lemon juice, 10 g sugar, and 0.5 g agar-agar. Bring to a boil, whisking constantly. Boil for 1 minute. Pour into a shallow dish. Chill completely until firm. Once firm, cut into chunks. Blend in a high-speed blender until completely smooth and fluid. Pass through a fine-mesh sieve for ultimate smoothness.
