Transfer to a squeeze bottle.

To Assemble: On a chilled fine-dining plate, arrange a natural, flowing line or curve of compressed apple and pear cubes. Using a small spoon or piping bag, place two small, distinct quenelles or dots of vanilla bean crémeux next to the fruit. Repeat with two small quenelles or dots of dark chocolate crémeux, creating a subtle visual tension. Gently drizzle or create a small pool of the apple-pear fluid gel around the elements. Garnish with a single micro-basil leaf or a tiny edible flower for a pop of color and freshness. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Mediterranean Lemon Herb Chicken with Quinoa
recipes.visual_description: A seared, golden-brown chicken breast, sliced into thick medallions, is the focal point, positioned slightly off-center on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. Beside it, a generous mound of fluffy quinoa salad, vibrant with finely diced cucumber, halved cherry tomatoes, and finely chopped red onion. Fresh green parsley and mint leaves are mixed throughout the quinoa and lightly scattered over the chicken. A bright yellow lemon wedge sits near the chicken, and a sprinkle of crumbled white feta cheese with a few dark Kalamata olives adds visual interest and flavor. The dish has natural, balanced colors and varied textures. The setting is a modern bistro with a simple wooden table and a neatly folded cotton napkin beside the plate. Natural, even lighting highlights the fresh ingredients. The entire single portion is clearly visible, presented professionally yet approachably.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm crusty bread to sop up any juices.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C (375°F).
Season chicken breasts generously with salt, pepper, and dried oregano.
Heat 30ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken breasts 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown.
Transfer skillet to preheated oven. Bake 10-15 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from oven, rest 5 minutes.
While chicken bakes, rinse quinoa thoroughly under cold water.
In a medium saucepan, heat 15ml olive oil over medium heat. Add minced garlic and half of the diced red onion. Sauté 2 minutes until fragrant.
Add rinsed quinoa to saucepan. Toast 1 minute. Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer 15 minutes, or until liquid is absorbed and quinoa is fluffy.
Remove quinoa from heat. Let stand covered 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork.
In a large bowl, combine cooked quinoa, remaining diced red onion, halved cherry tomatoes, small diced cucumber, chopped parsley, and chopped mint.
Drizzle quinoa mixture with remaining 15ml olive oil and fresh lemon juice. Season with salt and pepper. Toss gently to combine.
Slice rested chicken breasts into thick medallions. Do not fan out slices.
Portion quinoa salad onto plates. Arrange sliced chicken medallions beside quinoa. Garnish with crumbled feta cheese and Kalamata olives if desired. Serve immediately.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Rhubarb Confit, Fromage Frais Parfait, Rhubarb Tuile
recipes.visual_description: A single, elegantly plated dessert designed with architectural minimalism on a smooth, matte bone china plate in a pristine white hue. The central focus is a pristine, cylindrical Fromage Frais Parfait, its surface subtly frosted, positioned off-center to allow abundant negative space. Around its base, several pieces of translucent, pale pink rhubarb confit are artfully arranged, their softened forms creating a gentle contrast to the parfait's sharp edges. Scattered precisely are a few small, clear cubes of vibrant ruby-red rhubarb gel, catching the light and adding a burst of intense color and sharp geometric counterpoint. A single, delicate, crisp rhubarb tuile, thin and irregularly shaped, leans gracefully against the parfait, its golden-pink hue providing a textural and color contrast. Two or three delicate candied violet petals, a soft lilac, are thoughtfully placed as the sole garnish, offering a subtle floral whisper and a final touch of sophisticated color. The composition is clean, airy, and intentional, each element meticulously placed. The entire plate is visible, showcasing the thoughtful arrangement and generous white space. The setting features a polished white Carrara marble surface, reflecting subtle professional lighting from the side, creating soft shadows. A crisp white linen napkin, precisely folded into a sharp triangle, rests beside the plate. The overall impression is one of refined elegance and understated luxury.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve chilled on a cold plate.
Pair with a delicate, crisp Swiss white wine like a Chasselas, or a light fruit eau-de-vie.
instructions: Rhubarb Confit:
Wash 50g rhubarb. Cut into 2 cm oblique pieces.
Combine rhubarb, 30g sugar, 50ml water in a small saucepan.
Cook over very low heat 15-20 minutes. Do not stir. Rhubarb should be tender but hold shape.
Cool completely.
Rhubarb Gel:
Soak 1g gelatin in ice water.
Juice 50g fresh rhubarb using a juicer or blender then fine-mesh sieve. Reserve 35ml juice.
Heat 30ml rhubarb juice with 10g sugar until sugar dissolves.
Squeeze excess water from gelatin. Stir into warm juice until dissolved.
Stir in remaining 5ml cold rhubarb juice.
Pour into a shallow container. Chill until set. Cut into small cubes.
Fromage Frais Parfait:
Soak 2g gelatin in ice water.
Whisk 1 egg yolk with 10g sugar until pale.
Heat 20ml water with 10g glucose syrup to 118°C.
Slowly pour hot syrup into egg yolk mixture while whisking constantly. Continue whisking until cool and thick. This is a pâte à bombe.
In a separate bowl, whip 70ml heavy cream to soft peaks.
Gently fold 100g fromage frais into the cooled pâte à bombe.
Melt soaked gelatin over a double boiler or microwave. Stir a small amount of parfait mixture into melted gelatin, then fold back into main parfait base.
Gently fold whipped cream into parfait base.
Pour into a small mold (e.g., silicone cylinder or small rectangular mold). Freeze minimum 4 hours.
Rhubarb Tuile:
Melt 10g butter.
Whisk 1 egg white with 10g sugar until frothy.
Add 10g flour, melted butter, and 5ml rhubarb juice (from juicing step). Mix until smooth.
Spread very thinly on a silicone mat or parchment paper in an irregular, organic shape.
Bake at 160°C for 8-10 minutes until golden and crisp.
Cool completely.
Assembly:
Carefully unmold frozen parfait. Place centrally on a chilled plate.
Arrange rhubarb confit pieces around the parfait.
Place rhubarb gel cubes artfully around the dish.
Gently lean the rhubarb tuile against the parfait.
Scatter 2-3 candied violet petals for garnish.
notes: Ensure all components are perfectly chilled before assembly for optimal texture and presentation.
Precision in cutting and shaping is key for the minimalist aesthetic.

recipes.recipe_name: Apricot Textures, Chamomile, Buttermilk Crisp
recipes.visual_description: A minimalist, ultra-sophisticated dessert is artfully plated on a round white bone china plate. Three to four precisely cut, firm apricot wedges, a vibrant orange, are arranged organically on one side of the plate. Adjacent to them, small, glistening dots or a delicate swipe of intensely flavored apricot gel provide a contrasting smooth texture and rich color. A small, ethereal pool of pale yellow chamomile crèmeux, subtly fragrant, sits elegantly nearby. Several shards of golden-brown buttermilk crisp stand upright, adding architectural height and a crisp texture. The composition utilizes abundant negative space, highlighting each component's pristine execution. The setting features a premium grey-veined marble surface, a pristine white linen napkin folded into a precise triangle, and dramatic, focused lighting creating elegant shadows. The entire plate is visible, showcasing the exquisite plating and refined portion size.
instructions: Prepare Compressed Apricots: Halve and pit apricots. Prepare a syrup with 20g sugar and 50ml water. Add 2ml lemon juice. Place apricot halves in a vacuum bag with syrup. Vacuum seal. Gently poach sealed bag in a 70°C water bath for 15 minutes. Chill immediately in ice bath. Remove from bag. Cut into precise wedges.

Prepare Apricot Gel: Dice 1 apricot (about 70g). Blend with 30g sugar and 50ml water until smooth. Strain through a fine-mesh sieve. Heat strained apricot liquid with 1g agar-agar, whisking constantly, bring to a simmer for 1 minute. Pour into a shallow dish. Chill until set. Once set, blend until completely smooth and glossy.

Prepare Chamomile Crèmeux: Heat heavy cream until just simmering. Remove from heat. Add chamomile flowers. Steep for 15 minutes. Strain cream, pressing flowers to extract flavor. Chill cream thoroughly.

Prepare Buttermilk Crisps: Whisk buttermilk, flour, melted butter, glucose syrup, and a pinch of salt until smooth. Spread very thinly onto a silicone mat or parchment paper. Bake at 150°C for 10-12 minutes, or until golden brown and crisp. Cool completely. Break into irregular shards.

Assembly: On a pristine white plate, arrange compressed apricot wedges with deliberate negative space. Place small dots or a delicate swipe of apricot gel beside the apricots. Spoon a small, elegant pool of chilled chamomile crèmeux onto the plate. Stand several buttermilk crisp shards vertically or artfully placed. Garnish with a single edible flower petal for color contrast.

recipes.recipe_name: Seared Apricots with Fermented Apricot Reduction & Cultured Quark
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of seared apricots rests on a light cream-colored, handcrafted ceramic plate with subtle organic texture, on a reclaimed light wood surface. Two apricot halves, cut-side down, display deep golden-brown caramelized surfaces and vibrant orange flesh. Beside them, a clean dollop of creamy white quark sits. A glossy, deep amber fermented apricot reduction is artfully drizzled over apricots and quark, creating natural trails. A sprinkle of lightly toasted flaked almonds or sunflower seeds adds contrasting texture and earthy tone. The composition emphasizes natural shapes and negative space. An undyed linen napkin in natural beige is casually placed. The background is clean and minimalist, with soft natural light highlighting the ingredients' pure beauty.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve as a light, natural dessert after a meal.
Pair with a small glass of mineral water or a light herbal tea.

ingredients.name: Toasted flaked almonds or sunflower seeds

instructions: Prepare fermented apricot reduction: Roughly chop overripe apricots. Combine with 5 ml honey and 15 ml water in a clean jar. Cover loosely with cloth. Ferment at room temperature for 3-5 days, or until slightly bubbly and tangy. Strain liquid through a fine sieve. Press solids to extract all liquid. Reduce liquid in a small saucepan over low heat until syrupy. Set aside.
Prepare fresh apricots: Halve ripe apricots. Remove pits.
Sear apricots: Heat a dry pan over medium heat. Place apricot halves cut-side down. Sear for 2-3 minutes until caramelized and slightly softened. Turn and sear skin-side for 1 minute.
Plate the dish: Arrange seared apricot halves on a small, natural ceramic plate. Add a dollop of quark or crème fraîche beside them.
Finish and serve: Drizzle the fermented apricot reduction generously over the apricots and quark. Sprinkle with toasted flaked almonds or sunflower seeds. Serve immediately.
notes: Adjust fermentation time based on desired tanginess and ambient temperature.
The fermented apricot reduction can be made in advance and stored in the refrigerator.

recipes.recipe_name: Alpine Beef & Spelt Soup with Fermented Roots
recipes.special_requests: Swiss cuisine, must include (apart from the main ingredient, beef) vegetables and carbohydrates. Must not include potato. Please use unconventional flavour combinations
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of hearty Alpine Beef & Spelt Soup is presented in a handcrafted ceramic bowl with a matte, earthy beige finish, reflecting traditional Swiss pottery. The rich, clear amber beef broth cradles tender, 2cm beef cubes and plump, creamy pearl spelt grains. Interspersed are softened 1cm diced fermented carrots and parsnips, offering subtle color variations and a hint of tang. Freshly wilted, dark green Swiss chard leaves provide a vibrant contrast. The soup is naturally garnished with a sprinkle of finely chopped fresh chives and a scattering of golden-brown, irregular crispy beef cracklings, adding texture and a zero-waste element. The bowl sits on a light, naturally textured reclaimed wood table surface. A simple, rustic metal spoon rests beside the bowl on an undyed linen napkin. The background is clean and minimalistic, bathed in soft, natural light, with a hint of a green plant visible, emphasizing sustainability and the dish's natural origins.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a slice of crusty rye bread.
Accompany with a small, simple green salad dressed with a light vinaigrette.
instructions: Prepare Fermented Root Vegetables (1 week ahead): Combine 1cm diced carrots and parsnips in a clean glass jar. Dissolve salt in filtered water to create a brine. Pour brine over vegetables, ensuring they are fully submerged. Seal jar loosely or use an airlock lid. Ferment at room temperature (18-22°C) for 5-7 days, or until desired tanginess. Burp daily if not using an airlock. Store in refrigerator after fermentation.

Make Beef Broth: Preheat oven to 200°C. Roast beef bones and trimmings on a baking sheet for 30 minutes until browned. Transfer roasted bones and trimmings to a large pot. Add cold water, quartered onion, roughly chopped carrot, roughly chopped celery, bay leaf, and peppercorns. Bring to a gentle simmer. Skim any foam. Reduce heat to low. Simmer for 4-6 hours, partially covered. Strain broth through a fine-mesh sieve. Discard solids. Separate beef trimmings. Render any fat from trimmings in a small pan over low heat until crispy cracklings form. Reserve cracklings and rendered fat. Cool broth. Skim any excess fat.

Cook the Soup: Pour 500 mL of prepared beef broth into a medium saucepan. Bring to a simmer. Add 2cm cubed lean beef. Cook for 15 minutes, or until beef is tender. Add rinsed pearl spelt to the soup. Simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until spelt is tender. Drain 100 g of fermented root vegetables from their brine. Add them to the soup during the last 5 minutes of cooking. Stir in chopped Swiss chard or spinach. Cook until just wilted. Season soup with salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste.
Serve: Ladle hot soup into a serving bowl. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley or chives. Sprinkle crispy beef cracklings over the soup. Serve immediately.
notes: This recipe utilizes beef bones and trimmings for a flavorful broth and crispy garnish, embodying a zero-waste approach.
Fermenting vegetables is an ancient preservation technique, adding depth and a unique tang while extending the shelf life of seasonal produce.
Spelt is an ancient grain, a sustainable and nutritious alternative to more common carbohydrates.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken Breast with Lemon-Cinnamon Butter and Savory Meringue Crumble
recipes.visual_description: A single pan-seared chicken breast, golden-brown with a crisp exterior, rests centered on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. A vibrant yellow lemon-cinnamon butter sauce pools around the chicken, reflecting light. Scattered across the chicken and sauce are irregular, light orange and white savory meringue crumbles, providing a textural contrast. Finely chopped fresh green parsley is sprinkled over the dish, adding a pop of color and freshness. The chicken is presented as a whole piece, not sliced. The plate is set on a simple wooden table surface, with a folded cotton napkin and standard flatware to the side. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and colors against a minimal, casual restaurant-style background.
instructions: Preheat oven to 120°C. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.

For the savory meringue crumble: In a clean, dry bowl, whip egg whites until soft peaks form. Gradually add granulated sugar, salt, garlic powder, and smoked paprika. Continue whipping until stiff, glossy peaks form.
Spread meringue thinly onto the prepared baking sheet. Bake for 60-75 minutes, or until dried and crisp. Let cool completely. Break into small crumbles.
Season chicken breasts generously with salt and black pepper.

Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken breasts for 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown. Internal temperature should reach 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from skillet and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add butter to the same skillet. Once melted, add lemon zest and ground cinnamon. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in chicken stock and lemon juice. Bring to a simmer, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan. Cook until sauce slightly thickens, about 3-5 minutes.
Return chicken breasts to the skillet, basting with the lemon-cinnamon butter sauce. Cook for 1-2 minutes to warm through.
Chop fresh parsley finely.

To serve: Place one chicken breast on each plate. Spoon generous amounts of lemon-cinnamon butter sauce over the chicken. Sprinkle savory meringue crumble over the chicken and sauce. Garnish with chopped fresh parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Seared Beef with Fermented Pear & Spelt
recipes.special_requests: Swiss cuisine, must include (apart from the main ingredient, beef) vegetables and carbohydrates. Must not include potato. Please use unconventional flavour combinations
recipes.visual_description: A single, refined portion of seared beef is the centerpiece, presented as thick, rustic chunks, not sliced. The beef boasts a deep, caramelized crust and a tender interior. Alongside, a mound of earthy spelt berries, their natural texture visible. Irregularly cut, lightly seared carrots and celeriac chunks, showcasing their vibrant natural colors, are artfully arranged. Wilted Swiss chard leaves and thinly sliced stems add a touch of deep green. Two to three translucent, subtly yellow fermented pear slices are carefully placed, offering an intriguing visual contrast. A light, savory jus is delicately drizzled over the beef and vegetables. The composition is minimalistic, emphasizing natural forms and textures. The plate is a handcrafted ceramic in a natural cream or beige tone, allowing ample white space. The setting features a light, reclaimed wood table surface, an undyed linen napkin in natural beige, and soft, natural light. A simple, out-of-focus potted green plant provides a subtle background element. The entire plate is visible, showcasing a clean, uncrowded presentation that celebrates each ingredient's pure beauty.
instructions: Rinse spelt berries. Cook spelt in 200 ml salted water for 25-30 minutes. Drain excess water. Keep warm.
Peel carrots and celeriac. Cut into irregular 1-2 cm chunks. Blanch in boiling salted water for 3-4 minutes. Drain. Set aside.
Wash Swiss chard. Separate leaves from stems. Roughly chop leaves. Thinly slice stems.
Pat beef dry. Season beef generously with salt and pepper.

Heat olive oil in a heavy skillet over medium-high heat. Sear beef for 3-4 minutes per side for medium-rare. Adjust time for desired doneness. Add garlic clove and thyme sprig to skillet during last minute of searing.
Remove beef from skillet. Rest on a cutting board for 5 minutes.
Add blanched carrots and celeriac to the same skillet. Sauté for 2-3 minutes until lightly browned. Add Swiss chard stems. Sauté 1 minute. Add chard leaves. Cook until wilted.
Deglaze skillet with vegetable broth. Scrape up any browned bits. Reduce slightly to form a light jus.

Slice beef into two or three thick pieces, not fanned. Place beef on a plate. Arrange cooked spelt alongside. Place sautéed vegetables and chard around. Neatly arrange fermented pear slices on the plate. Drizzle jus over beef and vegetables. Garnish with a fresh thyme sprig.

recipes.recipe_name: Mango Passion Coconut Delice
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of an ultra-sophisticated dessert is artfully arranged on a round, modern designer plate made of pristine white bone china. The plate rests on a cool white Carrara marble surface, softly illuminated by professional, dramatic lighting that creates subtle shadows. The main element is a perfectly formed, pale yellow mango passion fruit mousse, its surface smooth and inviting. Beside it, a rectangular piece of golden-brown coconut dacquoise provides a textural contrast. Small, vibrant green dots of kaffir lime gel are meticulously piped in an organic, flowing pattern around the base of the mousse and dacquoise, adding a burst of color and a hint of tartness. A delicate, curved toasted coconut tuile, light golden-brown and translucent, leans gracefully against the mousse, offering an architectural element and a crisp texture. The plate is largely negative space, emphasizing the minimalist composition. A single, tiny edible flower petal or a few micro mint leaves are precisely placed for a final touch of color and freshness. The overall presentation is one of refined elegance, showcasing mastery of technique and sophisticated flavor balance.
instructions: Preheat oven to 170°C. Line a baking tray with parchment paper.
Whisk egg whites until soft peaks form. Gradually add 75g granulated sugar. Whisk until stiff, glossy meringue.
Sift 25g icing sugar and almond flour. Fold into meringue.
Gently fold in 25g desiccated coconut.
Spread dacquoise mixture thinly (approx. 0.5 cm thick) onto prepared tray.
Bake 15-20 minutes, or until lightly golden and firm.
Cool completely. Cut into 4 equal rectangles or discs.
Combine 100ml water, 20g granulated sugar, and torn kaffir lime leaves in a small saucepan. Bring to a simmer.
Steep 10 minutes. Remove kaffir lime leaves.
Whisk in agar-agar powder. Bring to a boil. Simmer 1 minute, whisking constantly.
Pour into a shallow dish. Chill until set (approx. 30 minutes).
Once set, blend until smooth gel forms. Transfer to a piping bag.
Hydrate gelatin leaves in cold water.
In a saucepan, whisk mango purée, passion fruit purée, 40g granulated sugar, and egg yolks.
Cook over medium-low heat, stirring constantly, until mixture thickens slightly (approx. 80-82°C). Do not boil.
Remove from heat. Stir in squeezed gelatin until dissolved.
Pass mixture through a fine-mesh sieve. Cool over an ice bath until lukewarm (approx. 25°C).
Whip cold heavy cream to soft peaks.
Fold whipped cream into the fruit base in two additions.
Spoon mousse into desired molds (e.g., silicone half-sphere molds) or pipe directly onto plates for immediate serving.
Chill mousse a minimum of 4 hours, preferably overnight, until firm.
Preheat oven to 160°C. Line a baking tray with silicone mat or parchment paper.
Whisk melted butter, 30g icing sugar, all-purpose flour, 15g desiccated coconut, and egg white until smooth batter forms.
Spread thin circles or desired shapes onto prepared tray using a small offset spatula.
Bake 8-10 minutes, or until edges are golden brown.
Immediately remove from tray. Gently drape over a rolling pin or curved surface to create a curved shape.
Cool completely. Store in an airtight container.
Place one dacquoise piece slightly off-center on each plate.
Gently unmold one mango passion fruit mousse. Place next to the dacquoise.
Pipe small, organic dots or a delicate smear of kaffir lime gel around the mousse and dacquoise.
Carefully place one curved toasted coconut tuile leaning against the mousse or dacquoise.
Garnish with a few micro mint leaves or small edible flower petals.
Ensure abundant negative space around elements for minimalist, artistic presentation.

recipes.recipe_name: Herb-Roasted Chicken Thighs with Garlic Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single, perfectly roasted chicken thigh, golden-brown with crispy, rendered skin, rests slightly off-center on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. The chicken is presented as a whole piece. Around and partially beneath the chicken are scattered generous portions of roasted potato wedges, their skins a deep golden-brown and interiors tender, showing some caramelized edges. Interspersed among the potatoes are a few soft, roasted garlic cloves and aromatic sprigs of rosemary and thyme, hinting at their infused flavor. A vibrant sprinkle of freshly chopped green parsley garnishes the entire dish, adding a burst of fresh color. The presentation is clean and organized, with moderate negative space. The dish is set on a simple light wooden table surface, with a folded white cotton napkin placed to the side. Natural, even lighting highlights the textures and colors, creating an inviting, casual dining ambiance.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread to sop up pan juices.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Peel potatoes. Cut into 2cm wedges.
Smash garlic cloves. Do not peel.
In a large roasting pan, combine potato wedges, smashed garlic, rosemary sprigs, and thyme sprigs. Drizzle with 30ml olive oil. Season with salt and pepper. Toss to coat.
Arrange potatoes in a single layer in the pan. Place chicken thighs skin-side up on top of the potatoes.
Drizzle remaining 30ml olive oil over chicken.
Roast for 25 minutes.
Pour chicken broth into the pan. Squeeze lemon half over chicken and potatoes. Add lemon half to the pan.
Continue roasting for another 20-25 minutes, or until chicken skin is golden and crispy, and internal temperature reaches 75°C. Potatoes should be tender and lightly browned.
Rest chicken for 5 minutes before serving.
Chop fresh parsley. Garnish dish before serving.
notes: Using bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs ensures maximum flavor and a crispy skin.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Beef Fillet, Tonka Bean Parsnip Purée, Braised Endive, Coffee Jus
recipes.special_requests: must include (apart from the main ingredient, beef) vegetables and carbohydrates. Must not include potato. Please use unconventional flavour combinations
recipes.visual_description: A single, perfectly roasted beef fillet chunk, deep brown with a visible sear, anchors the center-right of a pristine white bone china plate. Beside it, a delicate, artful swoosh of silky, pale cream-colored tonka bean parsnip purée extends gracefully. Two halves of braised Belgian endive, their edges softly caramelized, are meticulously placed to complement the composition. A glossy, deep brown coffee-infused jus forms a refined pool at the base of the beef, catching the light. The overall plating is minimalist and sophisticated, with abundant negative space. The setting is a luxurious white Carrara marble surface. A precisely folded white linen napkin and a single modern fork lie to the left. Dramatic professional lighting casts soft shadows, emphasizing the dish's elegant simplicity and rich textures.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C. Season beef fillet with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in an oven-safe pan. Sear beef fillet 2 minutes per side until golden brown.
Transfer pan to oven. Roast beef 8-10 minutes for medium-rare, or until desired doneness. Rest beef 5 minutes.
Peel and dice parsnips. Boil parsnips in salted water until very tender, about 15 minutes. Drain well.
Combine cooked parsnips, heavy cream, 20g butter, and grated tonka bean in a blender. Blend until smooth. Season with salt. Keep warm.
Halve endive lengthwise. Heat remaining 10g butter in a small pan. Place endive cut-side down. Braise gently until tender and slightly caramelized, about 5-7 minutes.
For the jus, finely mince shallot. Sauté shallot in a clean saucepan until softened. Deglaze with red wine. Reduce by half.
Add beef stock and coffee to the pan. Simmer until reduced to a glossy sauce consistency, about 10-12 minutes. Strain through a fine-mesh sieve. Season with salt and pepper.
Slice rested beef fillet into two thick medallions. Place a swoosh of parsnip purée on the plate. Arrange beef medallions next to the purée.
Place braised endive artfully beside the beef. Spoon coffee jus around the plate. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Creamy Mushroom Rice and Roasted Broccoli
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, centrally composed with moderate negative space. A generous portion of creamy mushroom risotto forms the base, its pale, rich texture visible. Thick, golden-brown pan-seared chicken chunks are placed atop the risotto, showcasing a perfectly seared crust and moist interior. Beside the chicken and risotto, vibrant green roasted broccoli florets are arranged, exhibiting slight charring on their edges and a tender appearance. A sprinkle of fresh, chopped parsley provides a final touch of color and freshness over the chicken and risotto. The overall presentation is balanced and inviting, highlighting distinct textures and natural colors. The plate rests on a simple wooden table surface with a cotton napkin beside it. Natural, even lighting illuminates the food, creating a modern bistro ambiance.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Toss broccoli florets with 10 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking sheet. Roast for 15-20 minutes until tender and slightly charred. Set aside.
Pat chicken thighs dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and pepper.

Heat 20 ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken thighs for 6-8 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through to an internal temperature of 75°C. Remove chicken from skillet. Rest on a cutting board.

Reduce heat to medium. Add 30 g butter to the same skillet. Add diced onion. Sauté until translucent, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic and sliced mushrooms. Cook until mushrooms soften and release their liquid, about 5-7 minutes.
Add Arborio rice to the skillet. Stir constantly for 1 minute to toast the rice.
If using, pour in white wine. Stir until completely absorbed.
Add hot chicken broth, one ladle at a time. Stir continuously. Wait for each ladleful to be almost fully absorbed before adding the next. Continue for 18-20 minutes until rice is creamy and al dente.
Remove skillet from heat. Stir in remaining 30 g butter and grated Parmesan cheese. Stir in half of the chopped parsley. Season risotto with salt and pepper to taste.
Slice rested chicken thighs into thick chunks. Do not fan slices.
Spoon creamy mushroom rice onto individual plates. Arrange chicken chunks on top of the rice. Place roasted broccoli florets beside the chicken and rice. Garnish with remaining fresh parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Beef Short Rib, Smoked Potato Puree, Espresso Caramel Glaze, Pickled Red Onion
recipes.special_requests: must include (apart from the main ingredient, beef) vegetables and carbohydrates. Please use unconventional flavour combinations
recipes.visual_description: A single, perfectly braised, dark mahogany beef short rib chunk, approximately 8x6x4 cm, rests elegantly on a large, matte dark grey bone china plate. A smooth, light grey-brown smoked potato puree forms a refined quenelle beside it. A few vibrant, translucent rings of thinly sliced pickled red onion are artfully placed, providing sharp color contrast. A glossy, dark espresso caramel glaze is delicately drizzled, forming abstract, flowing lines. The braising liquid reduction lightly coats the beef, adding a rich sheen. A single, tiny sprig of bronze fennel micro-herbs offers a subtle green accent. The composition is minimalist, with abundant negative space. The plate is centered on a premium dark wood table, bathed in dramatic professional lighting that creates soft shadows, highlighting textures. The background is ultra-minimalist, ensuring the dish is the sole focal point.

ingredients.name: Red Onion, thinly sliced into rings

instructions: Preheat oven to 160°C.
Season beef short rib generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in an oven-safe Dutch oven or heavy-bottomed pot over high heat.
Sear beef short rib on all sides until deeply browned. Remove beef from pot.
Add diced carrot, celery, and yellow onion to pot. Sauté until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Add crushed garlic, thyme, and bay leaf. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Deglaze pot with red wine. Scrape up any browned bits from bottom of pot. Reduce wine by half.
Return beef to pot. Pour in beef stock. Liquid should almost cover beef. Bring to a simmer.
Cover pot tightly. Transfer to preheated oven. Braise for 3-4 hours, or until beef is fork-tender.
Remove beef from pot. Strain braising liquid through a fine-mesh sieve into a saucepan. Discard solids.
Reduce braising liquid over medium-high heat until thickened to a glaze consistency. Season with salt and pepper. Keep warm.
For Pickled Red Onion: Combine white wine vinegar, water, sugar, and salt in a small saucepan. Bring to a simmer until sugar and salt dissolve.
Pour hot pickling liquid over thinly sliced red onion rings in a heatproof bowl. Let cool to room temperature. Chill until ready to serve.
For Smoked Potato Puree: Peel and cut Yukon Gold potatoes into uniform chunks.
Place potatoes in a saucepan. Cover with cold salted water. Bring to a boil. Cook until very tender, about 15-20 minutes.
Drain potatoes thoroughly. Return to hot saucepan over low heat for 1 minute to dry. Press potatoes through a fine-mesh sieve or ricer into a bowl.
Heat heavy cream and butter in a small saucepan until just simmering.
Gradually whisk hot cream and butter into riced potatoes until smooth and creamy. Season with salt.
Place potato puree in a sealed container or bowl. Use a smoking gun to infuse with wood smoke for 5-10 minutes. Seal container to hold smoke. Repeat if stronger smoke flavor is desired. Keep warm.
For Espresso Caramel Glaze: Combine granulated sugar and water in a clean, heavy-bottomed saucepan over medium heat. Cook without stirring until sugar dissolves and turns a deep amber color.
Carefully add heavy cream (for caramel) and espresso powder to hot caramel. Whisk vigorously until smooth. Be careful, mixture will bubble up. Remove from heat. Keep warm.
To Serve: Reheat braised short rib gently in the reduced braising liquid/glaze.
Spoon a swoosh or quenelle of smoked potato puree onto the center of a large, minimalist plate.
Place the braised beef short rib chunk next to the puree. Drizzle generously with the reduced braising liquid/glaze.
Artistically arrange a few pickled red onion rings around the beef and puree.
Drizzle the espresso caramel glaze sparingly around the plate, creating delicate lines or dots.
Garnish with a tiny sprig of micro-herbs, if using.
notes: Ensure short rib is fork-tender for optimal texture.
For a deeper smoke flavor in the puree, smoke the potatoes twice.
The espresso caramel glaze is potent; use sparingly to balance flavors.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Beef Tenderloin, Pomme Anna, Glazed Carrots, Bordelaise
recipes.special_requests: must include (apart from the main ingredient, beef) vegetables and carbohydrates
recipes.visual_description: A single, perfectly plated Pan-Seared Beef Tenderloin dish rests on a pristine white Carrara marble surface, presented on an exquisite round bone china plate with subtle, abstract grey patterns. The rich, deeply crusted beef tenderloin, a whole, unsliced piece, anchors the composition, showcasing its tender, juicy interior. Adjacent, a precisely formed, golden-brown disc of Pomme Anna, revealing delicate, layered potato rounds, adds textural contrast. Three vibrant orange glazed baby carrots are artfully placed, their glossy surface catching the light. A rich, dark Bordelaise sauce forms an elegant pool beside the beef, reflecting dramatic professional lighting. Abundant negative space surrounds the elements, emphasizing sophisticated minimalism. A single, small fresh thyme sprig provides a subtle green accent. A crisp, white linen napkin, precisely folded, enhances the luxurious, uncluttered aesthetic.
instructions: For Pomme Anna: Preheat oven to 190°C. Slice potato into very thin, uniform rounds (1-2 mm thick) using a mandoline. Melt 30g butter. Arrange potato slices in a small, oven-safe round mold or ring, overlapping tightly. Brush each layer with melted butter. Season lightly with salt and pepper every few layers. Press down firmly. Bake for 40-50 minutes, or until golden and tender. Remove from oven, press again, and let cool slightly. Carefully remove from mold.

For Glazed Carrots: Peel baby carrots. In a small saucepan, combine carrots with 15g butter, 30ml water, a pinch of salt. Cook over medium heat, shaking pan occasionally, until water evaporates and carrots are tender and glossy. About 8-10 minutes.

For Bordelaise Sauce: Finely mince shallot. Crush garlic clove. In a small saucepan, melt 5g butter. Sauté shallot until translucent. Add red wine, thyme, and crushed garlic. Reduce by half. Add beef stock. Continue to reduce until sauce coats the back of a spoon. Strain through a fine-mesh sieve. Whisk in remaining 10g butter and optional bone marrow until melted and emulsified. Season with salt and pepper. Keep warm.

For Beef Tenderloin: Pat beef dry. Season generously with sea salt and black pepper. Heat olive oil in a heavy-bottomed, oven-safe skillet over high heat until shimmering. Carefully place beef in skillet. Sear for 2-3 minutes per side until a deep brown crust forms. Reduce heat to medium. Add 5g butter, a sprig of thyme, and garlic clove to skillet. Baste beef continuously for 3-4 minutes, turning once, until desired internal temperature is reached (e.g., 54°C for medium-rare). Transfer beef to a wire rack. Rest for 8-10 minutes. Do not slice.

Assembly: Place the Pomme Anna disc or rectangle slightly off-center on a bone china plate. Position the pan-seared beef tenderloin beside it as a whole piece. Arrange glazed baby carrots elegantly. Spoon a generous pool or artful drizzle of Bordelaise sauce around the beef and potato. Garnish with a tiny, fresh thyme sprig.
notes: Achieving a perfect crust on the beef requires a very hot pan and dry meat.
Resting the beef is crucial for juiciness.
Use a mandoline for uniform potato slices for Pomme Anna.

recipes.recipe_name: Sous Vide Beef Short Rib, Celery Root Puree, Glazed Carrots, Beef Jus
recipes.special_requests: must include (apart from the main ingredient, beef) vegetables and carbohydrates
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Sous Vide Beef Short Rib is meticulously plated on a matte black ceramic plate, showcasing modern minimalist elegance. The beef, a deep mahogany brown from precise searing, rests as a whole, succulent piece. Beside it, a swathe of velvety, pale ivory celery root puree forms a smooth, organic curve. Three perfectly glazed, vibrant orange carrot batons are artfully arranged, adding a pop of color and architectural precision. A glossy, dark amber beef jus pools gracefully around the elements, connecting them. The composition emphasizes clean lines, contrasting textures, and rich, earthy tones against the dark plate, leaving ample negative space. The dish is presented on a natural light wood table, accompanied by a folded pristine white linen napkin and minimalist silver cutlery.
instructions: Season beef short rib generously with salt and pepper. Place in a vacuum-sealable bag with one thyme sprig and the garlic clove. Vacuum seal the bag.
Cook beef in a water bath at 62°C for 24 hours.

Peel and dice celery root into 2cm cubes. Place in a small saucepan, cover with cold water, and add a pinch of salt. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer until very tender, about 15-20 minutes.

Drain celery root well. Transfer to a blender. Add 20g butter and whole milk. Blend until perfectly smooth and creamy. Pass through a fine-mesh sieve for ultimate silkiness. Season with salt to taste. Keep warm.

Peel carrots. Cut into precise 4cm batons. In a small saucepan, combine carrots, 10g butter, 50ml water, and a pinch of salt. Bring to a simmer. Cover and cook until tender-crisp and liquid has evaporated, about 8-10 minutes. Uncover and continue cooking until carrots are lightly glazed and tender.

Once beef is cooked sous vide, remove from bag. Pat dry thoroughly with paper towels. Heat olive oil in a small, heavy-bottomed pan over medium-high heat. Sear beef short rib on all sides until deep golden brown and caramelized, about 2-3 minutes per side.
Transfer seared beef to a wire rack. Rest for 5 minutes.
Gently warm the reduced beef stock in a small saucepan.

Spoon a generous dollop of celery root puree slightly off-center on a warm designer plate. Place the rested beef short rib beside the puree. Arrange the glazed carrot batons neatly next to the beef. Drizzle the rich beef jus around the beef and carrots. Garnish with a small, fresh thyme sprig if desired. Serve immediately.
notes: For best results, use a high-quality beef short rib with good marbling.
The beef jus should be intensely flavored and naturally thickened.

recipes.recipe_name: Sous Vide Beef Tenderloin, Smoked Potato Foam, Mushroom Dust
recipes.visual_description: A single, perfectly seared beef tenderloin medallion, sliced thick, rests slightly off-center on a pristine white bone china plate. Its deep, caramelized crust contrasts with the rosy, medium-rare interior. Adjacent, a cloud of light, airy smoked potato foam forms an organic, flowing shape, its creamy hue a soft counterpoint to the beef. A delicate dusting of dark, earthy mushroom powder is artfully scattered across the foam and plate, adding a subtle, rich texture and visual depth. Abundant negative space surrounds the components, emphasizing the dish's architectural precision and minimalist elegance. The setting is a polished white Carrara marble surface, illuminated by dramatic professional lighting that casts soft shadows, creating a sophisticated and luxurious ambiance. A crisp white linen napkin, folded precisely, complements the refined presentation.
instructions: Preheat oven to 120°C.
Spread dried porcini mushrooms on a baking sheet. Dehydrate in oven for 30-40 minutes until brittle.
Cool mushrooms completely. Grind into a fine powder using a spice grinder. Set aside.
Season beef tenderloin generously with salt and pepper.
Place beef, thyme sprigs, and garlic clove in a vacuum-sealable bag. Vacuum seal the bag.
Cook beef in a sous vide bath at 54°C for 2 hours.
Peel and dice potatoes. Boil potatoes in salted water until very tender.
Drain potatoes completely. Pass hot potatoes through a fine-mesh sieve or use a potato ricer for a smooth puree.
In a saucepan, heat milk, cream, and butter until butter melts. Stir in liquid smoke.
Slowly whisk liquid into potato puree until smooth. Season with salt. If using, whisk in a tiny pinch of xanthan gum.
Pass potato mixture through a fine-mesh sieve into a siphon. Charge siphon with one N2O cartridge. Shake well. Keep warm in a water bath.
Remove beef from sous vide bag. Pat very dry with paper towels.
Heat olive oil in a heavy-bottomed skillet over high heat until smoking.
Sear beef 1-2 minutes per side until a deep brown crust forms. Remove from heat.
Rest beef 5 minutes.
Slice beef tenderloin into two thick medallions.
Place medallions slightly offset on one side of a large, minimalist plate.
Dispense a small, organic mound of smoked potato foam next to the beef.
Lightly dust the plate and beef with mushroom powder. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Smoked Paprika & Cheddar Stuffed Chicken Breast
recipes.visual_description: A single golden-brown, pan-seared chicken breast, generously stuffed with a creamy smoked paprika and cheddar filling, takes center stage on a clean white porcelain plate. The chicken, cooked to a perfect 75°C, exhibits a crisp, savory exterior with a tender, juicy interior, showcasing the rich, melted cheese and herbs subtly peeking from the cut side. Beside the chicken, a neat cluster of vibrant green, perfectly roasted asparagus spears adds a fresh, crisp texture and earthy counterpoint. A smooth, glossy red pepper coulis is artfully drizzled around the plate, providing a striking color contrast and sweet, smoky notes. The dish is presented on a simple wooden table, accompanied by a folded cotton napkin, under soft, natural light, emphasizing a refined yet approachable casual dining experience.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
For the stuffing: Combine grated cheddar, smoked paprika, minced garlic, minced shallot, and chopped parsley in a bowl. Mix well. Season with salt and pepper.
Prepare chicken: Butterfly each chicken breast. Carefully pound each breast to an even thickness of about 1.5 cm.
Stuff chicken: Divide the cheese mixture among the chicken breasts. Place the mixture on one half of each breast. Fold the other half over to enclose the filling. Secure edges with toothpicks.

Sear chicken: Heat 30ml olive oil and butter in a large oven-safe pan over medium-high heat. Season stuffed chicken breasts with salt and pepper. Place chicken in the hot pan. Sear 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown.
Roast vegetables: While chicken sears, toss asparagus spears with 15ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Arrange on a baking sheet.

Finish cooking: Transfer the pan with seared chicken to the preheated oven. Add the baking sheet with asparagus to the oven. Cook chicken 15-20 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Roast asparagus 10-12 minutes, until tender-crisp.

Make red pepper coulis: While chicken cooks, halve and deseed red bell peppers. Place cut-side down on a baking sheet. Roast in the oven with chicken/asparagus for 20-25 minutes, until skins are blistered and charred. Remove from oven, let cool slightly. Peel skins from peppers. Transfer roasted peppers to a blender with chicken broth. Blend until very smooth. Strain coulis through a fine-mesh sieve for a silky texture. Season with salt and pepper.
Rest and serve: Remove chicken from oven. Let rest 5 minutes before serving. Remove toothpicks. Serve each chicken breast with roasted asparagus. Drizzle red pepper coulis around the plate.

recipes.recipe_name: Spanish Braised Beef with Bell Peppers
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Spanish Braised Beef is presented in a deep, clean white porcelain bowl. Hearty, irregular 4-5 cm beef chunks, rich mahogany-brown from braising, are nestled among vibrant, diced red and green bell peppers and softened onion pieces. All ingredients are coated in a glossy, thick, reddish-brown sauce, infused with paprika. The beef shows its tender, slow-cooked texture. A sprinkle of bright green, freshly chopped parsley provides a contrasting pop of color on top. The bowl rests on a simple, rustic wooden table surface. A neatly folded white cotton napkin is placed beside the bowl. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish. A heavy-gauge fork and spoon are arranged to the right. The background is a subtle, blurred indication of a casual bistro setting with warm tones, focusing attention on the inviting meal.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread for dipping in the rich sauce.
Pair with a robust Spanish red wine, such as Tempranillo.
instructions: Cut beef chuck into 4-5 cm chunks. Season beef generously with salt and black pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven or heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat.
Sear beef chunks in batches until well browned on all sides. Do not overcrowd the pot. Remove beef and set aside.
Add diced onions to the same pot. Sauté until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Add minced garlic and diced red and green bell peppers. Cook for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until slightly softened.
Stir in tomato paste and smoked paprika. Cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Deglaze the pot with red wine, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom. Reduce wine by half.
Return seared beef to the pot. Pour in beef broth. Add bay leaf and thyme sprigs.
Bring the mixture to a gentle simmer. Cover the pot tightly.
Transfer the covered pot to a preheated oven at 160°C (325°F).
Braise for 2.5-3 hours, or until the beef is fork-tender.
Remove bay leaf and thyme sprigs from the stew.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper as needed.
Garnish with freshly chopped parsley before serving.
notes: For a thicker sauce, remove beef and vegetables, then reduce the sauce over medium-high heat until desired consistency.
This dish tastes even better the next day; flavors deepen overnight.

recipes.recipe_name: Mandarin Honey Cream Cheese Mousse with Almond Sablé
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of an elegant dessert is presented on a modern designer plate, likely matte white or light grey, set on a pristine white Carrara marble surface. The focal point is a perfectly formed, velvety quenelle of Honey Cream Cheese Mousse, its creamy, pale yellow hue contrasting with the plate. Around the mousse, vibrant orange dots and delicate swirls of Mandarin Fluid Gel are artfully placed, creating a flowing, organic composition. Two or three thin, crisp Almond Sablé shards, with a golden-brown hue, are strategically positioned, leaning against the mousse, adding architectural height and textural contrast. A light scattering of fine, reddish-brown Cinnamon Crumble subtly enhances the visual depth and aroma. A few translucent, finely julienned strands of Candied Mandarin Peel adorn the top of the mousse, providing a sophisticated garnish. Abundant negative space surrounds the components, emphasizing the minimalist and precise plating. The scene is lit with dramatic professional lighting, casting soft shadows that highlight the textures and forms, with an ultra-minimalist background.
instructions: For the Honey Cream Cheese Mousse: Bloom gelatin in cold water. In a bowl, whisk cream cheese until smooth. Gently warm honey. Stir bloomed gelatin into warm honey until dissolved. Pour honey mixture into cream cheese. Whisk until fully combined. In a separate bowl, whip heavy cream to soft peaks. Fold whipped cream into cream cheese mixture in two additions. Transfer mousse to a piping bag. Pipe into small molds or onto a lined tray. Chill for at least 4 hours, or freeze briefly for easier handling.

For the Mandarin Fluid Gel: Combine mandarin juice, agar-agar, and granulated sugar in a small saucepan. Bring to a boil, whisking constantly for 1 minute. Pour into a shallow dish. Chill until set, about 30 minutes. Once firm, blend the gel until completely smooth. Pass through a fine-mesh sieve for ultra-smooth consistency. Transfer to a squeeze bottle.

For the Almond Sablé: Preheat oven to 160°C. In a bowl, whisk almond flour, icing sugar, and egg white until combined. Stir in melted butter. Spread mixture very thinly onto a silicone mat or parchment paper. Bake for 8-10 minutes, or until golden brown and crisp. Cool completely. Break into irregular shards.
For the Cinnamon Crumble: Combine ground cinnamon with a small amount of granulated sugar (e.g., 10g). Mix well.

For the Candied Mandarin Peel: Peel one mandarin. Slice peel into thin julienne strips. In a small saucepan, combine water and 30g granulated sugar. Bring to a boil. Add mandarin peel. Simmer for 10-15 minutes until translucent. Drain and cool.

To Assemble: Place a chilled Honey Cream Cheese Mousse quenelle or molded shape slightly off-center on each plate. Artistically dot the plate with Mandarin Fluid Gel around the mousse. Arrange 1-2 Almond Sablé shards leaning against the mousse. Sprinkle a small amount of Cinnamon Crumble around the plate. Place a few strands of Candied Mandarin Peel on top of the mousse or alongside. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Schwarzbier Schweinebauch with Potato Royale
recipes.visual_description: A single, impeccably plated starter course features a compact, golden-crisp square of slow-braised pork belly, seared to perfection, positioned elegantly on one side of a pristine white bone china plate. Adjacent to the pork is a smooth, ivory-colored quenelle of ultra-silken Potato Royale, its surface gleaming softly. A rich, dark amber reduction of Schwarzbier is artfully drizzled in a natural, flowing line around the main elements, adding a deep, glossy sheen and visual depth. A delicate, irregular shard of golden-brown rye bread, dusted subtly with fine black mustard seed powder, stands upright or rests artfully beside the pork, providing textural contrast. The composition is highly minimalist, emphasizing abundant negative space. A few vibrant green microgreens or finely snipped chives are precisely placed on the pork or potato, offering a singular pop of color. The setting is a luxurious, polished dark wood table with subtle grain. Professional, dramatic lighting casts soft shadows, highlighting the textures and rich colors of the dish. A pristine white linen napkin, folded into a precise triangle, and a single piece of polished silver flatware rest elegantly in the background, maintaining a clean, uncluttered scene.
instructions: Score pork belly skin in a crosshatch pattern. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Sear pork belly skin-side down in a hot pan until golden brown and crisp. Remove excess fat.
Add diced carrot, celery, onion, garlic, thyme, and bay leaf to the pan. Sauté until softened.
Deglaze with dark beer. Reduce by half. Add chicken stock. Bring to a simmer.
Transfer pork belly and liquid to an oven-safe dish. Ensure pork skin is exposed. Braise at 150°C for 2.5-3 hours until very tender.
Remove pork belly from braising liquid. Strain liquid and reduce to a thick, glossy sauce. Skim fat.
Press pork belly between two heavy objects in the refrigerator for at least 4 hours, or overnight. This creates a compact, uniform block.
For Potato Royale: Peel and dice potatoes. Cook in salted water until very tender. Drain well.
Pass hot potatoes through a fine-mesh sieve or use a potato ricer for extreme smoothness.
Gently warm cream and butter. Whisk in egg yolks and Dijon mustard.
Gradually whisk cream mixture into riced potatoes until completely smooth and silken. Season with salt. Keep warm.
For Mustard Seed Crisp: Grind black mustard seeds into a fine powder.
Cut rye bread into very thin, small squares or irregular shards. Brush lightly with vegetable oil.
Bake rye bread shards at 160°C until crisp. Sprinkle with mustard seed powder immediately after baking. Cool.
To serve: Cut pressed pork belly into 4 cm x 4 cm squares. Pan-sear skin-side down until very crisp and hot.
Spoon a quenelle of Potato Royale onto each plate. Place a seared pork belly square next to it.
Drizzle dark beer reduction around the pork and potato. Place a mustard seed crisp artistically on the plate.
Garnish with a few microgreens or finely snipped chives.
notes: Ensure pork belly is pressed thoroughly for a clean cut and crisp skin.
The Potato Royale must be exceptionally smooth; passing through a sieve is critical.
The dark beer reduction should be thick enough to coat a spoon, but still pourable.

recipes.recipe_name: Cornmeal and Tatsoi Pancakes with Poached Egg
recipes.visual_description: A stack of three golden-brown cornmeal and tatsoi pancakes sits centrally on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The pancakes, approximately 10 cm in diameter, have slightly crisp edges and a fluffy interior, speckled throughout with vibrant, dark green, finely chopped tatsoi. Perched atop the stack is a perfectly poached egg, its bright white albumen encasing a soft, rich yellow yolk that gently oozes onto the pancakes. A delicate scattering of bright green, finely chopped chives provides a fresh garnish. The plate is positioned on a simple, light-colored wooden table surface, with a neatly folded cotton napkin and polished flatware beside it. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, creating soft shadows. The background is clean and slightly blurred, suggesting a modern bistro atmosphere.
instructions: In a large bowl, whisk together cornmeal, flour, baking powder, and salt.
In a separate bowl, whisk milk, the single large egg, and melted butter.
Pour wet ingredients into dry ingredients. Whisk until just combined. Do not overmix.
Gently fold in the finely chopped tatsoi.
Heat a large non-stick pan or griddle over medium heat. Lightly oil the surface.
Pour 80ml of batter per pancake. Cook 3-4 minutes per side, until golden brown and cooked through. Keep warm. Repeat for remaining batter to make 8-12 pancakes (2-3 per serving).
For poached eggs, fill a medium pot with water. Add white vinegar. Bring water to a gentle simmer.
Carefully crack one egg into a small bowl. Gently slide egg into simmering water. Repeat for remaining eggs, cooking 2-3 at a time depending on pot size.
Poach eggs 3-4 minutes for a runny yolk. Remove with a slotted spoon. Drain excess water.
To serve, stack 2-3 pancakes on each white porcelain plate. Top each stack with a poached egg. Sprinkle generously with fresh, finely chopped chives.

recipes.recipe_name: Seared Beef Medallion with Sweet Corn Puree, Bell Pepper Julienne, and Mushroom Jus
recipes.visual_description: A seared beef medallion rests centrally on a large, pristine white bone china plate. The beef, with a dark, crusty sear and rosy interior, is thick-cut. A vibrant, silky yellow sweet corn puree is artfully swished across one side. Adjacent to the beef, a small, elegant nest of finely julienned red and yellow bell peppers adds color and texture. A glossy, deep brown mushroom jus is precisely drizzled around the beef, forming an organic pool. Abundant negative space emphasizes architectural placement. A single, delicate sprig of fresh thyme garnishes the beef. The setting features a premium grey-veined marble surface, with the plate, a pristine white linen napkin (triangle fold), and minimalist cutlery. Dramatic professional lighting casts soft shadows, highlighting the dish's sophisticated simplicity and premium quality.
instructions: Prepare Mushroom Jus: Slice mushrooms. Dice shallot and one garlic clove. In a saucepan, heat 15 ml olive oil. Sauté mushrooms until browned. Add shallot and garlic; cook until fragrant. Deglaze with white wine; reduce by half. Add beef stock. Simmer for 20 minutes. Strain through a fine-mesh sieve, pressing solids. Return liquid to pan. Reduce until slightly thickened. Whisk in 20 g butter. Season with salt and pepper. Keep warm.

Prepare Sweet Corn Puree: In a small saucepan, combine corn kernels with 50 ml water. Simmer until tender, about 5 minutes. Drain well. Transfer corn to a blender. Add 15 g butter. Blend until very smooth. Pass through a fine-mesh sieve for ultimate silkiness. Season with salt. Keep warm.

Prepare Bell Pepper Julienne: Halve and core red and yellow bell peppers. Cut into very fine julienne strips (approximately 2 mm thick). Finely mince red chili. In a small sauté pan, heat 10 ml olive oil. Add bell pepper julienne and minced chili. Sauté briefly, 2-3 minutes, until tender-crisp. Season lightly with salt. Set aside.

Cook Beef Medallions: Pat beef tenderloin dry. Cut into four equal medallions, approximately 150 g each. Season generously with salt and black pepper on all sides. Heat a heavy-bottomed skillet over medium-high heat. Add 5 ml olive oil. Once shimmering, add beef medallions. Sear for 3-4 minutes per side for medium-rare, or to desired doneness. Add remaining 15 g butter and one crushed garlic clove and one thyme sprig to pan during last minute of cooking; baste beef. Remove beef from pan. Rest for 5 minutes.

Plate the Dish: Spoon a generous swish of warm corn puree onto one side of each large, round designer plate. Place one rested beef medallion precisely in the center of the plate. Arrange a small, artful nest of bell pepper julienne next to the beef. Drizzle the rich mushroom jus elegantly around the beef, creating a pool or delicate lines. Garnish each plate with a single, small fresh thyme sprig. Serve immediately.
notes: Ensure all components are prepared and kept warm for seamless plating.
For the silkiest corn puree, pass it through a fine-mesh sieve after blending.

recipes.recipe_name: Moroccan Chicken with Preserved Lemon and Olives
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented in a traditional shallow terracotta tagine base on a rustic wooden table. Four whole, golden-browned chicken thighs are nestled in a vibrant, thick yellow saffron sauce. The chicken skin is crispy and glistening. Bright green cracked olives and translucent yellow strips of preserved lemon rind are scattered across the sauce. Freshly chopped green cilantro and parsley provide a vivid color contrast. The entire plate is visible, showing the rich texture of the braised onions in the sauce. A side of fluffy steamed couscous in a small ceramic bowl and a piece of crusty khobz bread sit nearby. The lighting is natural and warm, highlighting the moist texture of the whole chicken pieces.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with steamed couscous
Accompany with crusty Moroccan khobz bread
Pair with hot Moroccan mint tea

ingredients.name: Preserved lemon, pulp removed and rind sliced

instructions: Pat chicken dry with paper towels.
Season chicken with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large tagine or heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs skin-side down for 6 minutes until golden.
Flip chicken and sear for 4 minutes.
Transfer chicken to a plate.
Add onions to the pot and sauté for 5 minutes.
Stir in garlic, ginger, turmeric, saffron, and Ras el Hanout.
Cook spices for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in chicken stock and deglaze the pot.
Return chicken to the pot skin-side up.
Add preserved lemon rinds and olives.
Reduce heat to low and cover.
Simmer for 30 minutes until chicken reaches 75°C internal temperature.
Stir in cilantro and parsley before serving.
notes: Ensure the preserved lemon pulp is removed to prevent excessive saltiness.
Use a heavy-bottomed Dutch oven if a traditional tagine is unavailable.

recipes.recipe_name: Spaghetti Carbonara with Fermented Garlic Scape Pesto
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of classic Spaghetti Carbonara, artfully twirled into a neat mound in the center of a handcrafted, matte cream ceramic bowl. The golden strands of spaghetti are generously coated in a luscious, emulsified sauce of egg yolk, grated Pecorino Romano, and starchy pasta water, creating a glossy, creamy texture. Interspersed throughout are small, crispy rendered cubes of guanciale, providing contrasting texture and deep savory notes. A vibrant green dollop of fermented garlic scape pesto is placed subtly to the side, offering a fresh, pungent counterpoint. Coarsely ground black pepper is sprinkled over the dish. The bowl sits on a light, textured reclaimed wood surface, accompanied by a simple silver fork and a natural, undyed linen napkin. Soft, natural light illuminates the scene from the side, highlighting the dish's rich colors and textures. The background is clean and minimalist, with a hint of green from a potted herb, maintaining focus on the food.
instructions: Cut guanciale into small cubes (lardons).
Heat a large dry pan over medium heat. Add guanciale.
Cook guanciale slowly until crispy and fat is rendered. Remove crispy guanciale. Reserve rendered fat in the pan.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a rolling boil. Cook spaghetti according to package directions until al dente.
While pasta cooks, whisk egg yolks, whole egg, and grated Pecorino Romano in a bowl. Add a generous amount of freshly ground black pepper.
Before draining, reserve 250 ml of starchy pasta water.
Drain spaghetti. Immediately add hot spaghetti to the pan with rendered guanciale fat. Toss to coat.
Gradually add the egg and cheese mixture to the pasta, tossing vigorously. Slowly add reserved pasta water, 30 ml at a time, continuously tossing until a creamy emulsion forms. Do not cook the eggs.
Stir in the crispy guanciale cubes.
Divide spaghetti among four bowls. Top each serving with a dollop of fermented garlic scape pesto.
Serve immediately with extra black pepper and Pecorino Romano.
notes: This recipe emphasizes zero-waste by utilizing starchy pasta water for sauce emulsion.
Fermented garlic scape pesto adds a unique tangy flavor and utilizes seasonal produce that might otherwise be discarded.
Source high-quality guanciale from ethical producers for a sustainable approach.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken Thighs with Apricot-Olive Pan Sauce
recipes.visual_description: Two pan-seared chicken thighs, their skin rendered crispy and golden-brown, are presented on a simple, round off-white ceramic plate. The chicken pieces are arranged naturally. A rich, glossy pan sauce, studded with vibrant orange chopped dried apricots and dark purple halved Kalamata olives, is generously spooned over and around the chicken. The sauce has a deep amber hue with subtle red notes from the raspberries. A few fresh rosemary leaves are scattered on top for green color and aroma. The plate sits on a well-used wooden dining table, with a casually folded cloth napkin and classic stainless steel cutlery. Warm, soft kitchen light illuminates the dish, highlighting its comforting textures and inviting colors. The background hints at a lived-in kitchen, maintaining a homely atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with couscous or crusty bread to soak up the sauce.
Accompany with a simple green salad.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Place chicken thighs skin-side down.
Sear chicken for 8-10 minutes until skin is crispy and golden brown. Flip chicken. Sear for 5-7 minutes.
Transfer chicken to a plate. Drain excess fat from skillet, leaving about 15ml.
Add diced onion to the skillet. Sauté for 3-4 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic and chopped rosemary. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in balsamic vinegar. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the skillet.
Stir in chopped dried apricots, halved Kalamata olives, and chicken broth. Bring to a simmer.
Return chicken thighs to the skillet, skin-side up. Reduce heat to medium-low. Cover.
Simmer for 15-20 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
Remove chicken from skillet. Stir fresh raspberries into the sauce. Simmer for 2-3 minutes, gently mashing raspberries.
Adjust sauce seasoning if needed. Serve chicken with generous spoonfuls of the apricot-olive-raspberry sauce.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Pollo en Salsa Roja
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Pollo en Salsa Roja served in a shallow matte-gray ceramic bowl. Two whole, skin-on chicken thighs sit at the center, coated in a thick, vibrant deep-red tomato and guajillo sauce. Large wedges of softened white onion and blistered serrano chilies are nestled around the meat. The sauce has a glossy finish with visible specks of charred vegetable skin. Fresh cilantro leaves are scattered on top. The dish is set on a light oak table next to a small basket of warm corn tortillas and a lime wedge. Natural side-lighting highlights the texture of the sauce and the crispy chicken skin. The background is a blurred modern bistro with white porcelain accents.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas
Accompany with Mexican red rice
Provide fresh lime wedges for acidity

ingredients.name: White onions, cut into thick wedges

instructions: Heat a dry skillet over high heat.
Char tomatoes, half of the onion wedges, and serrano chilies until skins are blackened.
Toast guajillo chilies in the same skillet for 30 seconds.
Soak toasted guajillos in hot water for 10 minutes until soft.
Blend charred vegetables, soaked chilies, and garlic into a smooth sauce.
Season chicken thighs with salt.
Heat oil in a heavy pot over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken skin-side down until golden brown.
Flip chicken and sear for 2 minutes.
Remove chicken from pot.
Sauté remaining onion wedges in the pot until softened.
Pour blended sauce and chicken stock into the pot.
Return chicken to the pot.
Simmer for 20 minutes over medium-low heat.
Ensure chicken reaches internal temperature of 75°C.
Garnish with fresh cilantro.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches 75°C at the bone
Charring vegetables is essential for authentic smoky flavor
Strain the sauce after blending for a smoother texture if desired

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Mushroom & Macaroni Fritters
recipes.visual_description: A casual sharing platter of golden-brown Fermented Mushroom & Macaroni Fritters rests on a light, textured reclaimed wood surface. The fritters are rustic, slightly irregular patties, approximately 5cm in diameter, showcasing a crispy exterior. Inside, the fritters reveal a soft, cheesy interior with visible pieces of dark, earthy fermented mushrooms, small macaroni tubes, and tiny, reddish-brown diced bacon lardons. They are arranged organically, not stacked, with ample negative space around them. A vibrant green basil oil is generously drizzled over and around the fritters, creating small pools of intense color. A few small, whole fresh basil leaves are scattered artfully for a natural garnish. The serving vessel is a handcrafted, off-white ceramic platter with a matte finish, reflecting an earthy, natural aesthetic. The background is minimalist, with soft, diffused natural light highlighting the textures and colors of the food. A natural beige undyed linen napkin is subtly placed.
instructions: Ferment Mushrooms: Slice 200g mushrooms thinly. Dissolve 5g fine sea salt in 250ml water to make a brine. Pack sliced mushrooms tightly into a clean glass jar. Pour brine over mushrooms, ensuring they are fully submerged. Use a fermentation weight or small plastic bag filled with water to keep mushrooms submerged. Seal loosely with a lid or airlock. Ferment at room temperature (20-24°C) for 3-5 days. Bubbles indicate fermentation. Store fermented mushrooms in the fridge once desired sourness is reached.
Prepare Bacon: Dice bacon into small lardons. Cook in a dry pan over medium heat until crispy. Remove bacon with a slotted spoon. Reserve rendered fat.
Cook Macaroni: Cook macaroni according to package instructions until al dente. Drain well.

Sauté Aromatics & Fresh Mushrooms: Dice remaining 100g mushrooms, onion, and garlic. Heat a small amount of reserved bacon fat or olive oil in a pan. Sauté diced onion and fresh mushrooms until softened. Add minced garlic; cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Grate Cheeses: Grate Bel Paese and mozzarella cheeses.

Combine Fritter Mixture: In a large bowl, combine cooked macaroni, crispy bacon lardons, sautéed onion-mushroom-garlic mixture, grated Bel Paese, grated mozzarella, egg, and breadcrumbs (preferably homemade from stale bread). Drain fermented mushrooms and finely chop. Add chopped fermented mushrooms to the mixture. Season with salt and black pepper. Mix thoroughly.
Form Fritters: Form mixture into small, flattened patties, approximately 5cm in diameter and 1.5cm thick.

Cook Fritters: Heat a thin layer of olive oil in a large non-stick pan over medium heat. Cook fritters for 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown and crispy. Alternatively, bake at 190°C for 15-20 minutes until golden.

Make Basil Oil: Blanch half of the fresh basil leaves in boiling water for 10 seconds. Immediately transfer to an ice bath to stop cooking. Squeeze out excess water. Blend blanched basil and remaining fresh basil with 50ml olive oil until smooth. Strain through a fine-mesh sieve for a clear oil, or leave unstrained for a rustic look. Season with a pinch of salt.
Serve: Arrange warm fritters on a serving platter. Drizzle generously with basil oil. Garnish with a few small fresh basil leaves.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Mushroom Dip with Crispy Macaroni and Bacon Dust
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a light, handcrafted ceramic sharing platter in a natural beige tone, set on a reclaimed light wood table. The background is clean and minimalist, with a hint of green from a subtly placed plant. Soft, diffused natural light illuminates the scene. A small, organic dollop of the creamy, earthy-brown fermented mushroom dip occupies the center of the platter, its surface gently textured. Around the dip, a scattered, natural arrangement of golden-brown crispy macaroni pieces creates a delightful textural contrast. A vibrant green basil oil is artfully drizzled over the dip, forming small pools and streaks that add a pop of color. A delicate sprinkle of dark, finely ground bacon dust lightly coats parts of the dip and macaroni, adding subtle visual depth. The presentation emphasizes negative space, allowing each element to stand out. The macaroni is small and irregularly shaped from crisping. The overall composition is clean, unfussy, and highlights the natural colors and textures of the ingredients in an eco-conscious, ingredient-focused manner.

ingredients.name: Mixed mushrooms (e.g., cremini, shiitake), cleaned, sliced 5 mm thick
Fresh basil leaves and tender stems

instructions: Prepare Fermented Mushrooms: Combine sliced mushrooms, 5 g non-iodized salt, and 250 ml filtered water in a clean glass jar. Ensure mushrooms are fully submerged. Seal with an airlock lid or burp daily. Ferment at room temperature for 5-7 days until tangy. Refrigerate after fermentation.

Cook Macaroni: Boil 500 ml water in a pot. Add macaroni. Cook until al dente, about 7 minutes. Drain macaroni. Spread macaroni in a single layer on a clean kitchen towel. Air dry for 1-2 hours until mostly dry.

Crisp Macaroni: Heat 5 ml olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Add dried macaroni. Cook, stirring occasionally, until golden brown and crispy, about 8-10 minutes. Remove from pan. Season lightly with salt.

Render Bacon and Make Dust: Place diced bacon in a cold pan. Cook over medium heat until crispy. Remove crispy bacon bits. Drain excess fat, reserving 5 ml for the dip if desired. Chop crispy bacon bits finely or pulse in a small food processor to create a coarse dust.

Make Basil Oil: Blanch basil leaves and stems in boiling water for 10 seconds. Immediately transfer to an ice bath. Squeeze out excess water. Blend blanched basil with 60 ml extra virgin olive oil until smooth. Strain through a fine-mesh sieve for a clear oil. Discard solids.

Prepare the Dip: In a food processor, combine drained fermented mushrooms, Bel Paese cheese, mozzarella cheese, and lemon juice. Blend until smooth and creamy. Season with salt and black pepper to taste. Adjust consistency with a small amount of mushroom brine if too thick.

Assemble and Serve: Spoon the fermented mushroom dip onto a handcrafted ceramic sharing platter. Arrange crispy macaroni around the dip. Drizzle basil oil over the dip. Sprinkle bacon dust over the dip and macaroni. Serve immediately.
notes: The fermentation process requires advance planning.
The macaroni crisps can be prepared a few hours ahead and stored in an airtight container to maintain crispness.
Reserve any leftover mushroom brine for other culinary uses, like salad dressings or cocktails, as part of a zero-waste approach.

recipes.recipe_name: Spanish Style Chicken and Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of Spanish Style Chicken and Rice is presented in a rustic, deep ceramic bowl on a well-used wooden dining table. Golden-brown, bone-in chicken thighs, cooked to tender perfection, are nestled amongst the vibrant, reddish-orange rice. The rice is moist, studded with visible diced red bell pepper, white onion, and small chunks of tomato. A sprinkle of fresh, bright green chopped parsley garnishes the top, adding a pop of color and freshness. The dish exudes warmth and comfort. A simple, sturdy fork rests beside the bowl. The setting is a cozy family kitchen, bathed in warm, natural light, reflecting a homely, lived-in atmosphere. The overall presentation is unpretentious and inviting, typical of a comforting family meal.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread to soak up the flavorful juices.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and black pepper.

Heat olive oil in a large, oven-safe pan or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear chicken, skin-side down, until golden brown and crisp, about 6-8 minutes. Flip and sear other side for 3-4 minutes. Remove chicken from pan. Set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion and diced bell pepper to the pan. Cook, stirring occasionally, until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic, smoked paprika, and dried oregano to the pan. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in crushed tomatoes. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring to combine.
Add rice to the pan. Stir well to coat the rice grains with the vegetable and tomato mixture.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring the mixture to a boil, stirring gently.
Nestle the seared chicken pieces back into the pan, skin-side up, ensuring they are partially submerged in the liquid.
Reduce heat to low. Cover the pan tightly. Simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until rice is cooked through and liquid is absorbed. Chicken internal temperature must reach 75°C.
Remove pan from heat. Let stand, covered, for 5 minutes.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Hoisin Glazed Shrimp and Cashew Egg Noodles
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented in a clean, white porcelain bowl, showcasing a vibrant, balanced composition. A bed of glossy, golden-yellow egg noodles forms the base, loosely piled. Succulent, curled pink-orange shrimp are artfully arranged among the noodles, coated in a rich, dark hoisin glaze. Thin, bright red strips of pimento pepper and translucent, thinly sliced bamboo shoots are interspersed, adding pops of color and crisp-tender texture. Scattered generously over the top are golden-brown, whole roasted cashews, providing a satisfying crunch. A sprinkle of fresh, vibrant green chopped scallions and cilantro adds a final flourish of color and freshness. The sauce glistens on the ingredients, creating an inviting sheen. The entire plate is visible, with moderate negative space. Served on a simple wooden table with a white cotton napkin and a pair of dark wooden chopsticks beside the bowl. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and colors in a modern bistro setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve hot with chopsticks

ingredients.name: Lemongrass
ingredients.quantity: 1 stalk, outer layers removed, finely minced (white part only)

instructions: Cook egg noodles according to package directions. Drain. Rinse with cold water to prevent sticking. Set aside.
Prepare the hoisin glaze: In a small bowl, whisk together hoisin sauce, soy sauce, rice vinegar, sesame oil, sugar, cornstarch, and water or chicken stock until smooth. Set aside.
Heat vegetable oil in a large wok or deep skillet over medium-high heat.
Add minced lemongrass, garlic, and grated ginger. Stir-fry for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add shrimp to the wok. Stir-fry for 2-3 minutes until shrimp turn pink and opaque. Do not overcook. Remove shrimp from wok and set aside.
Add sliced pimento pepper and thinly sliced bamboo shoots to the wok. Stir-fry for 3-4 minutes until vegetables are tender-crisp.
Return cooked shrimp to the wok. Add cooked egg noodles.
Pour the prepared hoisin glaze over the noodles, shrimp, and vegetables. Toss continuously for 1-2 minutes until everything is well coated and the sauce thickens and glistens.
Remove from heat. Stir in cashews.
Serve immediately in individual bowls. Garnish with fresh chopped green onions and cilantro.
