Briefly sauté diced onion and halved cherry tomatoes in remaining 15 ml olive oil in a small pan until softened, about 3-4 minutes. Season lightly.
Place a scoop of cheesy garlic mash on each plate. Arrange a glazed chicken thigh beside the mash. Add a portion of the apple-green salad. Scatter sautéed onion and cherry tomatoes around the plate.

recipes.recipe_name: Sustainable Chicken Roulade with Fermented Tomato
recipes.visual_description: A single starter portion is presented on a handcrafted ceramic plate in a warm cream hue, set on a light, textured reclaimed wood surface. Two thick, perfectly round medallions of poached chicken roulade are neatly arranged slightly off-center. The chicken is pale and moist, revealing a vibrant, rustic red-orange fermented tomato and herb filling at its core. A small pool of glistening, reduced tomato-thyme broth encircles the chicken, its color a deeper, richer red. A single, small sprig of fresh green thyme rests delicately on one of the medallions. The composition emphasizes natural shapes and textures. Negative space is abundant, creating a clean, minimalist aesthetic. The background is soft and uncluttered, with a hint of natural light casting gentle shadows. An undyed linen napkin in natural beige is folded simply beside the plate, complementing the earthy tones.
instructions: To ferment tomatoes: Dice 300g tomatoes into small cubes. Place in a clean jar. Add 8g sea salt and minced garlic clove. Stir to combine. Cover loosely with a lid or cloth. Let ferment at room temperature for 3-5 days. Check daily for desired tanginess. Refrigerate once ready.
Butterfly chicken breasts. Pound each breast to an even 5mm thickness. Season lightly with salt and pepper.
Drain fermented tomatoes, reserving liquid. Roughly chop 5g fresh thyme. Mix chopped thyme into the drained fermented tomatoes.
Spread fermented tomato mixture evenly over each chicken breast. Roll each breast tightly to form a roulade. Secure with kitchen twine.
In a shallow pot, combine remaining 100g fresh tomatoes (diced), reserved tomato liquid, remaining 10g fresh thyme sprigs, and vegetable stock. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Carefully place chicken roulades into the simmering liquid. Ensure chicken is mostly submerged. Cover and poach gently for 20-25 minutes. Internal temperature of chicken must reach 75°C.

Remove roulades from liquid. Rest for 5 minutes. Strain poaching liquid into a small saucepan. Reduce liquid over medium heat until slightly thickened, approximately 10 minutes. Adjust seasoning if needed.
Remove twine from roulades. Slice each roulade into 2-3 thick medallions. Arrange 2-3 medallions per plate. Spoon reduced tomato-thyme broth around chicken. Garnish with a small fresh thyme sprig.

recipes.recipe_name: Pollo Perfetto con Essenza di Pomodoro, Mozzarella e Tagliolini
recipes.visual_description: A refined individual portion of 'Pollo Perfetto' is presented on a pristine, large round white bone china plate. The composition is minimalist and artistic, showcasing abundant negative space. Thick, pan-seared chicken medallions, golden-brown and perfectly cooked, are arranged elegantly to one side. Adjacent to the chicken, a small, meticulously twirled nest of delicate fresh tagliolini rests lightly. A small, crystal-clear pool of vibrant, ruby-red tomato consommé forms the foundation, its clarity a testament to precise clarification. A single, pure white buffalo mozzarella pearl is placed with precision, adding a contrasting color and texture. A few drops of verdant basil oil are artfully dotted around the plate, enhancing the visual appeal. The overall presentation is clean, sophisticated, and architectural, emphasizing the natural beauty and precise execution of each component. The plate sits on a premium white Carrara marble surface, complemented by elegant, polished silver flatware and a crisply folded white linen napkin, all under dramatic, focused lighting with subtle shadows.

ingredients.name: Fresh buffalo mozzarella (pearls or small ball)

instructions: Prepare Tomato Consommé: Roughly chop Roma tomatoes, shallot, and garlic. In a large pot, combine chopped tomatoes, shallot, garlic, white wine, and chicken stock. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 30 minutes, crushing tomatoes occasionally. Strain mixture through a fine-mesh sieve, pressing solids gently to extract liquid. Do not force solids through. Line the sieve with cheesecloth. Pass the liquid through the cheesecloth-lined sieve multiple times until consommé is crystal clear. Season with sea salt and black pepper. Keep warm.

Prepare Fresh Tagliolini: On a clean surface, create a well with the '00' flour. Crack eggs into the well. Using a fork, gradually incorporate flour into eggs until a shaggy dough forms. Knead dough for 10-15 minutes until smooth and elastic. Wrap in cling film. Rest for 30 minutes at room temperature. Roll dough very thinly using a pasta machine or rolling pin. Dust with flour. Fold dough sheet. Cut into thin tagliolini strands. Separate strands. Set aside.

Prepare Basil Oil: Blanch half of the basil leaves in boiling water for 10 seconds. Immediately transfer to an ice bath. Drain well. Squeeze out excess water. Blend blanched basil with 50 ml extra virgin olive oil until smooth. Pass through a fine-mesh sieve for a clear oil. Set aside.

Cook Chicken: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season generously with sea salt and black pepper. Heat 1 tablespoon olive oil in an oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken breasts for 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown. Transfer skillet to a preheated oven at 180°C (350°F). Cook for 10-12 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Rest chicken for 5 minutes before slicing into thick medallions.
Cook Tagliolini: Bring a large pot of salted water to a rolling boil. Add fresh tagliolini. Cook for 2-3 minutes until al dente. Drain well. Toss lightly with a few drops of basil oil.

Assemble and Serve: Pour a small pool of warm tomato consommé into the center of each shallow bowl. Arrange 2-3 thick chicken medallions artfully on one side of the consommé. Place a small, elegant nest of tagliolini next to the chicken. Garnish with one or two small, pristine fresh buffalo mozzarella pearls. Drizzle a few drops of basil oil around the plate for visual and aromatic enhancement. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Beef Fillet, Asparagus & Garlic Velouté, Confit Mushrooms, Parmesan Crumble
recipes.visual_description: A single, perfectly seared beef fillet medallion, displaying a deep, caramelized crust and a tender pink interior, rests artfully on a pristine white bone china plate. Beneath the beef, a vibrant green, velvety smooth asparagus and garlic velouté is spread in an organic, flowing sweep, contrasting beautifully with the rich brown of the meat. Beside the beef, a few confit mushroom halves, glossy and deeply flavorful, are intentionally placed. A delicate scattering of golden, irregular parmesan crumbles adds a textural counterpoint and visual interest. The plate exhibits abundant negative space, highlighting the precise arrangement and premium ingredients. The scene is set on a luxurious white Carrara marble surface, with a pristine white linen napkin folded into a precise triangle. Dramatic professional lighting casts soft shadows, enhancing the dish's sophisticated simplicity. The background is ultra-minimalist, ensuring the dish is the sole focus of the image, showcasing refined restaurant plating for a single individual portion.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with elegant, minimalist flatware.
Pair with a robust red wine, such as a Cabernet Sauvignon or Bordeaux.
instructions: Preheat oven to 160°C.
For Parmesan Crumble: Grate 80 g Parmesan. Spread on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper. Bake 10-12 minutes until golden and crisp. Cool completely. Break into small crumbles.

For Confit Mushrooms: Halve or quarter mushrooms. Place in a small saucepan. Cover with olive oil. Add 2 crushed garlic cloves and 2 thyme sprigs. Cook over very low heat for 25-30 minutes, until tender. Remove from oil. Season lightly with salt and pepper.

For Asparagus & Garlic Velouté: Snap off woody ends of asparagus. Blanch asparagus in salted boiling water for 2 minutes. Immediately transfer to ice bath. Drain well. Sauté 2 minced garlic cloves in 10 g butter until fragrant. Add blanched asparagus and 200 ml stock. Simmer 5 minutes. Blend until very smooth. Pass through a fine-mesh sieve. Stir in heavy cream. Season with salt and pepper. Keep warm.

For Beef Fillet: Pat beef dry. Season generously with salt and pepper. Heat 20 ml olive oil and 20 g butter in a heavy-bottomed pan over high heat. Add beef. Sear 3-4 minutes per side for medium-rare, creating a deep crust. Add 30 g butter, 2 thyme sprigs, and rosemary sprigs to the pan. Baste beef continuously for 2 minutes. Transfer beef to a wire rack. Rest 10 minutes.

To Serve: Reheat velouté if needed. Place a generous pool of asparagus velouté on each plate. Slice beef into thick medallions. Place 2-3 medallions on the velouté. Arrange confit mushroom halves/quarters beside the beef. Sprinkle Parmesan crumble over the dish. Serve immediately.
notes: Ensure beef is at room temperature before searing for even cooking.
For a truly smooth velouté, pass it through a fine-mesh sieve after blending.
Do not overcrowd the pan when searing beef to ensure a proper crust.

recipes.recipe_name: Corn and Tomato Salad with Grilled Chicken and Cotija
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant Corn and Tomato Salad is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. Diced grilled chicken pieces are interspersed among charred corn kernels and halved cherry tomatoes. Thinly sliced red onion and fresh chopped cilantro add color and texture. A creamy, pale orange dressing lightly coats all components, ensuring a cohesive blend. Crumbled white cotija cheese is scattered generously over the top. The arrangement is natural and inviting, with moderate negative space. The plate rests on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by standard silver flatware and a folded cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its fresh ingredients and inviting colors, creating a casual bistro atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas on the side for scooping.
Offer a side of fresh salsa verde or pico de gallo for extra flavor.
instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season with salt, pepper, half of the chili powder, and half of the cumin.

Heat 15 ml olive oil in a grill pan or outdoor grill over medium-high heat. Grill chicken for 6-8 minutes per side, until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Rest chicken for 5 minutes. Dice into 2 cm cubes.
In the same pan, char corn kernels over medium-high heat for 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until slightly browned and tender-crisp.
Halve cherry tomatoes. Thinly slice red onion. Roughly chop cilantro.
For the dressing, combine mayonnaise, sour cream, juice from one lime, minced garlic, remaining chili powder, and cumin in a small bowl. Whisk until smooth. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
In a large bowl, combine diced chicken, charred corn, halved tomatoes, sliced red onion, and chopped cilantro.
Crumble cotija cheese over the salad ingredients. Pour dressing over the mixture. Gently toss to coat all ingredients evenly.
Squeeze juice from the remaining lime over the salad just before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Chicken and Roasted Tomato Rigatoni
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Braised Chicken and Roasted Tomato Rigatoni is centrally plated on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. Al dente rigatoni, coated in a rich reddish-orange sauce, forms the base. Tender, rustic chunks of braised chicken, with golden-brown exteriors, are nestled among the pasta. Halved, roasted cherry tomatoes, soft and slightly burst, add vibrant red and orange hues. Thinly sliced, caramelized red onion pieces are interspersed. Fresh green basil leaves, torn and scattered, provide striking color contrast. A light dusting of freshly grated Parmesan cheese adds delicate texture. The arrangement is organic, with moderate negative space. The dish sits on a simple wooden table, accompanied by silver flatware and a folded white cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish against a blurred modern bistro background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of crusty Italian bread to sop up the sauce.
Offer extra grated Parmesan cheese at the table.
Pair with a glass of dry red wine, such as Chianti.

ingredients.name: Dry red wine (e.g., Chianti or Merlot)

instructions: Season chicken thighs generously with salt, pepper, and dried oregano.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear chicken thighs until golden brown on both sides, about 4-5 minutes per side. Remove chicken and set aside.

Add sliced red onion to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 5-7 minutes. Add sliced garlic and halved cherry tomatoes. Cook for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until tomatoes begin to soften and burst.
Pour in red wine, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Let it simmer for 2 minutes until slightly reduced. Add chicken broth.

Return seared chicken thighs to the pot. Bring the sauce to a gentle simmer. Cover and braise in a preheated oven at 180°C for 25-30 minutes, or until chicken is tender and cooked through. Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C.
While chicken braises, cook rigatoni according to package instructions until al dente. Drain, reserving 125ml pasta water.
Remove chicken from the pot. Shred or cut chicken into large, rustic chunks.
Add cooked rigatoni to the pot with the tomato sauce. Add shredded chicken. Toss to combine. If sauce is too thick, add reserved pasta water gradually until desired consistency.
Stir in half of the fresh basil.
Serve immediately, garnished with remaining fresh basil and freshly grated Parmesan cheese.
notes: For best flavor, consider using bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs and remove skin/bone after braising.
Adjust seasoning to taste.

recipes.recipe_name: Harvest Chicken with Pickled Vegetables
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Harvest Chicken with Pickled Vegetables is presented on an off-white, matte ceramic plate, emphasizing minimalism and natural textures. A golden-brown, seared chicken breast, whole and unsliced, is placed slightly off-center. Beside it, golden, irregular 2cm confit potato chunks are loosely arranged, interspersed with earthy brown roasted mushroom halves and quarters. A cluster of bright green blanched broccoli florets adds a vibrant color contrast. A small, vibrant spoonful of the pickled relish, featuring halved red cherry tomatoes and finely diced pale green broccoli stem, provides a pop of color and fresh acidity. The plating is organic and unforced, with ample white space highlighting each ingredient's natural beauty. The scene is set on a light reclaimed wood table, with a natural undyed linen napkin, under soft, diffused natural light, ensuring a clean, uncluttered background.
instructions: Prepare garlic confit potatoes: Peel potatoes. Cut into irregular 2cm chunks. Place in small saucepan. Add peeled garlic cloves from one head. Cover with 200ml olive oil. Simmer gently over low heat for 25-30 minutes until potatoes are tender. Drain potatoes and garlic, reserving oil. Season with salt.

Prepare pickled broccoli stem and tomato relish: Separate broccoli florets from stem. Peel tough outer layer of broccoli stem. Finely dice the peeled stem. Halve cherry tomatoes. In a small saucepan, combine white wine vinegar, water, sugar, and a pinch of salt. Bring to a boil, then remove from heat. Add diced broccoli stem and halved tomatoes to the hot liquid. Let steep for 15-20 minutes. Drain the liquid.

Cook mushrooms: Clean mushrooms. Halve or quarter larger mushrooms. Heat 15ml olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Add mushrooms and sauté until golden brown, about 5-7 minutes. Mince the remaining 2 garlic cloves and add to the pan. Cook for 1 minute more. Season with salt and pepper.

Cook chicken: Pat chicken breasts dry with paper towel. Season generously with salt and black pepper. Heat remaining 15ml olive oil in the same large pan over medium-high heat. Sear chicken breasts for 6-8 minutes per side, until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from pan and let rest for 5 minutes.
Blanch broccoli florets: Bring a pot of salted water to a rolling boil. Add broccoli florets and blanch for 2-3 minutes, until tender-crisp. Drain immediately.

Assemble dish: Place one whole, unsliced seared chicken breast on an off-white, matte ceramic plate. Arrange a portion of the confit potatoes and roasted mushrooms beside the chicken. Cluster blanched broccoli florets for visual contrast. Spoon a small portion of the pickled broccoli stem and tomato relish near the chicken. Garnish minimally with chopped fresh parsley or chives if desired.

recipes.recipe_name: Poulet Sauté Crémé aux Kohlrabi et Blettes
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Poulet Sauté Crémé aux Kohlrabi et Blettes is presented on a simple, round, off-white ceramic plate. Two golden-brown sautéed chicken thighs, whole, are centrally placed, nestled among creamy, tender 1.5 cm kohlrabi cubes and vibrant green wilted chard leaves. The pale yellow cream sauce pools gently around the chicken and vegetables. Some kohlrabi pieces show slight caramelization. Freshly chopped tarragon is sprinkled over the dish. A small, separate mound of thinly sliced cucumber rounds sits casually beside the main dish, natural and unadorned. The setting is a well-used wooden dining table. A simple, folded linen napkin and classic, unadorned silver flatware are placed beside the plate. Warm, soft kitchen lighting illuminates the scene, creating a homely and inviting atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty baguette to sop up the sauce.
A simple green salad with vinaigrette.
Small boiled potatoes or rice.
instructions: Peel kohlrabi. Cut into 1.5 cm cubes. Separate chard leaves from stems. Chop chard stems into 1 cm pieces. Coarsely chop chard leaves. Slice cucumber thinly into rounds or half-moons.

Pat chicken dry. Season with salt and pepper. Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken thighs 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C). Remove chicken. Set aside.
Add butter to the skillet. Add minced shallots and kohlrabi cubes. Sauté 5-7 minutes until kohlrabi softens slightly and begins to brown. Add minced garlic and chard stems. Sauté 2 minutes more.
Pour in chicken broth. Scrape up browned bits from the bottom of the pan. Bring to a simmer. Cook 5 minutes until liquid slightly reduces.
Stir in crème fraîche and Dijon mustard. Return chicken to the skillet. Add chopped chard leaves. Simmer 3-5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until chard wilts and sauce thickens slightly.
Stir in fresh tarragon. Season with salt and pepper to taste. Serve chicken and sauce hot. Serve cucumber slices on the side.
notes: Chicken thighs are recommended for their flavor and tenderness in this type of dish.
Adjust sauce consistency by simmering longer for thicker or adding a splash more broth for thinner.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Chili Garlic Mushroom & Bean Rice Bowl
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented in a clean, white ceramic bowl, showcasing distinct components. Fluffy white Jasmine rice forms the base. Piled beside the rice are glossy, seared cremini mushrooms, cut into thick slices, coated in a vibrant red-orange chili-garlic sauce. Bright green blanched green beans, cut into 3cm pieces, are neatly arranged alongside the mushrooms. Scattered around are tender-crisp broccoli florets, roasted until slightly charred at the edges, adding texture and deep green color. A sprinkle of thinly sliced spring onions and toasted sesame seeds garnishes the bowl, providing fresh contrast and nutty aroma. The composition is balanced, with moderate negative space. The entire bowl is visible. Served on a simple wooden table with natural, even lighting, accompanied by a pair of dark wooden chopsticks and a folded cotton napkin.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with chopsticks in individual ceramic bowls.
Offer a side of pickled ginger or kimchi for an authentic accompaniment.
instructions: Rinse jasmine rice thoroughly. Cook rice according to package directions, or use a rice cooker, with 450ml water. Set aside.
Preheat oven to 200°C. Toss broccoli florets with 15ml vegetable oil, salt, and pepper. Roast for 15-20 minutes until tender-crisp and slightly charred. Set aside.
Trim green beans. Blanch in boiling salted water for 2-3 minutes until bright green and tender-crisp. Immediately transfer to an ice bath to stop cooking. Drain and set aside.
Slice mushrooms into thick pieces. Mince garlic and red chilies. Grate ginger.
Heat remaining 15ml vegetable oil in a large wok or frying pan over medium-high heat.
Add mushrooms to the hot pan. Sear without stirring for 3-4 minutes until golden brown. Stir and cook for another 3-4 minutes until tender. Season with salt and pepper.
Add minced garlic, red chilies, and grated ginger to the mushrooms. Stir-fry for 1 minute until fragrant.
In a small bowl, whisk together soy sauce, rice vinegar, and sesame oil. Pour sauce over mushrooms. Stir to coat. Cook for 1-2 minutes until sauce slightly thickens.
Add blanched green beans to the mushroom mixture. Toss to combine and heat through.
To serve, divide cooked rice among four white ceramic bowls. Arrange chili garlic mushrooms, green beans, and roasted broccoli florets neatly beside the rice.
Garnish with thinly sliced spring onions and toasted sesame seeds. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Mushroom and Broccoli Risotto with Chili Garlic Drizzle
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of creamy Mushroom and Broccoli Risotto is presented in a shallow, matte white porcelain bowl. The risotto, a fluid, pale golden hue, spreads naturally across the plate, showcasing its rich texture. Visible throughout are tender, earthy brown chunks of sautéed mushrooms, vibrant bright green broccoli florets, and soft white cannellini beans. A thin, glistening drizzle of red chili-garlic oil artfully zigzags across the surface, adding a pop of color and sheen. A sprinkle of fresh, finely chopped dark green parsley garnishes the center. The dish rests on a simple, light-colored wooden table, beside a folded off-white cotton napkin. Natural, soft lighting illuminates the scene, creating subtle shadows that enhance depth. The background is clean and minimally blurred, maintaining a professional yet approachable bistro aesthetic.

ingredients.name: Canned cannellini beans, drained and rinsed

instructions: Rehydrate dried porcini mushrooms in 250ml hot water for 20 minutes. Strain liquid through a fine sieve into a saucepan. Chop rehydrated porcini.
Add remaining vegetable broth to the saucepan with porcini liquid. Heat to a simmer. Keep warm.
Finely dice the shallot. Mince garlic. Thinly slice the red chili.
In a large, heavy-bottomed pan, heat 15ml olive oil over medium heat. Add diced shallot. Sauté until translucent, about 3-4 minutes.
Add Arborio rice to the pan. Toast for 2 minutes, stirring constantly until edges are translucent.
Pour in white wine. Stir until completely absorbed by the rice.
Add chopped rehydrated porcini and cremini mushrooms to the rice. Cook for 3-4 minutes until mushrooms soften.

Add one ladle of warm broth to the rice. Stir constantly. Continue adding broth, one ladle at a time, allowing each addition to be almost fully absorbed before adding the next. This process takes about 18-20 minutes.
While risotto cooks, prepare broccoli and chili-garlic oil. Blanch broccoli florets in boiling salted water for 2 minutes. Drain immediately and refresh in ice water to stop cooking. Drain again.
For chili-garlic oil, heat remaining 15ml olive oil in a small pan over low heat. Add minced garlic and thinly sliced chili. Cook gently for 2-3 minutes until fragrant. Do not brown the garlic.
When risotto is creamy and rice is al dente (firm to the bite but cooked through), remove from heat.
Stir in butter and grated Parmesan cheese. This step is called 'mantecatura'.
Fold in blanched broccoli florets and drained cannellini beans.
Season risotto with salt and black pepper to taste. Adjust consistency with a splash more broth if needed; it should be fluid.
Serve immediately in shallow bowls. Drizzle each portion with the chili-garlic oil. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Clarified Chicken and Roasted Tomato Consommé with Tortellini
recipes.visual_description: A single individual portion of a refined Italian consommé is presented in a wide, shallow, bone china bowl with a subtle pattern. The consommé is crystal-clear, a brilliant amber-gold hue, revealing its depth and clarity. Resting gracefully in the center are three perfectly formed, delicate tortellini, their pale, tender forms creating a focal point. A precise, controlled drizzle of vibrant green basil oil encircles the tortellini, adding a sophisticated color contrast. Scattered artfully around the tortellini are a few delicate, golden-brown crispy garlic chips, providing a textural counterpoint. A single, tiny sprig of micro basil rests on one tortellini. The composition is minimalist and organic, with abundant negative space. The bowl sits on a pristine white Carrara marble surface. A precisely folded white linen napkin and an elegant silver spoon complete the setting. Dramatic professional lighting casts soft shadows, highlighting the dish's pristine presentation.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve as a 'primo piatto' (first course) in a formal Italian meal.
Offer crusty artisanal bread, such as ciabatta, on the side for dipping.

ingredients.name: Fresh tortellini (small, ricotta or chicken filled)

instructions: Prepare chicken broth: Place whole chicken, onion, carrot, celery, and peppercorns in a large pot. Cover with 3 liters of cold water. Bring to a gentle simmer. Skim any foam. Simmer for 2 hours. Strain broth through a fine-mesh sieve. Discard solids. Chill broth completely.

Roast tomatoes and garlic: Halve plum tomatoes. Toss with 1 tablespoon olive oil and 2 unpeeled garlic cloves. Roast at 180°C (350°F) for 25 minutes until softened and slightly charred. Peel roasted garlic.

Prepare chicken for tortellini: Poach chicken breast in lightly salted water until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Shred finely. Mix with a small amount of ricotta if making a custom filling, or set aside if using pre-filled tortellini.

Clarify consommé: In a large pot, combine chilled chicken broth with roasted tomatoes and peeled roasted garlic. Add 4 egg whites and 100g finely ground chicken (optional, for extra clarity). Whisk until egg whites are frothy. Bring to a very gentle simmer. Do not stir. A 'raft' will form on top. Simmer gently for 45-60 minutes. The broth below the raft will become clear.
Strain consommé: Carefully ladle the clear consommé through a cheesecloth-lined sieve. Do not disturb the raft. Discard the raft and solids. Season consommé with flaky sea salt to taste.
Make crispy garlic chips: Thinly slice remaining 4 garlic cloves. Fry in 2 tablespoons olive oil over low heat until golden and crisp. Drain on paper towel. Season with a pinch of salt.
Cook tortellini: Bring a pot of salted water to a boil. Cook tortellini according to package instructions until al dente. Drain.

Assemble dish: Gently place 3-5 cooked tortellini in the center of each warm serving bowl. Ladle hot, clear consommé around the tortellini. Drizzle with basil oil (made by blending fresh basil with olive oil). Garnish with crispy garlic chips and a tiny micro basil leaf.
Serve immediately.
notes: The clarity of the consommé is crucial; take time with the clarification process.
Ensure the chicken breast for tortellini filling reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).

recipes.recipe_name: Cheesy Salmon & Vegetable Bake
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Cheesy Salmon & Vegetable Bake rests on a simple, round ceramic plate. A whole, baked salmon fillet, flaky and moist, is nestled among roasted vegetables. Carrots are tender, slightly caramelized chunks, onion wedges are soft and sweet, and halved tomatoes are blistered and juicy. A generous layer of melted, bubbly, golden cheddar cheese blankets the salmon and some of the vegetables. The dish exudes warmth with natural, inviting colors. The plate sits on a well-used wooden dining table, illuminated by soft, warm kitchen lighting. A casually folded cloth napkin and basic flatware complete the homely, comforting scene, highlighting the dish as a satisfying, straightforward meal.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Chop carrots into 2cm chunks.
Cut onion into wedges.
Halve tomatoes.
Toss carrots and onion with 15ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking tray.
Roast vegetables for 15 minutes.
Pat salmon fillets dry. Season with salt, pepper, and dried Italian herbs.
Remove tray from oven. Add salmon fillets and halved tomatoes to the tray.
Drizzle salmon and tomatoes with remaining 15ml olive oil.
Return tray to oven. Bake for 10 minutes.
Remove tray. Sprinkle shredded cheddar cheese evenly over salmon and vegetables.
Return to oven. Bake for 5-7 minutes, until cheese is melted, bubbly, and golden, and salmon is cooked through and flaky.
Serve hot directly from the tray or plated.

recipes.recipe_name: Apple & Beer Crumble with White Chocolate Ricotta Cream
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of warm Apple & Beer Crumble is presented on an everyday, slightly off-white ceramic plate. The crumble topping is golden brown and rustic, with visible oats and flour crumbs. Beneath, soft, amber-toned apple wedges are visible, some gently bubbling with beer-infused juices. A generous, irregular dollop of creamy white ricotta cream sits beside the crumble, its smooth texture contrasting with the rough crumble. Scattered over the cream and around the crumble are small, glistening pieces of dark brown candied bacon. The plate sits on a well-used wooden dining table, showing natural imperfections and a warm, inviting patina. A casually folded beige linen napkin is placed beside the plate. The scene is lit by warm, soft kitchen light, creating a cozy and lived-in atmosphere. The entire plate is visible, with ample negative space around the food, allowing the comforting textures and colors to stand out. The presentation is homely and natural, emphasizing comfort and approachability.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C. Grease a 20x20 cm baking dish.

Peel, core, and slice apples into 1 cm thick wedges. Place in a large bowl. Add 50 g granulated sugar, 5 g cinnamon, 2 g nutmeg, and 2 g salt. Toss to coat. Pour 150 ml beer over apples. Mix gently. Transfer apples to the prepared baking dish.

For the crumble topping: In a separate bowl, combine flour, oats, 100 g brown sugar, and 2 g salt. Cut in cold, diced duck fat with your fingers or a pastry blender until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
Evenly sprinkle the crumble topping over the apples in the baking dish.
Bake for 35-45 minutes, or until the topping is golden brown and the apples are tender when pierced with a fork.

While the crumble bakes, prepare the white chocolate ricotta cream. Melt white chocolate in a double boiler or microwave. Let it cool slightly. In a bowl, whisk ricotta cheese, heavy cream, cooled black tea, and vanilla extract until smooth. Fold in the cooled melted white chocolate until combined. Chill until ready to serve.
Prepare the candied bacon: Cook bacon in a skillet over medium heat until crispy. Drain on paper towels. Discard bacon fat.

In a small saucepan, bring Dr. Pepper to a simmer over medium heat. Reduce until slightly thickened, about 5-7 minutes. Add 20 g granulated sugar. Stir until dissolved. Dip crispy bacon strips into the Dr. Pepper reduction, coating both sides. Place on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper.
Bake candied bacon at 180°C for 5-7 minutes, or until crisp and glazed. Watch carefully to prevent burning. Cool completely. Chop into small pieces.
Serve warm apple crumble with a dollop of white chocolate ricotta cream. Sprinkle with chopped candied bacon bits.

recipes.recipe_name: Rustic Chicken and Potato Soup
recipes.visual_description: A comforting, single portion of Rustic Chicken and Potato Soup is presented in a deep, off-white ceramic bowl, resting on a well-worn wooden kitchen table. The rich, golden broth cradles tender, irregularly cubed potatoes, hearty chunks of shredded chicken, and diced pieces of bright orange carrot and pale green celery. A generous sprinkle of vibrant green, freshly chopped parsley garnishes the top, adding a fresh contrast. The soup fills the bowl naturally, allowing the varied textures and natural colors of the ingredients to be clearly visible. A simple, off-white cloth napkin is casually folded beside the bowl, with a plain metal soup spoon resting on it. Warm, soft lighting from an overhead kitchen fixture illuminates the scene, creating a cozy and inviting atmosphere, typical of a lived-in family dining area. The background is minimal, focusing entirely on the wholesome, homely comfort food.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs 3-4 minutes per side until browned. Remove chicken. Set aside.
Dice onion into 1.5 cm pieces. Mince garlic. Dice carrots and celery into 1 cm pieces. Cube peeled potatoes into 1.5-2 cm pieces.
Add onion, carrots, and celery to the pot. Sauté 5-7 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Return chicken to the pot. Add chicken broth and bay leaf. Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer 20 minutes.
Add cubed potatoes to the pot. Continue to simmer 15-20 minutes, or until chicken and potatoes are tender. Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
Remove chicken from the pot. Shred chicken into bite-sized chunks using two forks. Discard bay leaf.
Return shredded chicken to the soup. Stir well.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper as needed.
Ladle hot soup into individual bowls. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Rustic Chicken, Potato, and Pasta Skillet
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous serving of Rustic Chicken, Potato, and Pasta Skillet is presented in a deep, glazed terracotta bowl, resting on a well-worn, light-oak dining table. The dish features succulent, pan-seared chicken chunks, mixed with al dente penne pasta, soft diced potatoes, and vibrant tender-crisp bell pepper and onion pieces. Rich, stewed diced tomatoes and hearty cannellini beans coat all ingredients, creating a comforting, cohesive look. Colors are natural: golden-brown chicken, deep reds from tomato and bell pepper, and earthy greens from fresh chopped parsley scattered over the top. The textures are varied and inviting. A simple, silver fork rests casually beside the bowl on a casually placed, folded linen napkin. Warm, diffused kitchen light illuminates the scene, casting soft shadows and highlighting the inviting steam. The background is a blurred, homely kitchen setting.

ingredients.name: Cannellini beans, canned, rinsed and drained

instructions: Cut chicken thighs into 3-4 cm thick chunks. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large, deep skillet or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken chunks until golden brown on all sides. Do not overcrowd the pan. Cook in batches if necessary. Remove chicken and set aside.
Add diced onion and bell pepper to the same pan. Cook until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Stir in minced garlic and red pepper flakes. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add diced potatoes, diced tomatoes, rinsed cannellini beans, chicken broth, oregano, and thyme to the pan. Bring to a simmer.
Return seared chicken chunks to the pan. Reduce heat to medium-low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes.
Stir in the short pasta. Continue to simmer, uncovered, stirring occasionally, until pasta is al dente and chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C, about 10-12 minutes.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Stir in fresh chopped parsley before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Chicken & Tomato Pasta Bake
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Spicy Chicken & Tomato Pasta Bake is presented in a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The dish features a prominent golden-brown, crispy breadcrumb topping. Beneath the crust, tender chunks of seared chicken are nestled among al dente penne pasta, coated in a rich, vibrant red tomato sauce. Bright yellow corn kernels provide pops of color. The creamy cottage cheese sauce is subtly integrated, adding a smooth richness. Fresh green chopped parsley is scattered generously on top for garnish. The chicken is cut into medium chunks, onions are diced, and garlic is minced. The plate sits on a simple wooden table surface, with a folded cotton napkin beside it. Natural, even lighting highlights the textures and colors of the dish, set against a blurred, casual bistro background.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C. Cook penne pasta according to package directions until al dente. Drain and set aside.

Cut chicken breasts into 2-3 cm chunks. Season with salt and pepper. Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken chunks until golden brown on all sides. Remove chicken from skillet and set aside. Cook chicken to an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
Add remaining 30 ml olive oil to the skillet. Add diced onion and sauté until softened, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in diced tomatoes, tomato paste, chicken broth, and dried oregano. Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat and cook for 10 minutes, allowing sauce to thicken slightly.
Stir in hot sauce and corn kernels. Return seared chicken chunks to the skillet. Add cooked pasta and toss to coat evenly with the sauce.
In a separate bowl, whisk cottage cheese until smoother consistency. Season with a pinch of salt.
Spread half of the pasta mixture into a 23x33 cm baking dish. Spoon half of the whisked cottage cheese over the pasta. Repeat layers with remaining pasta mixture and cottage cheese.
Process stale bread into coarse breadcrumbs. Spread breadcrumbs evenly over the top layer. Bake for 20-25 minutes, or until bubbly and the breadcrumbs are golden brown and crispy.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley before serving.
notes: Ensure chicken is fully cooked to 75°C (167°F) for safety.
Do not overcook pasta; it will finish cooking in the oven.
For extra richness, a sprinkle of grated Parmesan cheese can be added with the breadcrumbs before baking.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Chicken and Vegetable Skillet Pasta
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of Hearty Chicken and Vegetable Skillet Pasta is presented in a deep, everyday ceramic bowl. The dish features tender, browned chicken chunks (3cm) nestled among al dente penne pasta, soft diced potatoes (2cm), and vibrant diced bell peppers and onions. The rich, rustic tomato sauce coats all ingredients, showcasing natural reds, golden browns, and pops of green. The texture is hearty and comforting, with components naturally overlapping. A sprinkle of fresh, chopped parsley adds a touch of green. The bowl sits on a well-used wooden kitchen table, illuminated by warm, inviting light, reflecting a relaxed family dining atmosphere. A simple, dark-colored cloth napkin is casually placed nearby.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve directly from the skillet or in individual ceramic bowls.
Offer with crusty bread for soaking up the sauce.

ingredients.name: Canned cannellini beans, drained and rinsed
Large bell pepper (e.g., red or yellow), diced

instructions: Cut chicken into 3cm chunks. Cut potatoes into 2cm cubes. Dice onion and bell pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add chicken chunks. Sear until browned on all sides. Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside.
Add diced onion and bell pepper to the skillet. Cook for 5-7 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in tomato paste. Cook for 2 minutes. Add diced tomatoes, chicken broth, dried oregano, and dried basil. Bring to a simmer.
Add cubed potatoes to the skillet. Return chicken to the skillet. Reduce heat to medium-low. Cover and simmer for 15 minutes, or until potatoes are slightly tender.

Stir in pasta and drained cannellini beans. Increase heat to medium. Cook, stirring occasionally, for 10-12 minutes, or until pasta is al dente and most liquid is absorbed. Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste. Remove from heat. Let stand for 5 minutes.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley or basil before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Cajun Smoked Sausage Jambalaya
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Cajun Smoked Sausage Jambalaya is presented in a white porcelain shallow bowl, centered on a simple wooden table. The dish features fluffy, reddish-brown long-grain rice, generously interspersed with substantial chunks of browned smoked sausage, vibrant diced green, red, and yellow bell peppers, and tender diced onions and celery. The rich color comes from the seasoned tomatoes and browned ingredients. A scattering of fresh, bright green chopped parsley and sliced green onions provides a contrasting garnish, adding freshness and visual appeal. The jambalaya is moist and cohesive, not dry or clumpy. A cotton napkin is folded neatly beside the bowl, with a standard fork and spoon. Natural, even lighting illuminates the scene, highlighting the dish's hearty texture and inviting colors.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a bottle of hot sauce on the side for individual customization.
Offer cornbread or French bread as an accompaniment.
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Add smoked sausage slices. Brown until crispy. Remove sausage from pot. Set aside.
Add diced onion, green bell pepper, red bell pepper, and celery to the pot. Cook 8-10 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in Cajun seasoning. Cook 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Pour in diced tomatoes with their liquid and chicken broth. Add bay leaf. Bring mixture to a simmer.
Stir in rice. Return browned sausage to the pot. Ensure sausage is submerged.
Cover pot. Reduce heat to low. Cook 20-25 minutes until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed.
Remove pot from heat. Let stand, covered, for 5 minutes.
Discard bay leaf. Fluff jambalaya with a fork.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste. Serve hot. Garnish with chopped fresh parsley and sliced green onions.
notes: Ensure the internal temperature of the smoked sausage reaches 75°C (167°F) for food safety, though it is typically pre-cooked.
Adjust the amount of Cajun seasoning to achieve desired spice level.

recipes.recipe_name: Belgian Beer-Braised Beef with Creamy Brown Rice and Swiss Chard
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Belgian Beer-Braised Beef is presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate. Large, tender, deep brown beef chunks are nestled on a bed of creamy, al dente brown rice. A rich, glossy, amber-hued dark beer sauce generously coats the beef and subtly pools around the rice. Beside the beef, a vibrant pile of sautéed Swiss chard, with its deep green leaves and tender, pale stems, provides a fresh contrast. A small sprig of fresh thyme garnishes the beef. The plating is organized yet natural, allowing moderate negative space. The setting features a simple light wooden table surface, a white cotton napkin folded beside the plate, and even, natural lighting creating soft shadows, evoking a modern bistro atmosphere.

ingredients.name: Dark beer (e.g., Belgian Dubbel or Stout)

instructions: Cut beef chuck roast into 5 cm chunks. Pat dry. Season beef generously with salt and pepper.
Dredge beef chunks lightly in flour.
Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven or heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat. Sear beef chunks on all sides until deeply browned. Work in batches to avoid overcrowding. Remove beef and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion, carrots, and celery to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 8 minutes.
Add minced garlic and tomato paste. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Deglaze the pot with dark beer, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom. Bring to a simmer.
Return seared beef to the pot. Add beef broth, thyme sprigs, and bay leaf. Ensure beef is mostly submerged. Add more broth or water if needed.
Bring to a gentle simmer. Cover the pot tightly. Transfer to a preheated oven at 160°C (325°F). Braise for 2.5 to 3 hours, or until beef is fork-tender.

While beef braises, cook brown rice. Rinse rice under cold water. Combine rice with 500 ml water and a pinch of salt in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 40-45 minutes, or until water is absorbed and rice is tender. If desired, stir in butter and grated Parmesan.

Once beef is tender, remove from oven. Remove beef chunks and set aside. Strain the braising liquid through a fine-mesh sieve into a clean saucepan. Discard solids. Skim any excess fat from the sauce. Reduce sauce over medium-high heat until slightly thickened, about 10-15 minutes.
Wash Swiss chard. Separate stems from leaves. Chop stems into 1 cm pieces. Coarsely chop leaves.
In a large pan, melt butter over medium heat. Add chopped chard stems. Sauté for 3 minutes. Add chard leaves. Sauté until wilted and tender-crisp, about 3-5 minutes. Season with salt and pepper.
Serve braised beef chunks over a bed of creamy brown rice. Spoon rich beer sauce over the beef and rice. Arrange sautéed Swiss chard alongside the beef. Garnish with a fresh thyme sprig.

recipes.recipe_name: Savory Rye Blinis with Smoked Trout and Horseradish Cream
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of savory rye blinis is presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate, set upon a simple wooden table surface. Two golden-brown blinis, approximately 7 cm in diameter, are stacked or slightly overlapped. Each blini is generously topped with a dollop of creamy white horseradish-sour cream, contrasting with the blini's warm hue. Large, flaky pieces of smoked trout, displaying their characteristic pinkish-orange color, are artfully placed over the cream. A vibrant green sprig of fresh dill rests atop the trout, adding a fresh aromatic element. A bright yellow lemon wedge is placed beside the blinis. The arrangement is balanced and professional, with moderate negative space. A folded light grey cotton napkin is beside the plate. Natural, even lighting highlights the textures and colors of the dish, creating an inviting, approachable restaurant atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a crisp, dry German Riesling or a light lager.
instructions: Prepare Blini Batter: In a large bowl, combine warm milk and yeast. Stir until dissolved. Add rye flour, egg, melted butter, and salt. Whisk until smooth. Cover and let rest in a warm place for 45-60 minutes, or until slightly bubbly and risen.

Make Horseradish Cream: While batter rests, combine sour cream, yogurt, prepared horseradish, lemon zest, lemon juice, and chopped dill in a small bowl. Mix well. Season with salt and pepper to taste. Chill until ready to serve.

Cook Blinis: Heat a non-stick pan or griddle over medium heat. Lightly grease if needed. Pour about 30ml of batter per blini, forming small, thick pancakes (about 6-7 cm diameter). Cook for 2-3 minutes per side, until golden brown and cooked through. Repeat with remaining batter. Keep warm.

Assemble and Serve: Arrange 2-3 warm rye blinis on each plate. Top each blini with a generous dollop of horseradish cream. Distribute flaked smoked trout evenly over the blinis and cream. Garnish with fresh dill sprigs and a lemon wedge. Serve immediately.
notes: Adjust the amount of prepared horseradish in the cream to suit your personal spice preference.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Beef and Chicken Ragu with Rigatoni
recipes.visual_description: The Hearty Beef and Chicken Ragu is served in a clean white porcelain pasta bowl. Al dente rigatoni pasta is generously coated in a rich, deep red ragu. Tender, 2.5cm cubes of braised beef and chicken are interspersed throughout the sauce. Finely diced bell pepper and onion are visible within the sauce, adding subtle texture. The dish is garnished with a scattering of freshly chopped vibrant green basil and parsley. A generous mound of finely grated golden Parmesan cheese crowns the center. The overall presentation is rustic yet refined, showcasing the hearty comfort of the dish. Natural light highlights the sauce's sheen and the fresh herbs' vibrancy. A cotton napkin rests beside the bowl on a simple wooden table.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread for dipping.
Offer extra grated Parmesan cheese at the table.
Pair with a robust red wine like Chianti or Sangiovese.
instructions: Pat beef and chicken dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear beef cubes in batches until deeply browned on all sides. Remove beef from pot. Repeat with chicken cubes until browned. Remove chicken from pot.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion and bell pepper to the pot. Cook, stirring occasionally, until softened, about 8-10 minutes.
Add minced garlic and tomato paste. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly, until fragrant and tomato paste darkens slightly.
Pour in red wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Bring to a simmer and reduce by half, about 5 minutes.
Return beef and chicken to the pot. Add crushed tomatoes, beef broth, bay leaves, and dried oregano. Stir to combine.
Bring ragu to a gentle simmer. Reduce heat to low, cover, and cook for 2 to 3 hours, or until meat is very tender and easily shreddable. Stir occasionally to prevent sticking.
Remove bay leaves. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Cook rigatoni according to package directions until al dente. Drain pasta, reserving 125ml of pasta water.
Add cooked rigatoni directly to the ragu. Add a splash of reserved pasta water if needed to loosen the sauce. Toss to coat the pasta thoroughly.
Serve immediately, garnished with fresh basil, parsley, and grated Parmesan cheese.

recipes.recipe_name: Provençal Veal and Vegetable Soup
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of hearty Provençal Veal and Vegetable Soup is presented in a classic white porcelain soup bowl, positioned centrally on a simple wooden table. The rich, rustic broth, a warm reddish-orange hue from the tomatoes, holds tender, irregular chunks of slow-simmered veal, along with softened, substantial cubes of potato and thick rounds of carrot. Each ingredient retains its distinct shape and texture. Scattered atop the soup are golden-brown, pan-seared tofu cubes, providing a textural contrast. A light sprinkle of fresh, vibrant green chopped parsley adds a final pop of color and freshness. The bowl sits on a clean, light-colored wooden table. A folded white cotton napkin and simple, classic silver cutlery are placed beside the bowl. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its comforting warmth and robust colors. A crusty slice of baguette rests subtly on the side. The background is minimally blurred, suggesting a casual, inviting bistro setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Crusty baguette
instructions: Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear veal cubes, cut into 3 cm, in batches until browned. Remove veal and set aside.
Add remaining 15 ml olive oil to the pot. Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion and cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and tomato paste. Cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Pour in white wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom. Cook until wine is mostly evaporated, about 2 minutes.
Return seared veal to the pot. Add carrots, cut into 1.5 cm rounds, potatoes, cut into 2 cm cubes, canned tomatoes with juice, beef broth, bay leaf, and Herbes de Provence.
Bring soup to a boil. Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 1.5 to 2 hours, or until veal is very tender.
While soup simmers, prepare tofu. Press firm tofu to remove excess water. Cut into 2 cm cubes.
Heat a non-stick pan over medium-high heat. Add a small amount of oil. Pan-sear tofu cubes until golden brown and slightly crisp on all sides. Set aside.
Once veal is tender, remove bay leaf from the soup. Season soup with salt and black pepper to taste.
Ladle hot soup into individual bowls. Top each serving with pan-seared tofu cubes. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley. Serve immediately with crusty baguette.
notes: For best texture, ensure tofu is well-pressed before searing.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Sweet Potato and Butternut Squash with Feta
recipes.visual_description: Roasted sweet potato and butternut squash, cut into rustic 2 cm cubes, are piled generously onto a warm, everyday cream-colored ceramic plate, their surfaces beautifully caramelized and slightly browned from roasting. Interspersed among the golden cubes are soft, translucent thin slices of red onion, adding a subtle savory depth. A generous scattering of crumbled white feta cheese melts slightly into the warm vegetables, creating creamy pockets. Fresh, vibrant green parsley leaves are loosely scattered over the top, providing a pop of color and freshness. The dish sits on a well-worn wooden dining table, illuminated by the warm, inviting glow of kitchen lighting, suggesting a cozy, lived-in family atmosphere. A simple, silver fork rests casually beside the plate. The presentation is natural, unpretentious, and inviting, reflecting wholesome home cooking.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (390°F).
Peel sweet potato and butternut squash. Cut into 2 cm cubes.
Peel and thinly slice the red onion.
In a large bowl, toss sweet potato, squash, and red onion with olive oil, salt, and black pepper.
Spread vegetables in a single layer on a large baking sheet.
Roast for 25-30 minutes, or until tender and lightly caramelized. Stir halfway through.
Remove from oven. Transfer roasted vegetables to a serving platter or individual plates.
Crumble feta cheese generously over the warm vegetables.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken and Chorizo Paella
recipes.visual_description: An individual portion of Chicken and Chorizo Paella is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The rice, vibrant golden-yellow from saffron, forms a cohesive base with visible, distinct grains. Interspersed are tender, browned 3 cm chicken chunks and rich red 1 cm chorizo rounds. Diced red bell pepper and finely diced onion pieces add color and texture. Fresh green chopped parsley is sprinkled generously over the top, and a bright yellow lemon wedge rests at the plate's edge. The presentation is organized but natural. The background features a rustic wooden table, with simple, elegant flatware and a small ceramic bowl for discarded lemon rind, all under soft, natural lighting, creating an authentic Spanish bistro atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately, offering extra lemon wedges for squeezing.
Traditionally enjoyed communally from a large paella pan, but individual portions are common in restaurant settings.
Pair with a crisp Spanish white wine or sangria.

ingredients.name: Saffron threads
ingredients.quantity: 0.5 g, steeped in 60 ml hot water

instructions: Heat olive oil in a large paella pan or wide, shallow pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken chunks until browned on all sides. Remove chicken from pan. Set aside.
Add chorizo to the pan. Cook until slightly crispy and fat is rendered. Remove chorizo. Set aside.
Add diced onion and red bell pepper to the pan. Sauté until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Stir in minced garlic and smoked paprika. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in crushed tomatoes. Cook, stirring occasionally, for 5 minutes until sauce thickens.
Add rice to the pan. Stir to coat rice in the tomato mixture. Cook for 2 minutes.
Return chicken to the pan. Pour in hot chicken stock and saffron water. Stir gently once.
Bring to a simmer. Distribute ingredients evenly. Do not stir further.
Cook uncovered for 15-20 minutes, or until most liquid is absorbed and rice is al dente.
Reduce heat to low. Continue cooking for 5-7 minutes, listening for a crackling sound to form the socarrat.
Remove from heat. Arrange cooked chorizo on top of the paella.
Cover pan with foil or a lid. Let rest for 5-10 minutes.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley and lemon wedges before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Slow-Braised Beef and Chicken Ragu with Pappardelle
recipes.visual_description: Plated on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, a generous portion of wide, flat pappardelle pasta is coated in a rich, deep red slow-braised ragu. The ragu features tender, shredded beef and succulent chunks of chicken, visibly intertwined with the pasta. The sauce has a glossy, rustic texture, clinging well to the noodles. Bright green flecks of fresh chopped basil and parsley are scattered throughout, providing a vibrant contrast to the deep red and brown tones of the meat and sauce. A light dusting of freshly grated pale yellow Parmesan cheese rests on top. The dish is presented with moderate negative space, showcasing the hearty portion. The setting is a modern bistro, with a simple wooden table surface. A white cotton napkin is neatly folded beside the plate. Traditional silver flatware is placed alongside. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, emphasizing its warmth and inviting texture.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty artisanal bread for dipping.
Pair with a robust red wine.
Offer extra grated Parmesan at the table.
instructions: Pat beef and chicken dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear beef cubes (3-4 cm) in batches until deeply browned on all sides. Remove beef from pot.
Add chicken cubes (3-4 cm) to pot. Sear until golden brown. Remove chicken.
Add diced onion, carrots, and celery to pot. Cook, stirring, until softened, about 8-10 minutes.
Stir in minced garlic and tomato paste. Cook for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Pour in red wine. Scrape up any browned bits from bottom of pot. Simmer until wine reduces by half, about 5 minutes.
Return beef to pot. Add crushed tomatoes and chicken broth. Bring to a simmer.
Reduce heat to low. Cover and cook for 2-3 hours, or until beef is very tender and easily shreddable.
Add chicken back to pot for the last 30 minutes of cooking. Chicken should reach 75°C internal temperature.
Remove beef and chicken from ragu. Shred beef with two forks. Dice chicken into smaller pieces if desired. Return both meats to the sauce.
Stir in chopped fresh basil and parsley. Taste and adjust seasoning.
Cook pappardelle according to package directions in salted boiling water until al dente.
Drain pasta. Add drained pasta directly to ragu. Toss to coat.
Serve immediately. Garnish with grated Parmesan.

recipes.recipe_name: Black Truffle Porcini Udon
recipes.visual_description: A refined individual portion of Black Truffle Porcini Udon is plated on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. Udon noodles are loosely coiled, coated with a glossy, light brown mushroom sauce. Thick, pan-seared slices of porcini mushrooms are interspersed. Vibrant green asparagus batons, cut to 5 cm, are artfully arranged. Delicate, translucent shavings of fresh black truffle are generously draped over the dish. Finely snipped chives add a final touch of freshness. The plate features moderate negative space. On a simple light wooden table, elegant wooden chopsticks rest beside the plate with a neatly folded light grey cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting highlights textures and colors. The background suggests a blurred, casual restaurant atmosphere, focusing on the food.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve hot immediately.
Enjoy with chopsticks.
instructions: Rehydrate dried porcini mushrooms. Place dried porcini in a bowl. Cover with 250 ml hot vegetable broth. Let steep 20 minutes. Strain liquid, reserving broth. Coarsely chop rehydrated porcini.
Prepare asparagus. Trim tough ends. Cut asparagus into 5 cm batons. Blanch in boiling salted water 2 minutes. Drain. Immediately plunge into ice water. Drain well.
Cook udon noodles. Cook according to package directions until al dente. Drain well.
Sauté aromatics. Heat olive oil and butter in a large skillet over medium heat. Add minced shallot and garlic. Sauté 2 minutes until fragrant.
Cook mushrooms. Add sliced fresh porcini mushrooms to skillet. Sauté 5-7 minutes until browned and tender. Add chopped rehydrated porcini. Sauté 2 minutes.
Deglaze and simmer. Pour in sake, mirin, and reserved porcini broth. Bring to a simmer. Cook 5 minutes, allowing sauce to reduce slightly. Stir in soy sauce.
Combine. Add drained udon noodles and blanched asparagus to the skillet. Toss gently to coat noodles evenly with sauce. Cook 1-2 minutes to heat through.

Finish and serve. Season with salt and black pepper to taste. Transfer udon to individual serving plates. Shave fresh black truffle generously over each portion. Garnish with snipped chives. Serve immediately.
notes: The quality of fresh black truffle significantly impacts the final aroma and flavor.
Adjust the amount of soy sauce to your preferred saltiness.
Ensure udon noodles are not overcooked; they should remain al dente.

recipes.recipe_name: Tomato and Eggplant Risotto with Fresh Basil
recipes.visual_description: A single individual portion of Tomato and Eggplant Risotto is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. The creamy risotto is naturally mounded in the center, exhibiting a fluid, unformed texture, showcasing its authentic al dente consistency. Visible throughout the vibrant red-orange risotto are tender, deep purple-brown 1.5 cm diced roasted eggplant cubes and flecks of bright green chopped basil. A few small, fresh whole basil leaves are artfully placed on top as a garnish. A light grating of pale yellow Parmigiano Reggiano dusts the surface. A subtle sheen of olive oil is visible. The plate sits on a simple, light wooden table surface, accompanied by polished Italian flatware and a folded cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's rich colors and textures. The background is a softly blurred modern bistro setting, suggesting a casual yet refined dining experience.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately, as risotto loses its ideal consistency quickly.
Offer extra grated Parmigiano Reggiano at the table.
Accompany with crusty Italian bread to scoop up any remaining sauce.

ingredients.name: Ripe tomatoes (diced or crushed San Marzano)
Parmigiano Reggiano (or vegetarian hard cheese), grated

instructions: Dice eggplant into 1.5 cm cubes. Toss with 15 ml olive oil and a pinch of salt. Roast in a preheated oven at 200°C for 20-25 minutes until tender and lightly browned. Set aside.
Finely dice the onion and mince the garlic.
Heat 30 ml olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium heat.
Add diced onion. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened and translucent.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant. Do not brown.
Add Arborio rice to the pot. Stir constantly for 2-3 minutes to toast the rice until edges are translucent.
Pour in white wine. Stir until completely absorbed.
Add diced or crushed tomatoes. Stir well to combine.
Begin adding hot vegetable broth, one ladleful (about 120 ml) at a time. Stir continuously. Wait until each ladleful is almost fully absorbed before adding the next.
Continue adding broth and stirring for 18-20 minutes. The risotto should be creamy and the rice al dente (tender with a slight bite).
Remove from heat. Stir in roasted eggplant cubes, grated Parmigiano Reggiano, and most of the fresh basil, roughly chopped. Reserve a few small basil leaves for garnish.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste. If too thick, add a splash more hot broth. The risotto should be fluid, not dry.
Let risotto rest for 2 minutes before serving.
notes: Ensure vegetable broth is hot before adding to the rice; this helps maintain the cooking temperature and consistency.
Continuous stirring is crucial for releasing starch from the Arborio rice, creating the characteristic creamy texture of risotto.
traditional_techniques: Risotto method (soffritto, toasting rice, deglazing, gradual broth addition, mantecatura)

recipes.recipe_name: Mediterranean Salmon with Tomato-Grapefruit Salsa
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of golden-brown pan-seared salmon is centered on a clean, round white porcelain plate. The salmon, presented as a thick, whole fillet, has a crisp, slightly charred skin and tender, flaky flesh. Beside it, a vibrant mound of fresh tomato-grapefruit salsa bursts with color. The salsa features diced red tomatoes, glistening pink grapefruit segments, finely minced red onion, and chopped green basil, all lightly coated in olive oil. Small, creamy white cubes of fresh mozzarella are melted over the salmon, creating a soft, appealing texture. A sprinkle of fresh basil leaves adds a final touch of green. The plate is set on a simple light wooden table, with a neatly folded off-white cotton napkin to the side. Natural, soft light illuminates the dish, highlighting its fresh ingredients and inviting textures, against a subtle, blurred bistro background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty baguette or focaccia to sop up salsa juices.
Accompany with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and lemon.
instructions: Pat salmon fillets dry with paper towels.
Season salmon generously with salt, black pepper, and Herbes de Provence.
Heat 30ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Place salmon skin-side down in hot skillet. Sear for 5-6 minutes until skin is crisp and golden-brown.
Flip salmon fillets. Cook for an additional 3-5 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 63°C (145°F).
While salmon cooks, prepare salsa. Dice tomatoes into small cubes. Carefully segment grapefruit, discarding membranes and seeds.
Finely dice red onion. Mince garlic cloves.
In a medium bowl, combine diced tomatoes, grapefruit segments, finely diced red onion, and minced garlic.
Add remaining 30ml olive oil, a pinch of salt, and a pinch of black pepper to the salsa mixture. Stir gently to combine.
Just before serving, place small pieces of fresh mozzarella over each hot salmon fillet. Allow mozzarella to melt slightly from residual heat.
Plate each salmon fillet. Spoon generous portions of the tomato-grapefruit salsa beside the salmon.
Garnish with fresh basil or parsley leaves. Serve immediately.
notes: For best results, use fresh, high-quality salmon fillets.
This dish pairs well with a crisp white wine, such as Sauvignon Blanc or Pinot Grigio.

recipes.recipe_name: Black Truffle & Parmesan Capellini with Umami Dashi
recipes.visual_description: A single, refined portion is presented on a pristine, superpremium white bone china plate with a subtle, organic rim. A delicate mound of perfectly coiled capellini pasta, glistening subtly, occupies the center-right of the plate, leaving abundant negative space. Thin, ethereal shavings of fresh black truffle are meticulously draped over the pasta, their dark, intricate patterns contrasting with the pale strands. A single, golden, irregularly shaped Parmesan crisp stands elegantly beside the pasta, adding a touch of architectural height and texture. A clear, amber-hued umami dashi broth is carefully spooned around the base of the pasta, creating a serene pool that reflects the light. A scattering of finely chopped vibrant green parsley provides a precise, restrained pop of color. The dish is illuminated by dramatic professional lighting, casting soft, intentional shadows, highlighting the textures and minimalist composition. The setting features a luxurious light grey veined marble surface, a pristine white linen napkin folded into a precise triangle, and elegant, modern silver flatware, emphasizing the ultra-sophisticated and restrained aesthetic.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with small, delicate ceramic spoons for the broth.
instructions: Prepare Dashi: Gently wipe kombu. Do not wash. Add kombu to 1.5 litres cold water. Slowly heat to just below boiling (around 60-70°C). Remove kombu before water boils. Add katsuobushi and rehydrated shiitake. Simmer for 1-2 minutes. Strain broth through fine-mesh sieve. Discard solids.
Season Dashi: Season strained dashi with light soy sauce, mirin, and sake. Keep warm.
Prepare Parmesan Crisps: Grate 50g Parmigiano Reggiano. Form small mounds on parchment-lined baking tray. Bake at 180°C until golden and crisp, about 5-7 minutes. Let cool.
Cook Capellini: Bring large pot of salted water to rolling boil. Add capellini. Cook al dente according to package directions, typically 2-3 minutes.
Assemble Dish: Drain capellini. Divide into four warmed shallow bowls. Neatly coil pasta in center of each bowl.
Add Truffle & Parmesan: Shave generous amount of fresh black truffle over each pasta portion. Carefully place a Parmesan crisp beside the coiled pasta.
Serve: Ladle warm dashi broth around base of pasta. Garnish with finely chopped fresh parsley. Serve immediately.
notes: Use highest quality fresh black truffle for best aroma.
Ensure dashi is strained perfectly clear for visual appeal.
Capellini cooks quickly; timing is crucial for al dente texture.

recipes.recipe_name: Mediterranean Baked Salmon with Tomato-Mozzarella and Salt Cod Croquettes
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Mediterranean Baked Salmon is centered on a clean white porcelain plate. A whole, un-sliced salmon fillet, with its flaky, pinkish-orange interior, is topped with melted, slightly browned fresh mozzarella. Roasted cherry tomatoes, vibrant red and slightly softened, are artfully scattered around the salmon. Three golden-brown, crispy salt cod croquettes are neatly arranged alongside the main fillet. The dish is lightly drizzled with olive oil, enhancing its natural sheen. Fresh green basil leaves provide a pop of contrasting color. The plate sits on a simple, light-toned wooden table. A folded cotton napkin and standard metallic cutlery are placed beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and colors against a soft, unfocused background of a modern bistro setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and lemon.
Offer crusty bread for dipping in the pan juices.
instructions: Begin desalting salt cod at least 24 hours prior. Change water every 6-8 hours.
Drain desalted salt cod. Place in a pot with fresh water. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat. Simmer 10 minutes. Drain. Flake cod, remove any bones and skin.
Boil diced potato until tender. Drain well. Mash potato.
Combine flaked salt cod and mashed potato in a bowl. Mix thoroughly. Form into 12 small croquettes.
Set up a breading station. Place flour in one shallow dish. Place beaten egg in another. Place breadcrumbs in a third.
Dredge each croquette in flour, then egg, then breadcrumbs. Ensure full coating.
Heat vegetable oil in a deep pot to 170°C. Fry croquettes in batches until golden brown and crispy. Drain on paper towels. Season lightly with salt.
Preheat oven to 200°C.
Pat salmon fillets dry. Season salmon with sea salt, black pepper, and Herbes de Provence.
Place salmon fillets on a baking tray lined with parchment paper.
Scatter halved cherry tomatoes around the salmon fillets.
Drizzle salmon and tomatoes with 30ml olive oil.
Bake for 12-15 minutes, or until salmon is cooked through.
Remove tray from oven. Distribute torn mozzarella over salmon fillets. Return to oven for 2-3 minutes, until mozzarella is melted and slightly bubbly.
Carefully transfer one baked salmon fillet to each plate. Arrange roasted tomatoes beside the salmon.
Place 3 salt cod croquettes next to the salmon.
Drizzle remaining olive oil over the dish. Garnish with fresh basil leaves. Serve immediately.
notes: Ensure salt cod is properly desalted to avoid excessive saltiness. Taste a small piece before cooking.

recipes.recipe_name: Lamb and Pineapple Stir-fry with Green Peas
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Savory Lamb and Pineapple Stir-fry is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. Tender, browned lamb cubes are mixed with bright yellow pineapple chunks, vibrant green peas, and crisp-tender red and yellow bell pepper squares. Thinly sliced carrot rounds add orange color. The ingredients are lightly coated in a glossy, savory-sweet sauce, arranged in a natural, slightly mounded pile in the center of the plate, leaving moderate negative space. The dish is garnished with a scattering of fresh, thinly sliced spring onions and a sprinkle of toasted sesame seeds for added texture and color. The setting features a simple wooden table surface. Beside the main plate, a small, white rice bowl holds perfectly steamed jasmine rice, and a pair of dark wooden chopsticks rests neatly alongside. Natural, even lighting illuminates the scene, highlighting the fresh ingredients and inviting textures, creating a professional yet approachable presentation.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with steamed jasmine rice.
Use chopsticks for eating.
instructions: Pat lamb cubes dry.
Combine soy sauce, rice vinegar, brown sugar, sesame oil, cornstarch, and chicken broth in a bowl. Whisk well to create the sauce.
Heat 1 tbsp vegetable oil in a large wok or skillet over high heat.
Add lamb cubes. Stir-fry for 3-4 minutes until browned on all sides. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Remove lamb to a plate.
Add remaining 1 tbsp vegetable oil to the wok.
Add minced garlic and grated ginger. Stir-fry for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add red bell pepper, yellow bell pepper, and carrot slices. Stir-fry for 3 minutes until crisp-tender.
Return browned lamb to the wok. Add pineapple chunks and green peas.
Stir the prepared sauce again. Pour into the wok.
Cook, stirring constantly, for 1-2 minutes until the sauce thickens and coats all ingredients.
Remove from heat. Serve immediately.
notes: Ensure lamb is cooked to a safe internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).

recipes.recipe_name: Spanish Roasted Chicken with Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Spanish Roasted Chicken with Potatoes is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, showcasing a rich interplay of colors and textures. A golden-brown, crispy-skinned roasted chicken thigh, cooked whole, anchors the dish. Alongside it are generous, irregularly cut 3 cm roasted potato chunks, their exteriors golden and slightly blistered, revealing fluffy interiors. Thick wedges of caramelized red onion and vibrant, tender-crisp strips of roasted red and green bell peppers are nestled among the potatoes. A light sheen of olive oil and pan juices coats the elements. The dish is garnished with a scattering of bright green, freshly chopped parsley and a bright yellow lemon wedge positioned to the side. The overall presentation is inviting, rustic-elegant, and balanced, with moderate negative space.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread to sop up pan juices.
Offer a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and sherry vinegar.
Pair with a glass of dry Spanish red wine or a light lager.

ingredients.name: Potatoes (e.g., Maris Piper or Yukon Gold)

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and black pepper.
Peel potatoes. Cut into 3 cm chunks.
Halve red onion. Cut into thick wedges.
Core bell peppers. Cut into 3 cm strips.
Crush garlic cloves.
In a large roasting pan, combine potatoes, onion, bell peppers, and garlic.
Drizzle with 40ml olive oil. Sprinkle with smoked paprika and oregano. Toss to coat vegetables evenly.
Nestle chicken thighs among vegetables in the pan, skin-side up.
Drizzle chicken with remaining 20ml olive oil.
Roast for 30 minutes.
Remove pan from oven. Pour chicken stock and white wine into the pan. Stir vegetables gently.
Return to oven. Continue roasting for 25-30 minutes, or until chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C and potatoes are tender and golden.
Rest chicken 5 minutes before serving.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley. Serve with lemon wedges.
notes: Ensure chicken is thoroughly patted dry for crispy skin.
Adjust roasting time based on oven and chicken piece size.
For an extra layer of flavor, marinate chicken for an hour before roasting.

recipes.recipe_name: Arroz con Pollo
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Arroz con Pollo presented on a clean white porcelain plate. Two whole, bone-in chicken thighs with deeply browned, crispy skin sit atop a bed of golden, saffron-stained rice. The rice grains are plump and distinct, interspersed with fine bits of softened onion and concentrated red tomato. The dish shows vibrant yellow and orange hues from the saffron and paprika. A generous sprinkle of bright green, finely chopped parsley is scattered over the top. A single lemon wedge is placed neatly on the side. The plate sits on a light oak wooden table with a folded white cotton napkin. Lighting is bright, natural, and even, highlighting the textures of the crispy skin and the moist rice grains.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of Alioli (garlic mayonnaise)
Accompany with crusty bread and a glass of chilled white wine
Present in a traditional terracotta cazuela for family-style dining
instructions: Season chicken thighs with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a wide shallow pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken skin-side down until golden and crispy.
Flip and brown the other side. Remove chicken from pan.
Add onion to the same pan. Sauté until translucent.
Stir in garlic and grated tomato. Cook until liquid evaporates and mixture darkens.
Add smoked paprika and rice. Stir to coat rice in oil for 2 minutes.
Pour in white wine. Deglaze the pan. Simmer until wine reduces by half.
Add hot stock and saffron. Stir once to distribute.
Place chicken thighs back into the pan on top of the rice.
Simmer undisturbed over medium-low heat for 18-20 minutes.
Ensure chicken reaches internal temperature of 75°C.
Remove from heat. Cover with a clean cloth. Rest for 5 minutes.
Garnish with fresh parsley before serving.
notes: Do not stir the rice once the stock is added to allow a crust to form on the bottom.
Use a wide pan to ensure even rice cooking.

recipes.recipe_name: Sweet & Sour Tomato-Gherkin Sorbet with Candied Pork Crackling
recipes.visual_description: A minimalist, natural presentation on a handcrafted ceramic plate in an earthy tone. A single scoop of vibrant, reddish-orange sorbet sits centered, its surface slightly textured from churning. Around the base of the sorbet, small, glistening pieces of sweetened, diced gherkin are scattered, adding a translucent green sparkle.
