In a separate pan, sear the marinated chicken chunks in a small amount of oil or ghee over medium-high heat until lightly browned on all sides. Do not overcrowd the pan; cook in batches if necessary. Chicken does not need to be cooked through at this stage.

Add the seared chicken chunks to the smooth tomato gravy in the pot. Add 150ml water or chicken stock. Bring to a gentle simmer. Cover and cook for 15-20 minutes, or until chicken is tender and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C).

Crush kasoori methi between your palms and add to the pot. Stir in garam masala. Add the remaining 30g unsalted butter and heavy cream. Stir until butter melts and cream is incorporated. Do not boil after adding cream.
Taste and adjust salt as needed. Garnish with fresh coriander leaves before serving.
notes: For best flavor, marinate the chicken overnight.
Adjust the amount of Kashmiri red chili powder to control the spice level; it primarily provides color.
The gravy can be made ahead of time and stored in the refrigerator for up to 3 days.

recipes.recipe_name: Agnolotti al Broccolo, Consommé di Pomodoro, Pancetta Croccante
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented with sophisticated minimalism on a pristine white bone china plate with a subtle, elegant pattern. Four to five perfectly formed, golden-yellow agnolotti, their edges delicately fluted, are artfully arranged in a flowing, organic cluster at the plate's center, leaving abundant negative space. A small, clear pool of intensely ruby-red tomato consommé, shimmering with clarity, cradles the base of the pasta. Each agnolotto is plump, revealing a hint of vibrant green broccoli-ricotta filling beneath its tender pasta shell. Scattered precisely are a few golden-brown, crispy pancetta lardons, adding textural contrast and a rich umami note. A single, tiny, tender-crisp broccoli floret, its vibrant green hue standing out, is placed beside the pasta cluster. A few drops of glistening, emerald-green extra virgin olive oil are strategically dotted on the consommé, catching the light. The setting is a polished grey-veined Carrara marble surface, illuminated by dramatic professional lighting that creates subtle, elongated shadows, enhancing depth and dimension. A crisp white linen napkin, folded into a precise triangle, rests elegantly beside a set of polished silver flatware, emphasizing the refined dining experience.
instructions: Make pasta dough: Combine flour, whole eggs, egg yolks, and olive oil. Knead 10 minutes until smooth. Wrap in cling film. Rest 30 minutes at room temperature.
Prepare broccoli filling: Blanch broccoli florets in salted boiling water 2 minutes. Immediately transfer to ice bath. Drain well. Squeeze out excess water. Chop finely.
Combine chopped broccoli with ricotta, grated Parmigiano Reggiano, nutmeg, salt, and pepper. Mix well.
Roll pasta dough thinly through a pasta machine. Cut into small rectangles or squares (approx. 4x4 cm).
Place a small amount of broccoli filling on each pasta square. Fold over to create agnolotti. Seal edges firmly. Use a fluted pastry wheel to trim.
Prepare tomato consommé: Roughly chop tomatoes, celery, carrot, onion, and garlic. Combine in a large pot. Add basil. Cover with water. Bring to a simmer. Cook 30 minutes.

Strain solids through a fine-mesh sieve. Discard solids. Line a separate sieve with several layers of cheesecloth. Slowly pour strained liquid through the cheesecloth. Do not press solids. Chill consommé completely.
Render pancetta: Cook cubed pancetta in a dry pan over medium heat until golden and crispy. Remove lardons with a slotted spoon. Reserve rendered fat.
Cook agnolotti: Bring a large pot of salted water to a gentle simmer. Add agnolotti. Cook 2-3 minutes until al dente. They will float to the surface.
Warm consommé gently. Do not boil.

To plate: Arrange 4-5 agnolotti in the center of each shallow bowl. Carefully spoon a small pool of warm consommé around the pasta. Garnish with a few crispy pancetta lardons and a tiny blanched broccoli floret. Drizzle with a few drops of high-quality extra virgin olive oil.
